seeds.name: HappyToHelp
seeds.oneLiner: Help your team resolve customer questions with shared conversations and a searchable help center.
seeds.summary: Help your team resolve customer questions with shared conversations and a searchable help center.
seeds.maturity: Public source is available. Assisted is in early access with hands-on onboarding. Managed is in early access; requesting access does not start a subscription.

clauses.title: Native owner installation
clauses.text: A clean owner can inspect the operating description before installing dependencies, install locked source, prepare local or selected remote bindings/migrations, build, verify and deploy through `rer`. Local setup exits with no app running; dev prints a private `RER_OPEN` address that enters as the real local owner through the rer dev v2 boundary, preserving native sessions, roles and passwords. Reset is explicitly confirmed and local; export/import preserve supported native data with documented exclusions. Deployment dry-run makes no provider requests. The delivered runtime requires no original checkout or PHP service. **Acceptance evidence:** Use a clean checkout through rer describe/check, locked installation, setup, dev, verify, reset, export/import and deployment dry-run; preserve owner/data/settings and refuse unconfirmed destructive work. Prove the runtime works independently of the original checkout; separately qualify remote provisioning.

clauses.title: Retained native password identity (owner decision 2026-10-08)
clauses.text: Preserve native password sign-in, first-owner setup, the accepted owner experience and prior account/workspace data with the maintained Base command mechanisms. Retain this edition's authentication and native owner setup. Existing tenant and permission checks continue to govern every session. A second factor for these native accounts is required by IDENTITY-003; it adds to native passwords and never replaces them. **Acceptance evidence:** Complete native password setup, login, recovery and workspace re-entry, then upgrade with prior owner credentials and data intact; configured providers must not replace native identity.

clauses.title: Scoped authority
clauses.text: Owner setup, registration, login/recovery, project switching, membership and widget admission establish native identity. Every private read/write enforces the current actor/project/role; blocked or deleted projects and revoked credentials lose access. Provider configuration never substitutes for user authority. The public widget key and origin are not a secret: visitor, registration and project-creation requests are bounded by D1-backed limits (`RATE_LIMITS`) and refused with HTTP 429 and `Retry-After`. **Acceptance evidence:** Through native session and widget routes, deny cross-tenant, blocked/deleted and revoked access; prove public admission returns 429 with Retry-After when limited and provider configuration conveys no actor authority.

clauses.title: A useful first workspace
clauses.text: First-run setup is one screen: the owner's email, a password, the website and, only where the server requires one, the private setup token. Missing names and colors are derived and every derived value can be changed. A completed installation leads the owner to a workspace that is already set up, whose Setup page lists only what cannot be done for them (an AI service key, the widget on their website and, with a hosted email provider, a verified sending domain), leads with the widget, lets the owner skip any of them for now, and shows everything else under "What we've set". Every workspace created by first-owner setup, signed-in workspace creation or email-verified registration, and never a demo workspace, is provisioned in one step: a starter assistant as its default visitor assistant, a reply-by-email mailbox when the installation holds `INBOUND_EMAIL_TOKEN`, and mail sent from the installation sender until the workspace's own domain is verified. The starter assistant answers visitors by itself once a provider key exists, within the daily AI ceilings; with no key no assistant is assigned to a new conversation, it stays with the team and the AI page and Setup say a key is missing. The first-run Create workspace action may send one welcome email to the owner; an uncertain send is never replayed. Ordinary workspace creation leads with the widget snippet; Advanced retains the server secret and verification examples. Empty inboxes offer installation, a link to Setup and a demo. Workspace headers follow workspace switching. Visitor headers retain the operator's display name. **Acceptance evidence:** Run fresh first-owner setup and signed-in workspace creation to Setup and an installable widget; inspect derived editable name/color, starter assistant, mailbox/sender, skip/Advanced controls and mobile headers. With no model key a new visitor stays with the team; with a configured provider exercise the capped starter. A workers.dev hostname must not become a business name.

clauses.title: Rer dev mail
clauses.text: Trusted local development configuration uses the rer dev v2 development transport: it validates and suppresses visitor and teammate mail, reports `development`, stores no messages and exposes no mail viewer. It sends no external email and never claims delivery. The local owner enters automatically through the dev boundary; native password identity, ordinary hosted email-link confirmation and prior stored data are retained. Production has no local dev surface. Missing credentials or failed remote delivery never select a local substitute. **Acceptance evidence:** Enter through rer dev v2; send visitor and teammate mail and prove development suppression without storage, viewer or external send; refuse forged and production dev entry and never substitute suppression for a failed hosted provider.

clauses.title: Durable transcript
clauses.text: Customer, operator, generation, import and administrative writers preserve stable message/command identity, revision/frontier, attachment ownership and final-reply admission atomically. Competing or repeated writes cannot admit two incompatible final replies. Owner/admin contact erasure removes message content while keeping identity, revision and frontier, so erased transcripts stay coherent. **Acceptance evidence:** Race visitor, operator, model and import writers through conversation routes with duplicate and lost responses; admit only compatible final replies. Erase a contact through the owner door and verify coherent identity/revision/frontier with content removed.

clauses.title: Live delivery and recovery
clauses.text: Persist before broadcast; reconnect/outbox replay and socket authorization recover committed messages after reload, disconnection or process wake. Provisional AI deltas never become durable final answers until guarded admission succeeds. **Acceptance evidence:** Disconnect/reconnect widget and operator sockets after persisted writes, restart the runtime and recover the same committed messages/attachments; unauthorized replay is denied and superseded AI deltas never become final replies.

clauses.title: Existing editable experience
clauses.text: Reuse the original React dashboard, transcripts/drafts/suggestions, settings and Shadow DOM widget; preserve useful desktop/mobile flows, attachment display, collector/privacy controls and errors. Native routing and transport use the configured application origin. **Acceptance evidence:** Use the native dashboard and separately installed widget at 1440 and 390 pixels with realistic conversations, attachments, drafts, errors and workspace switching; retain the approved desktop/mobile navigation and configured-origin transport.

clauses.title: Reviewed history import
clauses.text: Current workspace owner/admin reviewers privately upload, inspect per-kind plans, source-located omissions, rejections, conflicts and publication changes, then explicitly apply bounded, resumable imports of conversations, contacts, tags, saved replies and articles. Preserve source identities, timestamps, private notes and publication state; reject unsupported meaning rather than inventing it. Recheck current role and workspace authority for apply, resume and whole-import undo. Retain immutable source custody and conflict-safe reversal journals. Imports and undo send no mail, widget messages, model requests, assignment or connection notifications; imports are excluded from Reports. Native tag controls enforce workspace scope. Owner decision 2026-10-09 requires exact business-state repeat/undo equality, including contacts, conversations, messages, private notes, tags, source links and every other imported business table. Only platform counters/sequences, audit history and import journals are excluded. Synthetic 1,000-conversation datasets for Zendesk and Help Scout qualify this local flow. **Acceptance evidence:** Through Move in, exercise all five kinds, source custody, per-row omissions/rejections/conflicts, current-role denials, inert apply/resume/repeat/undo and exact business-state equality for synthetic 1,000-conversation Zendesk and Help Scout datasets; counters/sequences, audit and journals are the only named exclusions.

clauses.title: Resolution feedback and provenance
clauses.text: Current original visitor sessions may rate a closed resolution with thumbs up/down and an optional comment up to 1,000 characters. Changes retain history; reopened cycles cannot receive the previous resolution's rating. Operators retain access to each past resolution's latest feedback after reopening; visitor eligibility and report denominators remain tied to the current cycle. Erasure removes rating comments. Confirmed operator-sent drafts establish assisted outcomes, otherwise confirmed human replies establish human outcomes. AI requires a complete visible answer history without a person handoff; missing evidence remains unknown. Status, assignment and cancellation transitions recheck current authority atomically. **Acceptance evidence:** Close, rate, rerate, reopen and close again via widget/operator routes; prevent previous-session/cycle feedback, retain old-cycle operator visibility, redact erased comments and verify human/assisted/AI/unknown attribution from actual visible answers.

clauses.title: Workspace calendar reports
clauses.text: Native conversations created in the workspace IANA calendar range with at least one persisted message form the cohort; Move in and legacy imports are excluded. First visitor-to-visible-answer response and creation-to-first known-resolution durations use median and nearest-rank p90. Each conversation contributes its latest closed cycle once to outcome and satisfaction rates. Reopened conversations leave those denominators. Aggregate queries return bounded data; CSV streams every matching conversation with formula-safe cells. Empty widget conversations stay durable but are excluded from Reports and its analytics CSVs. A separate step-up guarded JSON export includes all workspace conversations, messages, private notes and attachment names across dates and imports; attachment bytes stay in the portable backup. **Acceptance evidence:** Compare Reports and formula-safe CSV to hand-calculated response/resolution median and p90, latest-cycle outcome and satisfaction cohorts across DST and tenants, including more than 10,000 rows and excluded imports/reopened cycles.

clauses.title: Workspace integrations
clauses.text: Owner/admin tokens have explicit scopes, optional expiry, one-time display, hashed storage and durable audit. Bearer-only API calls have no CORS, per-token limits and native guarded writes. Contact erasure fences API identity restoration and pending event payloads. Native events commit tenant-bound webhook and Slack intents; historical import apply and undo do not emit them. Slack projects bounded native visitor text through Base escaping. Base owns signing, durable attempts and retry policy. HTTP 500 stays uncertain and is not replayed; 429 retains bounded retries. **Scoped edition override, owner decision 2026-10-09:** this consumer uses ordinary platform HTTPS fetch through the unchanged Base wire interface. It refuses every 3xx with manual redirect handling, enforces a 10-second timeout, a 1 MiB request limit and 64 KiB streamed-response limit. Destination syntax and literal IP validation remain enforced. This expressly overrides Base's transport DNS-pinning requirement for this edition; it does not claim DNS pinning or change copied Base contracts. Local synthetic protocol checks do not establish a live Slack connection or hosted installation. **Acceptance evidence:** Issue, use, expire and revoke each scoped show-once token; exercise native API operations, erasure fences, signed events and Slack escaping. Refuse redirects/unsafe literal destinations and over-limit traffic; preserve timeout, streamed bounds, uncertain 500 without replay and bounded 429 behavior under the recorded HTTPS override.

clauses.title: Observed owner setup
clauses.text: An owner sees the durable, project-scoped eight-step list on the Setup page; the genuinely empty inbox shows one next action and a link to it, and loads none of it. A step is confirmed only by an observation, never by a saved configuration, an installer default or a preset, so a workspace with nothing observed yet is zero of its applicable steps. The system runs its own checks: while an owner is signed in the page asks the server to observe, bounded by freshness windows. These checks are non-generative metadata, domain and DNS reads and never send mail. They distinguish saved configuration from observed sender DNS, authenticated model metadata, an inbound receipt, effective runtime ceilings, allowed origin and an authenticated widget ping; whether an article is published is not one of them (that step stays among the eight ids but is hidden and never counted). Mail to the owner is confirmed by a used emailed sign-in link, or by the provider's reported outcome for the welcome or test email; local development mail is suppressed and never confirms delivery, and provider acceptance or queueing is pending. `GET` performs no provider work and writes nothing. Only an explicit owner action (Create workspace, or Send me a test) may send mail, to that owner's mailbox, with durable identity; ambiguous work is never replayed. Missing provider permissions and unsupported status APIs remain unavailable. Configuration changes invalidate observations; model and DNS validation expire after 15 minutes and every observation shows its time. The owner can skip an owner-only step (the widget, the AI service, the sending domain) for now, and undo it. A skip is stored on the server for the workspace, can be made by an owner or admin only, makes no provider request, and moves the step out of Needs you and out of the confirmed count and its total; a skipped step is never shown as confirmed. An observation always wins: a skipped step that is later observed is confirmed and counted, and a rejected provider key stays under Needs you whether or not it was skipped. Provider keys and their fingerprints never enter API responses or browser storage. **Acceptance evidence:** Read Setup without side effects, observe fresh/expired/rejected configuration and explicit provider outcomes, skip/undo owner steps and reload. A skip or preset never counts as confirmation; local suppression never proves delivery; keys/fingerprints remain server-only and uncertain explicit test/welcome mail is never replayed.

clauses.title: Configured model execution
clauses.text: Retain Ensemble model selection, context/tools, streamed events, normalization, raw per-round provider usage, attribution, bounded suggestions and reply lifecycle. Missing providers fail explicitly when AI is asked for, and a default assistant whose provider has no key is simply not assigned to new conversations; uncertain provider attempts remain uncertain and are not replayed automatically. Usage is diagnostic/provider accounting data, not an active payment, balance or debit system. Visitor-caused automatic AI work is capped per UTC day per project and installation (`AI_DAILY_CEILINGS`); a skipped reply is recorded as terminal and never replayed. **Acceptance evidence:** Request configured suggestions/replies through native routes; inspect normalized streaming events, per-round usage, context/tool and budget bounds, explicit missing-provider errors and durable daily-cap skips; crash/ambiguous attempts must not automatically replay.

clauses.title: Published knowledge
clauses.text: Dataset ingestion/crawl, retained corpus, lexical/selected semantic retrieval, citations and article/category authoring maintain project scope and publication state. A failed refresh cannot replace the last usable published corpus. Public pages exclude drafts/deleted projects and preserve original canonical article/search routes. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish and search articles/categories through authoring and public help-center doors; deny draft/deleted/cross-project access, verify citations and canonical links and retain the last usable published corpus after a failed refresh.

clauses.title: Attributed customer context
clauses.text: Profiles, monitoring, insights and context packets preserve evidence attribution, source bounds, consent and project ownership. Provider output must satisfy the selected schemas before becoming usable customer context. **Acceptance evidence:** Generate/read profile, monitoring, insight and context packets through native routes; reject ungrounded/schema-invalid or cross-project content, preserve attributed evidence and respect consent/source bounds.

clauses.title: Explicit local authority
clauses.text: Pairing, devices/grants, revocation, tool context and work/result states preserve investigation, resolve and advance-authorized resolve-and-reply distinctions. Revocation withdraws authority and never asserts that a local process stopped: started work becomes terminal with an unconfirmed outcome, and only the device may report cancellation. Local processes remain in the optional connector, never an implicit Worker capability. **Acceptance evidence:** Pair the packaged connector, investigate, separately authorize a child fix, obtain a distinct read-only observation and use human Send with exact-request replay. Refuse stale/revoked/offline/unverified/uncertain work and distinguish resolve from advance-authorized resolve-and-reply; revocation cannot assert process cancellation.

clauses.title: Durable evaluation
clauses.text: Training and evaluation preserve run/case state, model/budget selection, raw provider usage and cancellation/recovery. Synthetic data admission is explicitly local/test-only. Historical pending attempts require reconciliation; a fixture pass is not live-provider quality acceptance. **Acceptance evidence:** Create, run, cancel and recover persisted evaluations through training routes with model/budget selection and raw usage; reconcile historical pending/uncertain attempts and keep synthetic admission local/test-only, with live quality qualification separate.

clauses.title: Honest external effects
clauses.text: Email/inbound mail, GitHub, branding and knowledge imports use configured native adapters, tenant-scoped credentials, durable identity and ambiguous-outcome handling. Website previews use a separate origin, scoped expiring grants and public-network restrictions. Machine-generated inbound mail never triggers autonomous AI replies, notifications or outbound email; its classification is recorded before admission and survives recovery and redelivery. The `email:` message local-id prefix is reserved for inbound claims and refused by the message API. Shopify, Stripe and CRM support actions are required by COMMERCE-001, BILLING-001 and CRM-001. HappyToHelp never holds funds or becomes a payment processor; historical imported balances remain custody records, not executable authority. **Acceptance evidence:** Use configured email, inbound mail, GitHub and knowledge-import public doors; test idempotency, machine-generated-mail suppression, separate-origin preview grants and network denial. An operator reply emails the visitor even with an online/unverified widget; a visitor address matching the reply sender is intentionally excluded and the message status explains that cause. Test accepted, failed and uncertain outcomes without invented delivery; business-action evidence is also required by COMMERCE-001, BILLING-001 and CRM-001.

clauses.title: Public product source
clauses.text: The “Knows what your customer needs before they do.” public homepage pairs a proactive checkout widget offer with an agent-resolved conversation and human Send. It presents the customer chat widget, shared inbox, help centre and configured AI assistance, using labelled HTML/SVG drawings, self-hosted Outfit and reduced-motion support. Public /docs pages render the repository Markdown selected by docs/site.json at build time, with navigation and a branded 404 for unknown pages. Published help centres preserve project scope, canonical links, search and draft/deleted denial. The widget remains available through owner-configured installation. Conversation, ticket-history and automation import, reporting and compliance claims are absent from this homepage; broader marketing routes, pricing, legal, referrer, waitlist and public auto-widget behavior are outside this edition.

clauses.title: Prior-data custody
clauses.text: Explicit legacy artifacts preserve IDs, exact historical financial values, transcripts, object hashes, publication and permissions through resumable guarded D1/R2 import. Historical financial SQL, imported rows and reconciliation holds remain immutable archive custody; they never become active payments, balances or provider work. The one exception is an explicit owner/admin contact erasure: it takes precedence over archive custody for that contact's personal data and redacts the imported rows and their verbatim archive copies (row digests are kept, so replaying the bundle does not restore them), leaving a `contact_erasures` audit tombstone. Old credentials do not become trusted native authority. **Acceptance evidence:** Import representative legacy IDs, permissions, exact historical financial values and media hashes through local D1/R2; resume safely and refuse conflicts without external work. Erase an imported contact and prove archive redaction plus tombstone/digest fencing prevents restoration of erased personal data.

clauses.title: Author-owned capability graph
clauses.text: The edition selects maintained source with inspect/check/lock/release commands. Shared capabilities include substantial implementation, migrations and meaningful tests; a second consumer preserves its own policy. Release excludes credentials/private fixtures and retains asset provenance/licensing obligations. Original work is preserved. **Acceptance evidence:** Run inspect/lock/check and offline Base-copy verification on staged intentional source, exercise origin/drift/mode refusals and release only the selected licensed tree without credentials or private fixtures; source custody alone is not product acceptance.

nonGoals: Implicit deployment or provider execution from source inspection
Reusing legacy passwords or grants as native authority
Regenerating or erasing original owner checkouts

original.title: Public product source
original.text: The approved homepage (owner approval 2026-10-01, clarity pass 2026-10-02, hero redesign 2026-10-08, hero leading with help before they ask 2026-10-20) is the real public `/` experience, in this order: the hero, whose headline “Knows what your customer needs before they do.” stands left-aligned beside one hand-drawn picture of both moments on a pale aqua blob, joined by an aqua pen arrow: 1, a checkout page in its window with the widget's offer card (signed with the speech-bubble mark) floating over its corner; 2, a conversation already solved (a customer, Maya, cannot turn on the Spanish version of her store; the agent's fix, beside a code glyph, says it is fixed; the reply to Maya carries Send inside it, the only step left), each numbered on a filled aqua disc; with the subhead “Some customers who get stuck never write in. They just leave.”, the line “100% free, open source alternative to Zendesk, Intercom, Help Scout and Freshdesk”, an aqua pen-stroke flourish under the calls to action that draws itself in once, and under the picture the captions “Before they ask” (“When someone seems stuck, the widget offers a hand.”) and “When they ask” (“Your Codex or Claude fixes the problem and writes the reply. You press Send.”) on filled aqua number discs; “Not just better. Free.” (100% free and open source, free as in code and free as in cost, MIT licensed, “No seats. No plans. No fees.”, each promise after a line icon in a pale aqua circle, with the MIT license drawn as an ink card over a wordless code editor, “free of charge” and the rights highlighted in aqua); “The rest of your support desk” (chat widget, shared inbox, help center, suggested replies, as frameless ink cards numbered on filled aqua discs); “Try it beside what you have” (install, bring the help center from Zendesk, Intercom or Freshdesk, add the chat widget, on filled aqua discs, beside the finished import in its window); “Ready when you are.”, a big closing headline with an aqua pen line drawn under it; and the footer, signed with the header's lockup. Below the hero the drawings carry the hero's language: each floats on a pale aqua blob, the mark's three aqua sparks spring from the corner of four of its cards, a window frame stays only for the code editor, the checkout and the import, the text links carry the hero's aqua underline, and a full-width aqua pen line with one loop divides Free from the desk and the desk from Try it beside what you have. The page carries no price, hosting or provider line and no plug for any other service. The drawings mirror the real interface and make no claim the product cannot back; conversation, ticket-history and automation import, reporting and compliance claims are deliberately absent. It is a warm off-white page in one geometric sans-serif (Outfit, self-hosted from `public/fonts/outfit/`, so the page makes no third-party request, over a metric-matched local fallback, so no text moves when it loads) with near-black ink and black pill buttons; color appears only inside the drawings, which are labeled HTML/SVG rather than raster images, and in aqua accents outside them (the hero's and the desk's number discs, the promises' circles, link underlines, the hero flourish, the dividers, the closing line) and in the sparks of the speech-bubble mark beside the header and footer wordmark. The wordmark is not set in Outfit: it is drawn by hand as round-capped SVG strokes following Nunito's letter shapes (SIL OFL), with no font data embedded, and the link it sits in is named HappyToHelp by visually hidden text. The page's text and real links, derived from `package.json` `repository.url`, are ordinary DOM content; the hero flourish draws in once as the page appears, and each moment below the hero (a drawing, the promises, the steps, a desk card, a divider, the closing line) plays once, in under 1.8s, as it scrolls into view (an IntersectionObserver), moving only opacity, transforms, clipping and strokes, so nothing shifts; reduced-motion preferences remove all animation, transitions and smooth scrolling without changing layout, leaving every drawing in its final state and every stroke fully drawn. `/docs` renders, at build time, the Markdown files listed in `docs/site.json`, in the homepage's paper, ink and Outfit, with section navigation, page contents and GitHub links for everything unpublished; an unknown page gets the branded 404. Every build renders the current files, and an unlisted Markdown file fails verification. Dynamic published help centers retain project scope, canonical links, search and draft/deleted denial. The customer widget remains available through owner-configured installation; broader marketing routes, pricing, legal, referrer, waitlist and public auto-widget behavior are outside this edition. **Acceptance evidence:** Exercise the approved homepage and /docs requirements retained in this clause and the detailed acceptance specification at desktop/mobile, including keyboard/reduced motion, published Markdown manifest/link validation and draft/deleted help-center denial; target requirements do not authorize changed marketing claims.

seeds.name: Lamp
seeds.oneLiner: Keep customers informed with a status page and clear incident updates.
seeds.summary: Keep customers informed with a status page and clear incident updates.

clauses.title: Public owner documentation
clauses.text: The app host serves `/docs` and each published `/docs/<slug>` page as public documentation built from repository Markdown selected by `docs/site.json`. Documentation is available without an operator session; the public page host does not serve it.

clauses.title: Contents
clauses.text: `GET /` on the status page host returns, in one response: the overall status; every visible component with its current state and note; every unresolved incident with its 5 most recent published updates, newest first, and a link to that incident's page carrying all of them; every maintenance that is in progress and every scheduled maintenance starting within 14 days; and each visible component's uptime figure and daily record for the reporting window.

clauses.title: Readable without script
clauses.text: The complete content of PAGE-001, and the subscribe form of SUB-001, are present and usable in the initial HTML response. With JavaScript disabled, every status, update, and timestamp is rendered and readable and the subscribe form submits. Script preserves the page’s configured time zone and its visible label; operator entry, timelines, previews and public timestamps use that same zone.

clauses.title: Weight
clauses.text: At the component limit in `seed.json → limits`, the public page's initial HTML response is at most 50KB gzipped, and the page issues at most 4 further requests — stylesheet, font, logo, script — all to its own origin.

clauses.title: Overall status
clauses.text: *Policy: `page.status-rollup.v1`; default: the overall status is the most severe current state among visible components, under the order in COMP-001.* It is shown as one labeled state at the top of the page. With every visible component Operational and no unresolved incident, that label reads as operational.

clauses.title: Snapshot read path
clauses.text: Every change to the content in PAGE-001 writes a complete rendered snapshot of the public page, the Atom feed, and the widget payload to object storage. Serving those three surfaces reads the snapshot and issues no database query. A snapshot write that fails is retried until it succeeds and is reported as a failed job under BASE-OPS-004; the previous snapshot keeps serving until it does.

clauses.title: Serving through a failure
clauses.text: When the database, the queue, or object storage is unreachable, the three surfaces in PAGE-005 return 200 — from the current snapshot, or from the cached response under the `stale-if-error` directive of PAGE-007 when the origin itself cannot answer. They return 503 only when no snapshot has ever been written. A response that could not be built from current data states the instant its content was generated and is labeled as the last known state; no failed read ever produces the all-clear of PAGE-004. `/health` still reports 503 per BASE-OPS-001; the public page's availability does not depend on it.

clauses.title: Publish latency and caching
clauses.text: Stable public URLs validate the current snapshot generation on reuse with a generation ETag and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, stale-if-error=3600`. Immutable artifact bytes are cached by generation and artifact key; advancing the published generation makes previous cache entries ineligible for a healthy current response. An update, component state change, or maintenance transition is readable on the status page, history, incident and maintenance permalinks, Atom feed, widget and public JSON within 10 seconds of the request that caused it returning 200. An unreachable origin may use its retained response for the one-hour error window; the application also retains labeled last-known snapshots under PAGE-006.

clauses.title: Public read paths are not rate limited
clauses.text: The public read paths marked `read` in `seed.json → deploy.publicPaths` never return 429. Requests from one address up to the `publicPageRequestsPerSecond` limit in `seed.json → limits` all return 200. **Supersedes BASE-ACCESS-003** for those paths only. A status page is read hardest at the moment it matters most, and a per-address limit would reject real readers behind one egress address during an incident — but the decisive reason is mechanical: RFC 6585 requires that a 429 is never stored by a cache, so rate limiting the read path converts a cacheable traffic spike into an uncacheable one and sends it all to the origin. Those paths share immutable generation bytes in the edge cache. Healthy requests validate the current generation without querying the database; artifact caching reduces object-byte reads, while validation requests still reach the Worker. The public write paths (`/subscribe`, `/unsubscribe`, `/manage`, `/api/intake/*`) stay rate limited under BASE-ACCESS-003.

clauses.title: Time display
clauses.text: Every timestamp on a public surface or in a notification is rendered in the page's configured timezone with its UTC offset, and every timestamp on the page carries the same instant as an ISO 8601 value in a machine-readable attribute.

clauses.title: Atom feed
clauses.text: `/feed.atom` validates as Atom 1.0 and contains one entry for every published incident update and for every maintenance notice — scheduled, rescheduled, started, completed, canceled — from the last 12 months, ordered newest first. An entry's identifier is stable from first publication and is never reused.

clauses.title: Embeddable widget
clauses.text: One script tag renders a banner showing the overall status and any unresolved incident, read from the PAGE-005 snapshot. The script is at most 10KB gzipped, loads only from the deployment's origin, and renders only on the host origins listed in settings per BASE-PUBLIC-002.

clauses.title: Branding
clauses.text: Page name, logo, accent color, timezone, hostname, and a footer-credit toggle are set in settings without a code change. The footer credit is the plain static text `Powered by Lamp`, defaults on, and disabling it makes no network action. The logo is served from the deployment's own origin. The favicon composites a mark for the current overall status over the configured logo rather than replacing it, and the page carries Open Graph metadata whose title and image state the current overall status.

clauses.title: Enforced isolation
clauses.text: Every public page response carries a `Content-Security-Policy` whose `default-src`, `script-src`, `style-src`, `img-src`, `connect-src`, `form-action`, and `base-uri` name only the deployment's own origin, and `frame-ancestors 'none'`, together with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. The page contains no CAPTCHA and no consent banner, because it stores nothing on the visitor's device and loads nothing that would need either.

clauses.title: Live refresh
clauses.text: When script is available the page re-reads `/api/public/status` at most every 30 seconds and updates the overall status and the newest update in place. That response is a fixed set of fields whose size does not grow with the number of components. The region it updates is an ARIA live region, so a change is announced without a reload. With script disabled the page does not refresh itself and states the instant its content was generated.

clauses.title: States and their order
clauses.text: A component's public state is exactly one of Operational, Degraded performance, Partially unavailable, Major outage, or Under maintenance. Those states are ordered by severity, most severe first: Major outage, Partially unavailable, Degraded performance, Under maintenance, Operational. Every clause that says "most severe" means this order.

clauses.title: Grouping and order
clauses.text: A component belongs to at most one group. Operators set the order of groups and of components within a group, and the public page renders them in that order.

clauses.title: Append-only state history
clauses.text: Every change to a component's public state appends an entry recording the previous state, the new state, the instant of the change, and the operator or incident that caused it. An entry is never modified or removed; a correction under UPTIME-004 appends a superseding entry rather than altering the one it corrects.

clauses.title: State note
clauses.text: A component has a note of at most 250 characters, empty by default. When it is not empty it is shown beside that component's state on the public page exactly as entered.

clauses.title: Internal components
clauses.text: A component marked internal is absent from the public page, the Atom feed, the widget, and every uptime figure, and never contributes to the overall status.

clauses.title: Component state is claimed, not set
clauses.text: Three things claim a state for a component: an unresolved incident, an in-progress maintenance, and an operator's standing claim set outside either. An incident or maintenance claims a state per attached component, chosen when the component is attached. A component's public state is the most severe of the states claimed for it, and Operational when nothing claims it. Resolving an incident, completing a maintenance, attaching or detaching a component, and setting or clearing an operator claim each recompute that component's state by this rule within 10 seconds.

clauses.title: Deletion
clauses.text: Deleting a component removes it and its state history from the public page and from every uptime figure within 10 seconds. Incidents and maintenance that referenced it keep the component's name in their published updates.

clauses.title: Definition
clauses.text: For each visible component the page shows the percentage of the reporting window during which the component was not in a downtime state, computed from COMP-003 state history at one-minute resolution and rounded down to two decimal places, so a window containing any downtime never shows 100.00%. The reporting window is 90 days.

clauses.title: Downtime weights
clauses.text: *Policy: `uptime.downtime-states.v1`; default: a minute in Major outage or Partially unavailable counts as one downtime minute, a minute in Degraded performance counts as half a downtime minute, and a minute in Under maintenance counts as none.* Degraded performance is not weighted at zero: most published incidents never get worse than it, and discarding them is what makes an uptime figure disagree with the incident history printed beneath it.

clauses.title: Short history
clauses.text: A component whose earliest state history entry is later than the start of the reporting window shows uptime computed from that entry, and the page labels the figure with the number of whole days it covers.

clauses.title: Corrections
clauses.text: An operator can correct a closed interval of a component's state history, stating the correct state for that interval and a reason. The correction appends to the history per COMP-003, recomputes every uptime figure it affects within 60 seconds, and records the operator, the interval, and the reason in the audit log. A request without a reason is rejected with 400.

clauses.title: Stated method
clauses.text: Beside the uptime figures the page names each state's weight under UPTIME-002 and the length of the window under UPTIME-001, in text present in the initial HTML. Because UPDATE-001 refuses to publish an update that claims no component, every published incident moves these figures; none of the incident history printed on the same page is invisible to them.

clauses.title: Daily record
clauses.text: The page shows one mark per day of the reporting window for each visible component. A day containing any downtime minute is labeled with the number of downtime minutes in that day. A day before the component's earliest state history entry is rendered as having no data and is visually distinct from a day with no downtime.

clauses.title: Lifecycle
clauses.text: An incident is in exactly one of Investigating, Identified, Monitoring, or Resolved. It is created in Investigating, and its state changes only through a published update that sets it.

clauses.title: Impact
clauses.text: An incident's impact is the most severe state it has claimed on any attached component at any time since it was opened, so a resolved incident keeps the impact it reached. An incident with no attached components has no impact and cannot be published; UPDATE-001 requires at least one.

clauses.title: Reference
clauses.text: Every incident has a reference of the form `INC-` followed by digits and a permanent public URL containing it. New manual and alert-intake incidents share one durable, increasing `INC-n` allocation sequence. Existing references and URLs never change. A reference is never reused, including after INCIDENT-007, a restart, or a failed creation; a failed creation may leave a gap. Legacy timestamp-sized references do not determine the starting sequence.

clauses.title: Published updates are immutable
clauses.text: A published update is never edited or deleted. A correction is a new published update that names the update it corrects, and both stay on the public timeline in the order they were published.

clauses.title: Reopening
clauses.text: An incident resolved in error is reopened by publishing an update that sets it to Investigating. The resolution update and the reopening update both stay on the public timeline.

clauses.title: Overdue update
clauses.text: When the next-update time committed by an incident's latest published update passes with no newer update published, the incident is marked overdue in the operator app. The public page shows the committed time and never labels the incident overdue.

clauses.title: Deletion
clauses.text: Deleting an incident requires a reason and removes it from the public page, the history page, and the Atom feed within 10 seconds. A request without a reason is rejected with 400. The operator, the reason, and the time are recorded in the audit log.

clauses.title: Retroactive incidents
clauses.text: An operator can open an incident whose updates carry publication times in the past. Those times are what the public timeline and the history page show, the component states it claims are written into the state history at those times so UPTIME-001 counts them, and no subscriber is notified for any of its updates.

clauses.title: Internal notes
clauses.text: An incident carries internal notes visible only to a signed-in operator. A note never appears on the public page, in the Atom feed, in the widget, in any notification, or in any AI request.

clauses.title: Update due
clauses.text: *Policy: `incident.update-due.v1`; default: an update is due from 10 minutes before the committed next-update time.* From that lead until a newer update is published or the incident resolves, the operator app shows the incident as due at the committed time on Overview and on the incident list, with one action that opens its composer and brief, and the operator email of NOTIFY-006 is sent once for that committed time; after the time passes the incident is overdue under INCIDENT-006 and the overdue email is sent once. The scheduled trigger sends both, whether or not any operator page is open. A resolved incident, an incident with a newer update, and a retroactive update send neither, and a commitment that had already passed when this clause took effect sends no email. The public page shows only the committed time and never labels an incident due or overdue.

clauses.title: Template
clauses.text: Publishing an update requires at least one attached component, an affected-audience statement of at most 250 characters, a customer-impact statement of at most 250 characters, and, for a lifecycle other than Resolved, a next-update time. A resolved update requires no next-update time and carries no next-update promise on any surface, including when an older stored resolved update retains a time. A what-still-works statement of at most 250 characters and a details statement of at most 500 characters are optional. Every field is plain text; no HTML or markdown is interpreted. A publish request that omits a required field, exceeds a length, or attaches no component returns 400 and changes nothing. The next-update time is a commitment to publish again by then; it is never presented as an estimate of when the incident will be resolved.

clauses.title: One rendering
clauses.text: The public page, the Atom feed, the widget payload, and the notification email render an update from the same renderer. No surface omits a populated field of the update or shows a field the update does not carry.

clauses.title: Sets the lifecycle
clauses.text: Every published update sets the incident's lifecycle state. An update that sets Resolved records the incident's end time and recomputes every attached component under COMP-006.

clauses.title: Preview
clauses.text: Before publishing, the composer shows the update as the public page and as the notification email will render it, produced by the renderer named in UPDATE-002.

clauses.title: Drafts
clauses.text: An unpublished update appears on no public surface. A draft is saved within 2 seconds of the last edit and is restored unchanged after a browser reload. Publication consumes that draft and opens an empty draft for the next update, with lifecycle prompts. A stale tab cannot resurrect published wording or overwrite a newer acknowledged draft. Draft writes, template application, scheduling and publication require the acknowledged draft version. A fresh empty composer is not reported saved until a native write is acknowledged; Publish requires a complete acknowledged draft. Reconciliation after a lost acknowledgment identifies the attempted write and preserves later workflow changes.

clauses.title: Scheduled publish
clauses.text: An update given a future publish time publishes within 240 seconds of that time and appears on no public surface and in no notification before it. If UPDATE-007 review is in force and the update has not been reviewed when that time arrives, it is not published, stays a draft, and is reported under NOTIFY-006. The 240-second bound is a declared promise based on one local stress observation with 20 updates and 20 maintenance starts due in the same cron minute on a single workerd process on a shared runner; it is not a p95 over independent runs or a hosted Cron guarantee.

clauses.title: Review
clauses.text: *Policy: `update.review.v1`; default: no review is required. When review is required, a publish request for an update its author wrote is rejected with 409 until an operator other than the author marks it reviewed; the reviewer and the time are recorded on the update.*

clauses.title: Publish is atomic
clauses.text: One transaction commits the update together with the recipient set it will notify on each channel selected under NOTIFY-007. That set is fixed at publish time: a subscriber who narrows their selection afterwards still receives this update, and one who unsubscribes afterwards does not, per SUB-008. When the publish request returns 200 that transaction is committed, and PAGE-007 and NOTIFY-002 follow from it. When it returns an error the update is on no surface and no recipient is recorded for it. Dispatch of the committed set is retried until it succeeds and never blocks the publish.

clauses.title: Templates
clauses.text: An operator can save a template holding the update fields of UPDATE-001, the components it attaches with the state each claims, and the lifecycle state it sets. Applying a template fills the composer and attaches those components with those states, and publishes nothing.

clauses.title: Distinct from incidents
clauses.text: A scheduled maintenance has a start time, an end time, and attached components. It has a reference of the form `SCH-` followed by digits, and is listed separately from incidents wherever both appear. New maintenance references use a durable, increasing `SCH-n` allocation sequence independent of incidents and legacy timestamp-sized references. Existing references remain unchanged; deletion, restart and failed creation never permit reuse, and failures may leave gaps.

clauses.title: Automatic transitions
clauses.text: A scheduled maintenance moves from Scheduled to In progress within 240 seconds of its start time, and from In progress to Completed within 240 seconds of its end time, with no operator action. The 240-second bound is a declared promise based on one local stress observation with 20 updates and 20 maintenance starts due in the same cron minute on a single workerd process on a shared runner; it is not a p95 over independent runs or a hosted Cron guarantee.

clauses.title: Component states
clauses.text: A maintenance claims Under maintenance for every attached component while it is In progress, and claims nothing before it starts or after it completes. A component's public state follows from COMP-006 throughout, so a state an operator or an incident claimed before the window is still claimed after it.

clauses.title: Overrun
clauses.text: A maintenance still In progress 15 minutes after its end time is shown on the public page as running longer than planned, beside its original end time, until an operator completes it or extends the window.

clauses.title: Reminders
clauses.text: *Policy: `maintenance.reminders.v1`; default: subscribers are notified when the maintenance is scheduled, 24 hours before the start time, when it moves to In progress, and when it moves to Completed.*

clauses.title: Rescheduling and cancellation
clauses.text: Changing the window of a scheduled maintenance notifies every subscriber already notified about it. Canceling it publishes a cancellation notice to those same subscribers, removes it from the upcoming list within 10 seconds, and keeps it in the maintenance history marked canceled.

clauses.title: Subscribing
clauses.text: Submitting an email address on the public page creates a pending subscription and sends one confirmation email to that address within 60 seconds. That address receives at most one confirmation email in any 24 hours however many times it is submitted, which is what bounds a subscription-bombing attack. Unsubscribing through a link emailed to the address proves it is the subscriber's own and restores that allowance, so re-subscribing after unsubscribing sends a fresh confirmation. A pending subscription receives no other notification. The form is a standard POST that works with script disabled, is rejected with 403 when the request carries `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, and carries no CSRF token, because with no cookie and no session there is no ambient authority to forge.

clauses.title: Confirmation
clauses.text: *Policy: `subscriber.confirmation.v1`; default: a subscription becomes active only when the link in the confirmation email is followed.*

clauses.title: Pending expiry
clauses.text: A pending subscription not confirmed within 72 hours is deleted, including the address it holds. **Supersedes BASE-DATA-002** for pending subscriptions only: the address was supplied by an unverified visitor who may not own it, so it is held only as long as confirmation is possible.

clauses.title: Component selection
clauses.text: A subscriber selects which components they want updates about, on the subscribe form or later on the management page, and the subscription follows exactly the components ticked (none ticked follows all), and is notified about an incident or maintenance only when it claims a state for at least one component in that selection. A subscription whose selection has never been narrowed follows every visible component, including components added after it was created. A subscription with a narrowed selection is unchanged when a component is added. When a component is attached to an unresolved incident, every subscriber who follows that component and has received no notification for that incident receives exactly one notification carrying its most recent published update, and then receives subsequent updates normally.

clauses.title: Cookieless subscriber tokens
clauses.text: A subscriber is identified on public surfaces only by an opaque token of at least 128 bits of entropy that addresses one subscription, is carried in the URL of a link the deployment emailed to that subscriber, grants no other capability, and is revoked when the subscription is deactivated or deleted. No cookie is set on any public surface. Responses on token-addressed paths carry `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. **Supersedes BASE-PUBLIC-001** for token-addressed paths only, which transmit the token on load rather than after a first interaction, because SUB-006 requires an unsubscribe that completes without any interaction on our page.

clauses.title: One-click unsubscribe
clauses.text: Every notification email carries a `List-Unsubscribe` header with a `mailto:` and an `https:` value, a `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` header, and a visible unsubscribe link in the body. A POST to the `https:` value, with a body of `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` in either multipart/form-data or application/x-www-form-urlencoded, deactivates that subscription and returns 200 with no redirect, no cookie, and no further interaction. Both headers are named in the message's DKIM `h=` tag, without which receivers decline to offer one-click at all. That endpoint's BASE-ACCESS-003 rate limit is counted per subscription token, never per source address, so one mailbox provider's shared egress cannot exhaust the limit for other subscribers.

clauses.title: Managing a subscription
clauses.text: The token URL in every notification opens a page that shows the subscription's channel and component selection and lets the subscriber change the selection or unsubscribe, without a session.

clauses.title: Unsubscribe integrity
clauses.text: After a subscription is deactivated, no notification is delivered to it. A notification committed before the deactivation and dispatched after it sends nothing and records the outcome as suppressed.

clauses.title: Webhook subscribers
clauses.text: An endpoint URL and a contact email address together subscribe as a webhook subscriber; the address exists so SUB-010 can say why the endpoint was deactivated. Each notification is a POST carrying `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` headers, where the signature is a space-separated list of versioned HMAC-SHA256 values over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`, so a secret can be rotated without a gap. The body carries the incident, every update it has published, and each attached component's previous and new state, so a receiver that missed a delivery needs no prior state. It carries no subscriber address. A delivery succeeds only on a 2xx within 30 seconds; a redirect is a failure. An endpoint that is a Slack incoming-webhook URL (host `hooks.slack.com`) receives the same events, signed the same way, as Slack's message form: its text carries each bare `https://` URL from an update field as `<url>`, never `<url|text>`, and its rich-text link elements show the URL itself, so every field reassembles unchanged (UPDATE-013). Every other endpoint receives Lamp's format, whose update fields are the published text byte for byte.

clauses.title: Failing destinations
clauses.text: An address that hard-bounces once, or whose provider reports a spam complaint, is deactivated with that reason recorded. An address that soft-bounces on 5 consecutive notifications, and a webhook endpoint whose last 10 consecutive deliveries all failed under SUB-009, are deactivated with that reason recorded. Deactivating a webhook endpoint emails its contact address. A deactivated destination receives no further notification.

clauses.title: Operator view
clauses.text: Operators see every subscriber with channel, state of pending, active, or deactivated, component selection, and the reason and time of any deactivation. Deleting a subscriber deletes the address or endpoint it holds.

clauses.title: No enumeration
clauses.text: Submitting an address that already has a subscription returns the same status and body as submitting a new address and creates no second subscription. That address receives one email saying it is already subscribed, carrying its management link and nothing else.

clauses.title: What notifies subscribers
clauses.text: *Policy: `notification.events.v1`; default: an incident notifies on its first published update, on every subsequent published update, and on the update that resolves it; a scheduled maintenance notifies per MAINT-005; a component state change made outside an incident or maintenance notifies no one.*

clauses.title: Delivery time
clauses.text: At the subscriber limit in `seed.json → limits`, every eligible email notification for a published update is accepted by the mail provider within 5 minutes of the publish request returning 200.

clauses.title: Retry
clauses.text: A notification that fails with a retryable error is retried 5 times with exponential backoff over 1 hour. After the last attempt it is recorded as failed against that subscriber and that update.

clauses.title: Delivery log, without tracking
clauses.text: Every notification records the subscriber, channel, update, queue time, outcome, and outcome time. An outcome is one of queued, delivered, bounced, complained, suppressed, or failed. No notification carries a tracking pixel or a link that records who followed it, so no outcome describes reading. The log is filterable by channel, outcome, and update, and exports as CSV.

clauses.title: At most once
clauses.text: A subscriber receives at most one notification per published update per channel, whatever the number of times the publish is retried or the queue delivers the job.

clauses.title: Operator alerts
clauses.text: An operator email is sent, at most once per event, when an incident's next update becomes due under INCIDENT-010, when an incident becomes overdue under INCIDENT-006, when a maintenance overruns under MAINT-004, when a scheduled update is held back for review under UPDATE-006, when an alert creates a draft incident under INTAKE-002, and when a notification is recorded as failed under NOTIFY-003.

clauses.title: Channels are per update
clauses.text: The operator selects, for each update, which subscriber channels receive it, and selecting none is allowed. The public page, the Atom feed, and the widget always receive the update and cannot be deselected. The delivery log records the selection.

clauses.title: Who the deployment emails
clauses.text: The deployment sends email only to an operator, to an address with a pending subscription for its single confirmation email, and to an address with an active subscription. Every notification is sent through `mail.sender.v1` from the address configured in settings.

clauses.title: Mail headers
clauses.text: Every notification email carries `List-Id`, `List-Archive`, and `List-Help` identifying the page, `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated` so it triggers no vacation reply, and, for every update after an incident's first, `In-Reply-To` and `References` naming the message that carried the first, so a mail client groups an incident's updates into one thread. `pnpm setup` and `rer deploy` fail naming the record when the From address's domain has no reachable DKIM public key for the configured selector or no DMARC policy. Aligned DKIM is sufficient; SPF at the From domain itself is not required, because a provider may authenticate its separate return-path domain.

clauses.title: Delivery never blocks publication
clauses.text: A publish under UPDATE-008 returns 200 while the mail provider, the queue, or a subscriber endpoint is failing. The public page, the feed, and the widget update under PAGE-007 regardless, and the committed notification set is delivered under NOTIFY-003 when the channel recovers.

clauses.title: Slack and Teams channels
clauses.text: An operator adds a Slack incoming-webhook URL or a Microsoft Teams channel webhook URL, with the components the channel follows (none selected follows every visible component). The URL is stored only encrypted, is never returned by any API or shown again after saving, and never appears in a log. Only the provider's own webhook hosts are accepted.

clauses.title: Channel posts
clauses.text: Publishing an incident update with Slack and Teams selected for it (NOTIFY-007) commits, in the same transaction, one post to each channel that follows a visible component the update affects. Each post is delivered at most once, whatever the number of times the publish is retried or the delivery is re-run; a retroactive update posts nowhere.

clauses.title: Authenticated requests
clauses.text: Each source is configured with one of two credentials. With a signing secret, a request is accepted only when the HMAC-SHA256 over its timestamp header and raw body matches and the timestamp is within 5 minutes of the deployment's clock; the signature is verified over the received bytes before they are parsed. With a bearer token, a request is accepted only when it presents that token, which exists because most monitoring tools — among them Datadog, Pingdom, and Uptime Kuma — cannot sign a webhook at all. A request with an absent, malformed, stale, or non-matching credential returns 401 and creates nothing.

clauses.title: Alerts never publish
clauses.text: *Policy: `alert.intake.v1`; default: an accepted alert creates or updates a draft incident within 30 seconds and changes no public surface. An operator publishes it under UPDATE-008.* A buyer who wants a monitored component to change state without waiting for a person replaces this policy; the narrative still waits for an operator, because no alert payload contains the UPDATE-001 fields.

clauses.title: Deduplication
clauses.text: Alerts carrying the same deduplication key produce one incident for as long as that incident is unresolved: an alert whose key matches an unresolved incident is recorded against that incident and creates no second one. A redelivery of a request already accepted creates no additional incident, draft, or alert record and returns the same status as the first delivery.

clauses.title: Recovery alerts
clauses.text: An alert marked as recovered for a deduplication key records the recovery time on the matching alert record and changes no public surface and no incident lifecycle state.

clauses.title: Payload mapping
clauses.text: Each source configures, as JSON paths into its own payload, which field supplies the deduplication key, which supplies the title, and which distinguishes a firing alert from a recovered one. A request whose payload lacks the configured deduplication-key path returns 400 and is recorded against that source where an operator can see it.

clauses.title: Monitor presets
clauses.text: A source can be a preset for Datadog, UptimeRobot, Better Stack or Pingdom, mapped to one component. Its endpoint accepts only that tool's documented alert payload (Datadog's webhook variables in the template Lamp shows, UptimeRobot's JSON webhook variables, Better Stack's incident webhook, Pingdom's state change webhook), authenticated by the source's token presented as a bearer header or as the endpoint's last path segment for tools that cannot send a header; the token is shown once, when Lamp generates it. A missing or wrong token returns 401 and records nothing; any other payload returns 400 and is recorded against the source. A firing alert creates or updates a draft incident attached to the mapped component, never a published one.

clauses.title: Preset recovery
clauses.text: A recovery from a preset closes the matching draft incident as Resolved when it was never published, leaving no public trace; an incident with a published update keeps its lifecycle and the recovery is recorded under INTAKE-004.

clauses.title: Suggested update
clauses.text: When an AI provider is configured, an operator can request a suggested update for an incident. The suggestion fills the composer's text fields it has text for, leaving any field it returns empty as the operator wrote it, is editable in every field, and is not published. Each filled field names the references of the DRAFT-004 brief it rests on; only references to what the brief knows are kept (an open question is not a source), and the composer shows each field's sources beside it, openable in the brief, or marks a field with none as written by the assistant with no source. A suggestion proposes no lifecycle and no next-update time, which remain the operator's commitment under UPDATE-001, and it changes no incident, public page, feed, or widget.

clauses.title: Inputs
clauses.text: A suggestion is built from the incident's accepted alerts, its published updates, its attached components customers can see and their claimed states, and the tone instructions configured in settings. Internal notes under INCIDENT-008 and internal components under COMP-001 are not sent. The provider receives exactly the brief of DRAFT-004, unchanged.

clauses.title: Incident brief
clauses.text: The operator's incident page, including the draft an alert creates, shows a brief built with no model. What we know lists each accepted alert with its time and source name, each published update, and each attached component customers can see with its claimed state. What we do not know yet lists plain questions computed from the incident's saved state: no component attached; no affected-audience or customer-impact statement yet; an unresolved draft with no next-update time; a draft raised by an alert and never published; a monitor recovery recorded while the latest published lifecycle is not Resolved; and a committed next-update time that has passed with no newer update. Every item carries a stable reference. One function builds the brief from the inputs of DRAFT-002 alone, and the page shows, collapsed, exactly what a suggestion request would send.

clauses.title: Absent or failing provider
clauses.text: AI calls go through `ai.provider.v1`. With no provider configured the composer shows no suggestion control and the deployment makes no AI request. When a configured provider fails or does not answer within 20 seconds, the composer shows the error and every other publish path behaves unchanged.

clauses.title: Equal operators
clauses.text: Every operator can create, edit, publish, and resolve every incident and maintenance, change every component, and manage subscribers. There are no roles. The only gate on publishing is UPDATE-007.

clauses.title: Management
clauses.text: Operators are invited and removed in settings. The operator configured at setup can be removed only by themselves.

clauses.title: Attribution
clauses.text: Every published update, component state change, maintenance change, history correction, and subscriber deletion records the operator who made it. That operator's name is shown in the operator app and on no public surface.

clauses.title: Public history
clauses.text: The history page lists resolved incidents and completed maintenance grouped by month for the last 12 months, each with start time, end time, duration, the components it affected, and every update it published.

clauses.title: Post-incident report
clauses.text: An operator can attach one post-incident report to a resolved incident, holding a summary, a timeline, a cause, and remediation. It appears on that incident's public page within 10 seconds of publishing, and notifies subscribers on the channels the operator selects for it in the same way NOTIFY-007 selects them for an update.

clauses.title: Report due
clauses.text: *Policy: `postmortem.due.v1`; default: an incident that claimed Partially unavailable or Major outage on any component and has no post-incident report 7 days after resolution is marked as owing one in the operator app.*

clauses.title: Export contents
clauses.text: The export contains every incident, update, component with its full state history, maintenance, subscriber with channel and state, notification delivery record, post-incident report, setting, and audit entry as JSON, and every uploaded image as its original file.

clauses.title: Setup readiness
clauses.text: Setup asks the owner nothing that Lamp can do itself (owner decision, 20 October 2026). Every change republishes the public page, and Lamp checks its own public page and subscribe form after each publish and on the minute Cron, reading the real rendered form, and checks a hosted sender with the mail provider when it changes and daily. Overview shows one line: the page is live at its address, when it was published and when the page and form were checked, with Review page (Your page, `/app/page`: Lamp's preview of the page, what it checked and ways to try it) and Change address (Settings). A failing check turns that line amber with a short reason and the one thing to do. Results belong to the address they were read from. The deployment address is the public address by default; a custom domain is optional. Local development suppresses outgoing mail, offers no captured-mail inbox, and prepares automatic one-click owner entry without email (owner decision, 15 October 2026). To prove a subscriber notice was produced locally, publish to an active subscriber, let dispatch run, and inspect its `suppressed` outcome in Notifications or `GET /api/app/deliveries`; `notification_deliveries` records that outcome without a provider-acceptance claim. Locally the sender is reported as email being off, never as verified; the hosted check reads provider authentication and does not claim inbox delivery. Public GET paths remain database-free.

clauses.title: First-run setup
clauses.text: A signed-in owner whose installation has no stored first-run completion is sent from every operator document to `/setup`, which asks for their website first (owner decision, 20 October 2026). Lamp reads that public site once, refusing private and loopback addresses on every hop and running none of its scripts, and fills in what the site gives: page name, tagline, mark (stored as a PNG), accent colour and components from its navigation, plus the time zone from the browser; it never invents what the site did not give. A site that cannot be read, or no website, leaves plain defaults with one calm line. Every fact stays editable before and after; confirming stores the settings, the mark and the components and stores completion durably; afterwards `/setup` opens the app and settings remain editable in Settings. A signed-out visitor to `/setup` is sent to sign-in and returned there. An installation that already had an operator before this clause is recorded as complete by its migration. A setup rerun never clears completion.

clauses.title: Owner-terminal sign-in
clauses.text: An owner with installation database access through Wrangler and the installation's `SESSION_SECRET` can issue a link for an existing active, non-erased operator; the remote command reads that secret only from its environment and refuses, naming it, when it is absent. The command uses the native hashed, 20-minute, single-use magic-link flow, records “sign-in link created from the command line”, and prints its only copy of the raw link once on stdout. It creates no operator or session; sign-in consumption creates the session under BASE-ACCESS-001 and BASE-ACCESS-002. Unknown, deactivated and erased operators receive the same refusal. Optional OpenID Connect sign-in through Auth, Google, Microsoft or Okta is supported by Base, off until the owner links and enables a provider; email magic links remain available. This replaces the former SSO exclusion. SCIM and role synchronization remain out of scope.

clauses.title: Dry run first
clauses.text: An owner moving from Statuspage, Better Stack, Instatus or Sorry gives Settings → Move in either an API key with its page ID (read once with GET requests to the source's fixed API origin, never stored) or the source's saved API responses. A dry run counts every component, component group, incident with its updates, scheduled maintenance and subscriber as imported, changed, skipped or refused, names each reason, and writes nothing. An import applies only the reviewed dry run: if the source or this page changed since, it is refused and a fresh dry run is required.

clauses.title: Retroactive and silent
clauses.text: An import keeps every incident update's original publication time and derives each imported component's state history from those times, as INCIDENT-009 does; it queues no notification for any incident or maintenance and publishes no maintenance notice. A window already over is imported as completed. Each imported email subscriber is pending. Preview, apply, resume, job reads and Cutover checks send no mail. Only the authenticated owner’s explicit Send invitations action claims and sends each eligible pending email subscriber at most one confirmation invitation, mentioning no past incident. For Statuspage, Better Stack and Instatus, confirmation expires 72 hours from the import review time stored as created_at, even when sending is delayed; expired subscribers cannot be invited and SUB-003 deletes unconfirmed addresses. A claim precedes the transport call to prevent duplicates across concurrent batches and retries. Proven preparation failures remain retryable because no message was submitted; interrupted or uncertain claimed sends are not automatically retried.

clauses.title: One import per source
clauses.text: Running the same source again reports it as already imported and changes nothing and sends nothing. A record already imported is never imported a second time from another source.

clauses.title: Undo
clauses.text: Undo removes every record the import created that nobody changed since, sends nothing, and keeps each record an operator or subscriber changed, together with the records it still needs, naming them.

clauses.title: Old public addresses
clauses.text: Imported incident and maintenance source paths and supplied shortlink paths permanently redirect on the public host to each surviving record's Lamp permalink; maintenance has its own permanent page. Sorry numeric notice and supplied notice paths redirect to the matching incident or maintenance; `/notices`, `/history` and `/history/YYYY/month` (English month names) redirect to Lamp’s `/history/` while a Sorry import is retained. Source Atom paths (`/history.atom` for Statuspage and Instatus; `/feed.atom` for Better Stack) serve Lamp's Atom feed after import, even without incident history, until a complete undo removes the import. These responses come from the same versioned snapshot as the page, without database queries. A second apply duplicates no aliases; conditional undo removes exactly the removed records' aliases and keeps preserved records' aliases. New imports refuse and name unsafe addresses, native-path collisions and conflicting destinations; an older retained source reports unusable aliases without withholding the public snapshot. Missing shortlinks are never invented. Source-owned shortlink hostnames remain outside Lamp's control. Better Stack REST reports supply no documented public URL; their paths are unavailable unless an unchanged saved status-page webhook supplies an exact shortlink with a matching report ID. No `/incident/<REST-id>` path is guessed. Better Stack maintenance messages are retained as historical updates, without creating native lifecycle notices or replaying notifications.

clauses.title: Cutover preview
clauses.text: Settings → Cutover is available after a dry run and for saved imports. It shows up to the first 25 old incident and maintenance addresses with proposed or surviving native permalinks, unavailable addresses and source-host limits, source feed answers, unsupported JSON/RSS/widget consumers, and eligible invitations with their original expiry deadline. Once the owner selects a public origin, each Opens check uses a credentialless browser request that follows the redirect and verifies the final native address and successful HTML response; failures remain explicit. The ordered guide covers import, preview, explicit invitations, hostname/custom-domain instructions, rechecking and keeping the source through the confirmation window. It claims neither DNS validation nor inbox delivery.

nonGoals: Uptime monitoring, probing, or synthetic checks: Lamp reports state that operators or accepted alerts produce, and running probes would make it a monitoring product with a second, contradictory source of truth behind the public page. For observability, see [Porthole](https://github.com/just-every/run-porthole).
On-call scheduling, paging, and escalation: the buyer's existing alerting tool already does this, and it is the system that feeds INTAKE-001.
More than one status page per deployment: one business gets one public record, so a second page is a second deployment.

Private or audience-scoped status pages: visitor authentication would be a whole second access surface for a product whose value is being readable by anyone, at any time, with nothing between them and it.
Roles and permissions: these are one business's equal operators, and UPDATE-007 covers the one gate buyers actually ask for.
SMS and voice notifications: per-message cost, carrier registration, and per-country consent rules that a self-hosted deployment cannot satisfy generically.
Multi-language status pages: every incident update would need a translation before publish, which is the opposite of publishing in two minutes.
A general-purpose operator API authenticated by API tokens: BASE-ACCESS-002 requires a session on every operator endpoint, and machine writes have one narrow door, INTAKE-001, with its own secret.

SCIM and role synchronization: optional OpenID Connect through Auth, Google, Microsoft or Okta replaces the former SSO exclusion under ACCESS-001; provider sign-in stays off until the owner links and enables it, and magic links remain available.

Visitor analytics and email open tracking: BASE-PUBLIC-001 keeps the page free of cookies and visitor data, and NOTIFY-004 keeps tracking pixels out of notifications, because knowing who read an outage notice is worth less than being the one page a customer can open without being counted.
Native mobile apps: the public page is the mobile experience, and it has to work with script disabled.

externals.name: owner-website-reader
externals.reason: SETUP-002, at the owner's request: read the supplied public website, its declared manifest and mark, and its linked public status page to retain migration metadata. Page IDs are read only from an identified Statuspage provider's public /api/v2/summary.json or Better Stack's public /index.json. Public DNS-over-HTTPS at cloudflare-dns.com validates every destination and redirect; private addresses are refused. No source key is used and no public history is imported.
