clauses.text: Operators can list bookings filtered by the lifecycle states of `BOOK-004`, and independently by whether the start instant is in the future or the past, by event type, by date range, and by whether any external delivery has failed. Case-insensitive substring search over invitee name and email address returns within 500ms, on a single-host install and on a workspace at the `OPER-007` capacity (300 hosts and 1,000,000 bookings) alike. Lists are sorted by start instant. Each person lists and searches only the bookings they may read under `OPER-001`: a member their own, their delegated hosts' and shared team events; a team manager their teams'; owners, admins and viewers every booking. *Acceptance:* `tests/bookings-filters.test.mjs` and `tests/bookings-search-upgrade.test.mjs`: every filter combination, Unicode search and the 500 ms bound on the 100,000-booking fixture. With multiple hosts the same workspace adds host, team and payment-state filters under `REPORT-002`. Target: on the `OPER-007` capacity fixture (300 hosts, 1,000,000 bookings spread across them), the same search, alone and combined with a host filter and a team filter, returns within 500 ms. A member's list and search on the capacity fixture return none of another host's bookings outside a shared team event.

clauses.title: Booking record
clauses.text: A booking record shows the event type, every invitee answer and custom-field value, the start and end in both the host's and the invitee's IANA zones, the location or meeting link, the history from `BOOK-010`, the separate state of the calendar event, the meeting link, and each email, and every recorded failure with its `CAL-005` or `NOTIFY-005` reason. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-axe/acceptance-records.mjs` (run by `tests/booking-axe.test.mjs`): the booking record shows answers, both zones, history and each side effect's state and failure reason.

clauses.title: Owner editor
clauses.text: When configured, the native operator app mounts the Base editor only after an active native owner session authorizes a private, non-cached grant lasting at most 30 seconds. Session or grant expiry, revocation, refused refresh and logout remove editor authority. The app permits framing only by itself and the exact trusted management origin, retaining unrelated security directives. Editor grants are for owners only under `OPER-001`: an admin, team manager, member or viewer receives no editor configuration, and their grant request returns 403 `role_forbidden` with no grant issued. Until `OPER-001` ships every operator is an owner; the `role_forbidden` refusals above, their `ADMIN-002` entries and the role-scope Target below are `OPER-001`'s obligations. Sessionless callers receive no editor configuration. *Acceptance:* `scripts/verify-managed-editor.mjs` (CI partition `editor`; its assertions and result name `EDITOR-001`): grant lifetime, revocation, framing origins and sessionless refusal. Target, carried by `OPER-001`: in the `OPER-001` role-scope journey an admin, a team manager, a member and a viewer each get 403 requesting a grant and their app documents carry no editor configuration, while the owner's grant works as today.

clauses.title: Durable first run
clauses.text: On a local development checkout, `rer setup --owner-email <owner address>` followed by `rer dev` prints `RER_SIGNED_IN` and a credential-bearing `RER_OPEN` URL; opening that URL uses Base's development sign-in to establish the owner's native session and sends a fresh owner to private `/setup`, without reading a mailbox. Hosted installers claim the owner through the configured admission flow (`AUTH-006`), then use native email-link sign-in delivered through the configured mail provider; a fresh owner also arrives at `/setup`. Until the installation records completion, every `/app` document and hydrated app navigation redirects to `/setup` before workspace content; private APIs remain session-protected and callable by the setup editors. Setup provides the same real profile, connection, event and availability editors. A same-origin authenticated finish command requires a currently valid host profile and a published event with a persisted copy report for its current canonical booking URL, revalidating EVENT-006 readiness and the profile/event/report snapshot. **Copy booking link** persists that report after its clipboard write succeeds; when clipboard access is denied it shows the booking link in a selectable read-only field, and **I have shared it** persists the same report through the same authenticated, same-origin route. Request-only events require alternative requests and a successful mail check; they require no Google Calendar or availability window. Local development and demos validate and silently suppress outgoing mail without a local inbox or outbox, and their readiness result proves only that local path. Real outgoing mail uses the configured provider: an installer supplies its credentials and verified sender, checks connection readiness, and proves delivery by receiving the native sign-in link and booking or request mail in the intended real mailbox. Missing configuration and provider failures never select local delivery. Automatic booking requires saved availability and verified mail; a calendar is optional for fixed locations, while connected calendars and Google Meet retain their provider checks. Completion records a server timestamp once. Completed `/setup` visits go to `/app`; aging connection health, later edits or deletion never reopen first run. Owner reinvitation, setup reruns and whole-install export/restore preserve the marker. The forward migration marks already-existing setup identities with their creation time solely for upgrade compatibility, without asserting historical checklist completion. Owners claimed after migration start unfinished. Reset removes local completion with local owner data; the next fresh claim must complete setup again. *Acceptance:* `tests/dev-identity.test.mjs` and `tests/local-setup-journey.test.mjs` exercise keyed owner entry; `tests/first-run.test.mjs` covers the native setup gate and durable marker, and `tests/host-setup-journey.test.mjs` exercises the setup editors, finish requirements, copy report and persisted completion marker at 1440 and 390 pixels with provider HTTP synthetic. Check that local entry removes the credential fragment, establishes the named owner session and opens `/setup` before workspace content; a completed owner opens `/app`. Exercise local mail validation and suppression with no stored message or provider request. On the hosted install, receive and consume the native sign-in link, complete setup with the configured sender, and receive one booking confirmation or alternative-request acknowledgment with both MIME parts in the real mailbox. A local suppression result cannot satisfy that live observation.

clauses.title: Host profile
clauses.text: Each host edits their name, title, biography, avatar, IANA timezone, focus areas and social-proof entries, within the counts and lengths in `seed.json → limits`. A social-proof entry is a quotation and an attribution typed by an operator: Dial collects no invitee feedback and publishes no rating, score or count it did not receive from an operator. Each host has exactly one profile timezone, which is what every other clause means by "the host's zone" for that host's bookings; a team event's host zone is the assigned host's. The in-app preview renders the same content as the public page. *Acceptance:* `tests/operator-management.test.mjs` and `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs` prove the one-host profile, limits and preview; the target journey repeats it for two hosts in different zones and checks each host's slots and mail use their own zone.

clauses.title: Public profile
clauses.text: The host profile is served at `/book/<handle>`, where the handle is set by an operator. It shows the configured host content and every published, listed event type, and never a draft, unlisted, or disabled one. An operator can change the handle; the previous handle then answers per `PUBLIC-005`. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-http.test.mjs`: the public profile lists only published listed events and an old handle answers 404.

clauses.title: Avatar asset
clauses.text: Supersedes `BASE-INPUT-003` for the `/media/` prefix only. The avatar is an upload within the size and type limits in `seed.json → limits`, stored in R2 and served under `/media/` with its declared content type and inline rather than with a download disposition, because it renders as an image on the public profile and event pages. That prefix is the public delivery channel the baseline requires a product contract to name; every other upload rule still applies, and no other upload in this product is publicly readable. *Acceptance:* `tests/avatar-upload.test.mjs` and `tests/avatar.test.mjs`: size and signature validation, inline `/media/` delivery with `nosniff`, replacement and removal.

clauses.title: Event type lifecycle
clauses.text: Operators create, edit, publish, disable, and delete event types. An event type is draft, published, or disabled, and a published one is either listed on the public profile or unlisted and reachable only by its own URL. Each carries a title, description, one to four duration options of 5 to 480 minutes each with one of them the default (`EVENT-011`), color, location, and a slug unique among event types, and is served at `/book/<handle>/<slug>`. A slug can be edited; the previous slug is not retained and then answers per `PUBLIC-005`, while existing bookings and their manage links are unaffected. An operator can duplicate an event type: the copy is a draft with every setting, question, location, schedule binding, template (`NOTIFY-009`) and workflow attachment of the original, titled "<title> (copy)" with a new unique slug, and carries no bookings, requests or history. Creating or duplicating an event type past an event-type capacity of `OPER-007` is refused under that clause and creates nothing. *Acceptance:* `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs` and `tests/event-status-trigger.test.mjs`: create, edit, publish, disable and delete with slug rules; `tests/booking-wire/duration-journey.mjs` and `tests/booking-wire/location-journey.mjs` exercise the native duration and duplication cases: saving five duration options, or none, is refused with the field named, and 30 and 60 minutes with 30 as the default are kept; duplicating a published event type with two questions, a buffer and an edited confirmation template creates a draft copy with the same settings, a new slug, no bookings and no public page until published; remaining capacity journey: a host at the per-host event-type capacity is refused a create and a duplicate with `workspace_capacity_reached` naming `event_types_per_host`, and no draft exists afterwards. *Implementation:* `tests/booking-wire/duration-journey.mjs`, `tests/booking-wire/location-journey.mjs`, `src/core/features/event-types/duplicate.ts`. *Remaining:* Native event settings, independent draft duplication including every location, question, schedule binding and correspondence template, and one to four durations. Workspace/host capacity, reusable team templates and workflow attachments await OPER-007, TEAM-006 and FLOW-001.

clauses.title: Scheduling constraints
clauses.text: Each event type configures its recurring availability, date-specific overrides, slot start increment of 5, 10, 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes, minimum notice of 0 minutes to 7 days, a booking horizon that is rolling (1 day to `seed.json → limits.availabilityLookaheadDays`, counted in calendar days or in weekdays), a fixed date range, or indefinite (up to that same lookahead limit), before and after buffers of 0 to 120 minutes each, and an optional maximum number of bookings per host day, where a host day is one calendar date in the host's timezone. A new event type starts at a 30-minute duration, a 15-minute increment, 4 hours' minimum notice, a 60-day horizon, no buffers, and no host-day limit. *Acceptance:* `scripts/verify-availability-diagnostics.mjs` and `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`: increment, notice, horizon, buffers and host-day limit each exclude the expected times; a fixed date range offers nothing outside it, a 10-weekday horizon skips weekends in its count, and an indefinite horizon offers slots up to the lookahead limit; a 45-minute increment on a 09:00–12:00 window with a 30-minute duration offers 09:00, 09:45, 10:30 and 11:15. *Implementation:* `scripts/verify-availability-diagnostics.mjs`, `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`, `migrations/core/0052_booking_horizons.sql`; browser: `evidence/contract/2026-10-17/EVENT-002/`. The Status row records the complete clause as done on the local runtime; live observations remain separately required where listed.

clauses.title: Invitee questions
clauses.text: Each event type has ordered booking questions of type text, textarea, phone number, single choice, dropdown, multiple choice, or checkbox, each required or optional, within the question and option counts in `seed.json → limits`. Choice options have stable values and editable labels, and a submitted option not configured on the event type is rejected. A phone-number answer is validated as an E.164 number (US numbers accepted in national format), stored normalized and mapped to CRM phone fields (`INTEG-002` to `INTEG-004`, `INTEG-008`); a dropdown is a single choice shown as a select for long option lists. A name and a syntactically valid email address are always required. *Policy: `booking.questions.v1`; default: name and email, plus an optional agenda of at most 500 characters, on every new event type.* *Acceptance:* `scripts/verify-question-defaults.mjs` and `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`: ordered typed questions, required answers and refusal of unconfigured options before a claim; a phone question refuses `555-12` and stores `(415) 555-0100` as `+14155550100`, and a dropdown refuses an unconfigured value. *Implementation:* `scripts/verify-question-defaults.mjs`, `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`, `migrations/core/0051_phone_dropdown_questions.sql`; browser: `evidence/contract/2026-10-17/EVENT-003/`. *Remaining:* All question kinds, stable dropdown options and E.164 phone normalization implemented; mapping to CRM phone fields awaits INTEG-002 to INTEG-004 and INTEG-008.

clauses.title: Locations
clauses.text: An event type offers one or more locations, and when it offers several the invitee chooses one before confirming: a Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Webex or GoTo Meeting conference provisioned per booking under the host's own account (`CAL-003`, `MEET-001` to `MEET-003`); a fixed link the operator supplies; a host phone number the invitee calls; the invitee's phone number, which the host calls; an in-person address; a place the invitee supplies ("Ask invitee"), where the booking page asks the invitee for the meeting address, phone number or link as a required field with the operator's prompt, available on one-on-one, round-robin and collective events alike; or a custom instruction. The public event page shows only each location's label; the link, number or street address appears only after confirmation, in the receipt, the invitee's email and the calendar event. An invitee phone number is collected only for a location, an SMS reminder (`FLOW-002`) or a phone-number question (`EVENT-003`) that needs it, is validated as an E.164 US or international number, and is erased under `DATA-002`. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-wire/location-journey.mjs` proves multiple locations, required Ask invitee and E.164 invitee phone on native one-on-one events, with only the chosen private value disclosed after confirmation. The remaining provider and team journey publishes an event offering Zoom, a phone call and an address, books each choice, and checks that only the chosen location is provisioned and disclosed after confirmation; an "Ask invitee" location on a round-robin event refuses a booking with the field empty, and the invitee's address appears in the assigned host's confirmation, the calendar event and the booking record and in no other host's mail. *Implementation:* `tests/booking-wire/location-journey.mjs`, `src/core/features/event-types/locations.ts`, `src/core/features/public-booking/ui/booking-location.tsx`. *Remaining:* Native one-on-one multiple locations, required Ask invitee and E.164 invitee phone; public labels only, chosen private value in receipt/mail/calendar/operator record, duplication and archive validation. Zoom/Teams/Webex/GoTo provisioning and round-robin/collective host isolation await MEET-001 to MEET-003, TEAM-003/005 and NOTIFY-008.

clauses.title: Removing an event type
clauses.text: Supersedes `BASE-DATA-003` for event types only: disabling or deleting an event type removes its public page and all its future availability but does not cascade to its bookings, which keep their times, manage links, calendar events, history, and their own copy of the event title, duration, and location. Invitee data is erased under `DATA-002`, not by deleting an event type. *Acceptance:* `tests/event-status-trigger.test.mjs`: disabling or deleting an event type removes its page and future slots while bookings keep their copies.

clauses.title: Publication readiness
clauses.text: An event type can be published only when it has at least one open availability window and when its transactional-mail configuration, any connected destination calendar, and, where its location is provider-generated, its conferencing capability each passed a connection check within the last 24 hours or since they last changed. No connected calendar is required for a fixed link, phone number or in-person address: these events use saved availability minus persisted Dial bookings. Publishing explicitly turns on real bookings, with a notice that no external calendar conflicts are checked when disconnected. Google Meet always requires a healthy conference-capable destination calendar. An unhealthy or incomplete connection is never treated as absence. A connection check is a live read of the connected destination calendar, a credential probe against the mail provider, and, where conferencing is used, a capability check against the conferencing provider; an operator can run it on demand. The operator sees each unmet requirement named. A requirement that becomes unhealthy after publication does not unpublish the event type: the connection state changes under `CAL-006` and public booking behaves under `AVAIL-004`. As an explicit exception, an operator may open a draft or disabled event in request-only mode with a saved valid host profile/timezone, alternative requests enabled and a successful transactional-mail connection check. Request-only publication requires no open availability window, destination calendar or conferencing connection, offers no availability or bookable slots, and rejects booking creation; proposed request windows do not reserve time. Enabling automatic booking uses the normal publication checks above and clears request-only mode only after they pass. *Acceptance:* `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`, `tests/host-setup-journey.test.mjs` and `tests/booking-axe/request-only.mjs`: each unmet requirement is named; request-only and calendar-optional publication.

clauses.title: Product landing
clauses.text: An installed deployment's root `/` is the sessionless installed Lobby. Before setup completion is recorded it says the installation is waiting for its owner and offers a **Finish setup** action to `/setup`; after completion it names the deployment, offers a **Sign in** action and credits Dial with a link to its run site. A saved host profile alone never changes that state. The Lobby reads only the setup state, sets no cookie, writes nothing to browser storage, runs no analytics and has one top-level heading. The product landing for Dial itself is the separate run site at `run-dial.com`, built from `src/site` and deployed by the Run site workflow. It presents, in order, a hero with the product's headline, a description, directly beneath it in small text the single line "100% free, open source alternative to Calendly, Acuity Scheduling and SavvyCal" (the three company names in bold, the words of a name joined by a non-breaking space, the line wrapped evenly; repeated in plain text at the start of the page's meta description, with no email- or phone-shaped text and no comparative claim), then a **Run Dial** action to `/run` and a **Read the docs** action to `/docs`; sections for invitees, for the host, the booking essentials, alternative requests and self-hosting; and a closing section repeating both actions. Its header links home, to `/docs` and to the source repository, and its footer repeats those links as plain text links beside a small wordmark and single-line description; neither links an installation route (`/signin`, `/setup`, `/app`, `/auth`, `/book`). The site reads no installation data, sets no cookie, writes nothing to browser storage, runs no analytics or tracking, and loads only same-origin resources, with its typeface self-hosted and every drawing inline and decorative. It has one top-level heading, is readable without script, renders its final state with reduced motion (its only motion is a one-shot hero sequence), and keeps a fixed light palette regardless of the browser's color scheme. An installation's own public chrome (its `/docs` pages) adds a link to `/signin`, names the deployment-configured owner only when the deployment configures one (a new install configures none), and shows the `Powered by Dial · runeditrun.com` footer credit as a static link controlled by deployment configuration, enabled by default and omitted when disabled. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-axe.test.mjs` (public-site stage) and `tests/runtime.test.mjs`: Lobby states, run-site content, no cookies, no storage and no third-party requests.

clauses.title: Public documentation
clauses.text: The public paths `/docs` and `/docs/<slug>` serve Dial's first-party documentation: the Markdown files that `docs/site.json` lists as published, in the sections and order it gives, which is the only navigation. The documentation Markdown is rendered to HTML at build time: a Vite plugin renders each page when Vite loads it, in a build and in development, and never in the Worker or the browser, so the emitted Worker and client bundles contain no Markdown or syntax-highlighting code, and each page is its own lazily loaded chunk that the Worker renders per request inside the public site's shared header and footer. A page has its title as its one top-level heading (the header's wordmark is not a heading on a documentation page), a section menu, an on-this-page list, previous and next links, tables in labeled scrollable regions and an Edit-on-GitHub link. Every Markdown file at the repository root and under `docs/` is either published or listed in the manifest as GitHub-only with a reason, and an unlisted file, a broken link or anchor, raw HTML, an image outside `docs/media/` or an absolute build-machine path fails verification or the build. The documentation is served by `GET` only, reads no booking, invitee, host-profile or operator record or session, sets no cookie, runs no analytics or tracking and loads only same-origin resources. An unknown, miscased or nested slug answers the existing `404` page, and `/docs` shares the public admission budget of the other sessionless public paths. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-axe.test.mjs` (public-site stage): built documentation pages, manifest completeness, 404s and no cookies or analytics.

clauses.title: Event presentation
clauses.text: A published event page names the host and the event and shows its description, duration, public location label, the invitee's selected timezone, a day selector with each invitee-zone date shown once, up to five suggested times first for the selected day, each chosen by the native ranking of `AVAIL-007` and showing its reason, and every valid slot in the displayed week reachable by selecting its day. Only the selected day's times are listed; the initial selection is the first day with a valid slot. Week-by-week navigation is bounded by today and the booking horizon. The page also shows the change window the `booking.reschedule.v1` and `booking.cancellation.v1` policies currently enforce, and, when the event type enables it, the alternative-request path. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-axe.test.mjs` and `tests/booking-axe/day-picker.mjs`: day-first presentation, recommendations with reasons, week navigation bounds and policy windows.

clauses.title: Invitee-first flow
clauses.text: An invitee views availability and completes a booking without an account and without signing in. Before confirmation the flow asks only for the event type's configured questions, names who receives the answers — the host and, when connected, the calendar provider — and links the privacy notice URL configured for the deployment. *Acceptance:* `tests/embed-document-authorization.test.mjs`: account-free booking, configured questions only and named recipients of answers.

clauses.title: Progress and recovery
clauses.text: The public flow has distinct choose-time, details, and confirmation states, each at its own URL, and reloading or navigating back preserves a still-valid selection. The selection and its nonce are carried in the URL and in the browser's session storage; the public flow sets no cookie. An expired nonce, or an expired or rotated manage token, returns 410; an unknown or mismatched one returns 404. Both render a page that offers a fresh start and that contains no booking, invitee, or sample data. *Acceptance:* `tests/host-setup-journey.test.mjs` and `tests/ux-simplification.test.mjs`: per-step URLs, reload and back preserve selection, 410 and 404 recovery pages, no cookie.

clauses.title: Embed
clauses.text: Operators copy an asynchronous script tag naming a public event slug and `inline` or `modal` mode. Inline mode renders where the tag sits; modal mode opens only from an element whose `data-dial-embed` attribute names that embed. The initial script is under 50KB gzipped, and the embedded flow offers the same booking, reschedule, and cancel actions as the standalone page. *Acceptance:* `tests/embed-document-authorization.test.mjs`: inline and modal embeds on an allowed parent, bundle size, and booking, reschedule and cancel inside the embed.

clauses.title: Unavailable pages
clauses.text: An unknown, draft, disabled, deleted, or renamed profile or event URL returns 404 and reveals nothing about whether a record ever existed there. This governs profile and event URLs only; manage-token responses are governed by `PUBLIC-003`, where a rotated or expired token deliberately returns 410 so the invitee knows to ask for a new link. A published event type with no valid slot inside its horizon still returns 200, says so, and offers the alternative-request path when the event type enables it. *Acceptance:* `tests/embed-document-authorization.test.mjs`: unknown, draft, disabled, deleted and renamed URLs return the same 404; a full horizon returns 200 with the request path.

clauses.title: Abuse
clauses.text: A public request refused by the rate limits of `BASE-ACCESS-003` returns 429 and the flow keeps the invitee's selection and answers so the same person can retry without re-entering them. Owners and admins can block an email address or a domain for the whole workspace, and each entry records who added it and when; team managers, members and viewers cannot add or remove an entry (403 `role_forbidden`, no change, `OPER-001`); a submission from a blocked address is refused with a message that does not say it was blocked, and creates no booking, request, notification, or calendar event. The block list shows each entry's author ("a removed operator" once that operator's identity is erased under `OPER-002`) and the time it was added, in the host's zone. Until `OPER-001` ships every operator is an owner and the owner acts for the admin role; the `role_forbidden` refusals above, their `ADMIN-002` entries and the role-scope Target below are `OPER-001`'s obligations. *Acceptance:* `tests/public-blocking.test.mjs` and `tests/public-admission.test.mjs`: 429 keeps the selection; blocked addresses and domains create nothing and are not told why; each entry records and lists the operator who added it and when. Target, carried by `OPER-001`: in the `OPER-001` role-scope journey a member's and a viewer's domain block each return 403 and that domain still books; the admin's block lists its author and time.

clauses.title: Schedule and overrides
clauses.text: Recurring availability is a set of wall-clock windows per weekday in the host's IANA timezone. A date override replaces the recurring windows for one host date and may open or close that whole date. Editing a schedule or an override changes future availability only; it never alters a confirmed booking. *Acceptance:* `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`: weekday windows and date overrides change future availability only.

clauses.title: Valid slots
clauses.text: A slot is offered only when every one of these holds: its start falls on the event type's start increment measured from the start of its open window; the full duration fits inside that one window; the start is within the booking horizon and beyond the minimum notice; its host day is under the event type's booking limit; and it overlaps no booking in the `confirmed` state for this host on any event type and no busy interval from any selected conflict calendar, an external event the provider marks free being ignored. Dial's own managed event, read back from a conflict calendar where Dial last confirmed writing it, is the booking it represents rather than an external busy interval, so a canceled or moved booking releases its old time under `BOOK-007` and `BOOK-008` without waiting for the provider or its cached busy data. Anything else is not offered. *Acceptance:* `tests/dst-native.test.mjs`, `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs` and `tests/providers-d1.test.mjs`: every validity rule, free-marked external events ignored and Dial's own managed event not double-counted.

clauses.title: Buffers
clauses.text: The event type's before and after buffers extend the interval that must be free around a candidate slot, over both confirmed Dial bookings and external busy intervals. A buffer never changes the invitee's start or end time, the duration shown anywhere, or the times on the calendar event and invitation. *Acceptance:* `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`: buffers exclude adjacent times without changing displayed or calendar times.

clauses.title: Freshness and failure
clauses.text: Availability is recomputed when the event page or a week loads. Changing the invitee's timezone re-renders and re-ranks the same slots and needs no new calendar read, because slot validity does not depend on the invitee's zone. A displayed slot may rest on cached provider busy data no more than 5 minutes old; the final check in `BOOK-001` uses provider data no more than 60 seconds old. With no connected calendar, saved schedule rules and persisted Dial bookings are authoritative and no provider read occurs. This does not relax checks on an unhealthy, incomplete or revoked connection. Every selected conflict calendar is required, and a provider read that does not complete within 5 seconds counts as unreadable. If a required calendar is unreadable at either point, Dial offers and confirms no slot for that host and tells the invitee that booking is temporarily unavailable, rather than offering unverified time. *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journey 6) and `tests/host-setup-journey.test.mjs`: unreadable calendars fail closed and recover; calendar-optional events read no provider.

clauses.title: Timezones
clauses.text: Every invitee-facing time is rendered in the invitee's selected timezone, which starts as the browser's IANA zone when the browser reports one and as the host's zone when it does not. The zone is resolved in the browser and slot instants are fetched in UTC, so no visitor-derived value reaches the server on page load, as `BASE-PUBLIC-001` requires: the invitee's zone is sent only with a request their own action causes — changing the zone, moving week, or selecting a slot. The invitee can change the zone at any point before confirmation. The selected-day group names the invitee's zone once, and every selectable time carries its UTC offset so repeated wall-clock times remain distinct. Other invitee-facing times carry their zone name and UTC offset. In the selected-day picker, host time is shown only when the host's zone differs from the invitee's, including the host date when the local dates differ. The details and confirmation surfaces also show the host's local time, including when the zones match, preserving the receipt's both-zone requirement in `BOOK-005`. A confirmed booking stores the UTC instant and both the host's and the invitee's IANA zone identifiers. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-axe.test.mjs` (timezone stage) and `tests/booking-axe/timezone.mjs`: browser-resolved zone, offsets on every time, host time where zones differ.

clauses.title: Daylight saving time
clauses.text: A local time that does not exist during a forward transition is never offered. Repeated wall-clock times during a backward transition are shown with distinct UTC offsets, so each offered time maps to exactly one instant. A DST transition between confirmation and the meeting never moves a booking's stored UTC instant, and the host and invitee renderings each follow their own zone's rules. *Acceptance:* `tests/dst-native.test.mjs`: forward-gap times never offered, repeated times carry distinct offsets, stored instants never move.

clauses.title: Recommendations and filters
clauses.text: At most 5 recommended times are shown, each a slot already valid under `AVAIL-002` and each showing the reason it was chosen. The ordering is deterministic: the same inputs always produce the same order. The browser ranks the verified offers in both the host's and invitee's selected zones from the first display. It uses a free-time ordering supplied with the offers, without sending the device zone on page load or disclosing private occupancy intervals; action-triggered server reads use the selected zone under `AVAIL-005`. An invitee-facing filter only narrows or reorders slots already valid under `AVAIL-002` and can never surface one that is not. *Policy: `availability.recommendation.v1`; default: slots fully inside 09:00–17:00 in both the host's and the invitee's selected zone first, then the larger sum of contiguous free minutes immediately before and after the slot, then the earlier UTC start.* *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-axe/day-picker.mjs`: at most five deterministic recommendations with reasons, filters never surface an invalid slot.

clauses.title: Response time
clauses.text: Loading one week of availability for one event type returns within 2 seconds, for an event type of any kind, including a round-robin event type pooling 25 hosts and a collective event type of 10 hosts, on a single-host install and on a workspace at the `OPER-007` capacity alike. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-axe/acceptance-capacity.mjs`: one week of availability for one event type within 2 seconds on the capacity fixture. Target: on the `OPER-007` capacity fixture (300 hosts with 6 personal event types each, 50 team event types, 1,000,000 bookings), one week of a one-on-one event type, a 25-host round-robin event type and a 10-host collective event type each loads within 2 seconds.

clauses.title: Operator diagnostics
clauses.text: For any time an operator evaluates, Dial names which rule excluded it — schedule, date override, start increment, minimum notice, horizon, buffer, host-day limit, an existing Dial booking, or a conflict-calendar busy interval — without disclosing external event detail that `CAL-002` does not retain. *Acceptance:* `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`: each exclusion rule is named for an evaluated time without external event detail.

clauses.title: Final validation
clauses.text: Confirming a booking revalidates every answer against the event type's current questions and rechecks the selected slot under `AVAIL-002` against persisted Dial bookings and, when connected, a fresh conflict-calendar read. Any failure creates no booking, no calendar event, and no email, and names the reason: an invalid or missing answer returns 400, and a slot that is no longer valid returns 409. *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journeys 2 and 6) and `tests/availability-diagnostics.test.mjs`: invalid answers return 400 and a no-longer-valid slot 409, with no side effects.

clauses.title: Atomic claim
clauses.text: Every slot admits at most one booking in the `confirmed` state. Claiming the slot and recording its applicable calendar, meeting, and notification commands happen in one transaction that either commits entirely or leaves nothing behind. Of any number of concurrent confirmations for the same slot exactly one commits; every other returns 409 with a `slot_taken` code and is returned to the choose-time step with availability recomputed. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-lifecycle.test.mjs`: 50 concurrent claims yield one booking and `slot_taken` for the rest.

clauses.title: Idempotent confirmation
clauses.text: Replaying a confirmation with an already-consumed nonce and an identical payload returns the stored result of the original booking and creates no second booking, calendar event, meeting link, or email. Replaying it with a different payload returns 409 and creates nothing. *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journey 5): replayed nonces return the stored receipt; a changed payload is refused.

clauses.title: States and occurrences
clauses.text: A booking is confirmed, canceled, or rescheduled, and has one or more occurrences of which exactly one is current: a reschedule closes the current occurrence and opens a new one under the same booking ID and iCalendar UID. The calendar event, the meeting link, and each email carry their own pending, succeeded, or failed state; none of them changes the booking's state, and no external failure silently cancels or moves a booking. *Acceptance:* `tests/occurrence-mail-duration.test.mjs` and `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`: occurrences and independent side-effect states.

clauses.title: Confirmation receipt
clauses.text: Unless the event type or routing route redirects the invitee under `BOOK-013`, within 2 seconds of a successful claim the invitee is shown the event, the start and end in their own zone and in the host's, the duration, the host, the location or its pending state, the calendar file of `CAL-009`, and the manage link of `BOOK-006`. The join control is enabled only when a provisioned joining URL is stored on the booking; while `CAL-003` is still pending it is disabled and labeled as pending. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs` and `tests/booking-axe/booking.mjs`: receipt contents and the pending join control.

clauses.title: Manage link
clauses.text: Every confirmed booking has a manage link whose token carries at least 256 bits from a cryptographically secure random source and grants view and change access to that one booking, without creating an invitee account. The token is transmitted only to the invitee, in their own email and on their confirmation page; operator surfaces show the booking but never the token, offering an action that copies or resends the link instead. A reschedule keeps the token, which always resolves to the booking's current occurrence. The token expires 90 days after the booking's start instant, and an operator can rotate it, which invalidates the previous token immediately. A request with an expired, rotated, or unknown token answers per `PUBLIC-003` and discloses no booking data. *Acceptance:* `tests/embed-document-authorization.test.mjs` and `tests/booking-http.test.mjs`: token entropy, operator surfaces without the token, rotation and expiry.

clauses.title: Invitee rescheduling
clauses.text: The holder of a booking's manage link can move it to another slot on the same event type. The new slot is validated under `BOOK-001` with only this booking's own occurrence excluded from internal conflicts, then claimed under `BOOK-002` before the old slot is released; if any step fails, the original booking is unchanged and still confirmed. *Policy: `booking.reschedule.v1`; default: any number of reschedules, allowed until the booking's start.* *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journey 3) and `tests/booking-axe.test.mjs`: reschedule over its own time, reminders replaced, `.ics` SEQUENCE raised, one event moved.

clauses.title: Invitee cancellation
clauses.text: The holder of a booking's manage link can cancel it with an optional reason. Cancellation cannot be reversed, releases the slot and its buffers within 5 seconds and before the next availability computation, and repeating it returns the same result without sending a second notification. *Policy: `booking.cancellation.v1`; default: allowed until the booking's start.* *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journey 4) and `tests/booking-axe.test.mjs`: the slot is offered again at once and a repeat cancel sends nothing.

clauses.title: Operator changes
clauses.text: A person who may act on the booking under `OPER-001` (its host, a person the host delegated to under `TEAM-007`, a manager of a team the booking's event type or host belongs to, and owners and admins for every booking) can reschedule or cancel any confirmed booking under `BOOK-002`, `BOOK-007`, `BOOK-008`, `BOOK-010`, `CAL-003`, and `NOTIFY-004`. The reschedule and cancellation policies constrain invitees only: an operator may also act on a booking that has already started, and may reschedule onto a time outside published availability after confirming that override explicitly, but never onto a time that overlaps another confirmed booking. An imported booking that a catch-up lists as canceled at the source may instead be released under `DATA-003`. Instead of choosing the new time, the operator can ask the invitee to pick one under `BOOK-014`. A reschedule keeps the booking's host; handing a booking to another host is a reassignment under `TEAM-007`. A member acting on another host's booking without that delegation, and any viewer, gets 403 `role_forbidden` with the booking, calendar event and mail unchanged. Until `OPER-001` ships every operator is an owner and the owner acts for the admin role; the `role_forbidden` refusals above, their `ADMIN-002` entries and the role-scope Target below are `OPER-001`'s obligations. *Acceptance:* `tests/operator-change.test.mjs` and `tests/move-in-booking-actions.test.mjs`: operator reschedule and cancel, explicit availability override, never over another booking. Target, carried by `OPER-001`: in the `OPER-001` role-scope journey a member's and a viewer's reschedule and cancel of another host's booking each return 403 with nothing changed or sent, while the host, the manager of the booking's team and the admin each succeed.

clauses.title: History
clauses.text: Rescheduling records the original occurrence as rescheduled and links it to its replacement. Every creation, cancellation, and reschedule records who acted — the manage-link holder, the named operator, or the calendar provider under `CAL-008` — the time, the previous and new start, and any reason given. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`: actor, time, previous and new start and reason for each change, including the provider actor.

clauses.title: Attendance
clauses.text: After a booking has ended, a person who may act on it under `OPER-001` (its host, a delegate under `TEAM-007`, a manager of its team, or an owner or admin) can mark it attended or a no-show and add a note. The mark records the operator and the time, appears in the booking record and the export, changes no lifecycle state and no calendar event, and sends the invitee nothing. Another member and any viewer get 403 `role_forbidden` with no mark recorded. Until `OPER-001` ships every operator is an owner and the owner acts for the admin role; the `role_forbidden` refusals above, their `ADMIN-002` entries and the role-scope Target below are `OPER-001`'s obligations. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-axe/keyboard-bookings.mjs` (run by `tests/booking-axe.test.mjs`, `[BOOK-011]`): an ended booking marked attended with a note records its operator and time in the booking record, keeps its state and queues no mail or calendar command; `tests/move-in-runtime.test.mjs` marks attended and no-show; the `DATA-001` archive round trips carry the mark (`tests/archive/fixture.mjs`); `tests/person-erasure.test.mjs` erases it with the booking. Target, carried by `OPER-001`: in the `OPER-001` role-scope journey a member's and a viewer's mark on another host's booking return 403 with no mark recorded.

clauses.title: Operator-created booking
clauses.text: A person can create a booking for a host they may act for under `OPER-001` (a member for themselves and for hosts who delegated to them under `TEAM-007`, a team manager for their teams' members and event types, owners and admins for any host), for an invitee whose name and email address they enter, on any slot valid under `AVAIL-002`, optionally overriding the minimum notice and the horizon but never the conflict and buffer checks. The invitee then receives the ordinary `NOTIFY-001` confirmation and manage link, and `BOOK-010` records the operator as the actor. A member creating a booking for another host, and any viewer, gets 403 `role_forbidden` and no booking, mail or calendar event is created. Until `OPER-001` ships every operator is an owner and the owner acts for the admin role; the `role_forbidden` refusals above, their `ADMIN-002` entries and the role-scope Target below are `OPER-001`'s obligations. *Acceptance:* `tests/operator-creation-recovery.test.mjs` and `tests/operator-temporal.test.mjs`: operator-created bookings with notice and horizon overrides, ordinary confirmation and operator actor. Target, carried by `OPER-001`: in the `OPER-001` role-scope journey a member's and a viewer's booking for another host each return 403 with nothing created or sent, while the admin's and the team manager's bookings for a member of T confirm.

clauses.title: Calendar connections
clauses.text: Each host connects one or more calendar accounts through OAuth under `AUTH-004`: Google Calendar (`CAL-001` to `CAL-009`), Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com (`CAL-010`) and iCloud or another CalDAV server (`CAL-011`), up to the account and calendar counts in `seed.json → limits`. Across all of a host's accounts they select the calendars whose busy intervals block availability (`limits.maxConflictCalendars`) and exactly one calendar to receive Dial's bookings. A connection belongs to its host; reconnecting replaces it and keeps the selections, and the host or an admin can disconnect. Calendar connection is optional for fixed locations. After an explicit disconnect, sync stops and the connection shows as disconnected. Fixed-location published event types keep offering times from saved availability minus existing bookings; provider-conference events offer no slots until their provider is restored. Existing managed bookings retain their calendar obligation and cannot be rescheduled while disconnected; their history is unchanged. Each provider is implemented behind `calendar.provider.v2`. *Acceptance:* Today `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journey 1) and `tests/providers-d1.test.mjs` prove one Google account per deployment with multiple conflict calendars and one destination. The target journey connects a Google and a Microsoft account to one host, takes conflicts from both, writes to the chosen destination, and disconnects one account with the documented effects.

clauses.title: Busy privacy
clauses.text: A calendar read retains only the identifiers, time bounds, transparency, and deletion state needed for conflict detection and sync. Titles, descriptions, attendees, and locations from conflict calendars are never stored, and so are never shown to an invitee or to an operator. *Acceptance:* `tests/providers-d1.test.mjs`: stored busy rows hold only identifiers, bounds, transparency and deletion state.

clauses.title: Managed event
clauses.text: A booking made without a connected calendar durably records calendar delivery as not required, schedules no calendar commands on creation, reschedule, cancellation or erasure, and never claims provider success. Its receipt, mail and `.ics` remain available. Connecting later does not retroactively enqueue these bookings; a later reschedule checked against that connection can create its managed event. For a claim using a connected calendar, within 60 seconds the destination calendar holds one event for the booking carrying the title and description rendered from the event type's invitation templates (`NOTIFY-009`), the booking's start and end with explicit timezone data, a stable iCalendar UID, the configured location or a Google Meet conference provisioned for this booking, and the invitee as an attendee so the provider's own invitation and updates also reach them — or the booking's calendar state is pending and `CAL-005` applies. An unsuccessful or ambiguous result is handled under `CAL-004` and `CAL-005`. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`, `tests/providers-d1.test.mjs` and `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journeys 2–3): one managed event per booking with title, zoned times, UID, attendee and Meet; calendar-optional bookings schedule nothing; saved title and description templates render on native Google events and update on reschedule. Invitation links and the wider provider/template scope remain required under `NOTIFY-009`, `CAL-010` and `CAL-011`. *Implementation:* `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`, `tests/providers-d1.test.mjs`, `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs`, `evidence/contract/2026-10-17/CAL-003/`. *Remaining:* Native Google managed events render saved title/description templates and update them on reschedule without private answers or raw manage tokens. Unconfigured offers retain pre-template wording with the default invitation manage link; direct invitation links and wider provider/template scope remain under NOTIFY-009, CAL-010 and CAL-011.

clauses.title: Idempotent side effects
clauses.text: Every calendar and meeting command carries the booking and occurrence IDs as its provider idempotency key. After a timeout, a lost response, or any other ambiguous result, the next attempt looks the object up by that key and updates it instead of creating a second one. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`: a lost Google response is reconciled by the booking key with no second event.

clauses.title: Provider failure
clauses.text: A transient calendar or meeting failure is retried up to 5 times over 1 hour. Until it succeeds the operator and the invitee receipt show the side effect as pending; after the retries are exhausted the operator sees a typed sanitised error code, safe remediation, and a retry action, while the invitee sees only that calendar setup is incomplete and that they should contact the host. The booking stays confirmed, and raw provider errors are neither persisted nor rendered. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`: a 503 exhausts five bounded retries, the booking stays confirmed and an operator retry recovers.

clauses.title: Connection health
clauses.text: Revoked credentials, a refused token refresh, an invalid sync cursor, a push channel that cannot be renewed, or exhausted provider quota puts the connection in an unhealthy state that operators see in settings by name and that raises `calendar.connection-health-changed.v1`. An invalid cursor or a lapsed channel triggers a full resync before the next availability computation. While a required conflict or destination calendar is unreadable, public booking fails closed under `AVAIL-004` and no event type can be published under `EVENT-006`. *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journeys 6, 6b) and `tests/export-restored-behavior.test.mjs`: unhealthy states named, fail-closed booking and reauthorization.

clauses.title: Provider callbacks
clauses.text: Calendar push channels are renewed before they expire. A callback authenticated under `AUTH-005` is processed independently of arrival order: duplicate or out-of-order delivery cannot duplicate a booking change or undo a newer one, and a callback describing a state older than the one held is discarded. *Acceptance:* `tests/deletion-ordering.test.mjs`, `tests/providers-d1.test.mjs` and `tests/coordination.test.mjs`: duplicate and out-of-order callbacks cannot duplicate or undo a change.

clauses.title: External deletion and edits
clauses.text: Deleting Dial's managed event in the destination calendar cancels the booking exactly once and sends the ordinary cancellation notices of `NOTIFY-004`. Any other external edit to the event's time or location is recorded as a sync conflict on the booking showing both times; the operator resolves it by restoring the managed event to the canonical time or by canceling under `BOOK-009`, and Dial never adopts such an edit by itself. *Policy: `calendar.external-deletion.v1`; default: deletion cancels the booking.* *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journey 8) and `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`: deleting the managed event cancels once; other edits become sync conflicts.

clauses.title: Calendar file
clauses.text: The confirmation and manage pages offer an `.ics` download for the booking carrying its stable UID and current occurrence. A reschedule increments that file's sequence and a cancellation marks the occurrence canceled, so an invitee's calendar updates the same entry rather than gaining an unrelated one. The download makes no request to any provider not declared in `seed.json → externals`. *Acceptance:* `tests/calendar-file.test.mjs`: stable UID, SEQUENCE increments and cancellation status in the `.ics` file.

clauses.title: Compose
clauses.text: Where an event type enables it, an invitee can select future dates and time windows within the counts in `seed.json → limits`, whose starts precede their ends and which do not overlap each other, together with their IANA timezone, a name, an email address, and an optional note of at most 500 characters, and can review the exact request before submitting. A request that omits a date, a window, a name, or a valid email address, or that contains an overlapping or reversed window, is rejected with the offending field named and stores nothing. *Acceptance:* `tests/requests.test.mjs`: overlapping, reversed and incomplete windows are refused with the field named and nothing stored.

clauses.title: Submit
clauses.text: A valid request is recorded once, acknowledged to the invitee on screen, and notified to operators within 60 seconds. The acknowledgment states the response expectation the operator configured, or, where none is configured, only that the host will follow up by email. Replaying the same nonce returns the existing request. A request reserves no time and creates no booking. *Acceptance:* `tests/requests.test.mjs`: one record per nonce, on-screen acknowledgment and operator notice.

clauses.title: Operator workflow
clauses.text: A request's host, a person the host delegated to under `TEAM-007`, managers of the host's teams, and owners and admins (`OPER-001`) can list requests by submitted, handled, or closed state, open the invitee's windows rendered in both the invitee's and the host's zone, mark one handled or closed, and create a booking for an agreed time. That booking runs the ordinary `BOOK-012` path and marks the request handled. A member's list holds only their own and delegated hosts' requests, and their open, mark or booking of another host's request returns 403 `role_forbidden` with no change; a viewer reads requests and changes none. Until `OPER-001` ships every operator is an owner and the owner acts for the admin role; the `role_forbidden` refusals above, their `ADMIN-002` entries and the role-scope Target below are `OPER-001`'s obligations. *Acceptance:* `tests/requests.test.mjs` (`[REQUEST-003]`): list by state, both-zone windows, handled and closed once each; `tests/operator-creation-recovery.test.mjs` (its assertions name `REQUEST-003`): a booking from a request runs `BOOK-012` and marks the request handled. Target, carried by `OPER-001`: in the `OPER-001` role-scope journey the member's request list omits C's request R, and the member's and the viewer's open-to-change, mark and booking of R each return 403 with R unchanged.

clauses.title: Routing
clauses.text: A new request notifies the host recipients of the event type it was made on under `NOTIFY-008` — its host, or for a team event that team's hosts — unless the routing policy selects a subset of them or suppresses email; suppressing email never suppresses the in-app record, and no request is mailed to a person who cannot read it under `OPER-001`. The policy is set per event type with its email settings: every host recipient (the default), selected people, or no email. A selection names at least one person who currently has access; the policy applies when a request is created, so a later change neither resends nor withdraws earlier notices, and a selected person who has lost access by then is skipped. Routing governs the host notices only: the invitee's acknowledgment and the request in Requests are the same under every policy. Until `OPER-001` adds hosts and teams every operator is a host recipient; `OPER-001` carries the two-host routing step through `NOTIFY-008`. *Policy: `availability-request.routing.v1`; default: the event type's host recipients, which in a single-host install is every operator.* *Acceptance:* `tests/requests.test.mjs` (`[REQUEST-004]`): default routing notifies the host recipients, every operator of a single-host install; a subset mails only the chosen operators; suppressed email mails no operator and keeps the in-app record and the invitee acknowledgment; an empty, unknown or inconsistent selection is refused with nothing saved. The two-host routing check is carried by `OPER-001` under `NOTIFY-008`.

clauses.title: Invitee updates
clauses.text: Submitting sends the invitee one acknowledgment email restating the requested windows in their own zone. Marking a request handled or closed sends the invitee exactly one further email; the closed one says the host cannot offer a time, and neither is sent twice however often the state is set again. *Acceptance:* `tests/requests.test.mjs`: one acknowledgment and exactly one handled or closed email however often the state is set.

clauses.title: Booking confirmation
clauses.text: Within 60 seconds of confirmation Dial emails, through `mail.sender.v1`, the invitee and the booking's host recipients under `NOTIFY-008`: the event, the time in each recipient's relevant zone, the duration, the answers, and, for hosts, the current calendar state. Invitee mail omits host calendar setup details while naming a pending or unavailable joining link. The invitee's copy also carries their manage link and the `.ics` file of `CAL-009`, attached for direct providers and available through the private Add to calendar download link for RER Managed mail; no host copy contains the manage token. Where the meeting link is still pending the email says so instead of inventing one. The invitee's subject and body follow the event type's confirmation template (`NOTIFY-009`), which replaces the built-in text rather than adding a second message. A host recipient can mute booking mail — confirmations, changes, and reminders — for themselves in settings. The invitee's copy is sent unless the host turns it off for an event type whose managed calendar event invites the invitee (`CAL-003`, `CAL-010`, `CAL-011`); the provider's invitation, carrying the invitation manage link of `NOTIFY-009`, is then the invitee's confirmation, and a booking whose calendar delivery is not required or fails still sends Dial's confirmation, so no invitee is left without one. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`, `tests/mail-preferences.test.mjs` and `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journey 2): one confirmation per recipient, `.ics`, manage link only for the invitee, operator mute; `tests/booking-wire/correspondence-journey.mjs` exercises an edited confirmation template as the only confirmation sent. `tests/booking-wire/correspondence-journey.mjs` names NOTIFY-001 and exercises the default-on per-event switch: successful calendar delivery suppresses Dial invitee confirmation, including mail-first queue order; a calendar-optional booking and a failed calendar write each still send one. The switch applies to unsent confirmations; frozen mail retains its existing provider identity. The provider invitation carries NOTIFY-009’s invitation manage capability by default. `tests/booking-wire/invitation-manage-journey.mjs` proves invitee-only replacement email through Base SendGrid, refusal of the earlier manage link and the audited rotation; `tests/booking-axe/invitation-manage.mjs` follows the sessionless page and replacement link at 1440/390. Recipients are proven under `NOTIFY-008`.

clauses.title: Link completion
clauses.text: When a pending joining link becomes available Dial updates the managed calendar event and sends the invitee exactly one link-ready email, however many times the completion job runs. *Acceptance:* `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs` and `tests/providers-d1.test.mjs`: exactly one link-ready email for a pending Meet.

clauses.title: Reminders
clauses.text: A confirmed future booking schedules reminders for the invitee and the booking's host recipients under `NOTIFY-008`, carrying the event, the time in the recipient's zone, the location or join link, and, for the invitee, the manage link. A reminder is sent within 5 minutes of its scheduled offset. Rescheduling replaces the scheduled times and cancellation removes them, so no reminder is ever sent for a time the booking no longer holds. *Policy: `reminder.schedule.v1`; default: 24 hours and 1 hour before the start, scheduling only the offsets still in the future at confirmation or reschedule.* *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` and `tests/coordination.test.mjs`: reminders within 5 minutes of their offset, replaced on reschedule and removed on cancel. Custom timings and channels are `FLOW-001`.

clauses.title: Changes
clauses.text: A reschedule or a cancellation sends the invitee and the booking's host recipients under `NOTIFY-008` exactly one email naming who made the change, the previous time, the new time or the cancellation reason, and, for hosts, the current calendar state. Invitees receive relevant joining-link status without host calendar setup details. The one stated exception is `DATA-003`'s release of an imported booking that the source scheduler already canceled: the source has told the invitee, so the release sends no email; the ordinary operator cancellation beside it still sends exactly one. *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journeys 3–4) and `tests/move-in-catch-up.test.mjs`: exactly one change email each, and the `DATA-003` release exception.

clauses.title: Delivery failure
clauses.text: A transient email failure is retried up to 5 times over 1 hour. A permanent failure or a bounce is marked failed on the booking or request with a typed sanitised reason and safe remediation, and can be resent without duplicating a delivery that already succeeded. Raw provider errors are neither persisted nor rendered. *Acceptance:* `tests/managed-mail.test.mjs` names NOTIFY-005 and exercises a one-day Retry-After through all five retries within one hour; `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journey 7) and `tests/booking-wire.test.mjs`: typed failure and resend without duplicating a success.

clauses.title: No mail loops
clauses.text: Product mail is sent from the configured verified sender, any address on a verified domain. Dial never reads mail delivered to that address, so a reply never creates a booking, a request, or a notification. The sender address is never an email's `Reply-To`: replies go where `NOTIFY-010` sends them, and only an event type set to No-reply sends invitee mail without a `Reply-To`, its body stating that replies are not received. *Acceptance:* `tests/deploy-adoption.test.mjs` and `tests/mail-readiness-workerd.test.mjs`: verified sender, no inbound mail processing. Target: `NOTIFY-010`'s captured-mail journey finds no `Reply-To` equal to the sender address.

clauses.title: Connection alerts
clauses.text: Within 60 seconds of the calendar connection becoming unhealthy under `CAL-006`, the connection's owning host and the workspace's owners and admins (in a single-host install, every operator) are each emailed once, naming the cause and the reconnect action, because public booking is failing closed meanwhile. This alert is operational and the mute of `NOTIFY-001` does not suppress it. No further alert is sent for that connection until it has recovered, and recovery is announced the same way. *Acceptance:* `tests/lifecycle-journey.test.mjs` (journeys 6a–6d) and `scripts/lifecycle/connection-alert-timing.mjs`: one alert within 60 seconds of onset and one recovery notice.

clauses.title: Export contents
clauses.text: Supersedes `BASE-DATA-001` for credential and live-authority exclusions and documented canonicalization. `pnpm run export -- --output FILE` writes an owner-only archive outside tracked source; `pnpm run import -- --input FILE --yes` restores it only into a fully migrated empty install. The explicit `run` selects Dial’s script rather than pnpm’s built-in dependency importer. The archive contains every durable operator, host profile, host booking-link copy report, event type, question, availability rule and override, calendar-connection metadata and sync state, booking and occurrence, invitee answer and custom-field value, attendance mark, alternative request, delivery attempt, setting, and audit entry as JSON, plus every uploaded asset with its original bytes and content type. Unknown application tables fail closed. No OAuth access/refresh credential, session, sign-in/invitation link, setup/webhook secret, callback authority, private manage capability, or frozen capability-bearing mail is exported. Durable identities, consumed first-owner ownership, invitation cancellation guards and historical outcome records survive. Imported active operators sign in through new magic links; first-owner setup cannot be claimed again. Calendar health requires reauthorization under `CAL-006`, mail requires a fresh check, old private links remain invalid, and historical deliveries, deletion probes and cleanup targets cannot recreate provider effects. Export/import/export yields an equivalent entire archive under the explicit idempotent canonicalization in OPERATIONS.md; timestamps, IDs and original asset bytes are not discarded. Retain the source SESSION_SECRET privately outside the archive when transferring authenticated retry/erasure hash guards. Restore requires exclusive access to the empty destination; D1 and R2 are not jointly atomic; Base records owned object writes and commits D1 atomically, but an unsuccessful restore remains unpublished until recovered or repeated into a fresh empty install. Local transfer and native-owner authenticated hosted export are supported. Hosted export drains and fences application requests, background work and coordinator activity while capturing D1 and FILES, refuses pending erasure, expires abandoned maintenance without allowing expired jobs to download, and retains exact schema and original-salt checks at local import. Direct owner-account writes must remain quiesced. Queue messages and coordinator alarms are excluded execution authority; historical commands remain inert. Remote restore is not exposed. Legacy v2 archives are restored with their original revision before upgrading and re-exporting. *Acceptance:* `tests/export-base-adoption.test.mjs`, `tests/export-redaction.test.mjs`, `tests/export-restored-behavior.test.mjs`, `tests/export-json-numbers.test.mjs` and `tests/local-setup-journey.test.mjs`: archive contents, exclusions, canonical re-export and hosted export.

clauses.title: Destructive personal erasure
clauses.text: Deleting every booking and alternative request carrying an email address erases that person's invitee data from the deployment, including associated answers, notes, attendance, custom values, uploaded content and object metadata, private capabilities, local mail and reminders, provider facts, blocked identifiers, rate-limit identifiers, application logs and retained import copies. Each record can still be erased from its detail page; its manage link stops working, its managed calendar event is canceled without sending the invitee a Dial email, and its audit survives with the invitee reference anonymized, as `BASE-DATA-003` requires. The email flow makes that existing deployment-wide guarantee explicit: an owner or admin enters an email in Settings and receives a case-insensitive, write-free preview of matching bookings and requests. One confirmation erases every match within the request and returns an anonymous receipt with counts, completion time and separate calendar cleanup state. Success leaves no pending personal mail, reminders or import replay. Native entity deletion and its import custody, anonymous audit and portability fence commit together; a failed multi-record request may have completed earlier entities, issues no completed aggregate receipt, closes new admission for that address and is explicitly resumable with a fresh preview. Native calendar cleanup completes within five minutes when the maintained provider adapter answers; real provider failures remain visible. Old archives are refused by a destination retaining a trusted later erasure journal, including a journal carried by a post-erasure archive. An isolated old archive in a new empty store cannot know a future erasure. When the email also belongs to an operator, the same single confirmation erases all matching invitee records, including those of the acting or protected setup owner. The write-free preview and anonymous receipt explicitly report that the associated operator identity is retained; native accounts, sessions and sign-in authority remain usable. Operator identity removal is a separate OPER-002 action with its self, setup and last-owner holds. Invitee erasure never claims that a retained operator identity has been erased. Unrelated people, host configuration and shared assets remain. Email-wide erasure and per-record erasure from a detail page are for owners and admins only (`OPER-001`): a team manager, member or viewer sees no erasure entry in Settings or on a record, and their preview, confirmation or per-record erasure returns 403 `role_forbidden` with nothing previewed or erased; on a single-host install every operator is an owner, as today. ERASURE.md records the complete storage census, restore procedure, implementation gaps and external-copy limits. *Acceptance:* `tests/person-erasure.test.mjs` and `tests/import-custody-erasure.test.mjs`: email-wide preview, one-confirmation erasure, anonymous receipt and import tombstones. Target: in the `OPER-001` role-scope journey a member's and a viewer's email-wide preview, confirmation and detail-page erasure each return 403 and every matching booking and request remains; the admin's preview and one confirmation erase every match across hosts.

clauses.title: Move-in import
clauses.text: Owners and admins preview saved scheduling responses without writes, review losses and overlaps, download a report and acknowledge its fingerprint before a bounded, resumable import. Preview fixes the snapshot time and unsent capability hashes; upload identity is bound to the operator session and expires after 30 minutes. Other roles are refused. A fresh sign-in or restored archive requires a fresh review. Imported event types stay drafts; confirmed bookings retain source answers and locations, occupy their time and create no mail, reminder, calendar or meeting effects. Booking history labels the imported effective snapshot time and authenticated importing operator; later native actions retain their actual times. Unchanged re-imports are idempotent. Undo preserves edited records and required parents; erasure removes personal copies and prevents replay. Catch-up imports only new source records under a separate reviewed job and leaves existing native records unchanged. Source differences require recorded decisions; releasing a source-cancelled booking frees its time without emailing the invitee. Differences, decisions and source links survive archive restore without replay authority. A live switch-over checklist shows publication readiness, source links, outstanding differences and capture age. Dial never contacts or changes the source account. Qualification is synthetic-only until an owner-supplied account export is checked; no real-data importer is verified. The exact publisher clause and acceptance details remain in the linked contract.

clauses.title: Operator annotations
clauses.text: Owners and admins define, rename and delete the workspace's private field definitions for event types, bookings and availability requests in Settings (deleting one deletes its values under `CUSTOM-002`). A person edits values on a record they may act on under `OPER-001`, so a member edits values on their own event types, bookings and requests. A team manager, member or viewer creating, changing or deleting a definition gets 403 `role_forbidden` with no change, and a viewer edits no value. Until `OPER-001` ships every operator is an owner and the owner acts for the admin role; the `role_forbidden` refusals above, their `ADMIN-002` entries and the role-scope Target below are `OPER-001`'s obligations. Supported types are text (500 characters), long text (5000 characters), single choice (1–50 unique choices, each at most 120 characters) and checkbox. Labels contain 1–120 characters; definitions per entity type are bounded by `limits.maxCustomFieldsPerEntity`. The private routes validate entity ownership, field/entity matching, type, choice and size before writing. Booking annotations appear alongside invitee answers under OPER-004. Definitions and values are stored in extension-owned sidecars, reached through declared, typed source registry contributions and detail slots. *Acceptance:* `tests/custom-fields.test.mjs`: definitions, typed values, ownership and limits through the private routes. Target, carried by `OPER-001`: in the `OPER-001` role-scope journey a member's and a viewer's definition create returns 403 with no definition added; the member sets a value on their own booking; the member's value write on another host's booking and every viewer value write return 403.

clauses.title: Annotation privacy and portability
clauses.text: Custom definitions and values require a current operator session. They are never added to public documents, public API projections, outgoing mail or build-time browser source. Whole-install export and restore preserve definitions and values, including false checkboxes and multiline text; restore rejects invalid field types, references and choices before committing. Deleting a definition deletes its values; erasing a booking or request deletes its annotation sidecar; event deletion removes its own annotations without removing booking annotations. An additive upgrade preserves prior product data. *Acceptance:* `tests/custom-fields.test.mjs`: values absent from public documents and mail, archive round-trip and deletion rules.

nonGoals: Multiple hosts or workspaces
Roles and permissions
Team round-robin or collective scheduling
Group events, classes, waitlists, or resource capacity
Additional invitee guests on a booking
Bookings that wait for host approval before they are confirmed
Payments, deposits, refunds, or booking fees
Recurring booking series or scheduling polls
Marketplace discovery, ratings, or invitee-submitted reviews
SMS, WhatsApp, phone automation, CRM, campaigns, or marketing automation
Automatic adoption of arbitrary external-calendar time or location edits
AI routing or ranking
Native mobile apps

externals.name: google-calendar
externals.reason: A connected calendar supplies busy-time checks and destination events. An explicitly not_connected host can still publish from saved availability with a non-Meet location; a configured but unhealthy connection remains fail-closed, and Google Meet requires a healthy conference-capable calendar. The maintained setup journey covers the calendar-optional case at 1440 and 390 pixels.
data: host OAuth identity
calendar identifiers
booking event details
invitee name and email

externals.name: google-meet
externals.reason: The prototype's default location is a real Google Meet conference, which requires provider-side conference creation. EVENT-004 also lets an event type use a fixed link, a phone number, or an in-person address instead, so a deployment can run with no event type ever using Meet.
data: booking correlation ID
event title
start and end instant

externals.name: rer-managed-mail
externals.reason: Managed hosting supplies the mail.sender.v1 relay and installation credential. Direct provider credentials are not needed on Managed. No fallback is selected if the configured provider fails.
data: operator and invitee email
booking or request content

externals.name: sendgrid
externals.reason: Direct installs select SendGrid through mail.sender.v1 for sign-in and transactional messages. Managed installs use the RER relay instead. EVENT-006 blocks publication while the selected mail connection is unhealthy.
data: operator and invitee email
booking or request content
calendar attachment

externals.name: resend
externals.reason: Existing installations may retain their Resend credentials and mail.sender.v1 configuration. New setup selects SendGrid; an explicitly configured provider failure is not replaced with another provider.
data: operator and invitee email
booking or request content
calendar attachment

externals.name: operator-thank-you-page
externals.reason: After a committed booking, an event may navigate to the operator-configured HTTPS thank-you page. Only fields explicitly selected by the operator are appended; private answers and booking capabilities are excluded. This is browser navigation, not a server request or telemetry.
data: operator-selected booking fields
operator-selected non-private answers
operator-selected UTM and source values

operatingCost.basis: One host and operator, 1,000 unchanged bookings per month, four to six transactional emails per booking including the default reminders when both offsets apply (4,000–6,000 sends/month), with Google Calendar and Cloudflare usage inside the stated allowances.
operatingCost.notes: Twilio SendGrid Essentials 50k was $19.95/month on 2026-10-14; 4,000–6,000 sends use 8–12% of its 50,000 monthly allowance. The low estimate assumes the full Cloudflare runtime fits available free allowances. The typical estimate adds $5/month for Cloudflare Workers Paid, conditional on all metered use staying within included allowances; an owner already paying for that Cloudflare account may incur no additional $5 for Dial. Google Calendar standard use and first-tier R2 usage are assumed within their published free allowances. Estimates exclude overages, domains, taxes, optional tools and paid Google Workspace.
