clauses.text: An import stages records and files outside the live namespace, validates the whole archive, and publishes it in one step. A failed import leaves the deployment empty and can be retried.

clauses.title: Exporting a page or a container
clauses.text: A member can export one page, a page with its descendants, or a whole container as Markdown, HTML or PDF, with records as CSV, in one archive with its media. The export is readable without Slate, and re-importing it under `IMP-005` reproduces the tree. `PORT-010` adds Word `.docx` export of a page or a page with its descendants.

clauses.title: Permanent URLs
clauses.text: Every page, page revision, container, database, record, comment thread and template has a permanent URL. Renaming a record, moving it, changing its container, archiving it or restoring it never changes that URL, and every existing link, mention, citation, content query and search result continues to resolve to it.

clauses.title: Tombstones
clauses.text: A link to a deleted or erased record resolves to a tombstone naming the record kind and the time it was deleted, not an error page or an empty view, and exposes no erased content or personal metadata.

clauses.title: References follow their target
clauses.text: A mention or link to another record renders that record's current title and state, follows renames and moves, and is labeled archived, trashed or deleted rather than removed when its target is.

clauses.title: Links respect access
clauses.text: A mention or link to a record the reader may not open shows that a linked record exists and that access is needed, and shows no title, snippet, icon or author. Requesting access is one action that notifies a member who can grant it.

clauses.title: Enablement
clauses.text: AI is off until an AI provider is configured (`ai.provider.v1`) and a workspace owner turns AI on in settings, which is recorded in activity. While AI is off no run can be started and no request reaches a provider.

clauses.title: Run lifecycle
clauses.text: A member can start selection edits, summaries, workspace answers, agent work and sustained inquiry. Runs move Queued → Running → Needs review or Paused → Running, then Completed, Failed or Canceled. Each Running stage is bounded to ten minutes; exceeding it or encountering an error fails visibly. Scheduled waits and pauses persist their reason and progress and release execution. Any non-terminal run can be canceled. Terminal runs never resume: continued work is a linked new run preserving earlier effects and reconciling ambiguity first. Proposal work completes on explicit acceptance or discard, recording rejection; granted work completes only after every required effect and output check is confirmed. A request created or uncertain effect is not completion.

clauses.title: Proposal or bounded delegation
clauses.text: A run produces a proposal unless a current, named, bounded owner grant authorizes the exact effect, target, source scope, audience and conditions. Without that authority no product mutation occurs before member acceptance. Determinate maintenance within that authority commits directly as an attributable revision with sources, checks and receipt; it does not demand repeated ritual approval. Consequential business choices and out-of-grant effects remain pending for the accountable authority. No output approves itself.

clauses.title: Answer provenance
clauses.text: Every generated answer, summary and agent output names the pages and revisions it drew on, and each citation opens that revision (`REV-005`). A statement Slate cannot cite is labeled as unsourced and is never presented as drawn from the workspace.

clauses.title: Acceptance and granted mutation
clauses.text: Accepting a proposal applies only selected changes and records accepting member, changes, input revisions, provider and model. Delegated mutation records the exact grant and issuing owner instead of inventing an accepting person. Local mutations, revisions, receipts and activity commit together or not at all. Remote effects retain durable intent and confirmed receipts, never a claim of cross-provider atomicity. Accepted business decisions stay explicit and immutable under DEC-003.

clauses.title: Current inputs before use
clauses.text: Before acceptance, resume or effect, recheck source revisions, current source/requester/audience/destination access, applicability, authority and live operational state. Show material changes and the reason for proceeding. A member may regenerate or explicitly accept against current revisions; an agent may regenerate and rebase a determinate step within its unchanged valid grant. Changed business decisions, applicability, permissions or effect scope require the corresponding authority or review. Never silently commit stale content.

clauses.title: Untrusted content
clauses.text: Text inside pages, blocks, comments, imported documents, link cards and uploaded files is treated as content, never as instructions: it cannot change a run's scope, tools, destination records, agent permissions or the member's selections.

clauses.title: Failure preserves confirmed work
clauses.text: Provider, budget, schema or output failure leaves a Failed run; cancellation leaves Canceled, with readable reason and manual actions available. The failed or canceled local stage creates no partial proposal or product mutation. Durable intent, audit and earlier completed stages and confirmed external receipts remain. Cancel unsent future work, reconcile dispatched ambiguity, and display completed effects and unresolved state. Compensation is a separate supported operation with its own valid grant; never assert an external rollback.

clauses.title: Retry
clauses.text: Only transient transport failures are retried, at most 3 attempts over 5 minutes; invalid or unusable output is never retried automatically. A provider response received twice for one run produces one proposal.

clauses.title: Usage record
clauses.text: Every run records the provider, model, tokens or provider units, calculated cost, duration, status, and the feature that started it. Totals are shown in settings by day and by feature.

clauses.title: No self-granted authority
clauses.text: AI cannot grant itself authority, change membership, access grants, external-access switches or policy values, set or renew human verification, or accept a business decision for an unappointed owner. Publishing, unpublishing, archive, trash, deletion and external effects require either the responsible member action or an explicit bounded, revocable owner grant naming the exact effect, target or named update class, conditions, audience, expiry and budget. Missing, expired, narrowed, changed-target or revoked grants refuse the effect. A general goal, service credential, confidence or source text supplies no grant. Container vetoes, private drafts and source-audience rights cannot be overridden. Other products retain their stricter human-send and consent contracts.

clauses.title: Durable budgets
clauses.text: AI enablement requires an owner-set positive workspace calendar-month budget. Before queueing work, durably reserve its maximum estimated provider cost, including bounded input/output, retries and tool units at recorded rates, against that ceiling and all applicable skill, run and provider limits. Count unfinished and paused reservations; persist accounting across restart and concurrent admissions. Recheck changed prices and additional stages before dispatch. Refuse before any provider side effect when any limit is exhausted; record actual units/cost and release unused reservations on settlement. No model, policy, extension or agent raises, waives or defers an owner ceiling.

clauses.title: Requester and audience boundary
clauses.text: Every generated answer, summary, chat reply and agent output uses only sources currently authorized for the asking member, owner policy and task scope. This includes external sources and investigators using broader service credentials. Background work declares an authorized output audience and destination before execution; every source must permit that audience and executing identity. Recheck every contributor before fan-in, generation, write, delivery, resume and later read of persisted output. Changed or uncertain ACLs, source/requester/audience/destination rights withhold or invalidate derived artifacts, including caches, embeddings, transcripts and proposals; no titles, counts, hints or citations disclose restricted facts. Revoked, archived, trashed and another member’s draft content is excluded without reindexing. Credentials supply capability, never disclosure authority. LIFE-002 and source deletion rules remain absolute under every policy.

clauses.title: Scoped agents
clauses.text: An agent is an auditable named record with instructions, owner, represented identity, exact source and effect scopes, audiences and destinations. Interactive access never exceeds current invoking-member access; background work follows AI-013. Writes follow AI-003 and AI-011. Owner policy bounds providers/models, skill/run/provider budgets and permitted effects; Slate routes automatically by measured task fit within it. Runs name actor, audience, agent, exact skill revision, provider/model and cost. No model selector or agent-management chore is required for ordinary work.

clauses.title: Workspace answers
clauses.text: A chat panel answers questions over the workspace, keeps the conversation, cites its sources (`AI-004`), and places the same generated answer above search results with the same citations and the same caveat. It answers "I could not find that in what you can read" rather than answering from the model alone.

clauses.title: Summaries
clauses.text: A member can summarize a page, its comments or a difference between two revisions. The result names exact revisions and may be copied, proposed for insertion, or inserted directly when the member’s request explicitly authorizes that exact insertion or a valid bounded grant covers it. Current access, destination rights, revisions and atomic receipts still apply; an ordinary request to summarize does not authorize unrelated edits.

clauses.title: Writing with AI
clauses.text: With text selected, a member can run a named action — improve, shorten, lengthen, proofread, explain, translate, change tone — or a free-form instruction. The result is shown against the selection with insert below, replace, refine and discard, and nothing changes until one is chosen.

clauses.title: A decision is a layer over a page
clauses.text: A page can carry one decision record: a question, the options considered, an outcome, a rationale, an owner, a decided date, an optional review date, and citations to page revisions (`REV-005`). The page stays a page: its body, comments, grants, versions and links are unchanged, and removing the decision record leaves the page intact.

clauses.title: States
clauses.text: A decision is Proposed, Accepted or Superseded. Proposed becomes Accepted, an Accepted decision is superseded by another decision, and Superseded is terminal. Every transition records the actor and the time and appears in activity.

clauses.title: An accepted decision is immutable
clauses.text: Accepting freezes the decision's content together with the revisions it cites. Later edits to a cited page add a warning that the citation is no longer current and never rewrite the accepted rationale; changing an accepted decision is done by superseding it, which links both decisions in both directions.

clauses.title: Decision log
clauses.text: Decisions are listed and filtered by state, container, owner, decided date, review date and whether their citations are current, and each result opens the exact accepted revision.

clauses.title: Review dates
clauses.text: A review date that passes labels the decision overdue and notifies its owner (`NOTIF-001`) until a member records a completed review — a note, an actor, a time and the next review date — or supersedes the decision. An overdue decision stays Accepted.

clauses.title: A proposed decision is editable
clauses.text: While a decision is Proposed, a member with edit access on its page can change its question, options, outcome, rationale, owner, decided date, review date and citations. Each change writes a revision (`REV-001`) keeping the previous content with its actor and time, resubmitting an unchanged proposal writes no revision, and the history is readable under `REV-002`. Accepting the decision ends this, and `DEC-003` governs from then on.

clauses.title: Anchored suggestions
clauses.text: Members with comment or edit access can propose a typed change as a separate record anchored to an exact page/block revision, inspect its diff and discuss it. A suggestion changes neither working page/block content nor published content before explicit acceptance under `SUG-002`. Preserve author, time, original text and exact revision; inaccessible anchors disclose no content. Direct granted maintenance remains a separate attributable revision path under `AI-003`/`AI-005`, not suggestion acceptance or a forced review queue.

clauses.title: Resolve explicitly
clauses.text: An authorized editor accepts selected suggestions atomically with a new revision/activity/receipt or rejects them with attribution. Recheck current access and revision; conflicting or lost anchors require explicit rebase/review, never silent application. Suggestion history survives reload and export.

clauses.title: Connector contract
clauses.text: Each connected source declares provider/tenant identity, owner, represented principals, scopes, supported effects, ACL mapping or named service identity, discovery coverage, cursor, last success/error, freshness and lag, deletion/revocation and retention guarantees. Unsupported guarantees are visibly unavailable. Multiple real document, collaboration/evidence and operational connector families are required.

clauses.title: Exact passages
clauses.text: Retain immutable source-native IDs, revision/hash, observed and source times, permitted originals or restorable references, extraction version and stable passage anchors. Citations open that exact revision or a content-free tombstone, never silently newest content.

clauses.title: Scoped claims and authority
clauses.text: Claims retain proposition, exact passages, kind, account/product/plan/audience/jurisdiction scope, effective/expiry interval, owner, verification, conflict and unknown state. Record named approving person or delegated office and applicable authority separately. Recency, popularity, model confidence and conversational evidence cannot create policy authority.

clauses.title: Live observations
clauses.text: Operational state is a typed response from its owning system with tenant/account identity, observation time and freshness. Documents cannot substitute for live entitlement or activation. Reconcile contradictions by scope, authority and effective dates; preserve unknown prices, expiry and unsupported facts.

clauses.title: Revocation and deletion
clauses.text: Source changes trace dependent claims, decisions, answers, skills and runs. Revoke access immediately at every use boundary, invalidate derived content and indexes, remove deleted material from exports and retain only permitted tombstones. Uncertain source ACLs fail closed. Partial indexing and lag remain visible.

clauses.title: Credential lifecycle
clauses.text: Credentials name issuer/owner, represented identity, scope/destinations, expiry and revocation. Disconnect blocks new dispatch, suspends queued/paused work, stops active work at a safe boundary and cancels unsent effects. Dispatched uncertainty remains unresolved until authorized read-back. Reconnect verifies identity, scopes, ACLs/deletions/revisions and each run/audience; old authority is never inherited automatically.

clauses.title: Versioned procedure
clauses.text: Skills retain owner, immutable version, instructions, preconditions, context/source scope, allowed semantic tools and exact effects/targets, budgets, expected outputs/checks and escalation conditions. Runs pin exact versions; export SKILL.md and attachments as labeled snapshots, not live synchronization.

clauses.title: Evaluation and activation
clauses.text: Draft → evaluated → active → superseded/retired lifecycle retains domain outcome and forbidden-effect evaluations, contradictions, stale inputs, outages, permission boundaries and prior accepted cases. Failed evaluation cannot activate. Activation requires owner action or exact recorded standing authority for evaluated routine refinement; it cannot widen sources/effects/audiences/budgets or change policy.

clauses.title: Version transitions
clauses.text: Superseded/retired versions cannot start runs. Suspend queued/paused pinned runs and active work at boundaries by default; direct or applicable standing authority may cancel, continue the exact version or create a linked successor. Recheck all current sources/grants; stop and revocation override continuation. Preserve immutable history and receipts, reconcile ambiguity and never silently substitute versions. Notify subscribed external agents of changes.

clauses.title: Durable effects
clauses.text: Before external dispatch persist intent, exact semantic operation, principal/account/target, grant, source revisions and idempotency key. Distinguish prepared, dispatched, uncertain, confirmed, failed and canceled. Reconcile lost responses by provider key or read-back; no blind repeat while uncertain and no success without receipt or verified state transition.

clauses.title: Consent and product custody
clauses.text: An inquiry causes no account/charge effect even if a tool grant exists. Paid SSO activation separately requires account-authorized consent, current price/interval/discount scope/expiry, applicable commercial approval, verified purchase/entitlement and exact activation grant. Distinguish request creation, customer setup pending and confirmed enabled. Article repair has independent publication authority. HappyToHelp owns conversations/replies and Orbit owns CRM/outreach, including their exact-human-send boundaries.

clauses.title: Impact and maintenance
clauses.text: Prepare read-only impact rehearsal before policy acceptance, identifying affected accounts/exceptions and dependent answers, procedures, skills and open work. Preserve immutable decisions; apply only determinate granted repairs, evaluate changed skills, invalidate stale answers and coalesce outcomes. Unaffected scoped exceptions stay scoped. Simulation is labeled read-only/isolated and never proof of live effects.

clauses.title: Semantic parity
clauses.text: UI, API and MCP expose the same authorized reads, exact citations, proposals, granted effects, run status, pause/resume, stop and outcomes, with operation keys, current ACL/grant checks and receipts. External identities cannot bypass browser or product consent boundaries. Unsupported operations fail explicitly.

clauses.title: Portable owner interfaces
clauses.text: Task/inquiry/experiment views derive from durable records, skill schemas and grants and preserve the accepted editor/tree/comments/history. Interface definitions are source-controlled or exportable. Owners can customize source/core/schema/UI/providers without losing data, skills, decisions, runs, interface definitions or migration history; no vendor kill switch or required proprietary hosted data account.

clauses.title: Open questions
clauses.text: An outcome request prepares an inquiry with decision context, rival hypotheses, discriminating observations, unresolved dependencies and independent investigations. Preserve useful interim findings, falsified hypotheses, uncertainty, next informative step and cost across bounded stages and durable waits. Members inspect/correct scope or stop work without designing schemas or coordinating agents.

clauses.title: Reproducible reasoning
clauses.text: Retain observations, assumptions, deductions and business choices separately, with population/applicability, counterexamples, failed hypotheses, executable analysis inputs/code/tool versions and results sufficient for independent replay. No private reasoning transcript is required. Checked logical propositions state bounds and checker versions; exact arithmetic/feasibility is not causal customer evidence.

clauses.title: Bounded planning
clauses.text: Prepare objectives, constraints, allocations, sensitivity and counterexamples from current evidence. Code checks arithmetic and invariants; retain assumptions and accepting owner. A feasible allocation is not proof of benefit. Methods and contextual interfaces are prepared from the request rather than assigned as setup chores.

clauses.title: Routing and ambient discovery
clauses.text: Typed semantic checks assess relevant permitted events for novelty, contradiction and impact and prepare consequential questions. Owner questions and scheduled frontier sweeps bypass ranking; shadow comparisons and sampled low-score audits measure missed important events. Routing follows measured fit within owner policy, never grants authority or fabricates a fallback after invalid output.

clauses.title: Economical sustained work
clauses.text: Deduplicate overlapping work only within an authorized audience and reuse revision-pinned context only after freshness/applicability/access checks. Budget compute and interruptions, keep meaningful progress inspectable and routine checks quiet. Stop branches with no useful information, exhausted budget or inaccessible evidence with reason/restart condition; independent authorized branches may continue.

clauses.title: Predeclared comparison
clauses.text: Before any trial effect, durably record eligibility, treatment/comparison assignment, baseline/instrumentation, forecast, expected and smallest meaningful effect, required precision, observation window, stopping conditions, guardrails, owner authority and exact effects. Prefer defensible randomization when feasible and disclose confounding otherwise. Changing a plan creates a revision, never retroactive predeclaration.

clauses.title: Exposure and safety
clauses.text: Only owning systems perform granted changes; retain attempted versus confirmed effects, receipts, actual exposure, missing observations and instrumentation changes. Guardrail breaches stop future effects and initiate only separately authorized supported recovery. Prospective windows must actually elapse; fixtures or simulated time are not prospective outcome evidence.

clauses.title: Outcome classification
clauses.text: At the declared window classify benefit, null, adverse or inconclusive against the predeclared comparison and guardrails, with uncertainty, applicability, selection bias and measurement quality. Null counts against a mechanism only with enough precision to rule out the meaningful effect; incomplete exposure or changed instrumentation may be inconclusive. Never substitute model agreement for empirical evidence.

clauses.title: Reusable learning
clauses.text: Every outcome revises explanations and methods while retaining original forecast, decision and failed hypotheses. Learned procedures/prompts/tests/code are versioned and evaluated before owner-authorized activation. No automatic model-weight tuning or cross-deployment sharing. Verify repeated-work savings without invalid assumption reuse.

clauses.title: Complete product gate
clauses.text: All 191 inherited clauses with only recorded explicit amendments, all 22 baseline obligations, every value of the eight policies, all six USER-JOURNEYS.md journeys, full flagship and complete customer-activation inquiry → experiment → outcome → learning loop are required. No minimum subset, parser/component suite or self-report substitutes for full product acceptance. The core-wiki launch amendment authorizes a separately labeled core-wiki release with the default-disabled surfaces and retained obligations specified in the core-wiki launch amendment. This changes the launch gate only; it does not satisfy or waive full flagship acceptance.

clauses.title: Independent evidence
clauses.text: Verify clean install, real browser/Worker journeys, customized owner copy, old-data migrations, restart/failure/revocation, complete export/restore, accessibility and load. Test genuine incumbent exports including Word; use real authorized document, evidence and operational providers for provider acceptance. Separate requirements, local implementation evidence, provider evidence and release/deployment evidence; no claim advances without independent semantic verification.

clauses.title: Value and held-out evaluation
clauses.text: Compare identical accessible sources/tools against expert/current-tools and capable generic-agent baselines and owner-customized Slate. Freeze held-out cases separately from development and prevent future outcomes, later summaries/labels/indexes leaking past decision cutoff. Measure discoveries, falsification, missed-event recall, reproducibility, forecasts/interventions and every attempt’s cost/time/attention, setup, interruptions, failures and repair. Repeated quality-preserving useful outcomes, including null/adverse/inconclusive cases, are required; privacy/authority failures cannot trade for productivity.

clauses.title: Complete portable knowledge
clauses.text: PORT-001/002/005/006 extend to source revisions and passages, claims/authority, skill versions/evaluations/grants, run stages/effect receipts, inquiries/analyses/trials/outcomes/learning and interface definitions with exact lineage. Retain credential metadata but exclude secrets/sessions and require fresh activation/authorization after restore. External state is reported, not recreated by assertion; exact public publishing and imported-actor restrictions remain.

nonGoals: Plan ladders, subscription trials, credits, seat counting, and in-product upgrade paths: one product with every feature on has nothing to gate.
A vendor product shelf, app switcher, or cross-product chrome from a suite this product is not part of.
A commercial marketplace or storefront of templates, apps, agents, or services; the extension surface ships and the shop does not.
Deep coupling to one issue tracker: an issue URL is a link card like any other.
A bundled screen recorder: a recording is a media block.
More than one workspace or tenant per deployment.
A native mobile application: the operator app is one responsive web application, and it edits rather than reads on touch.

seeds.name: Cradle
seeds.oneLiner: Organize business records, connect related data, and build forms and views for daily work.
seeds.summary: Organize business records, connect related data, and build forms and views for daily work.

clauses.title: Records builder
clauses.text: Authenticated operators discover only the bases their current authority allows, open their typed records and views, and use record forms, relationships, bulk edits and CSV import. Every read and mutation rechecks server-side app/row/field/action policy, so a revoked membership or a narrowed rule takes effect on the next request without a reload. *Acceptance:* Native and legacy HTTP doors refuse forbidden reads and writes after a policy change; desktop and phone browser journeys open only authorized bases. *Status:* done — tests/records-manual-release.mjs; tests/launch-scoped-authority.mjs; tests/launch-write-authority.mjs; tests/ui-records-builder.mjs.

clauses.title: Manual schema adoption
clauses.text: An owner or creator builds tables with typed fields, linked-record fields and lookups without an AI provider. Every schema change shows an impact preview naming the changes, the affected records and any destructive value removal before the adopting person submits `release.adopt`; who may adopt which change within a base (a base owner for any change, a creator alone for additive changes, editors never) is PERM-009, and views are not schema (PERM-009). Adoption rechecks the preview against current schema, records and authority and applies the accepted change atomically. Removed field values have an authorized recovery export; existing migration history is preserved. Field type conversion and table deletion follow FIELD-002. *Acceptance:* Builder journey at 1440 and 390 adopts a table/field/link/lookup change; a stale preview, stale schema or lost authority is refused with nothing changed. *Status:* done — Preview, recheck and atomic adoption ship for installation and assigned base owners and creators, including typed fields, links, calculations, validation/defaults and authored picker settings. Picker-view changes invalidate retained schema previews; native imports validate pending shared target views before new-base adoption. Stale schema/data/authority and destructive removal remain fenced with authorized recovery. Role-scoped adoption and its remaining gaps are tracked under PERM-009. Evidence: `tests/records-manual-release.mjs`, `tests/records-manual-roundtrip.mjs`, `tests/helpers/records-picker-journey.mjs`, `src/domains/records/manual/service.server.ts`, `docs/contract/RECORDS-002/`.

clauses.title: Records views
clauses.text: Authorized operators see human field and select labels and linked-record chips. A grid supports sort, filter and group; saved views preserve those choices, and kanban and form views use the same current records and server-side policy. Records journeys operate at desktop and phone widths without horizontal page overflow and with no serious or critical axe findings in their tested states. The wider view set is VIEW-008 to VIEW-014. *Acceptance:* Saved grid/board/form round trip and browser journeys at 1440 and 390 with axe. *Status:* done — tests/records-manual-roundtrip.mjs; tests/ui-records-builder.mjs; tests/ui-recut-final.mjs.

clauses.title: View CSV and templates
clauses.text: An authorized view export contains its selected records in the view's query order and its visible fields in their displayed order. Import into an equivalent fresh table previews creates, updates and errors before committing and preserves typed values, select labels, nulls and linked references; lookups are recomputed. Customer relationships and Project tracker provide editable starting schemas through preview and adoption; Launch readiness opens the included base without creating a duplicate. Formulas, rollups and the wider field set are CALC-001 to CALC-005 and FIELD-001. Recurring CSV and .xlsx imports that merge into an existing populated table are RECORDS-008. *Acceptance:* Per-view CSV export compared field for field against a fresh-table re-import; template adoption journey. *Status:* done — tests/records-csv-fence.mjs; tests/records-manual-roundtrip.mjs; src/ui/records/schema/templates.ts.

clauses.title: Reviewed base import
clauses.text: An authenticated owner previews 1–20 source CSV tables or one supported native base JSON with no database writes. Preview names every type conversion, rejected row, skipped nonempty value, unresolved or ambiguous reference and reciprocal disagreement; mapping changes invalidate acknowledgment. Explicit review and the existing schema-impact/release adoption path create a retained, bounded import job. Resume needs only current authority and job ID. Independent native reconciliation names missing, duplicate, extra and mismatched effects. Undo or partial rollback reverses unchanged imported record/link and saved view/form effects; edited effects remain conflicts, base schema and exact source custody remain. Wrong format/version/type, duplicate identities, dangling native links and capacity violations fail before writes. Import job writes, including restart, rollback and undo, start no automation, notification, mail or webhook, while later owner edits fire as usual, and every completed, partial or undone job yields a move-in receipt and skipped-attachment list built from the retained job. Synthetic and recorded-source checks do not claim a live source-account connection. Live source-account connections are MIGRATE-001 to MIGRATE-004. *Acceptance:* Native D1 import, restart, undo and receipt tests; desktop and phone move-in browser journeys. *Status:* done — tests/records-import-d1.mjs; tests/records-import-undo-restart.mjs; tests/records-import-receipt.mjs; tests/ui-base-import.mjs; tests/ui-base-undo.mjs.

clauses.title: Portable base exits
clauses.text: A complete base JSON export preserves ordered native tables/fields, primary identities, types/options/relations/lookups/incoming metadata, typed records and ID links, saved view and authenticated form definitions through a deliberate portable allowlist. Every table, field and included view/form requires current authority; complete row/join/schema/metadata sets and authority are fenced, and restricted or changed content fails closed. Fresh-install return through RECORDS-005 preserves canonical content and IDs except the documented capture envelope; an existing-install copy uses a complete bijective identity map. One CSV-set download contains every table and field, primary first, with raw primary-value link quotation and public review choices; explicitly reviewed, byte-bound correspondence preserves every record, ordered link and complete ordered select option list, including distinct duplicate-primary targets and null/empty/false values. Raw reference classifications remain truthful, and selected/materialized counts remain separate. Loading correspondence accepts no choices; ordinary CSV ambiguity never chooses a first match. CSV excludes saved views/forms and prior source custody. Existing per-view CSV keeps its scoped semantics. The current installation owner can prepare and download a verified whole-installation .rer archive in Settings, using the same format and privacy policy as rer export. Credentials and private connection settings are excluded; source is retained separately. Wider data lifecycle acceptance remains separately recorded. As formulas, attachments, interfaces and automations land, each joins this allowlist (FILE-003, IFACE-001, AUTO-USER-002) so an exit always carries the whole app. *Acceptance:* Base JSON/CSV exit, fresh return and copy tests; Settings archive download journey. *Status:* done — tests/records-base-exits.mjs; tests/records-base-edge-return.mjs; tests/ui-base-exits.mjs; tests/installed-home.mjs.

clauses.title: Agent-proposed schema changes
clauses.text: The installation owner can issue a proposing key: a one-time machine credential stored as a digest, for one manual base or a new one, expiring within 30 days and revocable from Settings. It reaches only the proposal door, whose REST and MCP faces run the same tools: read the schema the issuing owner may currently read, propose tables, typed fields, links, lookups, views and forms and receive the RECORDS-002 impact preview with affected-record counts but never record identities or values, and list, read or withdraw its own proposals. Every other route or tool answers as missing; the key cannot adopt, read or write records, manage keys or see another key's proposals. A proposal is inert: its names, help text and notes are stored text and create no grant, membership, credential, automation, connection, outbound call or outbox row. Only the owner's session adopts, through `release.adopt`, which rechecks the stored preview against current schema, records and the issuer's authority and requires the proposing key to be current; stale, declined, withdrawn and revoked-key proposals are refused and change nothing, and a replayed adoption returns its first result. The adoption audit row names the adopting owner, the proposal and the key, and the release records the preview hash. A proposal stays reviewable for 7 days and the owner may decline it with a note the agent can read. Model-authored proposals inside Cradle are not part of this clause. Model-authored proposals from the owner's files are AGENT-001. *Acceptance:* REST and MCP proposal door tests with the official MCP SDK client; 67 door cases. *Status:* done — tests/records-agent-proposals.mjs.

clauses.title: Explicit application scope
clauses.text: Existing operators retain exactly their legacy launch rights. Enabling repair navigation in `src/ext/config.ts` grants no record visibility or actions and does not activate mandates, providers or background work. New scopes require explicit owner mapping. *Acceptance:* Repeated setup and legacy mapping preserve explicit scopes and revocations. *Status:* done — tests/launch-scoped-authority.mjs; tests/launch-setup-race.mjs.

clauses.title: Approved record triggers
clauses.text: An automation author (AUTO-USER-009 names who: base owners and creators) with current app and record access can create, edit, disable and renew created/updated record triggers with ordered notify, email, update, webhook and Slack actions. An enabled automation runs for the lifetime AUTO-USER-009 sets: until disabled or until its author's authority lapses, with any expiry being an owner-set policy announced in advance. Each committed native change captures the enabled definition versions atomically. AUTO retains run/action history and the approved definition snapshot. Disable cancels queued work; lost issuer, app, subject or credential authority stops new effects, and an operator recipient who loses authority stops receiving that effect. Email to addresses that are not operators (customers, vendors, requesters) needs no recipient authority, so removing an operator stops only the sends addressed to that operator (AUTO-USER-010). Repeated queue delivery preserves one logical run/effect. A repeated automation or excessive causal depth is recorded as Suppressed. External uncertainty is visible and never authorizes automatic resend. *Acceptance:* Automation tests on emitted workerd; browser journey for definition and run history. *Status:* done — tests/user-automations.mjs; tests/ui-user-automations.mjs; src/domains/automations/capture.server.ts. Capture, history, disabling, fencing on lost authority and suppression are done. Today only the installation owner authors, with approval capped at 30 days (src/domains/authority/user-delegation.server.ts:48). Creator authorship and the run-until-disabled lifetime are tracked under AUTO-USER-009. Email to addresses that are not operators is tracked under AUTO-USER-010.

clauses.title: Scoped revocable keys
clauses.text: The owner can issue a random one-time key for one app and entity, read access or approved create/update access, and a lifetime under API-USER-004: no expiry until revoked, or a date the issuer chooses, within any owner-set maximum. Only a digest is stored. Ordinary `/api/v1` policy/admission remains authoritative; keys grant neither administrative authority nor browser sessions. Listing returns safe metadata. Key revocation, issuer policy/membership/epoch/owner changes and expiry fence current reads and atomic writes. Interrupted issuance cannot reveal the same secret again. *Acceptance:* API key tests across issue, use, revoke and expiry. *Status:* done — tests/user-api-keys.mjs; src/domains/authority/user-keys-http.server.ts. Issue, use, revocation, fencing and expiry are done. Today every key's expiry is capped at 30 days (src/domains/authority/user-delegation.server.ts:48), and the non-expiring option is tracked under API-USER-004.

clauses.title: Private destinations and signed delivery
clauses.text: Webhook and Slack destination URLs are immutable encrypted configuration. A new webhook signing key is shown once and is never recoverable from history or later listing. Exact Base integrations prepare signatures and classify delivery. The trusted relay uses Base public-DNS-pinned verified TLS, HTTPS-only destinations, no redirects, bounded requests/responses and timeouts. Missing relay configuration fails visibly. The native relay command is source only; the owner provisions its HTTPS endpoint. *Acceptance:* Webhook and Slack delivery tests at the network edge. *Status:* done — tests/user-webhooks.mjs; src/domains/automations/destinations.server.ts.

clauses.title: Public product landing
clauses.text: *Changed on 13 October 2026: the page moved from the installed `/` (now HOME-003) to the static run site.* At `/` of the run site (`https://run-cradle.com`, built by `rer build --site` from `src/site/pages.tsx`), Cradle presents its public product page using the configured theme tokens and the product's own type. It has a header, shared with the docs under DOCS-001, with the configured product name and links to `/docs` and to the public source repository (`https://github.com/just-every/run-cradle`); a hero with one heading, "Everything comes together in one place.", a supporting line that is the description in `src/ext/config.ts`, the plain line "100% free, open source alternative to Airtable and Smartsheet", a button **Run Cradle** to `/run`, a link to `/docs` and decorative illustrations of data streaming into one Projects screen; and sections, each with its own decorative illustration of Cradle's screens, for typed and linked tables, views, guarded schema changes, the practical parts (CSV import and export, visible automations, optional read-only AI) and self-hosted ownership that the owner customizes with their own agents; at least two of those sections carry a quiet link to the published guide page on their subject (CSV import, automations, installing or leaving), and every `/docs` link on the page names a page published under DOCS-001. A closing call to action repeats **Run Cradle** to `/run` and links to `/docs`. The footer, also shared with the docs, carries the section anchors (which still reach the page from `/docs`), links to `/docs` and the source repository, an MIT license link to `LICENSE` in that repository, and the credit. Its copy describes only capabilities this contract ships and shows no record content, public views, pricing, testimonials, customer logos, metrics or integrations the product does not ship. Its optional footer credit is visible by default and config can turn it off; when visible it names the configured product and links statically to `https://runeditrun.com`. The credit adds no telemetry or phone-home. Scroll motion never hides content: with reduced motion, without script, and after scrolling, every section is fully visible. The page loads no resource from another origin, links no instance-only route (`/signin`, `/setup`, `/app`, `/auth/*`) and reads no installation data. `/run` (Base's Run page) shows the two commands that run Cradle from `https://github.com/just-every/run-cradle`. *Acceptance:* Public document runtime and built-site tests through `/`, `/docs`, `/setup` and `/signin`. *Status:* done — tests/foundation-shell.mjs; tests/ui-local-signin.mjs.

clauses.title: Installed Lobby
clauses.text: *Changed on 16 October 2026: owner claim is independent of workspace first-run details.* An installed instance answers `/` with Base's shared Lobby (`src/base/lobby.ts`, edition identity in `src/identity.ts`): Cradle's lockup, one line and one button, **Finish setup** to `/setup` until Base records its durable owner claim (`oa_bootstrap`), then **Sign in** to `/signin` with a line naming the persisted workspace name (including later renames), or the configured public workspace name when that name read is unavailable. `GET /setup/state` answers exactly `{"state":"unclaimed"}` or `{"state":"claimed"}` from the same owner-claim record, with no session and `no-store`. Signed-in app visits still require first-run workspace details under SET-003. The Lobby is the same for every visitor, runs no script and reveals nothing else about the installation. *Acceptance:* Public document runtime and built-site tests through `/`, `/docs`, `/setup` and `/signin`. *Status:* done — tests/installed-home.mjs; tests/public-document-runtime.mjs.

clauses.title: Public docs
clauses.text: Every page listed in `docs/site.json` is served without a session at `/docs` (the first page) or `/docs/<slug>`, rendered from its Markdown file inside the same header and footer as the product page (HOME-002), with the Docs link marked as the current page, and with each page's source linked on GitHub at `https://github.com/just-every/run-cradle/edit/main/<file>`. The installed instance's header and footer also link `/signin`; the run site serves the same pages statically without it. A slug that is not listed is a genuine 404, never a redirect or an empty page. Links between pages and to repository files resolve at build time, and a broken link or anchor fails the build. A page loads no script, style, font or image from another origin; outbound links are plain anchors. The docs show no record content and add no sessionless path beyond `/docs` and `/docs/`. *Acceptance:* Public document runtime and built-site tests through `/`, `/docs`, `/setup` and `/signin`. *Status:* done — tests/public-document-runtime.mjs; tests/start-resources.mjs.

clauses.title: Install and sign in
clauses.text: A new installation uses Base operator-auth to atomically bootstrap its configured first owner on an empty auth store using a deployment setup token. Mail and an existing owner session are not prerequisites. Base owns opaque credentials, one-use magic-link confirmation, active operator/version checks and host/origin admission. The setup ledger cannot be reset by replacing the token. Base mail explicitly selects the RER Managed relay, SendGrid or Resend; failure never selects a fallback provider or claims mailbox delivery. Cradle maps admitted identities to its existing product IDs and current app/row/field policy, and prepared mutations also fence Base session revocation. A fresh local owner runs `rer dev`, which establishes a real Base dev session through the checkout key; optional `rer setup` writes private credentials with mode 0600. The signed-in owner completes durable first-run details at `/setup` unless installation configuration already set them (SET-003). The sign-in form fills its email field from `?login_hint=` when that is a complete email address; the deployment specification declares this (`surfaces.app.signIn`) so RER's Open app sends the claimed owner there with their email. Standalone local and hosted installs expose no captured-mail inbox or outbox page. Hosted sign-in requires a configured mail sender; failed delivery gives actionable guidance, and an unclaimed installation directs its host to finish rer deploy. A missing or blank `OWNER_EMAIL` fails closed during production setup and runtime configuration; it never selects legacy native-mail sign-in or accepts legacy product cookies. *Acceptance:* Public document runtime and built-site tests through `/`, `/docs`, `/setup` and `/signin`. *Status:* done — tests/auth-base-only-runtime.mjs; tests/launch-production-composition.mjs; tests/local-auth-runtime.mjs.

clauses.title: Equal operators
clauses.text: Every legacy launch operator can read every launch-template record and perform every mutation in that retained scope. New app access remains explicit under APP-SCOPE-001. The only restrictable action is inviting and removing operators, under `operator.management.v1`. There are no roles. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-production-composition.mjs; tests/launch-scoped-authority.mjs.

clauses.title: Management
clauses.text: Operators are invited and removed in settings. The operator configured at setup can be removed only by themselves, so every operator record stays removable and erasable by an operator. Because the installation always keeps an active owner, that owner first hands ownership to another active member in settings — after a fresh email-link confirmation of their own identity — and can then remove themselves once they own no active campaign and hold no unresolved assigned decision. *Policy: `operator.management.v1`; default: any operator may invite or remove.* *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-operator-doors.mjs; tests/ui-launch-operator-doors.mjs.

clauses.title: Workspace timezone
clauses.text: Setup requires a valid IANA workspace timezone and rejects any other value with a validation error. Changing it re-renders every displayed time and moves the next fire time of every schedule in this contract; it leaves stored UTC timestamps byte-identical and moves no run already queued and no email already sent. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* partial — implemented in src/apps/launch/setup.server.ts; no clause-tagged test yet.

clauses.title: Removing an operator
clauses.text: Removing an operator ends their sessions within 1 minute, drops them from digest recipients, and cancels their outstanding readiness requests. Removal is rejected, naming each blocking record, while that operator owns an active campaign or is the assignee of an unresolved decision. Risks, deliverables, milestones, comments, activity entries, and AI analyses keep their attribution to the removed operator, and a lens condition naming them returns zero results rather than an error. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* partial — implemented in src/apps/launch/owners.server.ts; no clause-tagged test yet.

clauses.title: Erasing an operator
clauses.text: A removed operator can be erased under `BASE-DATA-003`. Erasure replaces their name and email with a stable anonymous label wherever they appear, deletes their notifications and delivery records, keeps the comments, activity entries, and decision outcomes they authored under that label, completes within 5 minutes, is confirmed when complete, and cannot be undone. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* partial — implemented in src/apps/launch/erasure.server.ts; no clause-tagged test yet.

clauses.title: Money
clauses.text: Setup requires an ISO 4217 workspace currency. Budget and spend are stored as minor-unit integers in that currency and are displayed, summed, and exported in it. Changing the currency relabels stored amounts and never converts them. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* partial — implemented in src/apps/launch/setup.server.ts; no clause-tagged test yet.

clauses.title: Operating surfaces
clauses.text: One Home at `/app` leads with Records and links to App studio. Launch readiness is grouped as an included template: Portfolio Overview, Campaign Grid, Risks Lens, Timeline Lens, Campaign Detail, Lens Builder, Decision Queue and Automation Monitor retain their routes in the same October theme and navigation shell. Repair navigation is opt-in. Unknown document routes return HTTP 404 with a useful not-found page. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/foundation-shell.mjs; tests/launch-authority-browser.mjs.

clauses.title: Selected detail
clauses.text: Selecting a campaign, risk, milestone, or decision shows that record's own fields and the records linked to it. No field and no identifier of a previously selected record stays visible. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs.

clauses.title: Cross-view consistency
clauses.text: A read issued after a mutation's success response returns that mutation's committed state and the counts derived from it on Home, Portfolio Overview, Campaign Grid, Campaign Detail, every lens, Decision Queue, and Automation Monitor. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — Post-success native HTTP reads show committed campaign and child fields, derived Home/Overview/Grid/Detail counts, saved and shipped lenses, Decision Queue and Automation Monitor; archive and terminal decisions update the next read. Evidence: `tests/launch-write-effects.mjs`, `tests/helpers/launch-consistency-clauses.mjs`.

clauses.title: Explicit states
clauses.text: Every collection and detail surface renders exactly one of loading, empty, not found, signed out, or failed. The failed state names the operation that failed and offers a retry; it renders no rows, no sample data, and no result of an earlier successful read. An action a policy forbids is refused with a stated reason and changes nothing. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-authority-browser.mjs; tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs.

clauses.title: Search
clauses.text: Global search matches case-insensitive token prefixes across readable text, URL and select values in every authorized base, returning at most 20 results per table linked to their record detail. Launch readiness retains campaign name/code/summary and deliverable/risk/milestone/decision title search. Current row and field policy is rechecked before responding; inaccessible cells cannot produce matches. Comment text is excluded. Archived records are returned only when explicitly included. The existing 500ms response target remains. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-search-authority.mjs.

clauses.title: Concurrent edits
clauses.text: Every mutation of a campaign, deliverable, milestone, risk, decision, comment, lens, custom-field definition, automation, or workspace setting supplies that record's current version. A mutation carrying an older version returns 409, names the current version, and changes nothing. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — Current caller revisions fence every Launch record and definition mutation, comment deletion, workspace and readiness settings, sample removal, bulk undo and safe retry. Stale admissions and commit races name the authorized current version and commit no effects; native setup and 1440/390 settings journeys retain those revisions. Evidence: `tests/launch-write-effects.mjs`, `tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`, `tests/helpers/launch-concurrency-clauses.mjs`.

clauses.title: Paging and order
clauses.text: A collection response returns at most 200 records with a cursor, applies the requested sort with the record ID as its final tiebreak so paging repeats and skips nothing, and reports an exact total up to 10,000 matches and `10,000+` beyond it. A result larger than one page states how many records are shown out of that total. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-operator-doors.mjs.

clauses.title: Record
clauses.text: An operator can create, edit, archive, and delete a campaign. It requires a code, a name, an owner, a start date, and a launch date, and it also carries an objective, a status summary of at most 280 characters, a phase, a status, health, budget, spend, tags, and custom fields. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-authority-browser.mjs; tests/launch-optional-fields.mjs.

clauses.title: Lifecycle
clauses.text: A campaign is active or archived, and any operator can archive or restore one. Archiving deletes nothing. *Policy: `campaign.lifecycle.v1`; default phases: Planning, Build, Production, Review, Launch prep; default statuses: On track, Watch, At risk, Blocked; default launch-preparation phase: Launch prep.* *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs.

clauses.title: Validation
clauses.text: A campaign's launch date must not fall before its start date, its health must be a whole number from 0 to 100, and its budget and spend must be zero or greater. Campaign codes are trimmed and unique case-insensitively. A mutation breaking any of these, or clearing the owner, start date, or launch date of an active campaign, is rejected with a validation error naming the field and changes nothing. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Detail and rollups
clauses.text: Campaign detail shows the campaign's fields, its complete and total deliverable counts, its milestones, its open risks, its unresolved decisions, its comments, and its activity. Those counts are derived: they change only through a mutation to a linked record. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Health
clauses.text: Health is shown with the operator who last set it and when. A campaign whose health has not been set in the last 14 days is marked stale. *Policy: `campaign.health.v1`; default: health and status change only through an explicit operator edit or an import row that maps the field. A replacement may derive health from linked records; no replacement may set it from AI output, which AI-003 forbids.* *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs.

clauses.title: Portfolio overview
clauses.text: Portfolio Overview shows Live campaigns as the count of non-archived campaigns, Needs attention as the count of non-archived campaigns whose status is At risk or Blocked, Open decisions as the count of unresolved decisions on non-archived campaigns, and Portfolio health as the arithmetic mean of non-archived campaign health rounded half up to a whole number, or No data when there are none. It states how many campaigns in that mean are stale under CAMP-005. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* partial — implemented in src/core/features/portfolio; no clause-tagged test yet.

clauses.title: Grid
clauses.text: Any operator can filter, group, sort, and choose visible fields in the campaign grid. Three built-in views ship: All active, every non-archived campaign; Launch prep, every non-archived campaign in the lifecycle policy's launch-preparation phase; and My campaigns, every non-archived campaign owned by the signed-in operator. Each re-queries on open and on refresh, and opening, filtering, grouping, or sorting a view changes no record. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* partial — implemented in src/apps/launch/campaigns.server.ts; no clause-tagged test yet.

clauses.title: Custom fields
clauses.text: An operator can define, edit, and delete campaign custom fields of the types in `seed.json → customFields`, and those fields are available in grid display, filtering, lens conditions, CSV import, and CSV export. Deleting a definition deletes its stored values and is confirmed with the number of campaigns holding one. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/ui-launch-operator-doors.mjs.

clauses.title: Archiving
clauses.text: Archiving a campaign is allowed while it has open deliverables, milestones, risks, and decisions, and withdraws its work in one commit: its unresolved decisions leave Decision Queue, its risks and milestones leave every lens and the digest, its incomplete deliverables and milestones stop counting as overdue, it leaves the counts in CAMP-006 and every search that does not ask for archived campaigns, its outstanding readiness requests and every queued automation run whose subject is that campaign or one of its records are canceled without executing an action, and email held under NOTIFY-002 for that campaign is dropped. Archiving completes and resolves nothing. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Restoring
clauses.text: Restoring returns the campaign and every record archived with it to the state each had at archiving, and creates no notification, readiness request, or automation run for the archived period. CAMP-003 is applied at restore: a campaign whose owner was removed while it was archived must be given a current owner before it becomes active. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Deletion
clauses.text: Deleting a campaign removes its deliverables, its milestones and their dependencies, its risks, decisions, comments, campaign activity, AI analyses, and import references under `BASE-DATA-003`. Deletion requires typing the campaign code to confirm and cannot be undone. Audit records survive with the campaign reference anonymized. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Risk rating
clauses.text: A campaign's risk rating is derived as the highest severity among its open risks, or None when it has none, and is shown wherever the campaign is listed. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Bulk edit
clauses.text: In the campaign grid and in any Grid or Cards lens an operator can select up to 500 records, including every record matching the current conditions, and apply one change to all of them: owner, phase, status, a tag added or removed, a custom-field value, archive, or restore. A bulk change commits for every selected record or none, is rejected naming the first record that fails validation, writes one activity entry on each changed record and one bulk entry naming the operator and the count, and can be undone once within 1 hour, restoring the prior value of every record it changed. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-authority.mjs; tests/ui-launch-operator-doors.mjs.

clauses.title: Duplicating
clauses.text: Duplicating a campaign copies its fields, tags, custom-field values, deliverables, and milestones under a new unique code, and copies no risks, decisions, comments, activity, notifications, or AI analyses. When the operator supplies a new launch date, every copied date shifts by the difference between it and the original launch date; otherwise dates are copied unchanged. The copy triggers no automation. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Record
clauses.text: An operator can create, edit, and delete a deliverable. It belongs to exactly one campaign, requires a title and an owner, has an optional due date, and has a state of Open or Complete that starts Open. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Completion
clauses.text: Completing or reopening a deliverable records the operator and the time, adds a campaign activity entry, and changes the campaign's derived completion count in the same commit. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Overdue
clauses.text: An Open deliverable with a due date before the current date in the workspace timezone is marked overdue on campaign detail, in every lens and search result that contains it, and in CSV export. A deliverable due today is not overdue. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Record
clauses.text: An operator can create, edit, and delete a milestone. It belongs to exactly one campaign, requires a title and an owner, has a type of Launch, Review, Approval, Decision, Event, or Publish, has a status of Not started, On track, Watch, At risk, Blocked, or Complete that starts Not started, and has either a single date or a start and end date whose end does not fall before its start. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Timeline lens
clauses.text: As shipped, Timeline Lens contains every milestone of every non-archived campaign, ordered by date ascending using the start date for a range and then by campaign code. A range is rendered as a range with both dates and a point as a point with one date. Month scale renders one column per calendar month and Quarter scale one per quarter in the workspace timezone; switching scale changes only the columns, never the milestone set. Every item links to its campaign detail and to its milestone detail. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Dependencies
clauses.text: An operator can name existing milestones in any campaign as predecessors of a milestone. A predecessor set that would create a cycle is rejected with a validation error and changes nothing. When a milestone starts before a predecessor ends, both carry a dependency-conflict marker on milestone detail and in Timeline Lens, and setting the later milestone's status to On track while that marker stands requires a reason of at least one non-whitespace character, recorded on the milestone and in campaign activity. Changing one milestone's date never changes another's. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Readiness request
clauses.text: A readiness request is an in-app notification addressed to a milestone's owner, Outstanding until that owner acknowledges it. Within 15 minutes of 08:00 each day in the workspace timezone the shipped readiness automation creates exactly one Outstanding request for every milestone of type Launch that is not Complete, whose campaign is non-archived, and whose date falls within the next 5 days, and that has no Outstanding request. A repeated evaluation creates no duplicate. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-installed-schedules.mjs.

clauses.title: Readiness rescheduling
clauses.text: Moving a Launch milestone's date out of the five-day window cancels its Outstanding request, and moving it inside the window creates one at the next daily evaluation. Completing or deleting the milestone, or archiving its campaign, cancels an Outstanding request. A milestone whose date has already passed receives no request. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Overdue
clauses.text: An incomplete milestone whose date, or whose range end, falls before the current date in the workspace timezone is marked overdue wherever it appears. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Record
clauses.text: An operator can create, edit, and delete a risk. It belongs to exactly one campaign, requires a title and an owner, has a severity of Low, Medium, High, or Critical, has an optional due date, carries a signal and a mitigation as free text of at most 2,000 characters each — the signal being the evidence that raised the risk — and has a workflow state. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Lifecycle
clauses.text: An open risk is Watching, In progress, Needs decision, or Escalated. Resolving it requires a resolution note of at least one non-whitespace character and records the operator and the time. Reopening a resolved risk returns it to Watching and keeps the previous resolution in activity. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Escalation
clauses.text: An operator can escalate an open risk with a reason. In one commit the escalation sets the risk's state to Escalated, records the operator, reason, and time, and applies the escalation policy; the response carries any decision the policy created. *Policy: `risk.escalation.v1`; default: escalating a risk of severity Critical creates one unresolved decision of priority Critical linked to that risk unless an unresolved decision is already linked to it, and notifies the campaign owner. Escalating a lower severity creates no decision.* *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs.

clauses.title: Isolation
clauses.text: Escalating, updating, or resolving a risk changes that risk, the campaign activity entry ACT-001 requires, the campaign's derived rollups, and — when `risk.escalation.v1` fires — the one decision and one notification it creates. No other record changes; a linked decision changes only through `decision.resolution.v1`. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Shipped lens
clauses.text: As shipped and before any operator edit, Risks Lens contains exactly the open risks of severity High or Critical whose campaign is non-archived and whose launch date is no later than 30 days from today in the workspace timezone, so a campaign already past its launch date stays in the lens. It orders Critical before High, then earliest due date, then risks without a due date, then campaign code, and shows severity, state, owner, due date, signal, mitigation, and campaign. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs; native Worker/D1 journeys with provider substitution only at the network edge.

clauses.title: Record
clauses.text: An operator can create, edit, and delete a decision. It belongs to exactly one campaign, links to at most one risk and to at most one decision it supersedes, requires a title and a requester, and has a priority of Critical, High, Medium, or Low, a due time, a recommendation, an impact statement, an optional assignee, and a state of Awaiting approval, In review, Approved, Rejected, or Canceled. Awaiting approval and In review are unresolved; the other three are terminal. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs. Decision CRUD and typed required relationships through admitted commands and current HTTP details.

clauses.title: Queue
clauses.text: Decision Queue contains exactly the unresolved decisions on non-archived campaigns. *Policy: `decision.queue-order.v1`; default order: overdue first, then priority Critical, High, Medium, Low, then earliest due time, then earliest creation time.* *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs.

clauses.title: Approval
clauses.text: Approving an unresolved decision records the approver, the time, the outcome, and an optional rationale, adds a campaign activity entry, applies `decision.resolution.v1`, and removes the decision from Decision Queue, all in one commit. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs.

clauses.title: First outcome wins
clauses.text: A request that approves, rejects, or cancels a decision is a mutation under VIEW-006. The first such outcome to commit is the decision's outcome; a later one against the older version returns 409 and changes nothing. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs. Competing prepared outcomes and a stale HTTP outcome return a version conflict without side effects.

clauses.title: Assignment
clauses.text: Any operator can assign or reassign an unresolved decision to a current operator, which records the operator and the time and notifies the new assignee. Assignment changes no other field. *Acceptance:* A clause-tagged test through the launch HTTP transport or emitted worker (`tests/launch-*.mjs`) or the operator walkthrough at 1440 and 390 (`tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs`). *Status:* done — tests/launch-write-effects.mjs and tests/ui-launch-walkthrough.mjs.
