seeds.name: Uptime
seeds.oneLiner: Monitor your sites and scheduled jobs, track outages and notify your team.
seeds.summary: Monitor your sites and scheduled jobs, track outages and notify your team.

clauses.title: Signed HTTP monitoring
clauses.text: Public hosted HTTP(S) and keyword checks run in the Cloudflare Worker; private checks use the separately scoped Node runner. They retain the exact immutable assertion bundle and bounded transport evidence, and require authenticated claims and signed results; the control plane must reject contradictory completion. Hosted Worker checks leave through Cloudflare's shared egress and have no dedicated source address; published allowlistable probe addresses and probe identification are PROBE-002's. See [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority) and [Network and credentials](#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance evidence:** Create an HTTP(S) and keyword monitor through the owner API, run scheduled hosted and signed runner work against a controlled HTTPS service, fail its status/text, recover it and inspect the immutable assertions and transport evidence.

clauses.title: Immutable scheduled evidence
clauses.text: Definitions, scheduled slots and every retry attempt retain revision, policy, fixed selected probes, runner identity, timings, status, assertions and error category; retries never erase failures, and observation/state/outbox commit atomically. See [Evidence and state](#evidence-and-state) and [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance evidence:** Through signed claim/result routes submit failure, retry, late and duplicate attempts, restart, and read history; each attempt and its revision remains identifiable and observation/state/outbox either all commit or none do.

clauses.title: Fixed coverage and incident hysteresis
clauses.text: Missing or expired passing coverage is Unknown, partial failure stays visible, independent-vantage agreement and scheduled confirmation determine Failing, and complete fresh scheduled passing evidence plus recovery threshold is required for recovery; manual checks and maintenance never rewrite observations or scheduled policy. See [Evidence and state](#evidence-and-state). **Acceptance evidence:** Run two assigned network vantages through partial, missing, stale, failing and recovering slots; inspect Unknown/Degraded/Failing and thresholds. A manual pass, absent probe or maintenance expiry cannot fabricate recovery.

clauses.title: Server-side scoped authority
clauses.text: Every private document, read, mutation and export requires server-side operator or scoped runner authority, missing configuration fails closed, browser mutations enforce configured origin, and expired/foreign attempts cannot alter current evidence, and duplicate attempt identities cannot overwrite it; a signature identifies a key holder rather than proving truthful observation. See [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance evidence:** Open private documents and call native/framework APIs while signed out, revoked, cross-origin or using a foreign/expired runner signature; require refusal with no product writes, then succeed with the authorized session or scoped runner.

clauses.title: Pinned bounded destination execution
clauses.text: Every public DNS answer and redirect hop is validated fail closed; private-runner numeric sockets preserve Host and TLS identity, hosted checks use Cloudflare’s public Internet fetch transport, unsafe/mixed addresses and HTTPS downgrade are rejected, cross-origin redirects strip request authority, and synthetic grants and protected origin-bound local credential files retain their separate custody limits. The PROBE-002 identification header follows these credential rules and is stripped on cross-origin redirects. See [Network and credentials](#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance evidence:** Exercise real controlled HTTP/TLS endpoints with mixed DNS, rebinding, hostname mismatch, redirects, downgrade, forbidden addresses, credentials and execution bounds; inspect requests and prove rejected destinations receive no connection or authority.

clauses.title: Revision-scoped receipt evaluation
clauses.text: Hashed owner-issued tokens and, in the header form, increasing sequences protect server-time receipts, ingress cannot advance health, and scheduled signed completion must match its exact installation-local claim snapshot; stale, future, paused, foreign-revision or imported receipts cannot establish Healthy. These rules bind every receipt form of the buyer-facing job heartbeat in HEARTBEAT-002. See [Network and credentials](#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance evidence:** Issue and rotate a heartbeat token through the owner door, send increasing receipts, miss one, and evaluate scheduled signed snapshots; replay, old tokens, imported or foreign-revision receipts cannot change current health.

clauses.title: Inactive validated restore
clauses.text: Bounded versioned archives require integrity and semantic validation before transactional restore into empty product data, preserve historical evidence, erasure receipts and the permanent anonymized action audit, create paused current revisions, interrupt leases and quarantine alerts; installation-local sessions, keys, grants, request credential values, heartbeat authority, contact, webhook and Slack URLs, and signing keys are excluded; destination definitions and retained notification histories are portable, and imported evidence cannot establish current health or replay events. The source erasure journal fences copies made before a later erasure when that journal accompanies the restore. A local CLI receiving checkout must run setup first to establish its owner and settings. The owner accepted this installation-authority and endpoint-credential archive policy on 2026-10-13; it is an intentional replacement, not BASE-DATA-001 equivalence. See [Portability and retention](#portability-and-retention) and [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance evidence:** Export a populated installation including TCP, DNS, TLS and domain monitors, establish a different receiving owner, import into empty product data, then export/read history and repeat the restore. Each protocol’s settings and immutable revisions/slots survive; definitions are paused, leases interrupted, delivery quarantined, secrets/authority absent, history retained and later erasure journals enforced; corrupt/nonempty imports write nothing.

clauses.title: Reviewed definition files and inactive imports
clauses.text: Versioned monitor definition files are previewed without writes and validated with the editor’s rules. Applying a matching plan creates paused monitors or new revisions that preserve existing enablement, maintenance and runner assignments. Files carry no request secrets or installation authority and cannot enable monitors, issue heartbeat tokens or change notification destinations. Batch undo preserves history and reports revision conflicts. No real third-party export or hosted import has been measured.

clauses.title: Explicit storage custody
clauses.text: Product and observation metadata and legacy development sign-in records have no automatic age/count deletion; operator erasure removes captures for the associated operator, and local reset clears the installation. Expired sessions, authentication/public rate-limit state and short-lived login-attempt counters are cleaned up. Expired or confirmed alert-drill links lose their capability material while drill history stays; retired destination secrets are scrubbed only after owner rotation/deletion and in-flight sends finish; a proven-unsent integration-attempt reservation can be removed while its delivery history remains. Other expired operational records, including discovery jobs, change status and remain stored unless an owner erases the associated entity or resets the installation. Raw target response bodies and probe-request secrets are not retained in observations; the only target content kept is EVIDENCE-002's bounded, redacted, access-controlled failure snapshot, stored apart from observations under owner-set retention, carried in archives and erased with its monitor or on owner request. Webhook and Slack endpoint URLs and signing keys remain installation-local, available email addresses travel as destination definitions, and retention changes must never silently improve the fixed denominator or historical health. See [Portability and retention](#portability-and-retention). **Acceptance evidence:** Judge custody and every declared cleanup class at current supported bounds. Populate product, authentication, rate-limit, drill, credential and attempt records; run expiry, maintenance and restart through runtime doors and compare surviving identities. Only declared transient data/secret material disappears; no cleanup improves uptime or removes retained product history.

clauses.title: Operator-directed entity erasure
clauses.text: An owner can erase a monitor with its evidence and dependent notification/heartbeat records, a destination with its credential copies, or an operator while another active owner remains. Monitor erasure requires typing the current monitor name. Each completed erasure returns a receipt with entity kind, per-table counts and completion time, and returns it only after the transaction containing the erasure, audit entry and portability fence succeeds. Requests based on stale monitor or destination state cannot re-create erased rows. The last active owner cannot be erased: local installations use `rer reset --yes`, while hosted installations require replacement by redeployment. Uptime has no R2 upload feature, so product erasure has no uploaded attachments to remove. Already downloaded archives, messages already sent to external recipients and requests already in progress remain outside local erasure. See [Erasure and audit](#erasure-and-audit). **Acceptance evidence:** Erase each supported entity through the owner API, including stale concurrent requests and the original owner with a successor. Inspect the atomic per-table receipt, audit and journal; the last owner is protected and an old archive with the later journal cannot resurrect erased records.

clauses.title: Durable anonymized audit
clauses.text: Destructive actions, automated notification attempts and operator authentication-mail sends record actor or feature, time, action, subject kind and an opaque subject reference. Audit history is portable and survives erasure of the subject; erasing an operator anonymizes its prior actor references. The audit contains no monitor names, target URLs, email addresses or destination URLs. See [Erasure and audit](#erasure-and-audit) and [Portability and retention](#portability-and-retention). **Acceptance evidence:** Perform destructive actions, notification attempts and authentication-mail attempts through public doors, erase an actor and round-trip an archive; inspect durable opaque subjects and anonymized actors without planted names, addresses, URLs or secrets.

clauses.title: Contact separate from health
clauses.text: Only accepted scoped claims and signed results refresh server-time contact, the 120-second freshness threshold never proves process liveness or target health, and restart, unavailable reads and archive omission preserve that distinction. See [Contact, interface and delivery](#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance evidence:** Read Never seen, make accepted idle claims/results, age contact, reject foreign requests and restart. Reads and health checks do not refresh contact; unavailable reads and restore cannot imply runner or target health.

clauses.title: Honest durable operator feedback
clauses.text: Textual state/freshness/reasons, immutable history, labels, keyboard controls and responsive layout expose persisted evidence; failed reads show Unknown, action errors survive polling, busy reconciliation excludes controls and editing rejects assertion overrides. See [Contact, interface and delivery](#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance evidence:** Use the real owner console at 1440 and 390 with healthy, stale, failing and unavailable monitors; edit assertions, force read/action errors and polling, navigate by keyboard and inspect focus, text state, overflow, accessibility tree and axe results.

clauses.title: Authorized installation-wide destinations
clauses.text: An owner may configure email, signed JSON webhook, or Slack incoming webhook destinations for all monitors in one installation; only scheduled incident transitions generate automatic notifications, and a test send cannot change monitor evidence or incident state. The hosted Worker submits email through the configured Base mail adapter and sends webhooks and Slack without a private runner; a private runner can also claim notification work. Webhook destinations also take WEBHOOK-001's configurable method, content type, custom headers and payload template. Destination credentials are installation-local and are not restored from archives. See [Contact, interface and delivery](#contact-interface-and-delivery) and [Network and credentials](#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance evidence:** Create/rotate/disable email, Slack and signed webhook destinations, cause scheduled failure/recovery and a test send through actual Worker/runner delivery doors; inspect one job per enabled destination, credentials, exact signing, escaping and unchanged health for tests.

clauses.title: Bounded notification acknowledgment
clauses.text: Each event and destination without receiver-side deduplication (email, Slack incoming webhooks and the other channels DELIVERY-002 names), every test send and every drill gets one automatic send attempt. A RER relay 429 with Retry-After confirms non-acceptance and queues another submission after that delay. For those sends HTTP 500, connection loss, timeout, and unknown outcomes remain uncertain and are not automatically sent again; deduplicating destinations retry and every route can fall back to another contact under DELIVERY-002. Accepted means the configured provider or endpoint acknowledged the request; it does not mean a person received, read, or acted on it. See [Contact, interface and delivery](#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance evidence:** At authorized provider edges return accepted, proven-unaccepted relay 429, HTTP 500, timeout and connection loss; restart during claims. Only the proven-unaccepted case requeues automatically; uncertain started sends never replay and acceptance remains distinct from receipt.

clauses.title: Public landing and documentation
clauses.text: At the app origin, `/` is the unauthenticated Lobby, `/docs` is public documentation, `/setup` is first-run setup, and the private operator console and editor are `/app` and `/app/monitor`; private documents require an owner session. The separate marketing site serves `https://run-uptime.com/` and `https://run-uptime.com/run`. The app Lobby at `/` and the marketing landing at the run-site `/` are distinct surfaces. **Acceptance evidence:** Open app-origin Lobby, docs and setup signed out, then sign in for /app and /app/monitor; separately read the marketing site and /run. Their routes remain distinct and private documents reject unsigned access.

clauses.title: Monitoring ownership and honest delivery claims
clauses.text: Uptime owns checks, evidence, routing, repeat reminders and monitoring reports. It feeds full paging and responder coordination to [Oncall](https://github.com/just-every/run-oncall), PagerDuty or Splunk On-Call, and public incidents, branded pages and subscriber updates to [Lamp](https://github.com/just-every/run-lamp) or Atlassian Statuspage. Teams, Discord, Telegram, SMS, voice and push are supported target channels under the clauses below. One network label is one vantage; provider acknowledgment never proves human receipt or response. Geographic placement, browser execution and accessibility require their own measured evidence. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure an alert and a sibling handoff, inspect acknowledged/received/responded as separate facts and simulate lost probes/providers; no duplicate network labels, acknowledgment or missing evidence becomes a delivery or availability guarantee.

clauses.title: Recipient-reported alert drills
clauses.text: An owner can run an alert drill on one destination: the existing test event with drill wording, sent once through the same path with no automatic resend, plus a one-time confirmation link (random capability, stored only as a bound hash, single use, 24-hour expiry, one drill and one destination). Opening the link shows a page; only a same-origin POST confirms, and unknown, used, expired and foreign links answer 404 alike. The console keeps Submitted, Acknowledged (or Uncertain/Failed with its code) and Recipient confirmed as separate lines, and does not measure whether anyone acted. A confirmed drill is a report by the recipient that one message reached a person at one time. It is never evidence of monitoring, a delivery guarantee or a human response, and it changes no monitor evidence, state or incident. Proof belongs to the destination's current credential: a new address or URL or a rotated secret makes it Never proven, and drill history stays with the installation, so a restored destination is Never proven. See [Alert drills](#alert-drills). **Acceptance evidence:** Drill email, Slack and signed webhook through the actual delivery runtime: GET/HEAD never confirm, same-origin POST confirms once, expired/replayed/foreign links refuse, 500 stays uncertain, rotation resets proof and archives/logs contain no capability or endpoint secret.

clauses.title: Required configuration diagnostics
clauses.text: A shared configuration table validates required and conditional bindings for the Worker, scheduled entry point, local app, preview, setup, deployment and private runner before each begins work. Missing or malformed required values stop the entry point and name the variable without printing its value; a Worker configuration failure returns 503, including at `/health`. Hosted mode requires the selected Base mail provider and its sender configuration. See [Configuration diagnostics](#configuration-diagnostics). **Acceptance evidence:** Start each runtime entry point with required and conditional bindings missing/malformed; diagnostics name bindings without values and health returns 503. Restore settings and recover; exercise D1/ASSETS faults inside the owner-approved three-second readiness response budget.

clauses.title: Declared sessionless paths and rate limits
clauses.text: Every sessionless route and emitted static path is declared in `seed.json` with its authentication rule and rate-limit class. D1 applies owner-tunable per-client limits in fixed 60-second windows and returns 429 with `Retry-After` after the class limit. A declaration does not bypass route-specific session, runner, heartbeat or development-key checks. Limit values are marked estimated and not load-tested. See [Public paths and rate limits](#public-paths-and-rate-limits) and [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance evidence:** Enumerate declared sessionless paths against emitted routes, exceed configured public limits, inspect Retry-After, and remove counter storage; each route retains its own authentication checks and admission fails closed.

clauses.title: Supported isolated browser transactions
clauses.text: Login, signup and checkout are supported monitored customer paths with explicit intended outcomes, immutable revisions, safe synthetic accounts and scheduled consensus. A constrained editor and isolated Playwright execution share the same evidence and authority rules. Every required outcome must pass; missing browser/credentials is Unknown. Per-run process/profile isolation, sanitized environment, network filtering, hard time/byte limits and credential-origin binding apply to all scripts. Human approval is required for effects beyond an explicitly authorized synthetic transaction. A changed-definition recovery is labeled and never presented as proof of the original outcome. Support qualification covers independently placed real-browser vantages and the complete login, signup and sandbox checkout outcomes. Reusable scripts and fixtures are required under FLOW-002, failure artifacts under FLOW-003, browser/device coverage under FLOW-004, and setup/teardown and effects grants under API-004; secret-bearing grants require ACCESS-003 second-factor step-up, and reports spanning migrated history require HISTORY-001 source segments. FLOW-001 is done only when its own acceptance and each of these dependent clauses are done. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure supported login, signup and sandbox checkout journeys, run independent real-browser vantages, break required outcomes and recover through signed results. Wrong credentials, missing elements, server errors, slow pages, private redirects/subresources, extra origins and absent browsers have distinct retained outcomes; weakened definitions cannot silently clear the original incident.

nonGoals: Real provider or production target actions before explicit authority and verification
Public communication, people paging, and independent geographic monitoring
Fresh-account hosted operation and recipient acceptance remain unverified

externals.name: cloudflare
externals.reason: An owner-directed deployment sends the application, migrations, configured Worker bindings and secrets, resource settings, and health requests to the owner's Cloudflare account; Cloudflare hosts the Worker, D1 database, and scheduled Cron.
data: Cloudflare API account and resource identities, deployment-token authorization, the Worker program and static assets, D1 schema and migrations, Cron settings, bindings, and configured deployment secret values
Deployment readiness requests and responses for the hosted Worker

Hosted Worker requests and responses carrying monitor definitions and target URLs, observations, owner identities and sessions, authentication mail state, notification events and delivery state, runner contact, and audit records
Product and installation records stored in the owner's Cloudflare D1 database, scheduled execution metadata, and configured secret bindings

externals.name: sendgrid-mail
externals.reason: SendGrid sends hosted sign-in, incident email and monitoring watch mail when selected as the Base mail adapter.
data: SendGrid API-key authorization, sender and recipient/operator email addresses, message subject and text/HTML body, and single-use sign-in links
Delivery ID in the rer_delivery_id custom argument; click, open and analytics tracking are disabled in the submitted provider settings
Incident/test title, target URL, state, monitor and incident identity when present, probe names/outcomes/reasons, explanation, observation time, and private console URL as rendered in message content
For an owner-run drill, the one-time recipient confirmation link and drill time
Owner stale-runner identity/network-label notice or all-healthy digest text, including any monitoring-configuration warning

externals.name: incident-webhook
externals.reason: Owner-configured webhook (custom-webhook) sends to custom destination owner-configured-json-receiver: deliver scheduled incident events to the owner's public HTTPS endpoint. The endpoint runs outside this installation.
data: The configured public HTTPS endpoint receives the selected GET, POST, PUT or PATCH request with JSON, form or query parameters, configured local custom header values, optional signature/timestamp headers, source address and delivery time
Event ID, type, incident key, monitor ID and revision, name, target URL, scheduled slot, state, observation time, probe outcomes and reasons, explanation, and private console URL

Versioned custom templates may send the documented monitor, incident, location, timing, certificate/domain expiry and heartbeat facts, including owner-zone times. Custom header values and signing keys stay encrypted locally and are excluded from lists and archives. Only an explicit owner request preview shows the receiver URL; its header secrets and signatures are masked.
A drill event additionally carries the one-time recipient confirmation URL, start time, and expiry; ordinary incident and test events do not
The endpoint's bounded HTTP status, headers and response body return to the dispatcher; the owner sees status and an escaped, secret-scrubbed excerpt of at most 512 characters

externals.name: slack-incoming-webhook
externals.reason: Slack (slack) sends to provider destination slack-incoming-webhook: post escaped notification content to the owner's incoming webhook. Slack runs outside this installation and accepts the configured remote request.
data: The configured Slack webhook receives the escaped message body, source address, and delivery time
Incident title and state, monitor identity and target URL, probe outcomes and reasons, explanation, observation time, and console URL
A drill message additionally carries the one-time recipient confirmation URL and drill time
The endpoint's bounded HTTP status, headers, and response body return to the runner for delivery classification

externals.name: external-heartbeat
externals.reason: Owner-selected independent HTTPS heartbeat service; optional empty GET while self-check passes. The configured URL is a capability and its path is sent to that service.
data: HTTPS host and capability path from the owner-configured URL, request time, and source network address; no request body or product record
The heartbeat service's response status is read and its response body is canceled rather than retained

externals.name: runner-watch
externals.reason: Independent webhook or Slack notice configured only in the runner environment.
data: Owner-configured webhook receives only unreachable/restored state and times; owner-configured Slack receives the same short notice text
Notification URL capability, runner source address, and request time; no monitor name, target URL, probe result, or product event
The destination's bounded status, response headers, and response body are read for transport classification

externals.name: owner-app-readiness
externals.reason: The local setup/dev/preview lifecycle checks the selected Uptime application readiness endpoint; it may be local loopback or an owner-selected remote origin.
data: A GET request for the selected application's readiness URL and any HTTP redirect destinations followed by the CLI; no request body or configured authorization header is sent
The destination sees the CLI source address and request timing; the CLI reads only the returned health status and JSON readiness value

externals.name: configured-dns-resolver
externals.reason: Private runners and owner tools use their configured DNS resolver. Hosted public checks validate A/AAAA answers through Cloudflare DNS over HTTPS; Workers fetch uses Cloudflare’s public Internet resolver and transport.
data: Queried hostnames for A/AAAA or system address lookup, resolver source address, and lookup timing; DNS carries no URL path, request body, or HTTP credential
Hosted checks send the target and canary hostnames as A/AAAA queries to https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query; no target URL path, body or credential is included.

externals.name: public-monitor-targets
externals.reason: The hosted Worker or an explicitly assigned private runner sends scheduled requests to the owner’s public target and optional canary URLs. A private runner also acquires or refreshes OAuth tokens only at the exact public HTTPS token URL authorized in that monitor's local credential file.
data: Target hostname, path and query, method, request time and runner source address; configured headers and request body where the monitor has them

Owner-held Basic, bearer or Digest credentials, generated JWT authorization and configured headers/body are sent only to the exact authorized target origin and monitor; a configured client TLS certificate and proof of key possession may be sent there, while its private key remains local. Credentials, custom headers, body and client certificate are permanently stripped on a cross-origin redirect

Owner-authorized OAuth token acquisition and refresh send a form-encoded HTTPS POST to the exact public token URL: client ID and secret through the declared Basic or form authentication mode, grant type, requested scopes and the refresh token when applicable. Public DNS answers are validated and pinned; token redirects and target TLS trust exceptions are refused. Acquired access and rotated refresh tokens remain in owner-only runner-local state, outside observations, logs and product archives
The target returns status and headers plus a bounded response body used for assertions; raw response bodies are not retained in observations
An external canary is a status-only GET: it sends no request credential, custom header or body and reads zero response-body bytes; validated public redirect hops may also be contacted

Failing HTTP response excerpts are redacted before storage in a separate owner-only snapshot table; default retention is 90 days, configurable from 1 to 365 days. Body text is escaped in the console; no screenshot or script execution is enabled. Canary response bodies remain unread.

externals.name: public-protocol-targets
externals.reason: The hosted Worker or an assigned private runner opens a connection to the owner's public host and port to check that it accepts connections, its banner or its certificate.
data: Target host name, port, the validated public address connected to, connection time and the vantage's source address
A TCP check sends no data; with banner reading on, it reads at most 512 bytes the service sends first and keeps at most 256 printable characters

A TLS check sends a TLS ClientHello naming the host (SNI); the Worker reads the certificate chain from a TLS 1.2 handshake it does not complete and then makes one verified connection without sending application data; certificate subject, issuer, names, validity and SHA-256 fingerprint are retained
Private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses are refused before connecting; the Worker also refuses Cloudflare addresses, which its sockets cannot reach, and reports that vantage Unknown

externals.name: dns-over-https-resolvers
externals.reason: DNS monitors ask the owner-selected public resolvers (Cloudflare at cloudflare-dns.com, Google at dns.google) over HTTPS; the Worker also resolves TCP, TLS and registry hosts through Cloudflare before connecting.
data: The queried name and record type, request time and the vantage's source address
The resolver returns its answer code and records; at most ten normalised records of at most 255 characters per resolver and the response time are retained

externals.name: rdap-registries
externals.reason: Domain monitors read IANA's RDAP bootstrap (data.iana.org), the domain's registry RDAP service it names and the registrar RDAP record the registry links, over HTTPS only.
data: The monitored domain name, request time and the vantage's source address

Registry and registrar answers are read up to 64 KiB (the bootstrap up to 256 KiB); retained are each source URL and update time, the expiry date, registry status values and whether the date is redacted or the sources conflict

externals.name: site-discovery
externals.reason: The runner performs bounded read-only discovery of the owner's chosen site, following its public redirects and crawling permitted pages and related API/status hosts.
data: The owner-selected URL, request host/path/query, GET or HEAD method, discovery User-Agent and other headers, request time, and runner source address

The initial URL's public redirect chain, then robots files, pages, JSON/spec documents and redirect destinations on its permitted registrable domains and linked status hosts are read with bounded bodies in runner memory

Only the input/final URL, contacted hostnames, request count and duration, short notes, and validated proposed monitor definitions return to the console; raw target HTML, JSON and response headers are not returned, stored, logged, or rendered as console HTML

externals.name: isolated-browser-flow-targets
externals.reason: A fresh runner browser follows owner-defined flows through the filtering proxy; target pages and their public network dependencies receive ordinary browser requests.
data: Owner-defined top-level URLs and paths, redirects that remain within the declared origins, and requests to public subresources and WebSocket destinations initiated by those pages; DNS names, source address, and request timing are visible at the relevant destinations

Browser-generated request headers, referrer/origin information, and cookies a destination sets may be sent to the relevant public destination; page content is processed locally in the runner to execute steps, while no raw page body or screenshot returns in the control-plane result or observation

A named owner-held flow credential is filled only at its exact configured origin and may be sent by that site-form submission; the secret itself remains in runner-local custody and is redacted from traces

Private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses are blocked; top-level navigation is limited to declared origins, while public subresources and WebSockets are individually passed through the filtering proxy

externals.name: runner-control-plane
externals.reason: The separately operated runner uses signed HTTPS requests to the configured Uptime Worker control plane for enrolment, claims, results, discovery, notification custody, and contact.
data: Runner key authentication and signature, runner identity, declared network label, browser capability, request times, and claimed task identifiers
Assigned monitor and flow definitions, canary URLs, retry and lease data, and signed attempt evidence, including status, assertions, timings, and bounded flow trace
Discovery input URLs and derived host/proposal results

For notification delivery, the claimed endpoint URL, signing credential and event payload are returned to the runner for the one configured send; signed outcome and bounded provider response details return to the Worker

Redacted HTTP failure snapshots (16 KiB text, optional 64 KiB PNG, 120 KiB total) carry final request details, owner-approved safe header/email exceptions, measured phases and bounded diagnostics under the signed envelope. Opt-in isolated screenshots render the already received excerpt after inert parsing/redaction, without fetching any target or subresource; scripts, styling and media are removed. Generated PNGs are authenticated-encrypted at rest, read only by owners and explicitly granted per-monitor evidence viewers, portable as redacted archive data, and subject to snapshot retention and erasure. Masks and access grants stay installation-local. Alerts carry no artifact content.

externals.name: optional-identity-provider-setup
externals.reason: The shared setup CLI can read selected provider discovery documents. The completed local probe read dependency metadata, then failed at unmounted application dependency approval (404) before owner creation or any provider link request. Uptime does not mount linked-provider routes; runtime OIDC callback, token, JWKS and dependency exchange are unsupported.
data: Selected issuer hostname and read-only setup requests for its OIDC configuration, RER provider document, and dependency-interface metadata

A setup approval request to the Uptime origin carries issuer/interface and the configured setup token; the current unmounted route returns 404 before owner creation. The measured probe made no one-time provider link request. A future shared linking path may send app origin, interface and a temporary link capability, requiring separate adoption and evidence.

No linked sign-in, authorization-code callback, runtime token/JWKS exchange or user-profile exchange is implemented by the current Uptime server; do not infer an operational provider integration from the optional declaration

externals.name: optional-management-editor
externals.reason: An authenticated owner page may create the configured management editor iframe while the editor is hidden. This is an explicit private management integration, not a public embeddable widget. This is the explicit BASE-DATA-005 exception: the configured origin may belong to the author and receive opted-in requests; the native product has no operational dependency on this integration.
data: The exact configured management origin receives an iframe request containing the installation ID, parent page origin, and editor surface; after handshake it also receives the current page path

Rendered page title and up to 60 visible text/element descriptors are sent only after the owner opens the editor and explicitly enables context sharing; form values and private-marked elements are excluded
Editor protocol messages, live-edit requests and results are exchanged with the configured management origin

externals.name: resend-mail
externals.reason: Resend sends hosted sign-in, incident email and monitoring watch mail when selected as the Base mail adapter.
data: Resend API-key authorization, sender and recipient/operator email addresses, message subject and text/HTML body, and single-use sign-in links
Delivery ID in the Idempotency-Key request header
Incident/test title, target URL, state, monitor and incident identity when present, probe names/outcomes/reasons, explanation, observation time, and private console URL as rendered in message content
For an owner-run drill, the one-time recipient confirmation link and drill time
Owner stale-runner identity/network-label notice or all-healthy digest text, including any monitoring-configuration warning

externals.name: cloudflare-mail
externals.reason: Cloudflare Email Sending sends hosted sign-in, incident email and monitoring watch mail when selected as the Base mail adapter.
data: Cloudflare API-key authorization and configured account identity, sender and recipient/operator email addresses, message subject and text/HTML body, and single-use sign-in links
Account-scoped email-sending API request with no Uptime attachment payload
Incident/test title, target URL, state, monitor and incident identity when present, probe names/outcomes/reasons, explanation, observation time, and private console URL as rendered in message content
For an owner-run drill, the one-time recipient confirmation link and drill time
Owner stale-runner identity/network-label notice or all-healthy digest text, including any monitoring-configuration warning

externals.name: public-udp-targets
externals.reason: A pinned UDP socket sends one owner-configured packet and reads one bounded response; all resolved addresses must be public.
data: Target hostname, port, source address and request timing
Owner-configured request payload (at most 256 bytes); response at most 1024 bytes
Response bytes retained as hexadecimal in authenticated immutable evidence, archives and monitor erasure; never put secrets in UDP payloads

externals.name: authorized-private-targets
externals.reason: Private HTTP, TCP and isolated browser checks pin only RFC1918 or ULA addresses authorized by exact hostname, CIDR, port and expiry. Metadata and management targets remain forbidden.
data: Configured request paths, headers, bodies and origin-bound credentials reach only approved private targets; redirects and browser dependencies recheck the grant before connecting

Private target address, bounded assertion facts and sanitized browser trace return as signed evidence to the configured control plane; retained definitions/evidence travel in owner archives and are erased with the monitor
Grant files and credentials stay runner-local and never travel in archives; restored or imported references do not authorize execution

externals.name: icmp-targets
externals.reason: The private runner sends one to five bounded ICMP echo packets to the validated numeric IPv4 or IPv6 target. Each location requires system ping permission; no HTTP substitute is used.
data: Target IP address, source runner address, bounded echo packets and round-trip timing
Only sent/received counts, loss and minimum/mean/maximum RTT are retained in immutable observations; no raw packet capture. Evidence travels in inactive archives and is erased with its monitor.

externals.name: metrics-export
externals.reason: One-shot metrics export from the same captured report window; no automatic scheduler or retries. Datadog sites are fixed and webhook DNS is validated and pinned.
data: Bounded monitor/probe/runner identifiers, report window, availability and latency statistics, states, contact/evidence freshness, incident counts and delivery job counts
Datadog API key only to the selected official Datadog HTTPS API; HMAC signature to the owner-selected public webhook. Credentials are process environment values and never stored or archived.
No monitor names, target URLs, response bodies, provider credentials or Datadog-managed probe identities. The receiver owns its stored metrics; local erasure cannot recall exported data.

externals.name: bounded-route-diagnostics
externals.reason: Five numeric traceroute probes at most, using only the already validated public target address; no name lookup, request credentials or body. Private destinations and unsupported tools report unavailable.
data: Target numeric address and probe source address, TTL and round-trip timing visible to the target and intermediate routers

Only bounded numeric hops, one-sample packet loss, phase timings and fixed unavailable codes return in the signed failure snapshot; same retention, authenticated access, archive and erasure as that snapshot

externals.name: api-transaction-targets
externals.reason: The runner performs the owner-configured ordered requests and cleanup against one exact public origin using monitor-bound local authentication and in-memory extracted values.
data: Public target host, pinned address, source address, request timing, configured methods, paths, headers and bodies; runtime extracted values may be sent to later requests on that same origin
Local authentication is authorized for the monitor and exact origin; dynamic authentication headers require HTTPS and values extracted by earlier steps
Only fixed outcome reasons, HTTP status, per-step timing and cleanup outcomes are retained; request/response content and extracted values never enter observations or archives

externals.name: mail-protocol-targets
externals.reason: The runner opens pinned public mail-protocol connections, verifies TLS and optionally authenticates and sends one synthetic message to an explicitly dedicated test mailbox.
data: Mail server host, port, public pinned address, TLS SNI, source address and connection timing
Monitor-bound runner-local username/password sent only after verified TLS; protocol commands and optional synthetic sender, recipient, Message-ID and fixed synthetic message
Optional receiving mailbox authentication, Message-ID search and exact-message removal; no mailbox content, password, authentication exchange or server greeting is retained

Observations retain protocol step outcomes/timing, synthetic Message-ID, SMTP acceptance, mailbox receipt and cleanup confirmation; an unobserved late message needs owner attention in the dedicated mailbox

spine.record: Immutable scheduled slot observations and explained private alert outbox

limits.notes: Owner-tunable source settings; each class shares one fixed 60-second D1 window per client. Production assets retain their own budget. Local Vite compiler assets use a separate budget for the unbundled browser graph: about 140 module requests per console load, with room for twelve loads per minute. These defaults are estimated, not load tested. Hosted CF-Connecting-IP must be a valid single IP; missing/malformed values share an unknown-client bucket. Local mode ignores all forwarding headers and uses one loopback bucket. Only keyed hashes of client identities are stored.

releaseProvenance.note: Local tag and export; no push, deployment or visibility change.

sitePresentation.reason: Publish the product screenshot named in RELEASE.json and committed with this exact release; preserve the signed publisher manifest and documents unchanged.

clauseSummaries.text: Versioned monitor definition files are previewed without writes and validated with the editor’s rules. Applying a matching plan creates paused monitors or new revisions that preserve existing enablement, maintenance and runner assignments. Files carry no request secrets or installation authority and cannot enable monitors, issue heartbeat tokens or change notification destinations. Batch undo preserves history and reports revision conflicts. No real third-party export or hosted import has been measured.
clauseSummaries.reason: Describe the reviewed definition-file workflow without claiming support proven against real data from a named product. No verified real-data importer record is available. The exact publisher clause remains in the signed manifest and CONTRACT.md.

original.title: Reviewed definition files and inactive imports
original.text: A versioned definition file (2 MiB, 500 monitors, UTF-8 JSON, editor fields only, no request secrets or installation authority) or saved UptimeRobot v3 monitor pages are previewed without writes as create, unchanged, change, refused or unsupported per entry with a plan digest, validated by the editor's own validation; apply refuses a digest that no longer matches and otherwise writes the whole plan in one transaction as new paused monitors or new revisions that keep enabled, maintenance and runner assignments; nothing in a file enables a monitor, issues a heartbeat token, schedules a notification or touches a destination. Each apply is a batch; undo pauses what it created and restores what it changed while their revisions are unchanged, reports the rest and never removes history. Batches travel in archives as restored history without authority. Through this definition-file door a log export is recognized and counted only. Storing it as labeled source history for reports is HISTORY-001's migration import, and no imported history ever becomes evidence. Unmeasured: no real UptimeRobot export and no hosted run. See [Definition files and imports](#definition-files-and-imports). **Acceptance evidence:** Preview, apply, export and undo definition JSON and saved UptimeRobot pages through the owner routes and CLI. Malformed/hostile/secret-bearing inputs and stale digests write nothing; creations stay paused, changes keep operational state, unsupported fields are named and history is never made current evidence.
