seeds.name: Oncall
seeds.oneLiner: Coordinate incident response and on-call schedules alongside your existing pager.
seeds.summary: Coordinate incident response and on-call schedules alongside your existing pager.

clauses.title: Event identity and alerts
clauses.text: Persist accepted events separately from alerts and human incidents. Repeated source event IDs return the original receipt; changed bytes with the same identity conflict. A deduplication key groups active alerts only within its source/service/environment; recovery affects the matching alert and never resolves an incident. **Acceptance evidence:** POST signed and bearer events through /api/ingress/:source; repeat a normalized identity, conflict changed content, send recovery before trigger and after a newer generation, and inspect protected state. Verify grouping across multiple sources without merging service/environment boundaries. **Status:** partial

clauses.title: Routing replay
clauses.text: Retain routing policy version and explanation at admission. Replay is read-only, returns ordered decisions, and produces no alert, incident or external effect. Unmatched signals remain visible and unowned; suppression reasons remain inspectable. **Acceptance evidence:** Admit a severity-routed event, change policy, POST /api/replay and compare the immutable admission explanation with the proposed decision in submitted order; compare state before/after for zero writes.

clauses.title: Roles and authority
clauses.text: Incident changes require an active authorized session. Viewer reads; responder coordinates; admin manages services/policies/members/import. Ingest credentials grant no read or human authority. Bearer and signed intake return only `duplicate`, stored event `id`, source `eventId`, `service`, `observedAt` and `acceptedAt` (201 accepted; 200 deduplicated). Routing decisions, snapshots and alert identities stay behind session-protected read/export doors. Revocation takes effect on the next request. Every mutation enforces current authority server-side. The stakeholder role that reads only business-service status and approved updates is specified and tracked in OC-061. **Acceptance evidence:** Use anonymous, expired, revoked, viewer, responder and admin sessions on reads, commands, sources and archives; revoke or downgrade while a real HTTP mutation is incomplete and prove no publication. Verify minimal intake receipts disclose no private routing data.

clauses.title: Incident state transitions
clauses.text: Incident state transitions are explicit. Acknowledgment assigns responsibility. Resolution requires recovery evidence and a summary, independently of alert recovery. Optimistic revision checks reject stale edits. All accepted changes append an attributed timeline transactionally with state. This resolution rule governs declared incidents; an alert-only page that its source recovers closes without a human summary under OC-056. **Acceptance evidence:** Declare from admitted alerts, acknowledge, reject stale concurrent changes, clear the source alert, refuse resolution without evidence and summary, then resolve and inspect the attributed timeline over HTTP.

clauses.title: Copied runbooks
clauses.text: Runbooks are copied into the incident at declaration; future service edits never silently rewrite incident instructions. Follow-ups carry owner, due date, open/completed state and completion evidence. Resolved incidents retain open work and editable review. **Acceptance evidence:** Declare an incident, edit its service runbook and confirm the copied incident steps remain unchanged; create an owned due-dated action, require completion evidence and retain unfinished work and review after resolution.

clauses.title: No outbound incident effects
clauses.text: No paging provider notification, AI call, production action or Lamp publication occurs in release 1. Configured remote mail sends sign-in links only. Handoffs are minimum summaries with stable identity and visibility; exported draft is explicitly unreviewed. Source links grant no access. External acceptance/delivery/acknowledgment are distinct later records. **Acceptance evidence:** Use coordination and handoff preparation/export on a normal installation; prove no paging receipt, production action, AI call or external publication occurs. Confirm draft exports remain unreviewed and source links confer no access.

clauses.title: Native archive
clauses.text: Native archive preserves services, policies, incident/alert/event/timeline identity and attribution, runbook and follow-up history. Validate schema and references before atomic restore. Invalid restore preserves existing data. Do not export authentication secrets/sessions. Released migrations remain immutable; verify prior-data transitions. **Acceptance evidence:** Export through /api/archive; restore valid held records and reject malformed references/storage failures without losing prior data. Inspect event, incident, runbook, action, timeline and attribution identity and confirm authentication material is absent.

clauses.title: User-authored records kept
clauses.text: No automatic deletion of user-authored incident records. Owner export/restore is supported. Ingress accepts bounded structured fields, no arbitrary raw body storage; native Events API request bytes max 64 KiB. Incumbent-compatible endpoints and provider adapters use the larger per-provider bounds of OC-059. No arbitrary remote fetching or runbook execution. Display user content as text, never HTML. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit over-limit and malformed intake, hostile structured text and runbook links; verify bounded refusal, literal display with no script execution/fetch, and preservation of authored history after restart/export.

clauses.title: Accessible interface
clauses.text: Keyboard-complete responsive UI, labeled fields, focus-visible controls, status announcements, readable failure states and contrast. The conformance bar is WCAG 2.2 Level AA for every web surface and, for the OC-029 apps, the same success criteria as they apply to native iOS/Android plus Dynamic Type and Android font scaling to 200%. Named assistive-technology journeys are VoiceOver with Safari on macOS and NVDA with Chrome on Windows for web, and VoiceOver on iOS and TalkBack on Android for the apps; each completes sign-in, finding an incident in the filtered list (OC-060), acknowledge, snooze, reassign, schedule view and override. Each release publishes a conformance report (VPAT 2.5 Accessibility Conformance Report, WCAG 2.2 edition) stating the result per success criterion and per surface; an unsupported criterion is named, never omitted. A failed write is visible and never shown as saved. UI unavailable must not be described as pager coverage failure because stage 1 supplies no pager. **Acceptance evidence:** At 1440 and 390, use keyboard-only declaration, acknowledgment, notes, schedules, overrides and preview; inspect focus/labels, status announcements, literal hostile HTML and a real stale-write failure with no saved claim. Run axe-core with the WCAG 2.2 A and AA rule sets on every surface at 1440 and 390 in light and dark themes and record zero violations; complete the named VoiceOver/Safari, NVDA/Chrome, iOS VoiceOver and Android TalkBack journeys for acknowledge, snooze, reassign and schedule view with recorded outcomes; and publish the release's conformance report before any new target surface ships.

clauses.title: Health and honest commands
clauses.text: Health checks storage and identifies the deployed version, operating commands describe actual local and hosted effects, and acceptance records distinguish local evidence from remote/provider/pilot outcomes. Capacity promises require measured evidence. **Acceptance evidence:** Run check/describe and /health with storage available and unavailable; compare deployed identity to the actual build. Record local, hosted, provider and human-drill outcomes separately and test durable failure diagnostics for each new execution class. **Status:** done **Implementation evidence:** `src/api.ts`; `src/base/deployment-health.ts`; `OPERATIONS.json`; `tests/runtime.mjs`; `tests/coordination-health.mjs`; `tests/hosted.mjs`; `tests/transfer.mjs`. **OC-010 coordination health, deployment identity and honest command effects survive storage failure** checks the emitted build identity, real database loss (503 with the same identity and no success), recovery with unchanged records, and read-only check/describe through the pinned executable. Hosted-mode production serving checks its supplied source/fingerprint/version separately from the one-time real Cloudflare release evidence in ACCEPTANCE.md. Command declarations distinguish local setup/dev/reset/transfer, provider deployment/removal and dry-run provider reads without writes. No pager health, independent availability, measured capacity or human-drill outcome is claimed. OC-026/027/028/029 inherit pager/timer/mobile/standby health; OC-064 owns paging measurements. Every new execution class under OC-030–035, OC-039, OC-045–048, OC-051, OC-053–054, OC-056–058 and OC-063–072 inherits durable failure diagnostics before shipping.

clauses.title: Calendar-day rotations
clauses.text: Named-zone calendar-day rotations retain fixed primary/backup member slots. Hand-offs use the wall minute plus integer civil days, not fixed elapsed seconds. Repeated minutes explicitly choose earlier, later or reject; nonexistent/rejected boundaries produce visible gaps. Override intervals include their start and exclude their end; overlap in the same role is rejected. Inactive/viewer/missing members do not shift slots. A duplicated primary/backup assignment leaves backup unavailable. **Acceptance evidence:** Save primary/backup schedules and query HTTP preview across spring/fall DST, ambiguous/nonexistent minutes, override edges and overlap refusal; retain inactive/viewer/missing slots as gaps and detect duplicate primary/backup responders.

clauses.title: Paging off
clauses.text: Production paging is OFF. Every normal-installation delivery attempt refuses with an explanation that an independent standby and real-phone drill are required. No production paging provider sends, synthetic delivery proof, cron delivery, SMS, voice or push are performed. Existing pager is authoritative. Escalation policies are inspectable configuration data, not active timers. A labeled demo simulation is not production delivery or acceptance. **Acceptance evidence:** On a normal installation POST each delivery/job/tick/callback/resume door and confirm paging-OFF refusal with no receipt. Treat demo simulations as simulations. Native cutover additionally requires OC-026–029 and OC-038 real-phone/provider-failure acceptance.

clauses.title: Held history stays historical
clauses.text: Held synthetic job/receipt/callback identities remain historical data. Restore pauses pending jobs. Historical acknowledgment and explicit cancellation retain attribution; resume and new timer starts refuse while paging is OFF. An acknowledgment never proves recovery. **Acceptance evidence:** Restore held synthetic jobs/receipts/callbacks, observe pending work paused, acknowledge or cancel with attribution, reject resume, and verify incident recovery remains unchanged.

clauses.title: Side-effect-free previews
clauses.text: Schedule preview, now/next and replay are side-effect-free; actual historical delivery claims remain labeled synthetic. Nothing in this release certifies production delivery. **Acceptance evidence:** Read now/next and schedule/routing previews, compare durable state and receipt counts, and confirm no timers or provider actions were created and historical synthetic data stays labeled.

clauses.title: Strict module archives
clauses.text: Strict module archive validation and atomic replacement remain supported. Imported pending historical jobs pause. Scope and local capacity limits remain explicit. **Acceptance evidence:** Round-trip the strict module archive through protected HTTP; reject unknown fields, broken references and injected SQL failure atomically, retain callbacks and pause pending historical jobs.

clauses.title: Recovery checkpoint
clauses.text: A paired recovery checkpoint captures coordination and scheduling records with both revisions in one consistent storage snapshot, excludes authentication, and validates its envelope and intrinsic record integrity. Explicit current-admin restore replaces both datasets atomically, pauses imported pending jobs, preserves the current-password mapping rule and revokes prior authority exactly as coordination restore does. Missing references in retained paused/finished history remain evidence, never dispatch authority; missing references for pending jobs are invalid. Invalid input, capacity failures, storage failure or losing concurrent writes preserve the previous complete state and cannot revoke a winning restore's new session. Verify the actual emitted Worker/D1 and private local CLI workflow before claiming this target implemented. **Acceptance evidence:** Use /api/recovery/checkpoint and the private CLI to capture and restore both revisions; exercise malformed/capacity/storage failures and competing writes, identity mapping, orphan history and session revocation without revoking the winning restore session.

clauses.title: Reviewed handoffs
clauses.text: Persist explicitly authored, unsent handoff copy with an explicit intended audience, immutable incident/service snapshots and canonical content hashes. Preparation and review actions have stable identities that conflict on changed content. Only current active responders/admins prepare, review or withdraw; viewers inspect permitted internal records and admins restore. A review binds exact copy and source versions, becomes ineligible on source drift or a recovery hold, and never grants sending, publication, recovery verification or independent-review authority. Withdrawal is terminal and preserves attributed append-only history. Keep OC-006 and historical unreviewed envelopes unchanged. Use separate additive handoff storage/archive bounded to 64 records, 128 history entries per record, 128 KiB per record and 1 MiB aggregate. Explicit checkpoint version 2 includes handoffs; version 1 remains supported. Restore retains historical identities and holds active approvals atomically alongside existing recovery and credential/session safeguards. Invalid input, capacity/storage failure or losing concurrent writes preserve the complete prior state. HANDOFF-STAGE.md defines retained snapshots, eligibility and permissions; transfer proof exercises the protected HTTP review and restore flow. No provider send, remote fetch or Lamp publication is authorized. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare, review, inspect and export exact handoff copy over protected HTTP; change source/revision, withdraw, restore v1/v2 and race writes. Verify eligibility/holds, stable action identities, append-only attribution and all storage bounds with no send authority.

clauses.title: Maintained root commands
clauses.text: Maintained root seed commands use the pinned Base installer, owner identity, dev identity and theme. Ordinary email-link sign-in is kept and tested independently of dev identity. Setup creates no example incident or service. Release 1 supports hosted coordination beside the existing pager without an independent standby; portable SQL batch bindings are required. `rer deploy` verifies deployment identity, claims the configured owner automatically and retires the setup token. Hosted email-link sign-in requires a configured remote mail provider. Removal with the same Cloudflare credentials deletes only recorded deployment resources and verifies that they are gone. On local and hosted apps, the configured owner uses native email links, while admin-created team members use installation-local workspace names and passwords at `/signin/local`; no invitations are sent. Local dev identity never grants hosted access, and anonymous first-admin bootstrap at `/api/setup` remains loopback-only. **Acceptance evidence:** Exercise documented setup/dev/build/preview/reset/archive/deploy dry-run, owner entry and member password sign-in. Hosted acceptance must actually deploy, retire setup authority, use a real emailed owner link, coordinate with a member after reload, and remove recorded resources with empty provider readback.

clauses.title: Additive upgrade
clauses.text: The additive upgrade removes the one-row coordination store after migrating every entity and original array order to relational tables. Released migrations stay unchanged. Held passwords and identities are preserved. New Base identity cannot silently claim held coordination data. **Acceptance evidence:** Seed the held one-row SQL data, migrate, sign in with the held password and compare all entities, nested histories and original ordering through HTTP; repeat migration/restart without silent reassignment to Base identity.

clauses.title: Now/next and calendar feed
clauses.text: Now/next explains current coverage and each role's next effective hand-off. The private ICS feed uses the same resolved UTC boundaries including overrides/gaps and exports primary/backup separately. It requires a current session; default window is seven days, explicit windows are bounded to 31 elapsed days. Calendar downloads carry no public bearer access. Alert intake records immutable events with scoped source credentials; intake never starts paging. **Acceptance evidence:** Read now/next and authenticated ICS for seven-day default and bounded explicit windows; verify primary/backup UTC boundaries, overrides and gaps, deny unauthenticated access and confirm admission starts no paging.

clauses.title: Move-in preview
clauses.text: Opsgenie then PagerDuty file move-in uses Base import-kit D1. Preview writes zero rows. A current administrator must review the exact source fingerprint before applying. Users are matched by normalized email and grant no login rights; schedules and policy data stay paused. Original bytes, unmapped fields, rejected objects, journal and provenance are retained. Every unmappable rotation/rule is named; no partial rotation approximation is allowed. Missing detail exports reject. No account/API calls or routing credentials are activated. **Acceptance evidence:** Follow provider export instructions, preview saved Opsgenie and PagerDuty list/detail bundles with zero writes, inspect exact rejected/unmapped rules and fingerprints, apply paused and explicitly map people/services before adopting native coverage.

clauses.title: Resume and undo
clauses.text: Journaled imports support bounded resume after restart and explicit undo. SQL checks current actor/session/admin authority inside publication and reversal. Changed source identities conflict; duplicate unchanged sources are idempotent. Undo removes only unchanged attributed native objects; edits are preserved with an explicit conflict. Invalid input or failed publication leaves prior committed state unchanged; partial progress remains visible and resumable. **Acceptance evidence:** Apply, interrupt/restart, resume and undo both vendor imports over HTTP; revoke authority at publication, inject SQL failure, replay unchanged/changed identities and preserve native edits as named undo conflicts.
