seeds.name: Spool
seeds.oneLiner: Investigate application errors with grouped issues, source maps and evidence for reviewing fixes.
seeds.summary: Investigate application errors with grouped issues, source maps and evidence for reviewing fixes.
seeds.maturity: Local-first JavaScript, Python and Go evidence product with one owner and isolated projects; bounded native, Sentry and OTLP-log intake, private source maps, operator corrections, owner/project erasure, sandbox reproducer, granted GitHub fix branches and exposure measurement. Runtime checks and review evidence are recorded separately; source metadata does not establish hosted, provider or npm publication acceptance.

clauses.title: Bounded admission
clauses.text: Native version-1 JavaScript, Python and Go exception envelopes require active exact-project ingest credentials, registered release/build identity and bounded fields. Invalid, oversized, volume-limited and conflicting retries have explicit outcomes. Each project admits at most 120 outcomes a minute (`minute_budget`) and retains at most 10,000 events (`retained_event_budget`); over-limit intake returns 429 with `Retry-After` and a counted outcome. GOV-003 carries the target that replaces both limits with its named volume reasons and published sustained rate. Artifact URLs in envelopes are never fetched. Sentry error intake now implements SDK-009's default acceptance with no release or an automatically created release/dist; only its opt-in registered-sequence-only policy requires registration. Native version-1 intake keeps the registered release/build prerequisite. The broader SDK target is SDK-001. **Acceptance evidence:** Send valid, invalid, oversize, foreign-project and conflicting-retry envelopes through public ingest; inspect the outcome and unchanged rows for refusals. Exceed the per-minute and retained-event limits and confirm the explicit 429, `Retry-After` and counted reason, with no partial rows.

clauses.title: Atomic acceptance
clauses.text: Accepted means a sanitized occurrence, its group aggregate and its local new/regression alert commit atomically. Retry identity is project plus event ID and SHA-256 of canonical original accepted JSON before scrubbing: identical retry never increments, changed raw content conflicts even if its sanitized result matches. Raw bytes are not retained. Group algorithm version and basis remain inspectable. **Acceptance evidence:** Ingest an event twice, then change its raw secret under the same ID; inspect one occurrence and aggregate increment, one local alert and an explicit conflict without partial rows.

clauses.title: Scrub before storage
clauses.text: Apply the native allowlist, bounded text, query/fragment removal and sensitive-text scrubbing before persistence. Native envelopes contain no headers, cookies, request bodies or personal user identity; the `user` interface that unmodified Sentry SDKs send is governed by SDK-008's project identity policy instead. An optional random installation identifier supports bounded exposure measurement; it is never a name or address. Telemetry, source and notes are untrusted data and cannot authorize execution. The event fields SDK-010 keeps from unmodified Sentry SDKs (frame local variables, SDK-sent source context lines, exception values, tags, contexts, request, extra and thread stacks) pass through these scrubbers and SDK-003's server-side rules before storage, and default secret names are masked inside frame variables. Default protection persists when SDK-003 and CTX-002 introduce opt-in context; those captures require their own field policies and previews. Redaction does not promise removal of arbitrary semantic personal data. **Acceptance evidence:** Ingest privacy canaries and inspect stored events, issue views, packets, archives and delivery content; common secrets are removed while ordinary diagnostic content survives.

clauses.title: Separated authority
clauses.text: Every private API/document checks the current owner session or its exact ingest, deploy or read-only project grant itself. Cookie writes enforce same origin. Revocation and identity fencing take effect on the next request; confidential maps are never public. Ingest cannot read, deploy can only register releases/upload artifacts and record deployment starts/callbacks, and read-only agent grants cannot mutate. TEAM-001 extends this model to collaborative membership without broadening existing credentials. **Acceptance evidence:** Call each private transport anonymously and with wrong-scope, foreign-project, revoked and fenced grants; denied writes change no state, and direct map URLs reveal no private bytes.

clauses.title: Source map identity
clauses.text: Private flat Source Map V3 lookup matches project, release, build, debug ID and SHA-256 before presenting original coordinates. Missing, invalid or mismatched maps retain generated frames and a reason. Late uploads never rewrite immutable admission snapshots; current lookup is labeled separately. Lines are one-based, columns zero-based. A project stores at most 20 flat maps of 256 KiB; indexed (`sections`) maps are refused with a reason and `sourceRoot` is not applied. SRC-004 carries indexed maps, `sourceRoot`, published capacity and opt-in source fetching. Spool never fetches a remote URL. **Acceptance evidence:** Capture a minified second-origin exception before and after uploading the matching map; compare original coordinates, immutable admission diagnostics, mismatch refusal and confidential source exclusion from packets. Upload an indexed (`sections`) map and a 21st map in the same project and confirm each is refused with its reason. SDK-010 rich stacks retain up to 1,000 frames per exception, while current source-map lookup projects only 30 located coordinates; expanded mapped lookup is inherited by SRC-004 and this clause without discarding retained SDK stack evidence.

clauses.title: Audited triage and regression
clauses.text: Revision-checked open, acknowledged, resolved and suppressed changes are audited. An issue resolved in its current release reopens as a regression on a recurrence in a later release; delayed older-release events cannot invent one. For native version-1 events the order is the registered sequence, never guessed semver; Sentry events follow the project's stated rule in SDK-009, including releases later enriched by registration. SDK-009 implements resolve in the next or a named release and plain Resolve; TEAM-004 inherits resolution from a commit's release. Plain Resolve regresses on the next accepted event in any release. Recognized JavaScript bundle hash suffixes do not split grouping; native anchors and reported frames stay immutable. Corrections retain exact occurrence provenance and reversible fenced apply/undo. **Acceptance evidence:** Resolve a captured issue, admit its fingerprint in a newer and then older release, and inspect regression identity. Preview/apply/undo split and merge through owner HTTP/UI, reject stale revisions and inspect original membership.

clauses.title: Sanitized evidence packet
clauses.text: A compatible v1 packet exposes issue/lifecycle/grouping, retained release sequence and per-event release/build/environment, generated/original coordinates, immutable diagnostics beside current lookup, links and coded coverage gaps. UTF-8 JSON is bounded to 256 KiB and ten events, removing oldest events first and naming included/available counts even if none fit. It excludes source snippets, sourcesContent and artifact bytes. It carries the latest computed repair observation and newest three owner-recorded repairs, with omitted history named. CLI and stdio MCP keep exact-project read authority and untrusted/no-execution labels; they cause no model egress. **Acceptance evidence:** Read the same packet through HTTP, CLI and official MCP transport at size/retention/import/loss boundaries; compare projections and verify no secrets, source bytes, writes or cross-project reads.

clauses.title: Loss counters and repair observation
clauses.text: Expose windowed accepted/rejected/budget outcomes, SDK-reported discards by category and reason, and unknown pre-transport loss. Reported discarded errors are a loss input and prevent a quiet feed from proving a repair; other discarded categories do not imply lost errors. Only the owner records revision-checked repair links, scrubbed notes, checks, approval/merge/deploy facts and an exercised-flow record. Links are HTTPS origin/path text and never fetched. Manual repair writes send no notifications or external work. Compute recur/reasoned inconclusive/no-recurrence-after-exercise from stored release sequence, maps, events, exercise and loss; list older-release events separately. Missing exercise, capture, map, exposure or retention yields inconclusive. Never label a quiet feed fixed. AI-004 adds rate-based live proof. *Status:* done **Acceptance evidence:** Record a repair through owner HTTP, deny every project-grant write, then exercise deployed/no-events, healthy exercise, older-release event, loss and recurrence cases; inspect packet verdicts and absence of side effects from manual records.

clauses.title: Archive, restore and retention
clauses.text: Versioned private archives carry stored source bytes, checksums, migration identity, triage, maps, repairs/checks, operator corrections, reproduction/fix/exposure history, sanitized Sentry evidence, feedback, capture/grouping/release policies and erasure journal. Base owns staging, JSONL integrity, empty-target guards and atomic inactive restore; HTTP/CLI and legacy v1/v2 decoding share semantic validation. Run tokens, step leases, owner sessions, project grants, alert destination records/credentials and dispatch queues never travel; retained alert rules restore disabled and delivery history is historical. Older archives restore newly introduced collections empty under versioned rules. An archive holds at most 10,000 events and 20 artifacts per project and refuses more with `Archive event budget` or `Archive artifact budget`; GOV-003 carries streaming archives of any retained volume. Manual cutoff retention removes private derived content, keeps repair snapshots with coverage gaps and exposes the deduplication horizon. Imported history creates no active grant, dispatch or current repair proof. **Acceptance evidence:** Export a populated installation via browser and rer, restore into an independent empty destination, compare retained records and inspect inert work. Refuse tampered, conflicting and nonempty-target imports before mutation; retain repair gaps after cutoff.

clauses.title: Release gates
clauses.text: A release must exercise real capture, symbolication, privacy, permissions, persistence and independent restore through the shipped app. Fresh setup has no demo rows. Private flows are accessible and responsive with explicit empty, failure and unavailable states. Source presence, local providers or a green build cannot substitute for hosted, mobile, integration or real-account acceptance. UX-001 and each connector clause specify the expanded product gates. **Acceptance evidence:** Run the named implemented journeys on the emitted Worker, inspect 1440/390 end states, then qualify each supported runtime/device and configured real provider with a buyer-controlled account.

clauses.title: Base commands and native admission
clauses.text: The public rer command contract uses declared Node/pnpm pins and one setup manifest for terminal/browser. Setup claims or preserves the owner and private settings, stops its temporary app and leaves empty product data; rer dev uses real assets/HMR and private local identity. Local dev grants never authorize deployed entry. Reset is confirmed/contained and preserves source, exports and deployment receipts. Export/import share Base integrity and inactive empty-target restore. Deployment dry-run makes no provider request. Managed signed first-owner admission precedes auth dispatch; editor config independently checks the owner and has short expiry/exact-origin CSP. **Acceptance evidence:** Use public rer install/setup/dev/export/import/reset and deployment dry-run in a fresh checkout and independent destination; preserve existing setup, reject unsafe answer paths and reused managed claims, and deny anonymous/project-grant editor access.

clauses.title: Project and installation-owner erasure
clauses.text: The owner has count-only preview, typed confirmation bound to the exact current plan, resumable destructive steps and a completion receipt with per-table counts/times and no personal values. Project-root cascade, anonymized permanent audit, portability tombstones, source-import custody withdrawal, stale-write fences are preserved, and project erasure completes within five minutes for a project at today's 10,000-event admission limit. GOV-003 carries erasure within 15 minutes for 150,000 retained events. Owner self-erasure first transfers authority to a verified successor; it refuses unsupported/ambiguous attribution rather than damaging other people's data. All current declared tables and outbox copies participate; new capture stores must extend this declaration before release. **Acceptance evidence:** Run public setup/dev/HTTP/export/import erasure journeys with canaries in every declared store, count-only preview/receipt, wrong-scope/origin/stale denials, a 10,000-event project erased within 300 seconds, successor handoff, resumed partial erasure and same/fresh-destination old-archive fences.

nonGoals: Automatic hosted provisioning during local setup; actual owner-account deployment and mail sender acceptance require explicit owner action.
Sentry feature parity or a completed-migration claim; organization import has been exercised with synthetic fixtures only, and owner-export qualification is pending.
External paging, automatic retention, or guarantees of complete capture coverage.
Unbounded event payloads, remote artifact URL fetching, or execution of telemetry-provided instructions.
seeds.scope: One owner identity per installation with multiple isolated projects and project-scoped ingest and read grants.

spine.record: A sanitized JavaScript, Python or Go exception occurrence grouped into a project-scoped issue.

operatingCost.status: Unmeasured; owner-account deploy dry-run is implemented, but no live deployment or provider acceptance is claimed.

limits.status: Product bounds are implemented locally; representative capacity and large-instance economics are unmeasured.
limits.restoreSemantics: Native v1/v2 and Base portability JSONL restore into an empty domain database, preserve private maps and browser origins, and exclude owner/authentication state and credential grants. All formats validate domain integrity and per-project capacities. JSONL has per-line and per-part bounds, not a 16 MiB total archive or 10,000-row per-table limit.

accessibility.status: Automated axe and responsive checks cover bounded local operator states; full conformance is not claimed.
includes: Local owner and project workbench states

releaseProvenance.note: Local tag and export; no push, deployment or visibility change.

sitePresentation.reason: Publish the product screenshot named in RELEASE.json and committed with this exact release; preserve the signed publisher manifest and documents unchanged.

gallery.caption: Spool issue page at 1600 pixels: a TypeError issue with 85 retained occurrences, event search, status and resolution controls, and the evidence packet and capture receipts, from the product screenshot named in the v0.6.0 RELEASE.json, committed unchanged at the listed v0.6.0 revision.

seeds.name: Orbit
seeds.oneLiner: Turn customer activity into clear sales priorities and reviewed next steps.
seeds.summary: Turn customer activity into clear sales priorities and reviewed next steps.
seeds.maturity: complete-workflow-implementation; acceptance requires pinned runtime and native receipts

clauses.title: Equal operators
clauses.text: Every active full operator has equal access to the whole workspace: every record, field and action. An invited collaborator reaches only the records, fields and actions shared with them, and the server refuses the rest; a hidden control never stands in for that refusal. Restricted sellers, managers and analysts with role grants are TEAM-005. **Acceptance:** Sign in as two full operators and an invited collaborator; confirm both operators reach every record and action, and that the collaborator is refused records, fields and actions outside the share through UI and APIs.

clauses.title: Management
clauses.text: Any active full operator invites and removes operators in Settings. An invitation sends no email: the invited person requests their own sign-in link. Removing an operator revokes their sessions at once, and later sign-in requests for their address send no link. The setup owner can be removed only by themselves, and only while another active full operator exists. Invitations and removals are audited. Roles, teams and access review are TEAM-005; policy `operator.management.v1` may narrow who invites or removes without bypassing server-side checks. **Acceptance:** Invite an operator, sign in as them, remove them, and attempt a previously issued session and a new sign-in request; try to remove the setup owner as another operator and as the only operator.

clauses.title: One workspace
clauses.text: A deployment holds one business workspace. Its name, US operating timezone, USD default currency, working hours, stale and awaiting-response intervals, signal sources and free-mail domains are configured in Settings. Multiple sales pipelines are configured under OPP-009 inside that workspace; a second isolated deployment is a separate installation, not an extra pipeline. **Acceptance:** Complete first-run setup with US timezone and USD, change working hours and stale intervals, reload, and observe the persisted settings across records.

clauses.title: Removal handover
clauses.text: Removing an operator revokes their sessions, cancels their scheduled messages, and hands over or unassigns their open opportunities, open sales tasks and delegated handoffs. The removal review lists each of those sets, the remover chooses a receiving full operator or explicit unassignment for each, and the removal is refused until every set has a recorded choice or if the reviewed work changed meanwhile; revocation, cancellation and handover then happen together. Each handed-over opportunity gets one attributed owner-change timeline entry. Their notes, drafts, sent messages and timeline entries remain and stay attributed to them. Handing over owned contacts, leads, companies and custom-object records is RECORD-016, and active sequence enrollments are SEQUENCE-001. **Acceptance:** Remove an operator who owns an open opportunity, an open sales task, a delegated handoff and a scheduled message; choose a receiver for the opportunity and explicit unassignment for the rest, and verify revoked sessions, cancellation, the recorded choice per set, the attributed owner-change entry and attributed historical notes.

clauses.title: Core records
clauses.text: Operators can create, edit, and delete contacts, companies, and opportunities. A contact requires a name or an email address and may also hold a phone number, job title, and timezone; a company requires a name and may hold one primary domain; an opportunity requires a title and holds a pipeline stage, a value in the workspace currency, zero or one owner, an expected close date, at most one company, and any number of contacts. Each entity listed in `seed.json → customFieldEntities` also holds custom fields. Contact, lead, company and custom-object owners, independent of opportunity owners, are defined in RECORD-016. **Acceptance:** Through authenticated Records, create and edit a company, contact and USD opportunity with custom fields; reload and read back the associations and values.

clauses.title: Associations
clauses.text: A contact has at most one primary company and can have further explicit company relationships under RECORD-015, and can belong to any number of opportunities. An opportunity with contacts names one primary as its default outreach recipient; a deal without a contact is never recommended an email follow-up. Changing an association moves no old timeline entry. **Acceptance:** Associate two contacts and a company with a deal, choose the primary recipient, change the associations, and confirm historical timeline entries stay put.

clauses.title: Identity keys
clauses.text: A contact's key is its email address lowercased with surrounding whitespace removed; a company's key is its primary domain lowercased with a leading `www.` removed. A domain on the configured free-mail list is never a company key. Creating or changing a record to a key another record already holds returns 409 with that record's ID and writes nothing. A record with no key is created and edited normally, and signals never link to it automatically. Orbit never merges records by name similarity, fuzzy match, or score. *Policy: `record.identity.v1`; default: the rules in this clause.* **Acceptance:** Create case/whitespace email and domain collisions through Records; require a 409 naming the existing identity and no extra row; exercise free-mail and keyless records.

clauses.title: Duplicate merge
clauses.text: Merging two contacts or two companies requires an operator to choose the surviving record and the value of every conflicting field. The request is bound to both reviewed record states; a changed record refuses the merge without modifying either record, requiring a new review. Contactability is not a reviewed choice: a do-not-contact stop that lands after review is inherited by the merge. The merge moves associations and timeline entries once, retires the other record's key as an alias so later signals carrying it link to the survivor, creates no signal, recommendation, or outreach, and records the retired ID in the audit trail. **Acceptance:** Review two duplicates, choose field values and survivor, then change one reviewed record and require refusal; review again and merge once, inheriting a concurrent stop.

clauses.title: Timeline
clauses.text: A record's timeline lists its signals, stage and owner changes, notes, logged calls and meetings, recommendations, drafts, outbound attempts, replies, and merges, most recent occurred time first with ties broken by ID. Every entry shows its occurred time, its recorded time, and the operator, source, or feature that created it. **Acceptance:** Open a record containing mail, meetings, notes, changes and a merge; inspect occurred/recorded times, source and actor, including out-of-order events.

clauses.title: Search and views
clauses.text: Operators can search contacts, companies, opportunities, and timeline text, and can filter opportunities by state, stage, owner, band, and queue. A first page holds at most 50 matches. Answering that first page within 500ms at the declared capacity in `seed.json` is a capacity target qualified separately; this release makes no capacity promise. **Acceptance:** Search records and timeline text, apply state/stage/owner/band/queue filters and verify results and the first-page cap; qualify the 500 ms p95 at declared capacity separately.

clauses.title: Ownership
clauses.text: An opportunity has zero or one owner. Any operator can assign, reassign or unassign it; each change appears on its timeline as an attributed owner change and leaves its score unchanged. *Policy: `opportunity.assignment.v1`; default: an opportunity an operator creates is unassigned.* An opportunity created from a published form's enquiry belongs to the operator who published the form. Owners of contacts, leads, companies and custom-object records, and notifications to a deal's new owner, are RECORD-016. **Acceptance:** Assign, reassign and unassign an opportunity through its native control; reload and inspect its attributed timeline without changing score.

clauses.title: Import
clauses.text: Full native operators move contacts, companies, deals and notes through explicit CSV mappings and a mandatory saved dry run. New contacts are held by default unless mapped explicit subscribed permission or an explicit per-import operator contactability attestation permits contact. Existing do-not-contact stops always win. All suppression and remaining absent-consent holds publish before customer creation or sending; malformed suppression rows block application. Source IDs and explicit associations are retained with inert provenance. Existing native identities are associated without replacing their fields. Every rejected row names its file, row and reason and creates no customer record. Unchanged re-imports reuse native records, associations and notes. Base import-kit records originals, current-session authority, atomic progress and conflict-preserving undo; undo removes or restores only owned, unchanged effects and keeps native edits, independent suppression and their dependency closure. No import approves outreach or grants operator access. Contact-owner and company-owner columns are mapped under RECORD-016. **Acceptance:** Move mapped CSV contacts, companies, deals, notes and suppression through saved preview and Apply; replay, change a source row, interrupt and undo while preserving native edits and stops. The Site has no verified real-data importer receipt for named products.

clauses.title: Duplicate candidates
clauses.text: Orbit lists contacts sharing a name across companies, including contacts with no company, and companies sharing a name, as duplicate candidates; names are compared lowercased with runs of whitespace collapsed. A candidate is a review item only: nothing is merged, altered, or hidden until an operator completes RECORD-004. **Acceptance:** Create same-name contacts across companies and keyless records; review candidates without a mutation, then complete a chosen merge explicitly.

clauses.title: Manual entries
clauses.text: An operator can add a note to any record and log a call or meeting with an occurred time, duration, and attending contacts. A manual entry is attributed to its author, editable and deletable by any operator, never sent to a customer, and never contributes to a score. RECORD-017 adds @mentions of colleagues in these entries, and RECORD-018 attaches files to them. **Acceptance:** Log, edit and delete a note, call and meeting on a customer record; verify time, duration and attendees, and verify no score or external message changed.

clauses.title: Related records
clauses.text: A company page lists its contacts and its opportunities with each opportunity's stage, owner, and value, plus the total value of its open opportunities. A contact page lists their opportunities. Both reflect an association change on the next load. **Acceptance:** Open a company and contact, move a deal association, reload and compare linked deals, owner/stage and open-value total with the underlying records.

clauses.title: Contactability
clauses.text: A contact is contactable or do-not-contact. An operator can set do-not-contact at any time, and an unsubscribe event that identifies the person (OUT-012, OUT-020) or a permanent bounce also sets it, for that person only. An opt-out that cannot name one recipient of a multi-recipient message pauses those recipients' scheduled work rather than suppressing them (OUT-020). No operation sends customer email to a do-not-contact contact, the state is shown wherever the contact appears, and only an operator can clear it. A contact an operator creates by hand on a record page or through the Records API starts contactable unless the operator chooses do-not-contact or its address matches a retained suppression proof, in which case it starts do-not-contact; other doors state their own default (RECORD-008, CAPTURE-005, CAPTURE-012, FORM-001, OUT-019). **Acceptance:** Set do-not-contact, process unsubscribe and permanent-bounce events, then try immediate and scheduled sending; all remain blocked until an explicit current-state clear. Create a contact by hand and see it start contactable; recreate an erased contact's address and see it start do-not-contact.

clauses.title: Deletion
clauses.text: Deleting a company detaches its contacts and opportunities and deletes neither. Deleting an opportunity deletes its recommendations, drafts, and unsent scheduled messages, and leaves its contacts, its company, and their entries for messages already sent. Deleting a contact follows DATA-002. Each deletion is confirmed before it runs. **Acceptance:** Confirm each record deletion; company removal detaches dependents, deal removal preserves sent history, and contact removal performs the erasure journey.

clauses.title: Ingestion
clauses.text: A valid event from a configured source, carrying that source's signature, becomes one normalized signal within 10 seconds. The signal keeps its source, source event ID, type, subject, occurred time, received time, payload hash, and linking basis, and is never edited afterwards. **Acceptance:** POST a signed configured-source event through its ingestion route and read one attributed signal and linked timeline within the bound.

clauses.title: Signal types
clauses.text: Orbit accepts form submissions; email sent, opened, replied, bounced, and unsubscribed events; meeting viewed, booked, completed, and canceled events; page views; chats; content downloads; and firmographic changes. A source can add a type namespaced to itself, which changes no existing type. An event whose type is neither standard nor namespaced is rejected with 400. **Acceptance:** Submit every standard type, a source-namespaced type and an unknown type; accept the first two classes and reject the unknown without writes.

clauses.title: Idempotency
clauses.text: Repeated or concurrent delivery of one `(source, source event ID)` produces one signal and one set of downstream evaluations. Reusing that identity with a different payload hash is rejected and recorded as an error on that source. **Acceptance:** Deliver identical events concurrently and after restart, then change the payload under the same source identity; retain one effect and a visible conflict.

clauses.title: Linking
clauses.text: A signal links first by an Orbit record ID the source supplies, then by RECORD-003. A uniquely linked signal appears once on that record's timeline. A signal with no unique match is held in the unlinked queue, where it changes no score; an operator linking it later appends it to the chosen record's timeline exactly once and triggers one evaluation. **Acceptance:** Ingest exact, ambiguous and unknown identities; verify linked and held queues, then manually link the held event once and inspect evaluation.

clauses.title: Event time
clauses.text: A late or out-of-order event keeps its occurred time, appears in that position on the timeline, and triggers a fresh evaluation. It never overwrites a record field that a later-occurring event wrote. **Acceptance:** Deliver older evidence after newer evidence and inspect chronological history and fresh evaluation without overwriting later record state.

clauses.title: Evidence confidence
clauses.text: Every signal carries one confidence: observed, when the customer acted deliberately (form submission, reply, booking, meeting, download, chat), or inferred, when a tool reported activity (email open, page view). An inferred signal alone cannot create an opportunity, produce a high band, or satisfy ACTION-001's evidence requirement. **Acceptance:** Compare open/page-view inference with observed reply/booking evidence; inferred activity alone cannot create a deal, high band or evidence-backed action.

clauses.title: No tracking
clauses.text: Orbit serves no tracking script, pixel, or cookie, and performs no fingerprinting or cross-site collection. A page-view, chat, or download signal is accepted only when its source supplies the visitor identity it already holds and the basis for holding it; without that basis the event is held unlinked under SIGNAL-004 and never becomes contact history. The one exception is OUT-016's disclosed, opt-in, per-message open and link-click tracking of Orbit-sent customer mail, which adds nothing to Orbit's public pages, its app or any other site. **Acceptance:** Inspect public assets/network and submit identity-free page/chat events; no Orbit tracker runs and unsupported identity stays outside customer history.

clauses.title: Ingestion failure
clauses.text: A missing or invalid signature returns 401, a request naming a source this deployment has not configured returns 403, and a payload over `seed.json → limits.signalPayloadBytes` returns 413; none of them writes anything. A persistence failure returns 503 and writes no partial signal, timeline entry, or evaluation, so the source can safely replay the same event identity. Each source shows its last accepted event, its last error, and its rejected-event count in settings. **Acceptance:** POST invalid signatures, unknown sources, oversized input and injected persistence failure; verify status, no partial writes, replay safety and source diagnostics.

clauses.title: Signed sources
clauses.text: This clause supersedes BASE-ACCESS-004 for the paths `/api/v1/signals/` and `/api/v1/mail/events/` only: a request there is authorized by a signature from a source or mail provider configured in this deployment (or, at a source’s `/automation` endpoint only, its current private secret in an HTTPS Authorization Bearer header) instead of an operator session, and may write only signals, delivery states, and their timeline entries. Native operator mutations require a valid operator session and a server-side ownership check. The separately scoped application-delegation boundary below is the only additional authorization exception. **Acceptance:** Exercise signed callbacks and HTTPS source-scoped automation; refuse invalid, disabled and rotated authority while retaining native session and ownership checks.

clauses.title: File capture
clauses.text: An operator adds `.eml` files, an mbox or `.ics` calendar files on the Capture page. Each message or calendar event becomes one signal with the same columns, confidence and linking rules as SIGNAL-001 to SIGNAL-006, and keeps its original headers, body and non-inline attachments (RECORD-018) as the evidence the signal points to. Replay identity is the Message-ID, or the event UID with its SEQUENCE and what happened (booked, completed or canceled): adding the same item again changes nothing, and a changed copy with the same identity is refused and recorded on the capture source under SIGNAL-003. A calendar event keeps its original start and end times; a missing identity, a missing date or an unknown time zone is reported, never guessed. **Acceptance:** Upload mail and calendar files on Capture, replay and conflict them, then inspect original evidence and explicit invalid-date/identity/timezone errors.

clauses.title: Known participants only
clauses.text: A captured message or event is stored only when a participant other than an operator holds a contact's exact email key or a company's exact domain key (RECORD-003). Anything else is not stored, and the import reports how many items were not stored and why. An operator may keep unknown senders for one import; those signals wait in the unlinked queue under SIGNAL-004 and change no record. For a connected mailbox or calendar source (CAPTURE-010), an unknown external participant in a conversation with an operator becomes a held CAPTURE-012 new-prospect proposal instead of being discarded. **Acceptance:** Capture known and unknown participants; unknown mail is not retained by default and explicit one-import retention creates only held evidence.

clauses.title: What capture applies at once
clauses.text: A reply from the recipient of an Orbit send that carries that send's message headers attaches once to its opportunity under OUT-004. A delivery report for an Orbit send to that recipient records the bounce, and a permanent one sets do-not-contact under RECORD-012. A captured reply or booked meeting from a known contact cancels that contact's scheduled messages and marks their unsent drafts stale under OUT-007 and ACTION-005 in the same commit, while the proposals from the same message wait for review. An automatic reply stops nothing. **Acceptance:** Capture a threaded reply, booked meeting, permanent bounce and automatic reply; inspect atomic linking/stale/cancellation effects and verify automatic reply stops nothing.

clauses.title: Reviewed proposals
clauses.text: Everything else capture finds is a proposal that shows its evidence (sender, date, subject and the quoted lines it rests on): link this evidence to these records, create a contact at a known company by its exact email address, set a contact's name or phone, change an opportunity's next action, or set do-not-contact. A proposal that touches an existing value shows the current and proposed values side by side and is refused with 409 if the current value changed after it was offered. A person accepts, edits or declines each one. Accepting appends one timeline entry attributed to that person and to the capture source; a declined proposal is never offered again for the same evidence. Capture proposes no bought data and no identity guessed from a name, a lookalike address or a similar domain. **Acceptance:** Open evidence-backed field/link proposals, accept/edit/decline and repeat; a concurrent field edit refuses stale acceptance and a decline stays declined.

clauses.title: Human boundary
clauses.text: Capture never creates a draft, approves or starts a message, or makes a contact contactable. A contact created from a proposal is do-not-contact until an operator clears it under RECORD-012; the person accepting a CAPTURE-012 new-prospect proposal makes that choice explicitly in the same review, with the basis it records, and an unsubscribe request in a captured message is a do-not-contact proposal. Capture endpoints accept only a full native operator's session: a source signature, a delegation credential or an invited collaborator is refused, and the signed paths of SIGNAL-009 cannot write into a capture source. Mail delivered to an operator-created Orbit address (CAPTURE-008) is the only intake without a session; its authority is that address's private tag, and it writes only into that address's source. **Acceptance:** Attempt capture with native, collaborator, source and delegation authority; only permitted native/address intake succeeds, and a proposed new contact stays blocked.

clauses.title: Capture sources (capture.source.v1)
clauses.text: A source declares the mail folders or labels and the calendars it may read, keeps its cursor exactly as its provider gave it (a Gmail history ID or a Microsoft Graph delta link, for example), and shows its state, last success, last error, items captured, items not stored and proposals waiting. A crash before a page's cursor is stored re-reads that page without duplicating anything. A revoked grant stops intake and shows its error until the source is reconnected; a provider outage records its error and leaves records, queues and manual work unchanged. Disconnecting stops intake at once, deletes the stored credential and keeps captured evidence, shown as coming from a disconnected source. The file import is the first adapter and has no cursor or credential. **Acceptance:** Connect each Google/Microsoft read adapter, choose folders/calendars, page and crash before cursor commit; resume without duplicates, revoke, reconnect and disconnect with visible errors.

clauses.title: Captured data
clauses.text: Captured evidence, including its attachments (RECORD-018), proposals and source state are part of every export and restore under DATA-001; source credentials never are, so a restored provider source must be reconnected. Erasing a contact erases the captured evidence and proposals that carry them under DATA-002. The audit trail keeps counts and anonymous keyed replay proofs with erasure times, without addresses, original item identifiers or content, so later intake cannot recreate erased originals. Private matching contexts and proofs travel in archives; restoring an owner's historical archive retains DATA-001's existing behavior. **Acceptance:** Export/restore captured evidence and proposals, verify no source credential travels, erase a contact and replay intake to prove erased originals stay fenced.

clauses.title: Orbit address
clauses.text: When the installation names a receiving mailbox (`CAPTURE_MAIL_ADDRESS`, reached through Cloudflare Email Routing or signed SendGrid Inbound Parse), an operator can create a private Orbit address on the Capture page with no provider console: the mailbox with a random tag, kept sealed like a credential and never in archives. Only mail whose envelope names that exact tagged address is read, so a BCC copy, a forwarded message and automatic forwarding all count, and anything else is refused without storing. Each accepted message follows CAPTURE-001 to CAPTURE-004 exactly as an imported `.eml` file, and a forwarded message counts as coming from the sender it names. A forwarding confirmation from Gmail or Google Workspace is shown to the operator with its code and link instead of being stored as evidence. Replacing the address stops the old one at once and keeps everything captured; a message larger than 10 MB is counted as not stored rather than bounced. **Acceptance:** Create and rotate a tagged Orbit address, forward/BCC mail and a Gmail confirmation; accept exact envelope tags only and count oversized mail without retaining it.

clauses.title: Calendar link
clauses.text: An operator can add a calendar by the private iCal address its own calendar offers (Google, Outlook or iCloud), with no provider console. Orbit checks the link returns a calendar before saving it, keeps it sealed like a credential, reads it only with GET, and refreshes it about every 15 minutes. Each event inside the last 180 days or the next year is one calendar item under CAPTURE-001 to CAPTURE-004; an unchanged calendar is not read again event by event. A link that stops working (refused, missing or no longer a calendar) stops that source and shows its error under CAPTURE-006 until the calendar is added again. **Acceptance:** Add a private ICS link, advance the refresh clock, change/cancel an event, then break the link; inspect dedupe, preserved times and the halted-source reason.

clauses.title: Lifecycle
clauses.text: An opportunity is open, won, or lost. Closing it as won or lost records the operator, the time, and a reason, and removes it from NOW and NEXT. Later signals append to its timeline and never reopen it; only an operator can reopen it, which returns it to open without changing its stage or owner. **Acceptance:** Close a deal as won and lost with reasons, ingest later evidence, and explicitly reopen; inspect history and queue membership at every step.

clauses.title: Independent state
clauses.text: Stage, owner, score, band, and queue state are independent fields. A score or band change never changes stage, owner, or won/lost state, and a stage change never changes a score. **Acceptance:** Change stage and owner and ingest scoring evidence; verify lifecycle, queue, stage, owner and score remain independently represented.

clauses.title: Evaluation
clauses.text: A linked signal whose type carries a non-zero weight in the scoring policy, or a change to an open opportunity's stage, expected close date, value, owner, or associations, evaluates that opportunity within 30 seconds. The result records a 0–100 score, a low, medium, or high band, the evaluation time, the policy version, and each contributing signal's contribution. A closed opportunity is not evaluated. *Policy: `opportunity.scoring.v1`; default: each contributing signal's configured weight decays linearly to zero over the 30 days after its occurred time, the sum is clamped to 0–100, and 0–39 is low, 40–69 is medium, 70–100 is high.* **Acceptance:** Ingest weighted signals and edit an open opportunity; inspect computed score, band, contributions and policy version, including decay and closed-deal exclusion.

clauses.title: Explainability
clauses.text: The opportunity view shows every signal the current score used, by ID, with its source, occurred time, confidence, and positive or negative contribution, and shows the reason for the current recommendation beside them. **Acceptance:** Open a scored deal and follow every contribution to its source evidence and current action reason.

clauses.title: Evaluation failure
clauses.text: If an evaluation fails or returns output that does not validate, the previous score, band, and evidence remain readable and are marked stale with the time of the failed attempt. Orbit shows no score, band, or recommendation it did not compute. **Acceptance:** Cause evaluation to fail after a valid score; read the last value as stale with failure time and verify no fabricated replacement.

clauses.title: NOW ordering
clauses.text: NOW lists the open opportunities that OPP-007 placed there, ordered by score descending, then by the occurred time of their most recent contributing signal descending, then by ID. Operators can filter it by owner, stage, and band. *Policy: `opportunity.prioritization.v1`; default: the ordering in this clause, and every factor it uses is shown in the opportunity view.* **Acceptance:** Create tied and untied NOW opportunities, filter by rep/stage/band and verify deterministic persisted ordering.

clauses.title: Queue entry
clauses.text: An open opportunity enters NOW when its band rises, a customer form submission, reply or delivery problem arrives, a scheduled message cannot be sent, its expected close date passes, its last timeline entry becomes older than the stale interval, or an operator puts it there. It is in NEXT while it waits for a scheduled send or for a customer response inside the awaiting-response interval, and in neither when no action is pending. The stale interval defaults to 14 days and the awaiting-response interval to 5 working days, counted Monday to Friday in the workspace timezone. Every entry, move, and removal records its reason and actor on the timeline. **Acceptance:** Advance close/stale/awaiting clocks and deliver a form, reply, booking and send failure; inspect NOW/NEXT reasons and one timeline transition per event.

clauses.title: Manual completion
clauses.text: An operator can complete or skip the current recommended action without sending anything, with an optional note; the outcome, note, and operator appear on the timeline. *Policy: `opportunity.next-action.v1`; default: evaluate once, keep the opportunity in NOW if that produces a new recommendation, and otherwise remove it from NOW and NEXT.* **Acceptance:** Complete or skip the current action without sending; inspect the recorded outcome and only a genuinely new recommendation.

clauses.title: Pipeline stages
clauses.text: Operators configure multiple named pipelines with ordered stages, stage probabilities, required fields and stage-specific stale intervals. Deals retain their pipeline, stage and movement history; permitted users move a deal within or between pipelines with explicit destination mapping. Stage moves record previous stage, actor and time without silently changing lifecycle or score; a move by an AUTO-002 workflow applies the same required fields and records the workflow, its version and the trigger as actor. An occupied stage or pipeline cannot be deleted until its deals have been explicitly moved. Pipeline boards and list views expose the same records and filters. **Acceptance:** Create two pipelines with different ordered stages, move deals between stages and pipelines, and refuse deletion of an occupied stage; preserve move history and independent lifecycle.

clauses.title: Current recommendation
clauses.text: An open opportunity has at most one current recommended action, which is either an email follow-up or a manual action. It names the action, cites at least one observed signal by ID, and records the policy or model version that produced it. Its written explanation is generated under AI-001 and is absent when AI-003 applies. **Acceptance:** Read an open deal recommendation with observed evidence and version; disable AI and retain the named action/evidence without an invented explanation.

clauses.title: Replacement
clauses.text: A new contributing signal, a changed opportunity, a completed or skipped action, or an operator request replaces the current recommendation. The replaced one stays on the timeline marked superseded and can no longer be drafted from, sent, or completed. **Acceptance:** Supersede an action by new evidence or an operator change; the old action remains historical and cannot be drafted, sent or completed.

clauses.title: Draft on request
clauses.text: An operator can request a one-to-one email draft for the current recommendation. Generation reads the opportunity, the primary or operator-selected contact, that contact's company, the cited signals, the messages already exchanged with that contact, and the configured instructions, and sends nothing. *Policy: `outreach.instructions.v1`; default: at most 150 words, and no fact, price, discount, or commitment that a cited record or signal field does not carry.* OUT-017 offers the same draft request from a contact, lead or company record, with no recommendation or open opportunity, under the same preview and policy. **Acceptance:** Preview and request a draft from current customer evidence; inspect the unsent result for cited facts and configured instructions.

clauses.title: Durable draft
clauses.text: Recipient, subject, and body are visible and editable (the recipient being OUT-019's To, CC and BCC lists), and the draft is stored with its author, source recommendation, created time, and last edit time, and is readable after signing out and back in. **Acceptance:** Edit recipient/subject/body, sign out, return and read the saved draft with its original source and edit attribution.

clauses.title: Stale draft
clauses.text: A reply, meeting, unsubscribe, do-not-contact, permanent bounce, changed recipient, changed opportunity, or replaced recommendation marks a draft stale. A stale draft is shown as stale, and sending it returns 409 and writes no outbound message until an operator opens it, sees what changed, and confirms. **Acceptance:** Change the customer/deal or deliver a stop event after drafting; refuse sending until the operator sees and explicitly reviews current differences.

clauses.title: Human send boundary
clauses.text: No signal, score, recommendation, draft, job, or AI result can approve or start a customer message. A send requires an authenticated operator who has seen the exact recipient, subject, and body to invoke it, and a worker may dispatch only the unchanged content an operator approved for the schedule in OUT-009. For a message with several recipients, the exact recipient is the complete To, CC and BCC lists under OUT-019. For a SEQUENCE-003 batch, one approval covers each listed message whose exact recipient, subject and body the batch review rendered and made inspectable, and nothing else. No policy, adapter, extension, or setting removes this requirement. **Acceptance:** Attempt sending from ingestion, an agent and an unreviewed draft; only native exact-recipient/subject/body approval permits the unchanged message to dispatch.

clauses.title: Message states
clauses.text: Customer mail is submitted through `mail.sender.v1`. An outbound message is draft, scheduled, queued, reconciling, accepted, delivered, bounced, failed, canceled, or delivery-unknown. The operator view calls a message sent only after the provider accepts it, and delivered only after a delivery event. **Acceptance:** Drive provider acceptance, delivery, bounce, failure and ambiguous responses; inspect each persisted state and truthful buyer-visible labels.

clauses.title: Send idempotency
clauses.text: Repeated or concurrent use of one send idempotency key creates one outbound message and at most one provider submission. **Acceptance:** Submit the same approval key concurrently and after restart; observe one outbound intent and at most one provider submission.

clauses.title: Threading
clauses.text: An outbound message carries message and reference headers that return the customer's reply to the same opportunity. A reply carrying those headers is attached once; a reply without them becomes an unlinked activity for operator review rather than a subject-based guess. For a message sent with no linked opportunity, or to a contact whose deals are won or lost, OUT-017 returns the reply by the same headers to that contact and their company. A reply from any external recipient of the message, To, CC or BCC, threads back the same way onto that replier's contact (OUT-019). **Acceptance:** Deliver correct, foreign and absent reply headers with sender checks; attach the correct reply once and hold ambiguous mail for review.

clauses.title: Accepted outcome
clauses.text: When the provider accepts a submission, one local transaction records the reviewed content and provider message ID as a timeline activity, completes the recommendation, sets the next action to awaiting response, moves the opportunity from NOW to NEXT, and creates one notification for the responsible operator. A replayed provider event repeats none of it. This clause governs a send linked to an open opportunity; a send with no linked open opportunity records the same timeline activity and notification and opens OUT-017's contact-level awaiting-response obligation instead of a queue move. **Acceptance:** Accept an approved send, replay its provider response and inspect one timeline message, completed action, NEXT transition and notification.

clauses.title: Delivery failure
clauses.text: A transient submission failure retries up to 5 times over 1 hour. A permanent failure or an exhausted retry returns the opportunity to NOW, notifies the responsible operator once, and shows the provider's reason on the message. A permanent bounce also sets the contact do-not-contact under RECORD-012. **Acceptance:** Fail a submission transiently, permanently and ambiguously; verify bounded known-unsent retries, visible exhausted failure, one notification and permanent-bounce stop.

clauses.title: Stop conditions
clauses.text: A reply, a booked meeting, an unsubscribe, a do-not-contact, or a permanent bounce cancels that contact's scheduled messages and marks their unsent drafts stale under ACTION-005. A reply or a bounce ends awaiting response and returns the opportunity to NOW with the reply or the delivery problem as its next action. An OUT-020 unattributed stop request pauses, rather than cancels, the scheduled messages and sequence enrollments of every external recipient of its message until a user resolves it. **Acceptance:** Schedule a message, deliver reply/booking/unsubscribe/bounce or a manual stop, then advance dispatch; cancel the message and stale the draft without duplicates.

clauses.title: Quiet hours
clauses.text: A draft can be written at any time. Sending outside 08:00–18:00 Monday to Friday in the contact's timezone, or the workspace timezone when the contact has none, requires a second confirmation naming the recipient's local time; a scheduled send waits for the next permitted minute. *Policy: `outreach.quiet-hours.v1`; default: the window in this clause, with no holiday calendar.* **Acceptance:** Approve outside recipient-local quiet hours, including daylight-saving boundaries; require the extra immediate confirmation or delay the schedule to the permitted window.

clauses.title: Scheduled send
clauses.text: An operator can schedule one reviewed message for a future time and cancel it until it dispatches. Dispatch re-checks ACTION-005, RECORD-012, OUT-007, OUT-008, and OUT-010 against the current record and submits only the approved content; a stale or prohibited message is not sent, returns the opportunity to NOW, and shows the reason. **Acceptance:** Schedule/cancel approved content, then change its evidence, permission and recipient before dispatch; only unchanged current authorized content can reach the provider.

clauses.title: Sending limits
clauses.text: Before submission Orbit checks the shared transport's rate and each sender's one-to-one budget under OUT-018 (`seed.json` limits: 100 messages a minute and 1,000 a user per rolling day by default). A message over a limit stays unsent and visible with the limit that stopped it and the time it may be sent; Orbit neither retries it silently nor merges it with another message. Sequence budgets and mailbox pacing are OUT-018's. **Acceptance:** Exceed the per-minute and per-operator daily limits before immediate and scheduled submission; retain a visible unsent item with its reason and next permitted time, and see no silent retry.

clauses.title: Unresolved submission
clauses.text: Orbit records the outbound intent and its provider idempotency key durably before submitting. If the transaction in OUT-005 fails the message becomes reconciling; if the provider's response is a timeout it becomes delivery-unknown. In both states a job queries the provider by that idempotency key every 5 minutes, submits nothing again, and applies the OUT-005 outcome exactly once if acceptance is confirmed. With SendGrid the query uses its Email Activity API; on an account without that API each attempt records the lookup failure on the message. A SendGrid message still unresolved after 24 hours becomes a failure the operator can see, and notifies the responsible operator. Run Edit Run managed mail offers no lookup, so such a message stays delivery-unknown with that explanation, is never submitted again, and is left for the operator to reconcile. **Acceptance:** Lose the acceptance transaction or provider response; restart and reconcile the durable intent without submitting again, ending once as accepted or visibly unresolved.

clauses.title: Unsubscribe
clauses.text: An outbound customer message that carries opt-out under OUT-020 carries `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers handled by the mail provider, or by the installation origin for an OUT-013 mailbox send. An unsubscribe event that identifies one recipient sets that contact do-not-contact under RECORD-012 within 60 seconds and cancels their scheduled messages. OUT-020 sets which message types carry opt-out (sequence email on and one-to-one email off by default) and the scope of an opt-out from a message with more than one external recipient. **Acceptance:** Inspect unsubscribe headers on actual submitted mail of a type set to carry opt-out, receive a signed unsubscribe and confirm future sending and scheduled work are suppressed.

clauses.title: Provider and input
clauses.text: Recommendation explanations and email drafts go through `ai.provider.v1`. The request preview shows the operator every field, timeline entry, and instruction the request will carry, and nothing outside the preview is sent. **Acceptance:** Open an AI request preview, inspect all customer fields and instructions, then compare the provider-edge request with that exact unchanged preview.

clauses.title: Output validation
clauses.text: AI output must validate against its operation's schema and cite only evidence IDs present on the record. Output failing either check fails visibly and is never repaired with invented content or a semantic fallback. Only a transient transport failure is retried, at most twice within 30 seconds. **Acceptance:** Return invalid schema, foreign citations and a transport error at the provider edge; fail invalid content visibly with no invented repair and bound transport retry.

clauses.title: Provider failure
clauses.text: When the AI provider is unconfigured or unavailable, records, signal ingestion, linking, scoring, queue placement, search, manual updates, hand-written drafts, and sending all continue to work, and a recommendation still names its action and evidence. A generation request shows the failure and produces no explanation or draft. **Acceptance:** Leave AI unconfigured and fail a configured request; finish manual CRM, ingestion, scoring and handwritten outreach flows while generation reports failure.

clauses.title: Cost
clauses.text: Every AI call records provider, model, input and output tokens, feature, duration, status, and estimated cost. Operators can view totals by day and by feature in settings. **Acceptance:** Generate successful and failed requests, then inspect provider/model/tokens/duration/status/cost and day/feature totals in Settings.

clauses.title: Today's brief
clauses.text: The top of the operator home is a brief built from records only, so it works with the AI provider unconfigured (AI-003). Per account (the company when one is known, otherwise the opportunity, otherwise the contact) it lists the customer signals linked since the operator last marked the brief seen, or, before they ever have, over the stale interval counted from the start of the day (UTC), with replies and booked, completed or canceled meetings first and observed signals kept apart from inferred ones (SIGNAL-006); the account's overdue promises (BRIEF-002); and application handoffs waiting for review (BRIEF-005). Signals that match no record and replies without thread headers are listed as unresolved identity, never guessed; captured replies and meetings waiting for a person to accept or decline their proposed link are listed as held for capture review. Every line shows its occurred time and links to the record, timeline entry, draft, task or review item it rests on; a line without such evidence is not shown. Marking the brief seen records the operator and the time the brief was built in the audit trail, so anything arriving later stays new. A day with nothing says so. The brief is for full native operators; invited collaborators cannot read it. **Acceptance:** Open Today with fresh, held and unlinked events; follow every line to evidence, mark seen, receive a later event and confirm it remains new.

clauses.title: Overdue promises
clauses.text: Computed from records when the brief is built: an open internal next action (a handoff task a person wrote or accepted) or an open opportunity's next action past its due time; the latest customer reply on a record with no approved outbound message, captured sent message, logged call or meeting, or completed action on that record since, once the awaiting-response interval (TEAM-003, working days in the workspace timezone) has passed; a meeting completed within the last 120 days with no note, logged call or meeting, completed action, handoff, draft, approved message or captured sent message on its records after it; and a draft on an open opportunity left untouched longer than the workspace stale interval, with no outbound attempt and no customer stop event. A recommendation carries no due time and is never a promise by itself. **Acceptance:** Advance past each task/reply/meeting/draft deadline, complete the corresponding obligation and verify overdue lines appear and clear from actual records.

clauses.title: Account summary
clauses.text: With a provider configured (AI-001), an operator can ask for a one-paragraph summary of one account's brief lines. The request preview shows every field sent, and the request is sent only unchanged from that preview; a brief that changed since the preview is refused with 409. Output must validate and cite only evidence IDs from that account's lines (AI-002); failing or uncited output is recorded (AI-004) and shown as failed, never repaired or replaced. Summaries are not stored, and a provider failure leaves the brief whole. **Acceptance:** Preview an account summary, alter the brief before generation and require refusal; generate on a fresh preview and reject uncited provider output.

clauses.title: Meeting plan
clauses.text: A meeting signal linked to a record (booked, completed or canceled, from a source or from capture) has a plan page: its time exactly as the source gave it or the statement that none was given; attendees resolved by exact email key (RECORD-003) with their company and open opportunities; attendees with no record listed as unresolved, never guessed, with a way to create a contact with that exact address; the opportunities with value, stage and owner and their total open value; the last interactions on its records and the outstanding promises on them (BRIEF-002), each citing its timeline entry or record. The agenda and prep notes are saved as one note under RECORD-010 on the meeting's opportunity (or its company or contact) and edited in place. A person can turn a cited plan line into an internal next action on the meeting's opportunity that cites that line. Planning creates no draft and sends nothing (OUT-001). **Acceptance:** Open a linked meeting, inspect resolved/unresolved attendees and promises, save agenda/prep and create a cited internal task without customer outreach.

clauses.title: Agent handoff
clauses.text: Within the scoped application delegation below and with no new scope: `crm.evidence.read` also reads the brief, narrowed to lines resting on selected records, and the plan of a meeting that is selected or linked to a selected record, narrowed to the selected records and the contacts and company of selected opportunities; a line or interaction resting only on opportunities outside the grant is left out even when it shares a contact or company, records outside the grant are left off the lines shown, and unresolved attendees show only their address. A line seen only through a signal selected by id keeps only selected records; one left with none is listed apart from the accounts and links to that signal's evidence read. A held line names a proposed contact or company only when it is selected, and a selected contact's line is filed under its company only when that company is selected too. `orbit.handoff.upsert` content may cite evidence IDs; each must be a signal, timeline entry, draft or task on that opportunity, its contacts or its company, or the write is refused with 422. A handoff an application wrote is a proposal, shown in the brief and on the opportunity with its cited evidence (or the statement that it cites none), until a person accepts it, saves an edited version or dismisses it; that review appends one timeline entry attributed to the person and naming the application. No handoff can approve or start a message (OUT-001). Without consent, without the write scope or after revocation an application cannot write, and revocation stops its reads at once. **Acceptance:** Read a selected-record brief/meeting through delegation, propose a cited handoff, review it natively and revoke the grant; no outside evidence or sending becomes available.

clauses.title: Responsible operator
clauses.text: The responsible operator for an opportunity is its owner, or, when it is unassigned, the operator whose action appears most recently on its timeline. They receive one in-app notification when it enters NOW, when a customer reply arrives on it, and when one of its outbound messages fails, bounces, or becomes delivery-unknown. When an unassigned opportunity that no operator has acted on enters NOW, every operator is notified instead. Duplicate source or provider events add no notification. **Acceptance:** Trigger queue entry, reply and delivery problems on assigned and unassigned deals; verify responsible recipients and one notification on replay.

clauses.title: Read state
clauses.text: A notification is unread until the operator opens it or marks it read. The unread count updates within 5 seconds and never counts one event twice. **Acceptance:** Open and mark notifications read across sessions; inspect recipient-specific state and an unread count without duplicate events.

clauses.title: Landing page
clauses.text: GET / at the app origin returns the public Base Lobby without a session and links to native sign-in. The separate approved run site uses Orbit's public identity and images. Neither surface exposes this installation's contacts, companies, opportunities or signals. This target-contract round leaves the approved homepage and app interface untouched. **Acceptance:** Visit the public app Lobby and separate run site without a session; verify branding/sign-in links and no installation customer data in HTML or network.

clauses.title: Safe demo
clauses.text: When enabled in `ext/config.ts`, `/demo` presents a separate read-only example workspace with twelve fictional deals, relative dates, signals, drafts and a sent-message/reply story. It clearly labels these as examples before displaying them. No example data is written to the owner's database. The demo cannot load owner records, send mail, call AI, approve outreach or mutate data. Unknown demo paths return the styled not-found page. Disabling it returns 404. This deliberately replaces the former dedicated hosted-record walkthrough; all native session, exact-message review and customer-sending requirements remain unchanged. **Acceptance:** Browse the labeled fictional demo and unknown paths at desktop/mobile sizes; verify no owner-data read, D1 write, AI request or send.

clauses.title: Unconfigured sign-in
clauses.text: While no sign-in mail is configured, `GET /signin` answers without an operator session and states that sign-in email is unavailable. It presents no credential field, demo account, local-login action, or session bypass. **Acceptance:** Visit sign-in without configured mail/provider; see unavailable state and attempt to obtain a session without a valid native proof.

clauses.title: Native sign-in
clauses.text: Base operator-auth over Orbit's own operators: configured email-link delivery sends only to an existing active operator, gives the same request response for unknown and inactive addresses, and exchanges a hashed, single-use link, confirmed by POST from a read-only confirmation page within 15 minutes, for a secure native session. An optional linked identity provider (an Auth install) admits only existing operators and stays off until the owner turns it on. Return locations stay inside the operator app. Sign-out revokes that session. A missing or failed mail configuration cannot issue a session. Orbit’s sign-in path, brand and theme are declared in `src/identity.ts`. **Acceptance:** Request and confirm a native magic link, test unknown/inactive and expired/reused links, sign out and exercise optional linked identity without admitting new operators.

clauses.title: Export contents
clauses.text: The buyer can export and restore contacts, companies, opportunities, associations, custom data, source definitions without secrets, signals and captured evidence, evaluations with policy versions, recommendations, drafts, outbound content/status, tasks, timeline, notifications, settings, reports and audit as versioned data. Both supported archive paths disclose their format and eligible receiving state. Installation-local sessions, identity proofs, source/OAuth credentials, delegation authority, private import originals/custody and collaborator/public-form authority do not travel; reconnection and renewed authorization are explicit. DATA-003 extends these guarantees to every target feature. This records Orbit's installation-authority replacement for literal BASE-DATA-001 credential portability; it does not claim that excluded private originals are portable product records. **Acceptance:** Export through both supported archive doors, restore into eligible empty product state, export again and compare domain contents, captured evidence and audit with declared authority exclusions.

clauses.title: Contact erasure
clauses.text: Within 5 minutes of an operator deleting a contact, their email addresses, signal payloads, drafts, message bodies, and the notifications naming them are absent from records, search results, exports, and every later AI or mail request. Only audit entries survive, with the contact's reference anonymized, as BASE-DATA-003 requires. **Acceptance:** Delete a contact containing aliases, imported/captured mail and notes, drafts and transfer copies; verify search/export/AI/mail absence and anonymized audit within five minutes, including replay.

clauses.title: Selected application authority
clauses.text: The 27 September native delegation outcome supersedes BASE-ACCESS-002 and BASE-ACCESS-004 only for `/api/delegation/v1/`: an allowlisted application exchanges a single-use consent code bound to the native operator, workspace, exact callback, PKCE challenge, scopes and selected targets for a bearer credential expiring within 30 days. Ambient cookies confer no authority there. Every operation rechecks scope, expiry, active operator, enabled application and revocation; restore invalidates authority. Native consent, settings and task editing still require the operator session. `crm.evidence.read` reads only selected records, and lists them (with the handoffs on selected opportunities) by name and target ID only, so an application can offer them by name. `crm.handoff.write` permits only `orbit.handoff.upsert`, an internal task with title, description, assignee, due time and open/completed/canceled status. It confers no outreach or account-activation authority. Writes bind current source and audience revisions and commit task, timeline, contact provenance and receipt atomically. Exact key replay produces one effect; changed content conflicts. Immutable receipts remain separate from current authorized source readback. Native UI edits the same records. Actual archives retain tasks and contact provenance, exclude codes, credentials and receipts, and revoke restored-installation authority. Full verification includes the delegation D1, archive and native-browser regressions as well as all retained contract gates. **Acceptance:** Authorize selected records through native consent and PKCE, read and propose a handoff, refuse outside scope, revoke immediately, and restore without restoring credential authority.

nonGoals: A second workspace
Roles, territories, or private records
A second pipeline
Workflow builder
Bulk campaigns or sequences
Autonomous customer outreach
SMS, phone, or social sending
Attachments on outbound messages
Email or digest notifications
A tracking script, cross-site tracking, fingerprinting, or data-broker identity resolution
Hosted forms or landing-page building
Marketing CMS, ads, or multi-touch attribution
Per-record currencies
Plan or pricing pages
Revenue forecasting
Subscription billing or plan enforcement
Native mobile applications

operatingCost.assumptions: Cloudflare platform only, excluding buyer-selected mail and AI adapters: Workers Free is the $0 default while daily Worker requests stay at or below 100000, D1 stays at or below 5000000 rows read and 100000 rows written per day, R2 stays within its monthly free tier, and Queues stays at or below 10000 operations per day. Workers Paid is required to sustain the declared 600 signed-ingress requests per minute (864000 requests/day): 600 * 60 * 24 * 30 = 25920000 monthly Worker requests, or 15920000 above the 10000000 Standard-plan inclusion. At $0.30 per additional million, that is $4.78 request overage plus the $5 monthly Paid minimum, rounded up to the $10 high; this excludes CPU, D1 overages, and future Queue fan-out, which must be measured before those capabilities ship. One public IP at the declared 300 requests per minute reaches the Free Worker request ceiling in about 5.6 hours. Sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/pricing/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/platform/pricing/
