seeds.name: Nook
seeds.oneLiner: Keep team conversations, decisions and commitments together so work stays clear.
seeds.summary: Keep team conversations, decisions and commitments together so work stays clear.

clauses.title: Current identity and conversation membership (C1)
clauses.text: Every private API validates current active identity and current conversation membership. Search/replay/outcomes use the same policy. Workspace admins cannot read arbitrary DMs. **Acceptance evidence:** Through signed-in HTTP, SSR, search, replay and generated loaders, revoke or expire a session and remove a participant; every subsequent private read/write is refused, including a workspace admin attempting another person’s DM.

clauses.title: Atomic messages, retries and replay (C2)
clauses.text: Messages commit atomically with per-conversation event sequence and client intent key. Identical retries return the same message; changed retry payload conflicts. Replay pages preserve ordering; edits use compare-and-swap versions; deletes tombstone and erase original body from live revisions. **Acceptance evidence:** Send through the conversation API, repeat the same intent after a lost acknowledgement, then change its payload; observe one ordered message, the original retry result and a conflict for changed intent. Race edits and delete; replay shows current tombstones without deleted bodies.

clauses.title: Fixed DMs and channel membership (C3)
clauses.text: DMs have fixed participants. Channel owners control membership. Removal revokes reads and writes immediately, including replay and search. New members currently see entire channel history; UI and docs must disclose this. **Acceptance evidence:** Create channel/private/DM conversations through the app, add a channel member after earlier messages, and observe full-history disclosure and access. Remove that member and deny history/search/replay/files immediately; refuse DM participant changes and unrelated-admin DM access.

clauses.title: Decisions and commitments (C4)
clauses.text: A decision has a human author, conversation scope and immutable version history. Only its author revises it with version comparison. A commitment can become accepted only through the assignee's action. Completion is reported, never labelled verified. **Acceptance evidence:** From a discussion, record a decision and propose a commitment. Another participant cannot revise the decision or accept for the assignee; the assignee accepts the exact version and reports completion. Reopen history and see human authorship, source context and reported status.

clauses.title: Read cursors and attention (C5)
clauses.text: Read cursors persist per user and conversation, are monotonic and cannot exceed durable frontier. Attention/unread is separate from accepted responsibility. **Acceptance evidence:** Read a thread from two sessions, reconnect one, and observe monotonic unread recovery with own sends excluded. Refuse read markers beyond the durable frontier; closing Attention does not accept work or mark unseen messages read.

clauses.title: Offline restore (C6)
clauses.text: Restore is offline into an empty database with version and checksum verification and SQLite integrity checking. Current backups contain private content, never live sessions; password hashes belong only to explicitly supported legacy recovery inputs and never become new sign-in authority. No external effects on restore. **Acceptance evidence:** Use rer export/reset/import into an empty stopped installation, complete explicit identity recovery, and compare conversations, memberships, outcome versions, attention and downloaded file bytes. A populated destination, altered checksum or invalid graph is refused; no old delivery or session revives.

clauses.title: Safe rendering and local binding (C7)
clauses.text: Human text renders inertly. No message, plugin, link or AI output can trigger arbitrary code, client-side or credentialed fetching, or provider effects; the only server-side link fetch is NOOK-068's bounded, SSRF-safe preview service. Authorized app/agent/meeting effects require the explicit scoped doors in NOOK-022–030 and NOOK-054–059, not ambient conversation authority. Bounded bodies, session expiry, origin validation for mutations and loopback-only development binding remain required; production requires HTTPS. New sign-in uses invited Base magic links; legacy password hashes remain offline recovery inputs only. **Acceptance evidence:** Post active markup and malformed/oversized bodies through public APIs; markup stays inert and invalid input fails without writes. Cross-origin mutations, foreign sessions and unsafe local origins fail; production output excludes dev admission.

clauses.title: Evidence limits (C8)
clauses.text: The complete target in this contract remains an obligation until its acceptance evidence exists. Local tests, synthetic imports and substituted network edges establish only their bounded paths; hosted scale, legal/compliance operation, real inbox/device receipt, native push and live provider integrations require separate evidence. Missing proof changes the status, never the scope. Delivery/provider acceptance, device display, human reading and action are distinct facts. **Acceptance evidence:** For a release candidate, reproduce the documented local public-door journeys, then separately record hosted multi-device, provider, migration and capacity results before those target clauses become done. Failed or unmeasured end states remain visible.

clauses.title: Backup and export (C9)
clauses.text: Two full backup paths ship, neither an ordinary app-admin export. On a local install, the filesystem operator uses local-only `rer export` and `rer import` on a stopped checkout; operator disk access explicitly bypasses app privacy. For a hosted install, the [hosted backup/export path](docs/backups.md#export-a-hosted-nook) uses the owner’s `/export` download or the documented `node --input-type=module` command calling `scripts/local/remote-export.mjs` from a checkout with dependencies installed; it exports the authoritative D1 database records and actual private R2 object bytes into an owner-held verified archive with its erasure journal. Nook's `/export` and `/api/portability` doors admit only an active owner's current session and authorize no import. [Base's hosted-data rule](https://github.com/runeditrun/base/blob/main/export/RUN-LOCALLY.md#if-hosted-deployment-stops) distinguishes this from local-only `rer export`, which refuses a hosted origin: a platform D1 SQL export alone omits R2 files and cannot satisfy this full-backup guarantee. Restore is always local, into an empty destination, and validates table identities, foreign references, schema ledger and event/read frontiers. Archives exclude sessions and sign-in tokens. User-readable and policy-scoped exits are required by NOOK-047; this clause retains the full-backup guarantee and its explicit operator-custody exception. **Acceptance evidence:** **Local:** Stop the install, export with `rer export`, import into an empty stopped local install, complete explicit identity recovery and re-export; compare equivalent records, private media bytes and erasure journal. **Hosted:** Sign in as an active owner, follow the hosted backup/export path through `/export` and the documented helper command to download D1 records plus R2 bytes into an owner-held archive, import it into an empty stopped local install and complete identity recovery; compare records, file bytes, rebuilt search and erasure journal. Reject non-owner/expired hosted sessions and any remote restore. Inspect both archives for private records and media, with live credentials, devices and pending deliveries excluded.

clauses.title: Commitment revision and cancellation (C10)
clauses.text: Material text/deadline revision requires renewed assignee acceptance at the exact new version. Assignee and conversation are fixed; changing assignee means explicit cancellation and a fresh proposal, and scope cannot move across conversations. Cancellation is explicit, terminal and versioned; authors may cancel proposals/accepted work but cannot claim assignee completion. Deleted source refs become null; event rows preserve opaque sequence/object facts, never message bodies. Replay clients fetch current object state under current ACL and interpret tombstones. **Acceptance evidence:** Accept a proposal and revise its text/deadline: renewed acceptance is required at the new version. Cancel and create a new proposal to change the fixed assignee. Refuse stale acceptance, cross-conversation moves and author impersonation of completion; cancellation stays terminal in history and deleted source refs reveal no body.

clauses.title: Cached retries, synchronization and complete history (C11)
clauses.text: Cached retry responses require current ACL before lookup. Reads synchronize monotonically across sessions; replay cursors indicate per-conversation sequence and bounded catch-up, not read receipts. History pages must cover the complete tested log rather than silently truncate. **Acceptance evidence:** Page beyond the tested history window and reconnect after missed edit/delete events. Repeat a previously successful intent after membership revocation; it must be denied before cached response lookup, with no missing or duplicated durable history.

clauses.title: Private attachments (C12)
clauses.text: Attachments are 1 byte–25 MiB per file, five ordered files per message, with at most 50 pending/staged native uploads per uploader and no aggregate workspace byte quota. Actual bytes reside in private R2; D1 holds metadata and opaque object keys. Plain UTF-8 text, signature-checked PNG/JPEG/PDF only; forced attachment downloads plus private inline PNG/JPEG previews after structural byte validation and opt-in plain-text previews bounded to 64 KiB; no inline PDF preview or virus-scanning claim. Staged uploads last24h for binding/read eligibility, are uploader-only under current conversation ACL, and do not create attention. Unused staged bytes remain until explicitly removed. Binding uploader-owned same-conversation IDs and message/intent/event is atomic; exact ID order belongs to retry identity. Downloads recheck current membership; delete erases live bytes/name/checksum, and message deletion cascades. The media baseline archivev2 carries actual bytes plus hashes, state and binding; historical archivev3 retains these guarantees plus C13 triage and supports explicit prior-v1/v2 migration; current normalized Base portability archives retain the same custody guarantees, as described below. Backups/WAL/remnants retain their stated physical-erasure limits. These limits are the shipped baseline, not the target: NOOK-061 widens admission to any file type up to 1 GiB with in-app previews, malware scanning and admin file-type policy while keeping every custody guarantee in this clause. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload and bind ordered private files through the app, preview genuine PNG/JPEG and download exact bytes as an authorized participant. Deny outsiders and removed members, reject active/corrupt/oversized input, recover lost-put acknowledgements and verify deletion and backup round-trip.

clauses.title: Calm attention (C13)
clauses.text: Calm attention is explicit per-user triage, independent of unread and outcome authority. GET/PATCH `/api/conversations/:id/preferences` accepts boolean `muted`/`followed`, requires current membership, and returns those choices plus followed root-thread IDs. POST `/api/messages/:id/follow {follow:boolean}` targets a live root thread under current ACL. Choices persist across sessions; changes affect future routing only. Muting suppresses routine follows, never explicit mentions or commitment proposals. Automatic following when a member authors, replies in or is mentioned in a thread, and of every thread in a one-to-one DM, is NOOK-072 and writes this same followed state; an unfollow through this door also ends an automatic follow. Message sends accept ordered unique `mentions` (at most50 current member IDs), boolean `urgent`, and `urgentReason` (1–240 characters when urgent). Urgent requests require explicit recipients. All current channel members can see the message's Notified names, Urgent marker and urgent reason, including members who were not notified. Defaults `[]`, `false`, `null` join immutable intent identity. Identical committed retries survive recipient removal without rerouting; new sends revalidate recipients. Attention creation is atomic with durable message/outcome events and stores opaque references, not copied bodies. Precedence: urgent-request, mention, thread-follow, conversation-follow. Proposals and material revisions route to assignees; assignee actions route updates to authors. Self-authored events do not create self-attention. GET `/api/attention` returns current-ACL hydrated active items, `deferredCount`, `dndUntil`. Deleted sources hydrate tombstones, with no urgent-reason copy. GET/PATCH `/api/settings {dndUntil:epochMilliseconds|null}` controls quiet time. Quiet time defers routine items while urgent in-app requests remain visible; external delivery follows C14 email and C15 Web Push, and there is no paging guarantee. POST `/api/attention/:id {action:done|snooze,until?:epochMilliseconds}` requires item ownership and current ACL. Quiet/snooze deadlines must be future times within seven days. Snoozed items become eligible when due; routine items remain deferred during quiet time. Done changes only triage. Reading or accepting a commitment does not automatically close attention, and closing attention never accepts work. Schema5 preserves prior ledgers and appends explicit defaults to live prior intent payloads; erased markers remain erased. Archivev3 retains follows/preferences/quiet time/triage and validates source/event/scope references. Explicit v1/v2 imports add empty attention tables and normalize prior retry identity. Old-format archives cannot carry nonempty new attention state. Root SQLite v3 and native D1 recovery formats require an explicit separately verified mapping; a source manifest alone does not establish compatibility. C13 admission clarification: defaults apply only to omitted mentions/urgent fields, not explicit null. Explicit mentions:null or urgent:null is400 with no committed event/message/attention. Recovered dnd_until must be null or a safe integer; expired valid integers remain legal recovery values. Quiet-time domain checks precede database insertion. **Acceptance evidence:** At 1440 and 390, follow a thread, mute its channel, send explicit mentions/urgent requests, snooze and complete triage, and enter quiet time. Restart and sign in elsewhere: preferences persist, due items return under current ACL, and neither triage nor reads accepts responsibility. Automatic follows from authoring, replying, mentions and one-to-one DMs are proved under NOOK-072; an unfollow through `POST /api/messages/:id/follow {follow:false}` ends one.

clauses.title: Email notifications (C14)
clauses.text: Email notifications reach a member away from the browser under this delivery contract. Emailable events are an explicit mention, an urgent request, a commitment proposal or material revision to its assignee, and a completion report to its author; routine thread or conversation follows, reactions, replies without a mention, accept/cancel updates and imported history are never emailed. The destination is the member's own sign-in email (an active account, verified by its sign-in link); there is no free-form address. Every member's email is off until that member turns it on in their own settings, per account: one choice covers mentions and commitments, a second covers urgent requests, with a separate choice to let urgent requests through quiet time. GET/PATCH `/api/notify {mentions,urgent,urgentQuiet:boolean}` reads and changes the caller's choices. Turning a choice off stops the next email: each queued item is checked again when its email is built. Every email carries a link that turns email off without a session (`/notify/off`: opening it shows one button and changes nothing, because mail scanners open links; the button turns all three choices off) and a link to the signed-in settings. Queue rows are written in the same batch as the attention rows, only for recipients who turned the matching email on, and hold opaque references (recipient, conversation, actor, message or commitment, reason), never message text, file names or addresses. The ChatHub alarm drains them; pending rows keep it armed, so delivery needs no open socket and a restarted Worker resumes from D1. When an email is built, nothing is sent to an inactive member, about a conversation the member can no longer read, about a deleted or erased source, after the choice was turned off, or for an item the member already marked done or a mention they already read; each is cancelled with that reason. Quiet time (C13 `dndUntil`) holds every item until it ends; an urgent request goes through quiet time only when its recipient chose that. Each event is queued once per recipient (keyed by its attention item), so identical retries add nothing; a burst within five seconds folds into one email, and a recipient gets at most one email per conversation per ten minutes, with later items folded into a count. A failed send is retried after 15 s, 1 min, 5 min, 30 min and 2 h, then given up; a definite refusal is not retried, and a send the provider did not confirm, or that a stopped Worker may have made, is never repeated. A send being retried or given up shows as "email not delivered" with its reason class (not set up, refused, rate limited, not confirmed) to its recipient, to the member whose message caused it and to the owner for seven days, never as a silent success. Emails name the sender, the conversation (`#name`, or "a direct conversation") and a link; they never carry message text, file names, urgent reasons or commitment wording. This no-text form is today's behaviour and the `sender` level an owner policy can force; a member's opt-in to message text in email is NOOK-062's obligation. Hosted mail goes through the same configured sender as sign-in (the owner deployment's provider). Local development sends and stores no email and exposes no mail viewer. Tests fake only the provider network edge. Accepted by the mail provider is not proof of inbox receipt, and a test provider's acceptance is not live delivery. Urgent stays an in-app request, not paging; Web Push follows C15; there is no SMS or native push. Archives carry members' choices but not the queue, so a restore sends nothing old; erasure removes a member's choices and queued items and an erased message's items. **Acceptance evidence:** Run the emitted-Worker notification journey through sign-in and settings with only the provider network edge substituted: opt in, mention/propose, fold bursts, hold quiet items, cancel read/deleted/revoked items, restart a retry, expose refusal/uncertainty and use the scanner-safe unsubscribe POST. Inspect that mail contains no private body or file name.

clauses.title: Public documentation from Markdown
clauses.text: Public user documentation is rendered from Markdown sources declared in `docs/site.json`. Every root and `docs/` Markdown file is published or has a reason for remaining GitHub-only; missing files, links and heading anchors fail the build. Raw HTML in a page is reported and never rendered. **Acceptance evidence:** Build and open /docs; every declared page renders, links and anchors resolve, raw HTML remains inert, and every root/docs Markdown source is published or has a recorded exclusion reason. The app Lobby and private workspace keep their existing routes.

clauses.title: Member, message and imported-author erasure
clauses.text: Current owners/admins may erase accessible channel messages; roles never open an operator DM door. Authors retain their own delete/remove actions. Owners may erase eligible other members; admins only accounts with the member role, including guest access; self and the last active owner are refused. Every destructive commit guards current session, role and scope. Count-only preview, explicit confirmation and a subject-free receipt accompany operator erasure. Authored content, credentials and selected import copies are erased; authored work retains only scope/kind/version count/state. Other authors retain work and state without erased assignee/action attribution. Separate credential-free structural tombstones preserve threads, counters, fixed DM audiences and immutable import ownership; audit attribution and subject references are independently anonymised. D1 atomically records public Base erasure fences and durable blob obligations before R2 deletion. Completion requires verified blob absence, including resolution of uncertain puts; larger work remains pending with bounded continuation. Latest archives carry the journal and restore normally. Old archives are refused by nonempty-destination guards or the latest journal; a virgin destination without a later journal cannot recognize them. External archives, offline copies, provider backups/Time Travel and physical remnants remain outside logical erasure. **Acceptance evidence:** Through Team and message erasure doors, preview counts, confirm and resume a pending job. Try an unrelated DM, an insufficient role, self and last owner; deny each. Remove native/imported content and verified R2 bytes, preserve only declared structural tombstones, anonymise audit, and refuse an older archive when the latest erasure journal is supplied.

clauses.title: Web Push (C15)
clauses.text: Web Push is a separate opt-in channel under C14's current-identity, current-ACL, source, read/done, quiet-time, retry, visible-failure and no-paging rules. Migration 0023 preserves existing email rows and choices. **Defaults for a new member:** once the member grants browser notification permission, and without opening settings, DMs, mentions (including NOOK-065 broadcast mentions), keyword hits (NOOK-032), call invites (NOOK-022) and replies in followed threads (including NOOK-072 automatic follows) are on, matching Slack's default of desktop and mobile notifications for DMs, mentions and keywords; urgent-through-quiet starts off. Each member may change any of them, and owners set the organization defaults under NOOK-060. GET/PATCH `/api/notify` adds `push:{mentions,urgent,urgentQuiet,direct,threads,keywords,calls:boolean}`. Mentions covers the same commitment events as email. Ordinary DMs and followed-thread replies can push without changing email or in-app Attention. Conversation-follow for Attention alone never pushes; only a conversation set to the NOOK-032 `all new messages` level pushes each new root message and channel-broadcast thread reply. Explicit urgent and mention reasons take precedence and require their own choice; a routine followed reply precedes ordinary DM when both are enabled. Routine follows and DMs respect mute; self-authored and imported events never push. POST `/api/devices {transport:"webpush",subscription:{endpoint,keys:{p256dh,auth},expirationTime?:number|null}}` registers only the caller's browser subscription under the current session. GET returns only the instance VAPID public key and the caller's opaque device IDs, transport and timestamps. DELETE `/api/devices {id}` removes only an owned device. Endpoint ownership cannot transfer between accounts: unsubscribe in the browser before enabling another account. At most ten devices per person; HTTPS endpoints are restricted to the supported Apple, Google and Mozilla push hosts, keys must be valid P-256/16-byte material, redirects are refused. This browser door accepts only `transport:"webpush"` and rejects every other transport; native iOS and Android devices register their APNs, PushKit or FCM tokens through the native device door and push path that NOOK-078 defines, and desktop apps receive over their own authenticated connection to the installation. Web Push needs no publisher service: each installation signs with its own VAPID key and sends straight to the browser vendor's push service. Each delivery rechecks the device's original session, active version, membership, preferences, native source and unread/triage state. Expired or revoked sessions and provider-expired subscriptions retire the device. One durable queue row per event, recipient and device prevents duplicate alerts from overlapping reasons and successful-device repeats during another device's retry. Email and push have independent five-second gathering and ten-minute conversation folding windows; push windows are per device. The first due eligible item gathers the already-queued eligible burst, including items still in their initial gathering period; future retries, snoozes and quiet-held items stay deferred. A counted push uses one opaque delivery ID for the whole burst, and remains current while any folded item remains current. A conditional sending lease becomes visibly not-confirmed if interrupted, and uncertain network sends are never repeated. Failure classes show to the recipient, the sender and the owner for seven days; terminal delivery metadata lasts thirty days. Read and done transactions cancel pending push. Snoozes and quiet time defer delivery; only the separately enabled urgent-through-quiet choice overrides quiet time. POST `/api/devices/presence {id,page,visible:boolean}` records a current-session visible-page heartbeat. Today fresh visible presence holds all of the member's Web Push; NOOK-073's cross-device active-elsewhere rule replaces that hold for Web Push exactly as for native push: a focused page with recent input is an active desktop client, Web Push to the member's phones and tablets is held while they are active on desktop and released or cancelled under NOOK-073, and the active client itself shows the alert in-app. Open sockets alone never count as presence. Foreground pages renew every fifteen seconds, hidden pages release, and the alarm automatically releases expired forty-five-second presence. No browser page is needed for delivery. GET `/api/devices/sync` supplies current opaque delivered-notification IDs and badge count for foreground synchronization; the count includes unread active attention and ordinary push-enabled DM events, deduplicated across devices. Web Push uses RFC 8291 encrypted payloads and RFC 8292 VAPID. The instance generates its key pair once on first authenticated use, storing the private key AES-GCM encrypted under a key derived from SESSION_SECRET, and sends only its public key to browsers. The encrypted payload contains sender/conversation display wording (DMs use "a direct conversation"), an authenticated same-origin app link with opaque conversation/message IDs, opaque recipient/delivery IDs, notification tag and badge count. No message body, commitment text, urgent reason or file name is included; this is the `sender` preview level, and NOOK-062 adds default-on message-text previews (inside the same encrypted payload), org caps and notification actions. Push services see the endpoint, timing, encrypted packet size, TTL/normal urgency, VAPID public key and signed audience/expiry/contact URI. Subscription endpoints, public encryption keys and auth material remain private D1 records. Archives exclude keys, devices, presence and all delivery state; restored installations send nothing old. Member/message/outcome erasure removes associated push records. Logical erasure cannot retract packets already accepted by a push service or notices already displayed on a sleeping device. The installable PWA preserves Nook's UI and authenticates navigation on every notification tap. Its service worker caches no requests or private content. Permission requests require a gesture; the foreground reconciles allowed subscriptions and visibly reports re-enable failures. The previous open-tab OS notification path is removed; the title count remains. Every Web Push shows a visible notification and can update its badge. No badge-only or clear-only background Web Push is sent: WebKit revokes silent subscriptions. Foreground authoritative refresh closes read/revoked notices and updates badges through the service worker. Immediate clearing on a sleeping device, native iOS badge updates and Android native normal-priority clears remain blocked until a native transport exists. Browser acceptance is not proof of OS receipt; C8's evidence limits still apply. **Acceptance evidence:** Run pnpm test:push through subscription, preferences, emitted Worker and real alarm; independently decrypt the RFC 8291 packet and verify VAPID, revocation, quiet/read cancellation, per-device folding and visible failure. Separately demonstrate foreground/background/locked-device visible notification, tap authentication and badge reconciliation on supported Safari, Chromium and Firefox devices. **Defaults:** a newly invited member grants browser permission in a fresh profile without opening settings, and a DM, a mention and a keyword hit each show exactly one notification; a channel set to `all new messages` notifies on a colleague's plain message and a channel left at `mentions` does not. **Defaults include automatic follows:** a reply in a thread the member started in a `mentions` channel shows one notification without any explicit follow. **Cross-device routing:** with the member's Chrome page focused and in use, a DM shows on that page and no Web Push reaches their phone's installed PWA; after the page is idle 10 minutes the phone notifies (NOOK-073).

seeds.oneLiner: Grow your audience and send newsletters with reviewed content and delivery reporting.

clauses.title: Lobby and public landing
clauses.text: An installed Mango answers its sessionless root (`/`) with Base's shared Lobby (`src/base/lobby.ts`, edition identity in `src/identity.ts`): Mango's mark and name, one line about this newsletter, and one action, “Finish setup” (`/setup`) until the owner has saved the sender identity at first-run setup and “Sign in” (`/signin`) after; `GET /setup/state` answers exactly `{"state":"unclaimed"}` or `{"state":"claimed"}` from the same reading (owner decision, 12 October 2026). The landing below is the run site's homepage (`run-mango.com`, built by `rer build --site` from `src/site/pages.tsx`), where the primary action reads “Run Mango” and opens the Run page (`/run`) and no link reaches sign-in; everything else about it is unchanged. The landing is a static page for Mango's default newsletter profile, drawn in one hand-illustrated style. Its header carries Mango's mark and name with links to How it works, Docs (`/docs`) and, on an installed Mango's docs pages, the page's only link named “Sign in” (`/signin`). Its hero headline is the page's only top-level heading; directly under the lead, one line reads “100% free, open source alternative to Mailchimp and Klaviyo” with the two product names in bold and the wording unchanged (the same sentence, as plain text, ends the page's meta description, and `seed.json` `replaces` names both products), naming what Mango replaces without comparing against it; the hero offers “Start your newsletter” (`/docs/install`) and “Read the docs” (`/docs`). Sections then cover how a letter leaves Mango (collect, write, approve, schedule, deliver), consent, approval of the exact letter, scheduling, delivery reports and ownership, followed by a closing call to action; the footer repeats the section links, Docs and (on an installed Mango) operator sign-in and shows the configured deployment owner's name and one-line description. It may show the static credit `Powered by Mango · runeditrun.com` only when the owner enables it in configuration. It describes only capabilities the newsletter profile ships and contains no vendor pricing, testimonials, customer logos, ratings, metrics, cross-store claims, third-party brand logos or telemetry; sample addresses, names, counts and dates inside its drawings are pictures, never records. It reads no operator, contact or campaign record and no session, sets no cookies, is written once by the site build, serves every font, style, icon and image from the site's own origin (its drawings are inline), keeps its own fixed light palette in a dark-themed browser, and stays fully readable without scripts and with reduced motion.

clauses.title: Public documentation
clauses.text: The public paths `/docs` and `/docs/<slug>` serve Mango's first-party operator documentation: the Markdown files that `docs/site.json` lists as published, in the sections and order it gives, which is the only navigation, with the first page as the docs home at `/docs` (and `/docs/`). The Markdown is rendered to HTML at build time: a Vite plugin renders each page to static HTML when Vite loads it, in a build and in development, and never in the Worker or the browser. The emitted Worker and client bundles contain no Markdown or syntax-highlighting code, and each page is its own lazily loaded chunk that the Worker renders per request. A page has its title as its one top-level heading, a section sidebar listing the pages in manifest order with the current one marked, an on-this-page list of its sections, previous and next links, and a "Contents" disclosure for narrow screens, inside the public landing's shared header (with Docs marked as the current section) and footer, in the landing's palette, faces and paper drawings. Every Markdown file at the repository root, under `docs/` and as a top-level `<directory>/README.md` is either published or listed in the manifest as not published with a reason, and an unlisted file, a broken link or anchor, a link to a page the site does not publish, raw HTML, an image outside `docs/media/` or an absolute build-machine path fails verification or the build. The pages link to no source repository and offer no edit link. Published pages describe the default newsletter profile and contain no maintainer-only material. The documentation reads no workspace record, session or database row, sets no cookie, runs no analytics or tracking and loads only same-origin resources. An unknown, miscased or nested slug, and `/docs/index`, answer `404` with a short not-found page in the same shared header and footer that links back to `/docs` and `/`; a request for another host is answered as it is for every other path.

clauses.title: Operators and the default role
clauses.text: Until an owner assigns roles (OPER-004), every operator holds the Admin role and can see and act on every proposal, campaign, flow, contact, and setting. First-run `/setup` requires a native session and valid business sender identity before app documents open, on both server and client navigation. Saving through the existing sender settings authority completes setup; valid existing environment identity also counts. This navigation gate does not deny authenticated configuration APIs or claim provider readiness.

clauses.title: Management
clauses.text: Operators are invited and removed in settings. An invitation requires fresh email proof from the signed-in operator; a session without that proof cannot grant another operator access. Settings can request a confirmation link bound to the current session so the operator can confirm and retry the invitation. Confirmation GET and HEAD remain read-only; affirmative POST supplies the proof. The operator configured at setup can be removed only by themselves. *Policy: `operator.management.v1`; default: any operator may invite with fresh email proof or remove.*

clauses.title: Removal does not rewrite history
clauses.text: Removing an operator revokes their sessions and leaves every proposal, approval, revision, and audit entry attributed to them intact.

clauses.title: Store and event connections
clauses.text: One or more connections (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Stripe, Square, Stall and the events API: INT-001 to INT-007), each made by the owner from Settings with no developer step (for Shopify, INT-015), import customers, products, variants, inventory, orders, refunds, carts, checkouts, subscriptions and browsing events through `commerce.store.v1`, retaining each source record's identifier, connection and occurrence time. Each connection declares the source types it supplies (STORE-006); a contact seen through two connections is one contact (CONT-001) with both sources' records.

clauses.title: Source identity
clauses.text: A commerce webhook or scheduled sync carrying a source identifier already stored updates that source record; it never creates a second customer, order, cart, refund, or browsing event.

clauses.title: Freshness
clauses.text: The Decision Desk shows, per source type, the completion time of the last successful sync and the error of any sync that has failed since it.

clauses.title: Source failure
clauses.text: If the configured commerce adapter is unavailable, ingestion and proposal generation record a failed operation carrying the adapter's error; saved drafts and already recorded delivery outcomes remain readable and no campaign is sent as a side effect.

clauses.title: Stale sources block approval
clauses.text: A source type is stale when its last successful sync completed more than 24 hours ago or a sync has failed since it. A proposal or campaign whose inclusion or exclusion rule reads a stale source type is labeled stale and cannot be approved until that source type syncs successfully.

clauses.title: Declared adapter capability
clauses.text: The commerce connection declares which source types it supplies. An audience rule, exclusion, or proposal that requires a source type the connection does not supply is shown as unavailable and cannot be approved; it never resolves to an empty or partial audience.

clauses.title: Ingestion latency
clauses.text: A source record from an accepted commerce webhook is readable in the operator app within 60 seconds of the webhook being acknowledged.

clauses.title: Contact identity
clauses.text: Email addresses are compared case-insensitively after trimming, phone numbers are stored in E.164 form, and one canonical email address or phone number identifies at most one contact.

clauses.title: Channel status
clauses.text: Each contact has an independent state per channel: *pending* (consent captured, confirmation outstanding), *subscribed*, *non-subscribed* (no consent evidence recorded), *unsubscribed* (opted out), or *suppressed* (blocked by CONT-006 or CONT-013). Only *subscribed* is eligible for a marketing send. Store activity or consent on one channel never changes the other channel's state.

clauses.title: Consent evidence
clauses.text: Every subscription stores the channel, brand or legal sender, SMS sender or program where applicable, message subject or category, disclosed frequency, destination jurisdiction, capture method and source, occurrence time, consent text and version, and confirmation evidence. Consent applies only to that recorded scope and current recipient; a capture or import without the evidence creates a non-subscribed contact, except where the contact arrives subscribed from an incumbent or a connected store with the incumbent-held evidence CONT-024 defines, and a phone number reported as reassigned or no longer belonging to that recipient becomes non-subscribed until fresh evidence is captured.

clauses.title: Opt-out precedence
clauses.text: An email unsubscribe, one-click unsubscribe, or SMS opt-out sets that channel to unsubscribed before the request is acknowledged, and excludes it from every draft, scheduled campaign, and queued recipient-step. Later imports, syncs, store events, merges, or operator edits never reverse it. During a parallel run (MOVE-013), opt-outs and suppressions the incumbent reports apply the same way, and Mango's are written back to the incumbent.

clauses.title: Resubscription
clauses.text: A previously unsubscribed channel becomes subscribed only from new affirmative consent evidence recorded after the opt-out and confirmed per CONT-009. A suppressed channel also requires the suppression cause to be resolved. An operator edit alone cannot resubscribe either state. A person resubscribes themselves through a public form under CONT-027. During a parallel run (MOVE-013), a confirmed resubscribe is written back to the incumbent as subscribed where its API allows; otherwise it is listed in the cutover report (MOVE-006).

clauses.title: Email suppression
clauses.text: A hard bounce, spam complaint, or provider suppression suppresses that email address before the next hand-off to any campaign. Soft bounces are recorded and visible, and suppress the address according to the bounce policy; a later provider-confirmed delivery resets its consecutive-soft-bounce count. These facts arrive through the signed delivery webhook Mango creates when the sending provider is connected (DELIV-008); an installation whose webhook step has not passed cannot approve, so no address keeps being mailed after a bounce Mango could not see. *Policy: `contact.soft-bounce.v1`; default: suppress after three consecutive soft bounces.* - **2026-10-08 local authority clarification (CONT-004/006, OPER-001):** Refreshing local session/setup credentials while retaining D1 preserves the effective contact hash authority, including suppression and surviving opt-out records without contact rows. New local installations record a versioned independent contact salt in `.dev.vars`; missing, empty, unknown-version or unversioned authority fails closed. Explicit conversion of a verified legacy session-key installation retains its original effective session authority before rotating authentication credentials. An upgrade must never select a previously unused secret merely because it exists.

clauses.title: SMS compliance replies
clauses.text: A signed inbound SMS webhook consumes the adapter's canonical result for that sender, program, and destination jurisdiction. STOP, STOPALL, END, QUIT, CANCEL, UNSUBSCRIBE, OPTOUT, and REVOKE always opt out; HELP and INFO request help; START and UNSTOP begin the fresh-consent flow required by CONT-005 and never subscribe by themselves. Mango records each reply once and applies an opt-out before acknowledging the webhook. It returns the configured compliance response only when the provider has not already sent the required reply.

clauses.title: Contact history
clauses.text: A contact page shows source activity, consent changes, suppressions, campaign eligibility decisions, channel deliveries, and operator actions in time order. *Acceptance:* the native Worker/D1 contact-history journey shows those categories together at their original occurrence times, including confirmation, approved eligibility, dispatch exclusions, channel hand-offs and provider outcomes. At 1440 and 390 pixels, older events remain reachable, unrelated contacts and private payloads remain absent, and each event retains its source.

clauses.title: Confirmation
clauses.text: Where the opt-in policy requires confirmation for a channel, a contact captured with consent on it enters *pending* and receives one confirmation message on that channel; following its opaque per-contact confirmation link sets the channel to *subscribed* and stores the confirming request's time. A pending channel receives no marketing send, and a confirmation link stops working 30 days after it is issued. Where the policy does not require confirmation, the captured consent evidence of CONT-003 sets the channel to *subscribed* directly. An operator chooses single or double opt-in per form and per source under CONT-025. *Policy: `contact.opt-in.v1`; default: confirmation is required on both channels for Mango's own forms, popups, landing pages and API captures; CONT-025 states each source's default.*

clauses.title: Import
clauses.text: An operator imports contacts from a CSV whose rows carry an email address or phone number and, optionally, the consent evidence CONT-003 requires. Each row is validated independently; a row matching an existing canonical identifier updates that contact rather than creating a second; re-running the same file changes nothing further. The import reports created, updated, and rejected row counts with a reason per rejected row, and never sets a channel to subscribed for a contact CONT-004 has unsubscribed. A file the owner names as an export from another platform can carry that platform's subscribed status as incumbent-held evidence (CONT-024) under the owner's once-per-source attestation; a file with no named source stays under CONT-003's per-row rule. One review holds up to the import-row floor SCALE-001 sets.

clauses.title: Merge
clauses.text: An operator can merge two contacts. The surviving contact keeps the union of source activity, consent records, campaign history, and suppressions, and takes the most restrictive state per channel: suppressed beats unsubscribed, which beats non-subscribed, which beats pending, which beats subscribed. A merge cannot resubscribe a channel.

clauses.title: Dormancy without deletion
clauses.text: A contact with no recorded click, order, or consent change inside the dormancy window is labeled dormant and excluded by the audience policy (AUD-003, AUD-008). Each of these counts at the time it originally happened, including clicks, orders and consent changes a move-in imports with the time the incumbent recorded (MOVE-001 to MOVE-005, MOVE-009); opens never count. A contact whose move-in carried no engagement history for them is labeled `no-history`, not dormant, and their dormancy window starts when that move-in completed, so a migrated list is never excluded as dormant for lack of history Mango was never given. A dormant contact whose only imported activity inside the window is opens is labeled `open-only` within dormant, because Apple Mail Privacy Protection and image proxies make those opens unreliable (RESULT-002). Mango never deletes, unsubscribes, or suppresses a contact for inactivity; BASE-DATA-002 stands, and clearing a dormant list is an operator action.

clauses.title: Erasure and surviving opt-out
clauses.text: Deleting a contact removes their profile, source activity, consent evidence, message content, and delivery detail within five minutes, confirms completion, and anonymizes their actor identity in retained audit entries as BASE-DATA-003 requires. For each known unsubscribed or suppressed channel identity, including opted-out aliases, it retains an opt-out record with a one-way destination hash keyed with the installation secret, the channel, reason, and time. It also retains the `audience_portable_hashes` mapping from that local hash to the unsalted SHA-256 of `mango-audience-export-v1:` followed by the destination. Contacts CSV exports carry restrictions under this portable hash even after erasure, and complete local archives carry the retained mapping. These values contain no readable address but are not anonymous: a holder of a mapping or export can compare hashes of guessed addresses or an address dictionary without the installation secret, and the stable portable hash allows matching across installations and exports. Treat the retained mappings and exports as sensitive personal data. A later import, sync, or capture matching the local or portable identity preserves the restriction; erasure opt-outs make that channel unsubscribed. The person's own confirmed resubscribe through a public form is the one way back, and only for an unsubscribe or erasure reason, never a suppression (CONT-027). **Supersedes BASE-DATA-003 only for this opt-out dependency, including its retained portable mapping and exported hashes**; all of that baseline clause's other guarantees and all other personal-data entities remain unchanged. For subscribed identities with no surviving restriction, erasure removes all mapping aliases and retains no address-derived row tombstone. Restore uses source-wide epoch floors: any archive older than known local or supplied current matching authority is refused in full, including unaffected older archives. Nonempty legacy row journals are refused before staging. Upgrade 0044 retires legacy journals and transfers after advancing every known source floor; offline copies without current authority cannot reveal later erasure.

clauses.title: Decision Desk
clauses.text: The Decision Desk lists proposals in the *proposed* state ordered by the proposal policy, highest-ranked first. *Policy: `proposal.selection.v1`; default: rank by expected revenue where this deployment has enough of its own attribution history (RESULT-003) to estimate it, then by the earliest send-by instant; proposals with neither rank last.*

clauses.title: Evidence
clauses.text: A proposal names its triggering source events, lookback window, inclusion rule, exclusion rule, source-data as-of time, send-by instant, proposed channels and step instants, and the method behind every forecast or confidence label.

clauses.title: Counts
clauses.text: A proposal distinguishes candidates, excluded contacts, eligible contacts, and per-channel recipient-steps. No count is labeled recipients until exclusions have been applied.

clauses.title: Content
clauses.text: A proposal contains an editable campaign name, email subject and body, SMS body when SMS is proposed, sender identity, destination links, and a preview for every selected channel.

clauses.title: Owner control
clauses.text: A generated proposal is a draft and cannot schedule or send anything until an operator explicitly approves a particular saved revision.

clauses.title: Grounded generation
clauses.text: AI-generated audience explanations, timing claims, and forecasts use only this deployment's imported store data and configured knowledge, supplied to `ai.provider.v1`. A generation containing a claim not derivable from that evidence is rejected and the proposal is marked failed per PROP-007; no generic marketing copy is substituted.

clauses.title: Generation failure
clauses.text: If the configured AI adapter returns invalid output or does not complete within 60 seconds, the proposal is marked failed carrying the provider error, no semantic fallback is created, and existing proposals and campaigns are unaffected.

clauses.title: Forecast provenance
clauses.text: Every revenue, recovery-rate, or confidence figure names the deployment's own campaigns and store events it was computed from and the number of them. Mango never presents a benchmark drawn from other stores, and where its own history is too thin to compute a figure it says so instead of showing a range.

clauses.title: Proposal states
clauses.text: A proposal is *proposed*, *approved* (an operator approved a revision and a campaign exists), *dismissed* (an operator rejected it, with the reason recorded), *expired* (its send-by instant passed), or *failed* (PROP-007). Only a proposed proposal can be approved or dismissed, and every transition records its actor and time.

clauses.title: Review snapshot
clauses.text: Campaign review shows the audience rule and as-of time, candidate count, each exclusion reason with its count, eligible contact count, and the recipient-step count per channel.

clauses.title: Consent and suppression
clauses.text: Contacts whose state on a channel is pending, non-subscribed, unsubscribed, or suppressed are excluded from that channel regardless of segment membership or an operator-authored inclusion rule.

clauses.title: Commerce and dormancy exclusions
clauses.text: Contacts excluded by the audience policy are listed in review with their reason and count. *Policy: `audience.exclusions.v1`; default: exclude a contact from a product campaign for seven days after purchasing that product, while a refund or return of it is unresolved, and while the contact is dormant under a twelve-month dormancy window (CONT-012).* AUD-008 states which inactivity rule governs a send, what counts for migrated contacts and how an operator turns the dormancy exclusion off for one campaign.

clauses.title: Frequency protection
clauses.text: A contact inside the channel's frequency window is excluded from that step and recorded with the reason `frequency-window`, never silently deferred to a later time. *Policy: `audience.frequency.v1`; default: 24 hours since the contact's last marketing email and 72 hours since their last marketing SMS.* AUD-009 states how these windows combine with FLOW-014 caps and how an operator overrides them for one campaign, with the override recorded.

clauses.title: Dispatch recheck
clauses.text: Eligibility is recalculated when a step's dispatch begins and again immediately before each provider hand-off, so a purchase, refund, opt-out, bounce, complaint, consent change, merge, or frequency-window change after approval prevents that delivery and is recorded as the exclusion reason. Every source type used by the audience must still satisfy STORE-005; if refresh fails or the source becomes stale, the affected channel pauses before any further hand-off and resumes only after a successful refresh.

clauses.title: Multi-step exit
clauses.text: Each later step re-applies its audience and exclusion rules; a contact who converts or becomes ineligible after an earlier step receives no later step. *Status:* done. The two-step journey (`tests/go-live/multistep.journeys.ts`) exercises saved inclusion rules, custom exclusions and current consent after the first send, records each skip reason, and keeps newly matching contacts outside the frozen approved audience.

clauses.title: Frozen candidate set
clauses.text: Approval freezes the candidate set resolved at that instant. A contact who first matches the inclusion rule after approval is never added to the approved campaign, and each contact yields at most one recipient-step per channel per step even when they match the rule more than once. Exclusions still apply at dispatch (AUD-005).

clauses.title: States
clauses.text: A campaign is *draft* (editable, nothing scheduled), *scheduled* (an approved revision with a future step instant), *dispatching* (a step has begun handing off), *paused* (dispatch stopped by SEND-009), *completed* (SEND-007), *canceled* (CAMP-009), or *failed* (its first step could not begin before its deadline because a required adapter or sender registration was unavailable). Every transition records its actor or the feature that acted, and its time; an invalid transition is rejected.

clauses.title: Draft editing
clauses.text: Operators can edit and persist the campaign name, selected channels, audience rule, message content, sender identity, links, and schedule while a campaign is a draft. An email body saves whenever its sent size is within BUILD-012's limit; a larger one is refused with its measured size and the limit named, never truncated.

clauses.title: Revision preview
clauses.text: Desktop, mobile, and plain-text previews render from the saved revision that will be approved, including resolved personalization examples and the compliance footer or SMS opt-out text that will be sent.

clauses.title: Approval checks
clauses.text: Approval atomically validates the audience, consent, source freshness (STORE-005, including incumbent sync freshness during a parallel run, MOVE-013), sender registration, email authentication, sending reputation (MSG-011), compliance content, personalization, links (MSG-006, MSG-013 to MSG-015), schedule, and adapter configuration. A sender adapter must provide effective deduplication and provider reconciliation as required by SEND-001 and SEND-008. Any failure leaves the campaign a draft and names every blocking check.

clauses.title: Idempotent approval
clauses.text: Repeated approval requests carrying the same campaign and revision identifier produce one scheduled campaign and one set of steps and recipient-steps, whatever the number of requests.

clauses.title: Schedule
clauses.text: Each step stores an IANA time zone and the resolved UTC instant. A local time that does not exist or is ambiguous under daylight saving is rejected until the operator chooses an unambiguous instant. *Policy: `campaign.send-time.v1`; default: resolve every step against the store time zone and the operator-selected local time.*

clauses.title: Scheduled edits
clauses.text: Editing a scheduled campaign creates a new draft revision and leaves the approved revision active until the replacement passes approval. Replacement approval atomically makes the new revision the campaign's only active schedule and cancels every pending recipient-step of the prior revision. Once any step has begun dispatching, edits can only create a new campaign; the original campaign and its later steps remain active until the operator explicitly cancels them.

clauses.title: Test send
clauses.text: A test sends only to the configured operator test addresses or phone numbers, or to the typed addresses CAMP-019 admits, is visibly marked as a test in its content and in campaign history, and changes no contact activity, reporting, attribution, or frequency protection.

clauses.title: Cancellation
clauses.text: Canceling a scheduled, dispatching, or paused campaign stops every step and every recipient-step confirmed not handed to a provider within 30 seconds, records provider-confirmed hand-offs separately, and leaves an in-flight request in `handoff-unknown` until SEND-008 reconciles it. It never claims to recall a delivered message. Campaign detail shows the time remaining until the next step dispatches.

clauses.title: Step deadline
clauses.text: Each step carries a send-by instant, defaulting to the end of that step's scheduled local day. Recipient-steps not handed to a provider by then are skipped and recorded as `deadline-passed`; a step whose deadline passes before dispatch begins does not send.

clauses.title: Dispatch punctuality
clauses.text: Dispatch of a scheduled step begins within 60 seconds of its resolved UTC instant, and each step's instant dispatches exactly once even if the scheduler runs twice.

clauses.title: Campaign images
clauses.text: A signed-in operator can upload a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image within the byte and pixel limits in `seed.json`. Its type is read from the file's own header, never from the name or type the client declares, and the file must be complete; anything else is refused and nothing is stored. Each image is stored once under its SHA-256 and is never changed or deleted, so the bytes behind an approved revision cannot change, except that contact erasure (CONT-013) removes the bytes of an image holding an erased contact's identifier; such an image then answers 410 and blocks approval. It is served without a session at `/media/<sha256>` on this deployment with its exact content type, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, an immutable public cache and no cookie, answers 404 for an unknown name, and is rate-limited per image at the limit in `seed.json`, not per client address, returning 429 without affecting other images. Serving an image records nothing about who requested it. Every image is exported as its original file (DATA-001).

clauses.title: Optional design module
clauses.text: The design module is disabled while both `DESIGN_PROVIDER_API_KEY` and `DESIGN_PROVIDER_ORIGIN` are absent; supplying either requires both, and startup fails naming what is missing. The origin must be an HTTPS origin with no path; only a copy running on a computer may name a loopback `http:` origin. A disabled module constructs no adapter, shows no design-generation control, contacts no design service, and its routes refuse to start a run with `design_unavailable` naming the inputs. An enabled module contacts the design service only with the owner's own key and only because an operator started a design run or chose one of its candidates.

clauses.title: Draft-only design generation
clauses.text: From a draft's email editor an operator can ask the design service for two to four designs from a brief that starts as the draft's name, subject, preheader, sender name and current text and that the operator may edit. An estimate of the spend on the owner's design-service account is shown before each paid step: drawing the candidates and preparing the chosen layout. The run belongs to the draft and continues in the background: candidates appear as they land and the run is shown again after a reload. The operator chooses one with **Use this design** beside its image; Mango fetches its layout and then opens the design import path (DESIGN-004), where the browser builds the email; it opens by itself only as the continuation of that choice while the operator has done nothing else in the page, and otherwise the run shows a notice whose action opens it, so nothing opens over, or takes focus from, an operator who is working: photos hosted as campaign images, the HTTPS button destination the operator enters, the managed footer, and every design line not in the brief highlighted. The result is an unsaved edit of the email body that replaces existing content only after confirmation. The run and its candidates stay on offer until the draft is saved with the design or the operator discards them, so discarding the edit, reloading, a failed layout step or starting another run never loses a design that was paid for, and using the same prepared design again buys nothing. After a failed layout step the run says which step failed and whether the design service's allowance or wallet is the cause, and offers to try the layout again (a new paid layout) or choose a different design; a new run leaves earlier runs' designs reachable under the latest run. While the design service holds a run back, the editor says why and when Mango asks again, until the service answers. A run never saves, approves, schedules or sends; the body reaches the editor already in the canonical form saving stores (CAMP-003 policy), and the operator's Save stores it through the ordinary draft save path, where it passes every approval check like any other draft. A run that fails or outlives its deadline is shown as failed with Mango's own reason and changes nothing in the draft; Mango never substitutes content of its own for a design the service did not deliver.

clauses.title: Design data and records
clauses.text: A run sends the design service only Mango's fixed description of an email layout with the operator's brief, every `{{…}}` token removed, and then only the chosen candidate image: never a contact, audience, personalization value or token. Every paid request carries an idempotency key derived from the run, so a retried or replayed request never buys again. Each run records its brief, the service's run and layout identifiers, each candidate's outcome, SHA-256 and size, the chosen candidate, the operator, its times and a safe failure code, and is never deleted; the candidate images and the layout are stored in R2 as authoring evidence and exported with everything else (DATA-001). Each paid request records a cost fact (RESULT-004).

clauses.title: Design import
clauses.text: An operator editing a draft can import a design made with their own 12ui CLI: a LayerDoc version 2 file and the PNG candidate it was converted from. Mango compiles it in the operator's browser into the same email grammar every authored body uses (MSG-009, MSG-012): the photos become campaign images hosted by this deployment (CAMP-012), the design's button links to an HTTPS destination the operator enters, and its footer becomes the managed unsubscribe link and saved postal address. Layers Mango does not import are listed by their LayerDoc text, and every line of the design that does not appear in the operator's brief is highlighted for review. An unsupported version, a non-HTTPS button destination or a design the grammar cannot hold is refused visibly with the body unchanged; nothing outside the grammar is ever saved. Import only produces an unsaved edit of a draft's email body: it never saves, approves, schedules or sends, and the result passes every approval check and exact-revision approval like any other draft. Import itself makes no request to 12ui; generating designs inside Mango is DESIGN-001 to DESIGN-003.

clauses.title: Sender identity
clauses.text: Every email uses the configured business display name, From address, reply-to address, and physical postal address; every SMS uses a sender registered for the recipient's country.

clauses.title: Email authentication
clauses.text: A marketing email cannot be scheduled unless the mail adapter reports SPF, DKIM, and DMARC passing for the sending domain and the visible From domain aligns with an authenticated domain.

clauses.title: Email unsubscribe
clauses.text: Every marketing email carries a visible unsubscribe link and an opaque per-recipient HTTPS `List-Unsubscribe` URL with `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`; DKIM covers both headers. The one-click URL accepts a context-free HTTPS POST body of `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`, does not redirect, and applies CONT-004 before returning success. The visible link opens a page that applies CONT-004 on a single confirming action and never on page load, so a mailbox scanner or link prefetcher cannot unsubscribe anyone. Both paths are idempotent under repeats, need no session or cookie, and reveal no contact other than their own.

clauses.title: SMS permission
clauses.text: An SMS is eligible only when its phone number is subscribed for the recorded consent scope and the SMS adapter confirms an approved sender for that recipient's country. For every permitted sender and jurisdiction, the adapter must be able to receive and enforce the standard opt-out and help keywords in CONT-007; otherwise SMS is blocked for that recipient.

clauses.title: SMS opt-out
clauses.text: Every marketing SMS carries the configured program identity and `Reply STOP to unsubscribe`, or the jurisdiction's required equivalent, and the configured frequency disclosure where required. An opaque unsubscribe URL may be additional but never replaces reply-based opt-out. Review shows the exact compliance text and resulting segment count.

clauses.title: Links
clauses.text: Scheduling is blocked when a destination link is malformed; uses a scheme other than HTTPS or the contact schemes MSG-013 admits (`http:`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:` and every other scheme block); or resolves, on the link itself or on any redirect it follows, to a host outside the allowed link hosts MSG-014 sets out. Image sources must be HTTPS on an allowed host. Review names every blocked link with the scheme or host that blocks it, and offers MSG-015's allow action for each blocked host. Approval (CAMP-004), flow activation (FLOW-008), the link inspector and tracking (RESULT-005) apply this one rule.

clauses.title: Content checks
clauses.text: Review names blocking and advisory content findings per channel. An operator can acknowledge an advisory finding; the consent, sender registration, opt-out, authentication, link, personalization, and reputation checks are blocking and cannot be overridden.

clauses.title: Personalization
clauses.text: Every personalization token carries a fallback value. A bare token is refused by the authoring checks and blocks approval and scheduling even when every current eligible contact resolves it, because the audience can change before send. When a contact has no value for a valid token, its saved fallback is rendered and the count of eligible contacts using a fallback is shown in review.

clauses.title: Email body
clauses.text: Every marketing email is sent as multipart/alternative with an HTML part and a plain-text part carrying the same offer, links, and unsubscribe link, plus the preheader text set on the revision. Operator-authored HTML is saved as the WHATWG HTML parser reads it and transmitted exactly as saved within the allowed tag, attribute, and inline-style set and within the size limit BUILD-012 derives from delivery, which admits no script, form, stylesheet, class, or CSS function. The single exception is the responsive block BUILD-010 generates from builder settings: no author writes it, saving regenerates it, and the checker judges the email with and without it. One checker, reading the stored body with that parser, decides approval, test send, and delivery; the preview renders the HTML sanitized per BASE-INPUT-002 from the same parse and keeps its styles only when that checker passes, and the plain-text part is derived from the same parse.

clauses.title: Unsubscribe availability
clauses.text: The unsubscribe path answers within 2 seconds and is rate-limited per unsubscribe token at the limit in `seed.json`, not per client IP address. The token is the rate-limit key declared for this public path under BASE-ACCESS-003, so mailbox-provider requests for unrelated recipients cannot consume one another's allowance; an exceeded token allowance returns 429 without affecting other tokens.

clauses.title: Sending reputation
clauses.text: Once a sending domain has at least 1,000 marketing deliveries in the reporting window, scheduling a marketing email from it is blocked while provider-reported complaints divided by delivered marketing emails are at or above 0.3%, or hard bounces divided by attempted marketing hand-offs are at or above 5% (RESULT-006). A provider's stricter block applies at any volume. The block names each numerator, denominator, reporting window, and provider rule, cannot be acknowledged away, recomputes when late facts arrive, and clears only when every applicable threshold is below its limit.

clauses.title: Hidden or deceptive presentation
clauses.text: Authored presentation cannot hide or disguise content. Approval, test send, and delivery judge the tree mail clients build from the stored body. Only table cells and the email's outer wrapper paint a background, no element changes its display, and nothing in the grammar can carry text out of the table cell that holds it, so every text run is drawn on the background of its nearest table cell that paints one, or outside any on the wrapper or the white page; they are blocked, with the reason named, when text sits below 3:1 contrast against that background (text on the wrapper also against the white page, since a block does not hold what overflows it) in standards or quirks rendering, when a style hides, clips, fades, shrinks below 10px, moves, overlays, or reverses text, when presentation stands where the grammar does not admit it (a background outside a table cell or the outer wrapper, any display, a width or height that could make a box smaller than its text, a border on an inline element, a rounded painted corner over the text it holds, right-to-left text outside a cell, overlapping styled cells), when styled markup is not written the way HTML parsers build it, or when markup is written in a way mail clients read differently from how it looks. The unsubscribe link and postal address fall under the same rule.

clauses.title: Provider hand-off
clauses.text: Email uses `mail.sender.v1` and SMS uses `sms.sender.v1`. Every recipient-step carries a provider-effective idempotency key derived from the campaign, revision, step, and contact. Mango stores the provider message identifier before treating it as handed off. A timeout or lost response becomes `handoff-unknown` and is reconciled by provider lookup before any retry; an adapter whose deduplication retention cannot cover the campaign deadline and reconciliation window cannot pass CAMP-004. A retried job, redelivered queue message, or resumed dispatch therefore never produces a second provider message.

clauses.title: Quiet hours
clauses.text: SMS is handed off only inside the recipient-local legal and provider-required windows. The recipient time zone is resolved from recorded location evidence with its source and freshness, never substituted with the store time zone; an unknown or stale zone blocks hand-off; the US area-code evidence SMS-003 defines counts as recorded location evidence. Legal and provider windows are mandatory minima that a policy cannot weaken. *Policy: `sms.quiet-hours.v1`; default: defer until the next allowed instant at or before the step's send-by instant (CAMP-010), otherwise skip and record `quiet-hours-deadline`.*

clauses.title: Throttling and progress
clauses.text: Dispatch paces hand-offs to the provider and carrier rate limits in `seed.json`. Campaign status shows the estimated completion instant and updates the handed-off, delivered, skipped, and failed counts within 30 seconds of each change.

clauses.title: Transport failure
clauses.text: A transient provider or network failure on a recipient-step is retried up to 5 times over 1 hour with increasing delay, except that `handoff-unknown` is reconciled rather than retried. A permanent rejection or exhausted retry budget marks that recipient-step failed with the provider's error and campaign detail shows it; a hard rejection, complaint, or provider suppression also updates CONT-006 atomically before another hand-off.

clauses.title: Provider-event identity
clauses.text: Every signed provider webhook is stored once as an immutable fact using the strongest identity that adapter declares: provider event identifier where supplied, otherwise provider message identifier, event kind, provider event time or version, and a stable payload digest. Replaying or reordering delivery, bounce, complaint, suppression, and SMS reply facts produces the same derived delivery disposition and contact state, and an older fact never downgrades a later provider disposition.

clauses.title: Delivery truth
clauses.text: A recipient-step has a transport disposition of queued, handoff-unknown, handed-off, accepted, delivered, bounced, skipped, or failed, plus independent complaint and suppression facts. *Delivered* is recorded only from a provider fact asserting delivery; provider acceptance is never reported as delivery. A later complaint remains visible without erasing the earlier delivery fact, and a skipped disposition carries its reason.

clauses.title: Partial completion
clauses.text: A campaign becomes completed only once every recipient-step has a terminal transport disposition; `handoff-unknown` is not terminal. Its summary keeps delivered, skipped, failed, bounced, complained, and suppressed totals separate and never sums them into a single success figure. Later complaint or suppression facts update the completed campaign's summary and the contact ledger.

clauses.title: Resumable dispatch and reconciliation
clauses.text: Dispatch survives worker eviction, redeployment, and restart: it resumes from recipient-steps without a terminal transport disposition, sends nothing twice (SEND-001), and needs no operator action. At the reconciliation interval in `seed.json`, it queries the provider for handoff-unknown and other unresolved messages and imports missed provider facts. After the provider's declared lookup window expires, an unresolved message becomes failed with `outcome-unconfirmed`; it is never counted as delivered or retried blindly. A campaign never remains dispatching with no work or reconciliation in progress.

clauses.title: Provider outage
clauses.text: When hand-offs to a provider fail transiently for 5 continuous minutes, or the adapter reports the provider unavailable, the affected campaign channel moves to paused and no recipient hand-offs are attempted on it. The adapter runs a bounded health probe or non-recipient canary at the reconciliation interval in `seed.json`; a successful probe resumes dispatch automatically, subject to CAMP-010 and AUD-005. The pause and provider error are shown on campaign detail, and each operator is emailed once as soon as the mail provider is available.

clauses.title: Campaign history
clauses.text: Operators can list campaigns by state and channel, open the approved revision, and inspect its audience snapshot, delivery timeline, cancellation, and per-channel outcome totals.

clauses.title: Engagement
clauses.text: Clicks and store conversions are shown as observed events. Open tracking is off by default; when an operator enables it, opens are labeled privacy-sensitive estimates and never support a confidence, deliverability, or attribution figure.

clauses.title: Attribution
clauses.text: Revenue attributed to a campaign names the qualifying store event and attribution window, is reported separately from any forecast, and is assigned at most once per order. *Policy: `campaign.attribution.v1`; default: the most recent non-automated tracked click in the seven days before purchase wins; a cancellation or refund subtracts the corresponding attributed amount.*

clauses.title: Cost
clauses.text: Each AI call and provider hand-off records the external provider, model or channel, billable units, and reported cost; totals are visible by campaign and by day.

clauses.title: Link tracking
clauses.text: A tracked link is rewritten to an opaque per-recipient-step redirect on this deployment that records the request and forwards to the original URL. The redirect sets no cookie, loads nothing, and carries no address, name or contact ID in the destination URL; the only thing it adds is CONT-018's opaque, expiring click token, and only to a connected store's storefront host. Known mailbox security scanners and bot requests are retained as automated events but excluded from engagement and attribution. An operator can disable tracking per campaign, which sends the original URLs and records no clicks. Contact links (`mailto:`, `tel:`, `sms:`; MSG-013) are never rewritten and record no click.

clauses.title: Deliverability reporting
clauses.text: Per sending domain and SMS sender, Mango shows the delivered, bounced, complained, and failed counts and the resulting hard-bounce and spam-complaint rates over the reporting window in `seed.json`, and the rates MSG-011 is currently evaluating.

clauses.title: Export contents
clauses.text: The export contains every contact, source record, consent record, suppression and surviving opt-out record (CONT-013), proposal, campaign, revision, audience decision, message, recipient-step outcome, attribution event, setting, and audit entry as JSON, and every uploaded campaign asset as its original file.

clauses.title: Signed first-owner admission
clauses.text: A claim is bound to the trusted management issuer, installation, configured app origin and owner email, expires promptly, and can initialize an installation only once. GET and HEAD never initialize it. Admission uses ordinary Base operator-auth and its native owner session. An existing installation cannot claim another first owner.

clauses.title: Native owner editor
clauses.text: Only an active native owner receives a short-lived editor grant. The frame loads from the exact configured management origin and trusts messages only from that frame and origin. Anonymous visitors receive no widget. Logout, authorization loss and grant expiry remove it. Compiled visual edits apply after the real route leaf has hydrated. Mango product authority follows OPER-004's six roles (Owner, Admin, Manager, Author, Analyst and Support), separately from Base's unchanged owner/admin/member roles. The last product Owner is always protected, and product authority on restore belongs to the destination installation. CSV export remains Owner/Admin only.

nonGoals: Multiple stores or workspaces
A general CRM
Signup-form, landing-page, and website builders
Social and advertising campaigns
Store transactional messaging (order, shipping, and account notifications)
Autonomous sends
Visual journey automation
A/B and multivariate testing
Predictive send-time models
Multi-touch attribution
Purchased-list prospecting
Native mobile apps

externals.name: commerce-store
