externals.reason: Mango needs the buyer's real customers, products, carts, browsing signals, orders, refunds, and inventory to identify and recheck opportunities.
data: Webhook acknowledgements sent back to the store confirming receipt of an event
Explicit adapter requests for source records (customers, products, orders, refunds, carts, browsing events)

externals.name: ai-provider
externals.reason: A language model turns structured evidence into reviewable campaign content and explanations; Cloudflare primitives do not provide that model capability.
data: The proposal evidence required for the requested generation
The configured business context required for the requested generation

externals.name: design-provider
externals.reason: An image-generation design service (12ui, reached with the owner's own API key) turns an operator's brief into candidate email designs and a structured layout; Cloudflare primitives do not generate designs. It is contacted only when an operator asks for designs or chooses one, never otherwise. Privacy: No contact, audience, personalisation value or token is sent. 12ui's sub-processors are OpenAI, fal.ai, Google and Cloudflare, and 12ui may keep briefs and images in its internal evaluation corpus until the account owner asks for deletion. 12ui's generated artifacts expire after 7 days, so Mango stores the candidates and layout it uses in its own R2 bucket.
data: The operator's design brief, prefilled from the draft's name, subject, preheader, sender name and current text and edited by the operator, with every {{...}} personalisation or managed token removed, inside Mango's fixed description of an email layout
The chosen candidate image, sent back for layout conversion
The owner's design-service API key, as bearer authentication

externals.name: mail-sender
externals.reason: Internet email delivery, domain authentication, bounce handling, and complaint feedback require a delivery provider with established sending infrastructure. Managed hosting explicitly selects RER for transactional sign-in and subscription confirmations; Free and Assisted hosting retain their own-provider connections.
data: Approved email content
Sender metadata for direct providers; the RER relay chooses its own sending identity.
Each eligible recipient's email address
Operator email addresses that receive magic links, test sends, and dispatch-paused notices
Diagnostic sender-verification message and configured receipt mailbox; provider message IDs and sender-domain names for delivery reconciliation and authentication queries

With MAIL_PROVIDER=rer, only one recipient address, subject, text and optional HTML go to the RER-assigned HTTPS MAIL_RELAY_URL, authenticated by the server-only MAIL_API_KEY. Active Managed access and a valid credential are required.

externals.name: sms-sender
externals.reason: Registered sending numbers, carrier routing, country approval, compliance keywords, and delivery receipts require a telecommunications provider.
data: Approved SMS content
Programme metadata
Each eligible recipient's phone number

externals.name: link-dns-resolver
externals.reason: A public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver verifies that each approved external link, image and redirect target resolves outside private networks before dispatch. Images this deployment stores itself at /media/ are verified in its own storage and never resolved or fetched.
data: Approved link host names only

externals.name: signup-turnstile
externals.reason: Optional abuse prevention on hosted and embedded signup. Only a trusted pointer or keyboard interaction with the form loads the browser challenge. The server verifies the token before accepting consent.
data: After interaction, browser requests https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js and its challenge frames, disclosing the public site key, visitor IP and browser challenge signals to Cloudflare.

Server POST to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify sends the challenge token, visitor IP and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY; acceptance requires newsletter-signup action and the configured public hostname. No email address or consent evidence is sent to Cloudflare.

externals.name: sender-dns-resolver
externals.reason: Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS verifies sender domain authentication records before dispatch.
data: Sender domain and DKIM/SPF/DMARC record names queried at https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query; no recipients or message bodies.

externals.name: approved-content-destinations
externals.reason: Dispatch preflight checks explicitly approved external links and images, including each allowed redirect, for reachability after DNS safety checks.
data: Full approved destination URLs including paths and query parameters sent as HEAD requests to configured allowed hosts. No operator cookie or provider credential is attached. Deployment-hosted /media/ images use local storage instead.

externals.name: owner-editor
externals.reason: An authenticated owner can open the configured Run Edit Run editor and explicitly share page context for requested visual edits.
data: The configured management origin receives installation identifier and application origin in the editor iframe URL after the owner opens it.

The origin-checked protocol sends page path, editor visibility and edit results. Only while context sharing is enabled, it additionally sends page title, bounded visible DOM text and selected element metadata (excluding input values and private-marked elements).

externals.name: sender-receipt-receiver
externals.reason: An installer-selected authenticated receipt service supplies original diagnostic email and trusted authentication observations before marketing sending is enabled. The optional paired MAILBOX_RECEIPT_URL and MAILBOX_RECEIPT_RECIPIENT inputs select its HTTPS origin, secret URL token and diagnostic mailbox; redirects and off-origin responses are refused.
data: Authenticated GET requests carry the server-only receipt URL token, diagnostic recipient address, challenge nonce and sent-at timestamp to find the diagnostic email.
The matching receipt ID is sent to the same origin to retrieve original diagnostic message bytes; no audience contacts or campaign content are sent by this lookup.

seeds.scope: One self-hosted newsletter and its role-controlled operators. Mail is required; commerce, SMS, AI and email design are optional. Wider commerce and multichannel contract clauses remain release obligations.

operatingCost.assumptions: One store, 10000 contacts, 4 campaigns per month, 20000 email and 5000 SMS recipient-steps, and 500 AI generations. Queue messages are at most 64 KB and dispatch stays below 3334 recipient-steps per UTC day. Every campaign image fetched from an inbox is one Worker request and one D1 row write for its per-image rate counter; at 4 images per email, 20000 email recipient-steps add up to 80000 of each per month, concentrated on send days, and they count toward the same daily Free quotas as everything else. Each design run with the optional design module is one Worker request to start it, about 5 to 15 Queue messages while it polls (three operations each), one R2 write per candidate image and one for the layout, and a few D1 rows; 12ui itself bills the owner's own account at about $0.03 per candidate and $0.05 per layout at its 12 October 2026 list prices, free within its daily allowance of 20 images and 50 layouts.
operatingCost.cloudflareMonthlyUsd: $0 on the current Workers Free plan while the deployment stays inside every Free quota: at most 100000 dynamic Worker requests per UTC day with 10 ms CPU per invocation; 10000 Queue operations per UTC day (write, read, and delete are each one operation per 64 KB); D1 at 5 million rows read per UTC day, 100000 rows written per UTC day, and 5 GB total storage; and SQLite Durable Objects at 100000 requests and 13000 GB-s per UTC day. Workers Paid starts at $5/month and is required for the declared 100000-contact campaign: its 100000 recipient-step writes plus step and schedule mutations exceed D1 Free's 100000 rows-written-per-UTC-day limit.
operatingCost.externalMonthlyUsd: Not yet estimated because the reference commerce, email, SMS, and AI adapters have not been selected; required before first release.
operatingCost.totalMonthlyUsd: Incomplete until reference adapters and unit prices are selected.

releaseProvenance.note: Local tag and export; no push, deployment or visibility change.

sitePresentation.reason: Publish the product screenshot named in RELEASE.json and committed with this exact release; preserve the signed publisher manifest and documents unchanged.

gallery.caption: Mango v0.3.0 contact ledger at 1600 pixels: saved sample contacts with channel-specific email and SMS consent and last activity, from the product screenshot named in RELEASE.json.

seeds.name: Vector
seeds.oneLiner: Track issues, plan projects, and keep software delivery moving.
seeds.summary: Track issues, plan projects, and keep software delivery moving.
seeds.maturity: Third public release; independently gated on 19 October 2026 locally at 1440 and 390 and on own-account hosting with real SendGrid mail. Hosted HTTP restore into an rer-deployed installation is refused (known issue); Managed relay delivery, real Linear/Jira exports, hosted Cron timing and broader capacity remain unproven.

clauses.title: Public homepage
clauses.text: The owner-approved public marketing homepage at `/` remains exactly as approved, including its copy and assets and the line “100% free, open source alternative to Linear, Jira and Asana.” That line is product positioning; it does not promise feature parity or importer coverage for every named product. The page presents Vector with its headline, one supporting sentence, and source and docs links, followed by short sections (how Current explains each issue, free and open source, deferral, the rest of the product, trying it beside another tracker, a closing call to action), each drawing the product only from its real labels. The public site's “Run Vector” action remains unchanged and points to `/run`, the installation page. The installed application's root `/` serves the Base Lobby, whose Sign in entry satisfies this clause's sign-in requirement (owner decision, 13 Oct 2026 15:11Z). The page contains no pricing, hosting costs, customer testimonials or invented metrics, reads no installation data and is server-rendered. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs` (tests tagged HOME-001). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`.

clauses.title: Workspace access
clauses.text: Every workspace member sees every public team's issues, intake items, cycles, projects, initiatives, labels and shared saved views, and every notification addressed to them, and acts on them as the role matrix (ROLE-001, ROLE-008) allows; team membership organises work and, for a public team, never restricts access. Roles (ROLE-001), private teams (ROLE-002) and guests (ROLE-003) are the only rules that narrow access, and a private saved view (VIEW-002) is visible only to its owner. Every read, search result, notification, export, webhook, Slack unfurl, mobile payload, API response and agent context applies the same rule server-side. *Acceptance:* the existing equal-access tests plus a role-matrix journey that signs in as Admin, Member and Guest and checks every private route, `/api/v1` route, search and export against ROLE-001–003. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/search-access.test.ts`, `tests/worker/removal-boundary.test.ts` (equal operators; roles, private teams and guests open).

clauses.title: First workspace review
clauses.text: Fresh configured owners review their workspace at `/setup` before entering an app route. Signed-out visitors return there after ordinary sign-in. Only the recorded installation owner may complete setup through a same-origin, current-session transaction. Completion survives repeated setup, restart and local restore. Existing configured installations retain completion through the additive upgrade. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/first-run.test.ts` (tests tagged SETUP-001). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/first-run.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Member management
clauses.text: Members are invited, removed by suspension (OPS-004, ROLE-011), reactivated and erased (ROLE-012) in Settings → Members, and every invitation names the invitee's role (ROLE-001) and, for a Guest, the teams they join (ROLE-003). Owners and Admins invite and remove Members and Guests; only Owners invite, promote to or remove Owners and Admins. The installation owner can be removed only by themselves, and never while they are the last Owner (ROLE-001). Members and Guests cannot remove anyone but themselves. *Policy: `operator.management.v1`; default: Owners and Admins invite and remove; a workspace setting lets Members invite Members (never Admins or Guests).* *Acceptance:* the existing invite and removal tests plus the OPS-002 rows of the role-matrix journey (ROLE-001): a Member's invitation is refused 403 by default and admitted after the setting is enabled, a Member's attempt to invite an Admin is refused 403, and an Admin's removal of a Member succeeds. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/base-auth.test.ts` (invite and remove by any operator under the earlier equal-operator rule; role-restricted management is open with ROLE-001).

clauses.title: Workspace time
clauses.text: Settings hold one IANA workspace timezone. Every calendar day, due reminder, cycle start and end instant, and seven-day window named in this contract is evaluated in that timezone. Changing it never rewrites stored instants, closed cycle snapshots, or reminders already delivered. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-workspace-time-journey.mjs`, `tests/e2e/admin-access-journey.mjs`, `tests/e2e/admin-runtime.mjs` (tests tagged OPS-003). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/admin-workspace-time-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Safe removal
clauses.text: Removing a member from the workspace — by an Owner or Admin in Settings → Members (role matrix), by the member leaving themselves, or by SCIM deprovisioning (ROLE-004) — suspends them under ROLE-011 and never erases them; erasing their personal data is the separate, explicit action of ROLE-012. Vector rejects the suspension of the last Owner. A suspension revokes the member's sessions and credentials (ROLE-011), transfers each project they lead and each shared saved view they own to the person performing it — or to the longest-standing remaining Owner when they left themselves or SCIM removed them — handles their non-terminal issues as the person performing it chooses (ROLE-011), keeps their name on every comment, activity and audit entry, and writes one activity entry per changed issue and project. A failed step rolls back the whole removal. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/removal-boundary.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-runtime.mjs`, `tests/worker/base-auth.test.ts`, `tests/worker/foundation-rollback.test.ts` (tests tagged OPS-004) for session revocation, transfers, unassignment, the last-operator guard and rollback; plus the ROLE-011 suspension journey, in which a removed member's comments and activity still carry their name, and the ROLE-012 journey, in which only the explicit erase anonymises. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/removal-boundary.test.ts` (removal revokes sessions, unassigns, transfers and rolls back as one unit, but today every removal also deletes the member's private views and anonymises their references at once; suspension that keeps the name is open with ROLE-011 and the separate erase with ROLE-012).

clauses.title: Team identity
clauses.text: A team has a name and an identifier prefix, each unique across archived and non-archived teams. The prefix is two to ten uppercase letters and cannot be changed once the team has an issue, so existing identifiers stay resolvable. Every issue belongs to exactly one team. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-team-journey.mjs` (tests tagged TEAM-001). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/admin-team-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Team workflow
clauses.text: Every team has an ordered list of workflow statuses with at least one status in each of the Intake, Backlog, Unstarted, Started, Completed, Canceled, and Duplicate categories, and status names unique within the team. Owners, Admins and the team's owners (ROLE-007) can add, rename, and reorder statuses, and so can every member of the team while its *Who manages team settings* permission is All team members (ROLE-009); other Members and all Guests are refused. A status never changes category, and no category is added or removed. A team's *default status* in a category is the first status of that category in workflow order, and every clause naming a category as a destination moves the issue there. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-team-journey.mjs`, `tests/worker/base-auth.test.ts` (tests tagged TEAM-002) for the workflow rules, plus the TEAM-002 rows of the role-matrix journey (ROLE-001): a team owner renames a status, and a Member who does not own the team gets 403 under the default permission and succeeds once the permission is All team members. *Status:* partial — `tests/e2e/admin-team-journey.mjs` (workflow editing by any operator under the earlier equal-operator rule; the role restriction is open with ROLE-001 and ROLE-007).

clauses.title: Team archiving
clauses.text: Archiving a team stops new issues, intake, and issue moves from targeting it while preserving its issues, cycles, projects, identifiers, and history; a signal source request naming an archived team creates nothing and returns 409. Unarchiving restores normal use. Teams are never deleted; archiving is the only terminal state. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-archive-team-journey.mjs` (tests tagged TEAM-003). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/admin-archive-team-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Status removal
clauses.text: Removing a workflow status requires a destination status in the same category and atomically moves every issue to it. Vector rejects removal of a category's last status and records the status mapping in audit history. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-team-journey.mjs` (tests tagged TEAM-004). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/admin-team-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Creation
clauses.text: An operator can create an issue with a required title and team plus an optional Markdown description (written in the ISSUE-026 editor, with inline images and video under ISSUE-024 and checklists under ISSUE-025), assignee, project, cycle, priority, labels, estimate, due date, expected outcome, customer impact, and values for the custom fields defined for its team (FIELD-001, which carries their types and acceptance). It starts in the team's default Backlog status unless another non-Intake status is explicitly chosen. *Policy: `issue.defaults.v1`; default: unassigned, no priority, no cycle, and no project.* *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`, `tests/markdown-rendering.test.tsx` (tests tagged ISSUE-001). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`.

clauses.title: Stable identifiers
clauses.text: An issue identifier is its team's prefix, a hyphen, and an integer one higher than the highest ever allocated under that prefix, so a number is never reused after an issue is deleted. The identifier never changes, including when the issue moves teams (ISSUE-012); a prefix therefore records where an issue started, not where it lives. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/issue-deletion-relations.test.ts` (tests tagged ISSUE-002). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/issue-deletion-relations.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Priority
clauses.text: An issue has exactly one priority: Urgent, High, Medium, Low, or No priority. No priority is the default and sorts after Low. *Acceptance:* A test that sets each of the five priorities and checks that No priority is the default and sorts after Low. *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-board-journey.mjs`, `evidence/keyboard-board/ISSUE-003/`.

clauses.title: Status transitions
clauses.text: A version-checked operator mutation (ISSUE-006) can move an issue in any direction among the Backlog, Unstarted, Started, Completed, and Canceled statuses of its team's workflow. Vector rejects moving any issue into an Intake status. Leaving Intake uses INTAKE-005, INTAKE-007, or REL-003; entering or leaving Duplicate uses REL-003 or REL-005. Entering Completed records the completion time and entering Canceled records the cancellation time; leaving one of those categories clears the time it recorded and removes no activity. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/issue-session-projection.test.ts` (tests tagged ISSUE-004). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/issue-session-projection.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Assignment
clauses.text: An issue has at most one assignee. Assigning, reassigning, or unassigning it takes effect immediately and records the actor, the previous assignee, and the new assignee. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/removal-assignment.test.ts` (tests tagged ISSUE-005). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/removal-assignment.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Concurrent edits
clauses.text: Every issue carries an integer version that increases by one on each mutation that appends an activity entry under ISSUE-007. An issue mutation carries the version the client last read; if the stored version is higher, Vector rejects the mutation with 409 and returns the current issue and version, changing nothing. Adding a comment, evidence revision, follower, or notification does not change the version and is never rejected as stale. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-preferences.mjs`, `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts` (tests tagged ISSUE-006). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`.

clauses.title: Activity history
clauses.text: Creation and every change to title, description, team, status, priority, assignee, project, cycle, estimate, due date, labels, expected outcome, customer impact, custom fields, duplicate target, parent, or dependency append an immutable activity entry recording the time, the previous value, the new value, and the actor — the operator, or the named automation when a cycle closure, deferral return, or import acted. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/admin-label-journey.mjs`, `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts` (tests tagged ISSUE-007). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Comments, threads and resolution
clauses.text: Any member who can see an issue (a Guest only in invited teams) can add a Markdown comment in the ISSUE-026 editor, with inline images and video (ISSUE-024) and checklists (ISSUE-025). Each top-level comment starts a thread: members reply to it, and replies show under it in order. Any member who can comment can resolve a thread when its question is answered, which collapses it to one line naming who resolved it and when, and can reopen it; a new reply reopens a resolved thread. A comment can also quote highlighted text of the issue description or a document (PROJ-013) as an inline comment, which anchors the thread to that text and shows it in the margin; if the text is later removed, the thread stays in the issue with the quoted text shown as removed. Only a comment's author edits it; an edited comment shows its edit time. Authors delete their own comments; Owners, Admins and the team's owners delete anyone's (role matrix, ROLE-001); the entry records who acted. Deleting a comment removes its body, attachments, links, and search entry, leaves a tombstone and an activity entry in the thread, keeps its replies, and does not remove the follower state it created. A synced Slack or Teams thread maps to exactly one Vector comment thread (SLACK-002). *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/discussion-access.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-runtime.mjs`, `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs` (tests tagged ISSUE-008) for comment creation, editing, deletion and tombstones; plus a thread journey that replies twice to a comment, resolves the thread and sees it collapse to one line with the resolver, posts a new reply and sees it reopen, adds an inline comment on highlighted description text and finds it anchored in the margin, and is refused 403 editing another member's comment; plus the SLACK-002 fixture in which one Slack thread's replies land only in its mapped comment thread. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/discussion-threads.test.ts`, `tests/worker/discussion-access.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-threads-journey.mjs`; `evidence/comment-threads/ISSUE-008/` (threads with ordered replies, resolve and reopen naming who and when, reopen on a new reply, author-only editing refused 403, and deletion by the author or an Owner or Admin with tombstones that keep replies are implemented; inline comments quoting description or document text are not built; team-owner deletion waits on ROLE-007, Guest limits on ROLE-003, inline images and video on ISSUE-024, and the Slack thread mapping on SLACK-002).

clauses.title: Attachments and links
clauses.text: Operators can attach files and named HTTPS links to an issue or a comment. Removing either records the action; removing a file also deletes its blob under `BASE-DATA-003`. An image or video pasted, dropped or uploaded into a description, comment or document is an attachment under this clause and is shown inline where it was placed (ISSUE-024). *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/discussion-file-admission.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`, `tests/worker/link-cascade.test.ts` (tests tagged ISSUE-009). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/discussion-file-admission.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Deletion
clauses.text: Deleting an issue first moves it to Recently deleted (ISSUE-020), from which it can be undone or restored intact for 30 days. Permanent deletion happens when that retention ends, or at once when an Owner or Admin chooses "Delete permanently" (for erasure under SEC-003 and DATA-011): it removes the issue's comments, attachments, links, evidence revisions, dependencies, parent link, follower state, notifications, activity, and search entry; its children become root issues, and a duplicate is removed from its canonical issue's list. Vector rejects deleting a canonical issue that still has duplicates. Closed cycle snapshots (CYCLE-005) and audit entries keep only its identifier, and its source idempotency records (INTAKE-002) are retained so a re-delivery cannot resurrect it. *Policy: `issue.can-delete.v1`; default: Owners, Admins and the issue's creator; a workspace setting extends it to every Member of the issue's team; Guests never delete; only Owners and Admins delete permanently (role matrix, ROLE-001).* *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/issue-deletion-cascade.test.ts`, `tests/worker/collaboration-atomicity.test.ts`, `tests/worker/issue-deletion-import.test.ts` (tests tagged ISSUE-010) for the permanent cascade; plus the ISSUE-020 journey and the ISSUE-010 rows of the role-matrix journey: a Member who did not create the issue is refused 403 by default, its creator deletes it to Recently deleted, and a Member's "Delete permanently" is refused 403 while an Admin's succeeds and runs the cascade at once. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/issue-deletion-cascade.test.ts` (immediate permanent cascade by any operator; Recently deleted, undo and the role policy are open with ISSUE-020 and ROLE-001).

clauses.title: Estimates
clauses.text: An issue estimate is absent or an integer from 1 through 100 points. Changing an estimate never rewrites a closed cycle snapshot. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts` (tests tagged ISSUE-011). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Moving teams
clauses.text: Moving an issue requires a non-archived target team and an explicit target status in the same category as its current status, including Intake so a misrouted intake item reaches the right team without a decision. The move preserves the identifier (ISSUE-002), uncommits the issue from any cycle (CYCLE-002), keeps its project, assignee, labels, custom-field values and history, and writes one activity entry. Labels and custom-field values are preserved unchanged; the native move does not map them. All of it happens or none of it does. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/bulk-commands.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/core-stream-planning-journey.mjs` exercise team moves, including Intake and Started issues, stable identifiers, cycle uncommit and one activity entry. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/bulk-commands.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-stream-planning-journey.mjs`, `evidence/keyboard-planning/ISSUE-012/`.

clauses.title: Mentions
clauses.text: Typing `@` in an issue description or comment offers matching operators, and choosing one records a mention of that operator. Text resolving to no operator is stored and shown literally and mentions nobody. A mention adds a follower (NOTIFY-002) and notifies once (NOTIFY-001); editing text to add a mention notifies only the newly mentioned operator, and removing a mention notifies nobody and withdraws no delivered notification. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/collaboration-events.mjs`, `tests/markdown-rendering.test.tsx` (tests tagged ISSUE-013). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/collaboration-events.mjs`.

clauses.title: Labels
clauses.text: A label belongs to the workspace or to one team, has a name unique among the labels visible in that scope and a colour, and can sit in a label group (for example Area, Type) whose labels are mutually exclusive on an issue. Owners, Admins and Members create labels and apply them, and Guests apply existing labels in their invited teams; Owners and Admins rename, recolour, merge and delete workspace labels, and a team's owners — or all its members while its *Who manages team settings* permission is All team members (ROLE-009) — do so for that team's labels (role matrix, ROLE-001). Merging one label into another relabels every issue and saved-view filter in one change. Deleting a label removes it from every issue and from the filters of saved views naming it, and deletes no issue. An issue carries up to the number of labels in `seed.json → limits`. *Policy: `label.manage.v1`; default: as above; a workspace setting restricts label creation to Owners and Admins.* *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-issue-journey.mjs`, `tests/e2e/admin-label-journey.mjs`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-issue.mjs` (tests tagged ISSUE-014) for workspace labels; plus a journey that creates a team label and a label group, is refused applying two labels of one group, merges two labels and finds every issue relabelled, and the ISSUE-014 rows of the role-matrix journey (a Member's delete of a workspace label refused 403, an Admin's admitted). *Status:* partial — `tests/e2e/admin-label-journey.mjs` (workspace labels managed by any operator; team labels, groups, merging and the role policy are absent).

clauses.title: Unsent drafts
clauses.text: An unsubmitted new-issue form is retained in the operator's browser and restored the next time they open new issue there. A draft is not a record: it appears in no list, search result, notification, or export, and becomes an issue only when that operator creates it. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-draft-journey.mjs` (tests tagged ISSUE-015). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-draft-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Dependencies
clauses.text: An operator can record that one issue blocks another, across teams, and can remove the link. Vector rejects self-links, a link that already exists in either direction, and any link that would create a directed cycle. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts` (tests tagged REL-001). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Blocked state
clauses.text: An issue is shown as blocked while any issue that blocks it is outside a Completed, Canceled, or Duplicate category. Blocking never changes the issue's workflow status by itself. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts` (tests tagged REL-002). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Duplicate decision
clauses.text: Marking an issue as a duplicate requires one canonical issue that is neither itself nor already a duplicate, moves it to the team's default Duplicate status, and preserves its description, comments, evidence, attachments, and activity under the duplicate issue. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/issue-deletion-relations.test.ts` (tests tagged REL-003). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/issue-deletion-relations.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Canonical duplicates
clauses.text: A canonical issue lists every direct duplicate. If it is later marked duplicate, Vector atomically repoints its duplicates to the new canonical issue, so a duplicate chain or cycle is never exposed. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/issue-deletion-relations.test.ts` (tests tagged REL-004). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/issue-deletion-relations.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Undo duplicate
clauses.text: Undoing a duplicate decision removes the canonical link and restores the issue's most recent non-terminal status, or its team's default Backlog status if it has none, while preserving both decision activity entries. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/issue-deletion-relations.test.ts` (tests tagged REL-005). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/issue-deletion-relations.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Parent and child
clauses.text: An issue has at most one parent. An operator can set, replace, or clear it from issue details. Vector rejects self-parenting and ancestry cycles; changing a parent never changes status, team, project, cycle, or assignee, and deleting a parent makes each direct child a root issue. Issue lists can filter to roots or to children of one exact parent (VIEW-001). *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/issue-deletion-preimage.test.ts`, `tests/worker/parent-deletion-custody.test.ts` (tests tagged REL-006). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/issue-deletion-preimage.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Intake creation
clauses.text: A registered signal source (INTAKE-011) creates an intake issue with a title, team, observed time, its source ID, source display name, source record identifier, source revision identifier, summary, link, and optional structured measurements and customer reports. An operator creates one with a title and team and any of the same descriptive fields, attributed to that operator instead of a source. Either way it starts in the team's default Intake status and appears in Needs decision (CURR-002) within 5 seconds. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs` (tests tagged INTAKE-001). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Idempotent sources
clauses.text: Re-delivery of the same source ID, source record identifier, source revision identifier, and normalised payload returns the original result and creates nothing. Re-delivery of an identity whose issue has since been deleted (ISSUE-010) returns 410 and creates nothing. Reusing an identity with a different payload returns 409 and changes nothing. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`, `tests/worker/source-erasure-identity.test.ts` (tests tagged INTAKE-002). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Evidence revisions
clauses.text: A new source revision identifier for an existing source record appends immutable dated evidence even when revisions arrive out of order. The issue orders evidence by observed time, then receipt time, and shows a field-level change from the preceding observed revision. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts` (tests tagged INTAKE-003). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Inspectable assessment
clauses.text: An intake issue shows the evidence behind its attention reason, impact measurements, likely cause, recommended assignee, suggested priority, suggested labels and likely duplicates. Each assertion names whether it came from a source, an operator, a policy or an agent; an agent assertion also names the model, the records it read and when, and is shown as a suggestion until a person accepts it. Vector never presents an inferred assertion as a fact or applies one silently. *Acceptance:* the existing operator-intake journey plus a triage journey in which an agent suggestion is shown with its provenance and is applied only on acceptance. *Status:* partial — `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs` (source, operator and policy provenance; agent provenance is open with TRIAGE-003).

clauses.title: Accept
clauses.text: Owners, Admins and Members who can see an intake item's team accept, defer and decline it; Guests cannot (role matrix). Accepting an intake issue atomically records the actor, the time, and an optional reason; applies the chosen assignee, priority, cycle, and Started or Unstarted status; and clears any deferral. It leaves Needs decision and reaches its new Current and My work sections within the CURR-008 window. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs` (tests tagged INTAKE-005), plus the intake rows of the role-matrix journey (ROLE-001): a Guest's accept in an invited team is refused 403 and changes nothing. *Status:* partial — `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs` (acceptance by any operator; the Guest refusal is open with ROLE-003 and ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Defer
clauses.text: Deferring an intake issue (by an Owner, Admin or Member who can see its team; Guests cannot, role matrix) records who deferred it, an absolute return time strictly in the future, and an optional reason, and removes it from Needs decision. It returns there exactly once — within 5 minutes of the return time, or within 5 seconds of a new evidence revision (INTAKE-003), whichever comes first — and the return atomically clears the deferral and leaves the earlier decision visible. The same roles can defer it again or end a deferral early. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`, `tests/worker/issue-session-projection.test.ts` (tests tagged INTAKE-006), plus a Guest's defer and end-deferral in an invited team each refused 403 in the role-matrix journey. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`, `evidence/issue-follow-up/INTAKE-006/` (Timed, early and evidence-triggered returns clear deferrals atomically, preserve the decision and notify its deferrer once; Guest refusal remains open with ROLE-003 and ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Decline
clauses.text: Declining an intake issue — open to Owners, Admins and Members who can see its team, never to Guests (role matrix) — requires a reason, moves it to the team's default Canceled status, and removes it from Needs decision without deleting its evidence or decision history. *Acceptance:* A journey that declines an intake item without a reason (refused) and with one, and finds it Canceled with its evidence and decision history kept, and a Guest's decline refused 403. *Status:* partial — `src/core/features/issues/mutations.ts` (decline with a reason by any operator; no test names the clause yet, and the Guest refusal is open with ROLE-003 and ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Evidence after a terminal decision
clauses.text: Evidence received after an issue is Canceled or Duplicate is appended and visible but never reopens, reassigns, reprioritises, or resurfaces the issue. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts` (exercises this behaviour; the test does not yet tag INTAKE-008). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Source failure
clauses.text: A signal source request from an unknown or revoked source, or carrying a wrong signature, returns 401; one whose body fails validation returns 400; one naming an archived team returns 409 (TEAM-003). None of them creates anything. A valid request that cannot be stored durably returns 503 so the source retries. No request is acknowledged before its idempotency record and evidence are durable. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts` (exercises this behaviour; the test does not yet tag INTAKE-009). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Decision policy
clauses.text: Suggested assignee, priority, and start state are selected by the intake recommendation policy and are always editable before acceptance. *Policy: `intake.recommendation.v1`; default: every registered source pins its team; the signed source payload may explicitly recommend an assignee through a source-attributed `assertions.assigneeOperatorId` value. An absent assignee recommendation leaves the issue unassigned in that team's triage, with No priority and Unstarted as the acceptance defaults. The recommendation never assigns the intake item before acceptance.* *Acceptance:* A test that delivers two signed items to a registered source's pinned team, one with an explicit assignee recommendation and one without an assignee recommendation, checks both stay unassigned in that team's triage, and checks that assignee, priority and start state recommendations stay editable before acceptance. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/intake-policy.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-intake-policy-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Source registration
clauses.text: An Owner or Admin registers a signal source (integration management in the role matrix; Members and Guests are refused 403) with a display name, a source ID unique in the workspace, and a signing secret; the `signal.source.v1` adapter normalises that source's signed request into INTAKE-001. Rotating a secret (by an Owner or Admin) accepts both secrets for a configurable overlap of at most 24 hours and then rejects the previous one. An Owner or Admin revoking a source rejects every later request under INTAKE-009 and deletes no evidence. A secret is shown once at registration or rotation and never again. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts` (tests tagged INTAKE-011), plus the INTAKE-011 rows of the role-matrix journey: a Member's registration, rotation and revocation are each refused 403 and change nothing, and an Admin's succeed. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts` (registration, rotation and revocation by any operator; the Owner/Admin restriction is open with ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Disjoint stream
clauses.text: Current places an issue in at most one section using this precedence: Needs decision, Now, Next, then Recently done. Canceled, Duplicate, deleted, and actively deferred issues do not appear. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/current-disjoint.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-current-disjoint-journey.mjs` place each kind through public routes, assert exact and disjoint membership with overlapping eligibility, exclude canceled/duplicate/deferred/deleted issues, and move Next work to Now through the native status selector at 1440 and 390. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/current-disjoint.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-current-disjoint-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Needs decision
clauses.text: Needs decision contains every Intake-category issue whose deferral has expired or is absent and which has not been accepted, declined, or marked duplicate. Every expired deferral returns to Current: none is hidden, and more than one page is reachable through paging or an explicit total and Show more control (for example, “50 shown of 132, show more”), in CURR-007 order. *Acceptance:* A journey that defers, returns and declines intake items and asserts Needs decision membership; it defers 120 issues until all are past due, opens Current and reaches all 120 across pages in CURR-007 order, with the total and remaining issues visible until every issue has been reached. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/current-intake-pagination.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-current-intake-pagination-journey.mjs` (every expired deferral is included before bounded return automation drains; Needs decision shows totals and Show more through all 120 items at 1440 and 390, in CURR-007 order).

clauses.title: Now
clauses.text: Now contains non-terminal issues outside the Intake category that are overdue or in a Started status, excluding anything already in Needs decision. An issue is *overdue* when its due date is earlier than the current calendar day in the workspace timezone (OPS-003). *Acceptance:* A journey with a Started issue and an overdue Unstarted issue at a workspace-timezone day boundary. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/current-now.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-current-now-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Next
clauses.text: Next contains non-terminal issues in an Unstarted status that are committed to their team's active or next cycle (CYCLE-001) or due within the next seven calendar days, excluding anything already in a higher-precedence section. *Acceptance:* A journey with active-cycle and due-in-seven-days Unstarted issues. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/current-next.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-current-next-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Recently done
clauses.text: Recently done contains issues moved to a Completed category in the previous seven calendar days, ordered by the completion-time exception in CURR-007. *Acceptance:* A journey that completes issues across an eight-day window and checks the seven-day cut-off and completion-time order, including identifier ties. In the same Current view, two in-progress issues of different priority follow the normal CURR-007 order while two done issues completed at different times appear newest completion first even when their priority, due date or last update would put them in the opposite order. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/current-recently-done.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-current-recently-done-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Explainable attention
clauses.text: Every issue in Current shows one primary inclusion reason — Awaiting decision, Started work, Overdue, Cycle commitment, Due within seven days, or Completed within seven days — and every applicable context reason from Customer escalation, Unresolved dependency, Unassigned urgent work, Project risk, and New evidence since the most recent intake decision. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts` (tests tagged CURR-006). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Ranking
clauses.text: Within every Current section except Recently done, the default order sorts by priority (Urgent first, No priority last), then by due date (overdue first, then earliest first, then issues with no due date), then by most recent update, and finally by stable identifier, so the order is total and stable. Recently done (CURR-005) instead sorts by completion time, newest first, with stable identifier as the tiebreak; priority, due date and last update do not affect that section. *Policy: `current.ranking.v1`.* *Acceptance:* A ranking test over priority, due date, update time and identifier ties, plus completion time and identifier ties in Recently done. One Current view shows two in-progress issues of different priority in normal ranking order alongside two done issues completed at different times in newest-completion-first order, with priority, due date and last update opposing the done issues' completion order. *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-stream-controls-ranking.mjs`, `evidence/current-controls/CURR-007/`.

clauses.title: Freshness
clauses.text: A decision or issue mutation that changes an issue's Current membership, section, or reasons is reflected in an already open Current view within 5 seconds without an operator-initiated reload, and in the next response to any other request. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-current-journey.mjs` (tests tagged CURR-008). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-current-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Stream controls
clauses.text: Operators can filter Current by team, project, priority, item type, assignee, and attention reason. The default includes all teams and all operators and shows Recently done. *Acceptance:* A browser journey applying each Current filter and its reset. *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-stream-controls-journey.mjs`, `evidence/current-controls/CURR-009/`.

clauses.title: Personal queue
clauses.text: My work contains every non-terminal issue assigned to the signed-in operator outside the Intake category, grouped disjointly in this precedence: Waiting for issues blocked under REL-002, Now for those the CURR-003 rule would place in Now, and Next for every issue still remaining, each group ordered by CURR-007. An issue assigned to the operator while in an Intake status appears in Current's Needs decision, not here. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts` (tests tagged WORK-001). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Personal defaults
clauses.text: Completed, Canceled, Duplicate, and actively deferred issues never appear in My work; an operator reads their finished work from Current's Recently done filtered to themselves (CURR-005, CURR-009). When no issue qualifies, the view states the operator is caught up and offers new issue and Current as next actions. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts` (tests tagged WORK-002). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/dependencies.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Cycle context
clauses.text: My work shows one row for each team that has an active cycle containing an issue assigned to the operator, giving that cycle's name, start and end dates, and progress, with completed and total committed scope labelled in the unit CYCLE-003 used. *Acceptance:* A journey with an active cycle containing the operator's issue that checks the cycle row's dates, progress and unit. *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-stream-controls-journey.mjs`, `evidence/current-controls/WORK-003/`.

clauses.title: Project record
clauses.text: A project has a name unique in the workspace, a Markdown description, exactly one lead who is a workspace member, an optional start date, an optional target date that is on or after the start date when both are set, a priority (Urgent, High, Medium, Low or No priority, as ISSUE-003), project labels (workspace labels marked for projects, filterable by PROJ-007), a status (PROJ-016), an optional colour, an optional icon, and values for the custom fields that apply to projects (FIELD-001). Its status is one of the project statuses of its primary team or the workspace (PROJ-016), each in one of the categories Backlog, Planned, Started, Paused, Completed and Canceled, and a new project starts in the default Planned status unless another is chosen. Start date, target date, priority and labels are set in the project page, the projects list, the roadmap timeline (INIT-003) and `/api/v1`, and each change is a project activity entry. Linear project start and target dates, priority and labels import onto these fields (DATA-014). Owners, Admins and Members create projects and edit these fields; Guests see the projects their invited teams contribute to and cannot create or edit one (role matrix). *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-project-cycle-journey.mjs` (tests tagged PROJ-001) for name, description, lead, target date and native lifecycle; `tests/worker/project-fields.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/core-project-fields-journey.mjs` set start and target dates, High priority and two enabled workspace labels through the project page, projects list and scoped `/api/v1` routes, refuse a target before the start with 400, filter by label, sort by priority and check one activity entry per changed planning field at 1440 and 390; `tests/worker/project-fields-upgrade.test.ts` and `tests/worker/data-http.test.ts` retain those fields through populated upgrade and archive restore. Remaining acceptance sets project custom-field values, configurable project statuses and primary teams, colour and icon, edits planning fields on the roadmap, imports Linear project dates, priority and labels, and refuses a Guest's project creation or edit with 403. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/project-fields.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-project-fields-journey.mjs`, `tests/worker/project-fields-upgrade.test.ts`, `tests/worker/data-http.test.ts` (native names, descriptions, leads, start/target date validation, priority, project labels, per-field activity, page/list editing and scoped project API are proven at 1440/390 and through populated upgrade/archive restore. Project custom fields, configurable statuses/primary teams, colour/icon editing, roadmap editing, Linear project-field import and Guest restrictions remain unbuilt).

clauses.title: Manual lifecycle
clauses.text: A project's status (PROJ-016) is changed only by a person — an Owner, Admin or Member; Guests are refused (role matrix). Completing or canceling all of its issues never completes or cancels the project. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-project-cycle-journey.mjs`, `tests/e2e/admin-access-journey.mjs` (tests tagged PROJ-002), plus a Guest's lifecycle change refused 403 in the role-matrix journey. *Status:* partial — `tests/e2e/admin-project-cycle-journey.mjs` (manual lifecycle by any operator; the Guest refusal is open with ROLE-003 and ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Project membership
clauses.text: An issue belongs to at most one project. Removing an issue from a project or archiving a project never deletes the issue; deleting a project detaches all of its issues but deletes none of them. *Acceptance:* A journey that removes, archives and deletes projects and checks no issue is deleted, including canceling and confirming deletion through the browser at 1440px and 390px. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/project-membership.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-project-membership-journey.mjs` (the project administration form has a Delete project control with cancellation and explicit confirmation; confirmed deletion detaches issues and preserves their identities and content).

clauses.title: Progress
clauses.text: Project progress counts issues: completed project issues divided by all project issues outside the Canceled and Duplicate categories. The interface shows the completed and total counts beside the percentage and reports no progress when the denominator is zero. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs` (tests tagged PROJ-004). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-runtime.mjs`.

clauses.title: Health
clauses.text: Health is reported only for projects whose status is in the Started category (PROJ-016); a project in any other category, Paused included, reports no health and is excluded from health filters and counts. A *remaining issue* is a project issue outside the Completed, Canceled, and Duplicate categories. A Started project is Blocked, At risk, On track, or Unknown, evaluated in that order. The default reports Blocked when at least one remaining issue exists and either an Urgent remaining issue has an unresolved blocker (REL-002) or every remaining issue is blocked; At risk when its target date is in the past, a remaining Urgent issue is unassigned, or its remaining estimated points committed to any team's active cycle exceed that cycle's capacity; On track when a target date in the future, every applicable capacity, and every remaining active-cycle estimate exist and no earlier rule matches; and Unknown otherwise. Remaining scope exactly equal to capacity is not At risk. *Policy: `project.health.v1`.* *Acceptance:* A health test covering each Blocked, At risk, On track and Unknown rule and the equal-capacity edge. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/project-health.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-project-health-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Risk explanation
clauses.text: Every Blocked or At risk project shows the exact issues and measurements that triggered its health, including unresolved dependencies, unowned urgent work, target-date exposure, and committed scope against capacity. *Acceptance:* A journey that opens a Blocked and an At risk project and finds the triggering issues and measurements. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/project-risk.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-project-risk-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Portfolio
clauses.text: The Projects view shows the count of projects in each health and lifecycle state and can filter by lifecycle, health, lead, team, target date, and label. Counts and rows use the same active filters. The team filter selects contributing teams; target-date bounds are inclusive and exclude projects without a target date when either bound is set. The label filter selects workspace labels marked for projects (PROJ-001). *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/project-fields.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/core-project-fields-journey.mjs` apply lifecycle, health, lead, contributing-team, inclusive target-date range and project-label filters individually and together, checking matching health/lifecycle counts and rows at 1440 and 390; the browser journey also sorts by priority and edits a project from the list. `tests/e2e/admin-access-journey.mjs` retains empty-portfolio coverage (tests tagged PROJ-007). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/project-fields.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-project-fields-journey.mjs` (lifecycle, health, lead, contributing team, target-date range and label filters, including combined filters, use the same rows for health/lifecycle counts; native 1440/390 journeys also exercise priority order and list editing).

clauses.title: Historical truth
clauses.text: Later issue edits update live project progress and health but never rewrite a closed cycle snapshot shown in that project's history. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts` (tests tagged PROJ-008). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Project archiving
clauses.text: Archiving a project removes it from the default portfolio and stops new issues from joining it while preserving its lifecycle, issues, history, and closed-cycle snapshots. Operators can include archived projects in filters or unarchive one. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-project-cycle-journey.mjs` (tests tagged PROJ-009). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/admin-project-cycle-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Time box
clauses.text: A cycle belongs to one team and has a name unique within that team, a start instant, an end instant after the start, and an optional capacity in estimate points, all interpreted in the workspace timezone (OPS-003). Vector rejects a cycle whose dates overlap another cycle of the same team, so a team's *active cycle* — the one whose start is at or before now and whose end is after now — is unique, and its *next cycle* is the cycle of that team with the earliest start at or after the active cycle's end. Owners, Admins and the team's owners create, edit, complete and delete its cycles, and so do all its members while its *Who manages cycles and templates* permission is All team members, the default (ROLE-009); Guests never do (role matrix). *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-project-cycle-journey.mjs` (tests tagged CYCLE-001), plus the CYCLE-001 rows of the role-matrix journey: a non-owner Member creates a cycle under the default and is refused 403 under Team owners only, and a Guest is refused 403 under both. *Status:* partial — `tests/e2e/admin-project-cycle-journey.mjs` (cycle rules, created by any operator; the role and team-permission restriction is open with ROLE-008 and ROLE-009).

clauses.title: Commitment
clauses.text: A non-terminal issue can be committed to at most one cycle, and only to a cycle of its own team. Anyone who can edit the issue commits, moves or uncommits it — Owners, Admins, Members who can see its team, and Guests in an invited team (role matrix). Committing, moving, and uncommitting record both cycle identifiers and update both cycles atomically. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/admin-cycle-list-journey.mjs`, `tests/e2e/admin-issue-journey.mjs` (tests tagged CYCLE-002), plus a Guest's commit admitted in an invited team and refused 404 in another team. *Status:* partial — `tests/e2e/admin-cycle-list-journey.mjs` (commitment by any operator; Guest scoping is open with ROLE-003).

clauses.title: Progress and capacity
clauses.text: Cycle progress is completed committed estimate points divided by all non-Canceled, non-Duplicate committed estimate points when every included issue is estimated; otherwise it uses issue counts and labels the result `by issue count`. With no included issues it shows `No committed work` and no percentage. Capacity risk is Unknown unless capacity and every remaining estimate exist, At risk when remaining points exceed capacity, and Within capacity otherwise. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts` (tests tagged CYCLE-003). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Closure and rollover
clauses.text: Within 5 minutes of a cycle's end instant Vector closes it exactly once however many times the closing job runs, and by default moves committed issues in an Unstarted or Started status to the team's next cycle (CYCLE-001) and uncommits committed issues in an Intake, Backlog, Completed, Canceled, or Duplicate status. A closed cycle's name, dates, capacity, and snapshot cannot be changed, and a closed cycle is never reopened. *Policy: `cycle.rollover.v1`.* *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts` (tests tagged CYCLE-004). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Closure snapshot
clauses.text: Closing a cycle records committed and completed issue IDs, each issue's project ID at close, estimate totals, capacity, progress, additions and removals during the cycle, and the close time. The snapshot is immutable. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts` (tests tagged CYCLE-005). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Missing next cycle
clauses.text: If rollover is required and no next cycle exists, the cycle still closes, its unfinished issues become uncommitted, and one visible failed-operation entry names the affected issues; creating a later cycle does not move them. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts` (tests tagged CYCLE-006). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/cycle-closure.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Global search
clauses.text: Search covers issue identifiers, titles, descriptions, expected outcomes, customer impact, comments, evidence summaries, project names, label names, and saved-view names visible to the operator, and returns within 500ms. Issues of archived teams and projects are excluded unless the operator asks for them. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/search-access.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/dev-runtime.mjs`, `tests/worker/search-exact-admission.test.ts` (tests tagged SEARCH-001). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/search-access.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Exact identifier
clauses.text: An exact issue identifier lookup reads the primary record and returns it even while full-text indexing is delayed or unavailable, subject to the archive choice in SEARCH-001. On a successful full-text read, that exact issue ranks first, without duplicating it or dropping other matching issues, projects or accessible saved views; results remain bounded. Primary identity, archive choice and operator/session/workspace admission are rechecked before returning results, including after an index failure. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/search-exact-admission.test.ts`, `tests/worker/search-access.test.ts` (tests tagged SEARCH-002). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/search-exact-admission.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Index freshness
clauses.text: Created or changed searchable text appears in full-text results within 10 seconds. Database triggers maintain the full-text entries in the same transaction as searchable source changes, so a committed source change cannot leave its corresponding entry behind. If an index query fails, the exact primary-record lookup remains available under SEARCH-002; other searches are reported unavailable with the last successful index time; Vector never presents a known index failure as a complete empty result. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/search-access.test.ts` (tests tagged SEARCH-003). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/search-access.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Issue controls
clauses.text: Issue lists can filter by status, status category, priority, assignee, team, project, cycle, label, due date, blocked state, and parent (all issues, root issues, or children of one exact parent identifier); sort by newest, oldest, Urgent-to-No-priority, workflow status order, due date, or last update; and group by none, status, assignee, priority, project, cycle, or team. Completed issues are hidden by default outside Current. Grouped pages order by the group key before the selected sort and stable identifier. Only groups with rows on the page are rendered, with counts for the complete filtered result; a group may continue onto another page. The issue-list HTTP response exposes page-present `groups` with full filtered counts and `allGroups` with the complete filtered grouping aggregate. Positive offsets require the response `revision` for the same query and workspace calendar date; invalidated or missing identity returns HTTP 409 `pagination_invalidated` without mixed rows, and browsing restarts visibly at offset zero. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/dev-runtime.mjs` (tests tagged VIEW-001). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/dev-runtime.mjs`.

clauses.title: Saved views
clauses.text: Anyone signed in can save a named combination of filters, sort, grouping, and list or board layout as a private view, then update, duplicate, or delete it; Owners, Admins and Members can also save a view as shared with the workspace or a team or switch it to shared, and a Guest's views are always private (role matrix). A private view is visible and editable only by its owner; anyone who can see a shared view's teams can open or duplicate it (a Guest only when it covers only their invited teams), but only its owner can update or delete it, and ownership changes only under OPS-004. Deleting a view never changes an issue. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/views-removal.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-keyboard-journey.mjs`, `tests/worker/search-access.test.ts` (tests tagged VIEW-002), plus the VIEW-002 rows of the role-matrix journey: a Guest's attempt to share a view is refused 403 and a Member's update of another member's shared view is refused 403. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/views-removal.test.ts` (private and shared views and owner-only edits; the Guest restriction is open with ROLE-003 and ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Control persistence
clauses.text: The filters, sort, and grouping an operator last applied to Current, My work, the Projects portfolio, the issue list, and the board are stored for that operator and restored on their next visit from any browser, and one visible control resets them to the defaults. A saved view's layout belongs to that view. Opening a saved view never changes the stored controls of the list or board it was opened from. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/views-removal.test.ts` (tests tagged VIEW-003). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/views-removal.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Bulk edit
clauses.text: An operator can select several issues in a list and set status, assignee, priority, project, cycle, or labels on all of them in one operation, up to the batch limit in `seed.json → limits`. The operation is atomic: if any selected issue fails ISSUE-004, ISSUE-006, or CYCLE-002, nothing is written and the response names the failing issues by identifier. A successful operation writes one activity entry per issue and is undone as one action by Undo or Command/Ctrl-Z within the ISSUE-020 window. *Acceptance:* A browser journey selecting issues with X and setting status in one operation, plus a failing selection that writes nothing and names the failing identifiers. *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-keyboard-journey.mjs`, `tests/e2e/core-undo-journey.mjs`, `tests/worker/issue-undo.test.ts`, `evidence/issue-undo/VIEW-004/`.

clauses.title: Team board
clauses.text: The board shows one explicitly selected team's workflow at a time; it never guesses a team in a multi-team workspace. It displays every configured status as a column in that team's workflow order and places the matching issues from the current filtered page in those columns, ordered by the selected derived sort. Each card has a labelled, keyboard-operable status selector. A status change uses the existing version-checked issue mutation (ISSUE-004, ISSUE-006); intake and duplicate decision rules cannot be bypassed, and a stale conflict shows the current server issue and refreshes the board without applying the rejected move. At 390px, a labelled column selector lets the operator choose which status column to view. Board pages explicitly request `pageSize=100` and `grouping=status` through the same issue-list URL and API; ordinary list requests default to 50 and the accepted page sizes are bounded to 50 or 100. Status counts use the same SQL filters as cards across the complete result, with page counts distinguished from totals. Paging reaches cards beyond the first page; completed work remains hidden until explicitly requested. *Acceptance:* A board journey at 1440px and 390px that changes status from a card and recovers from a stale conflict. *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-board-journey.mjs`, `evidence/keyboard-board/VIEW-005/`.

clauses.title: Command palette
clauses.text: The command palette searches issues, projects, saved views, and available commands from one input. The up and down arrows move the highlight, Enter opens the highlighted record or performs the highlighted command, and Escape closes the palette without acting. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-palette-journey.mjs` exercises search, arrow-key highlight, Enter and Escape, alongside `tests/e2e/core-keyboard-journey.mjs`. *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-palette-journey.mjs`, `evidence/keyboard-board/CMD-001/`.

clauses.title: Keyboard navigation
clauses.text: Outside editable controls, Command/Ctrl-K opens the palette, C opens new issue, G then M opens My work, G then C opens Current, G then P opens Projects, and Escape closes the topmost transient surface. Every command also has a visible, keyboard-operable control. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/core-keyboard-journey.mjs` (tests tagged CMD-002). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-keyboard-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Focus and selection
clauses.text: The up and down arrows move a visible focus indicator through the rows of the active list, Enter opens the focused row, X adds or removes it from the selection VIEW-004 acts on, and Escape returns focus from an open detail pane to the row it was opened from. Changing a filter, sort, or grouping keeps the focused row focused while it remains in the list and focuses the first row when it does not. *Acceptance:* A keyboard journey moving focus with arrows, selecting with X, opening with Enter and returning focus with Escape. *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/core-stream-planning-journey.mjs`, `tests/e2e/core-keyboard-journey.mjs`, `evidence/keyboard-planning/CMD-003/`.

clauses.title: Inbox events
clauses.text: Vector creates an in-app notification, visible within 5 seconds, for assignment of an issue to the member, a direct mention (ISSUE-013), a comment on an issue they follow, the return of an intake item they deferred, the resolution of the last blocker on an issue assigned to them, a due reminder (NOTIFY-005), a triage item they are responsible for (TRIAGE-001), a project or initiative update they follow (PROJ-010), a delegated agent's question or completion (AGENT-002), a review request or status change from Git (GITHUB-005) and an SLA warning (AUTO-004). Members who follow an issue (NOTIFY-002) — its creator, assignee, commenters, mentioned members and explicit followers — are also notified when it is completed, when it is canceled or marked duplicate, when its status changes to another status (one notification per change, grouped with any other change made in the same mutation), when its priority is raised to Urgent, when it becomes blocked by a newly added blocker or a blocking relation on it is added or removed, when its due date changes, and when a resolved thread they took part in is reopened (ISSUE-008). Each event notifies each follower once, never the actor (NOTIFY-003), and a completion caused by automation or Git (GITHUB-003) names that automation as actor. The inbox is always delivered; email, Slack, Teams, mobile push and desktop follow NOTIFY-006 and NOTIFY-007. *Acceptance:* the existing collaboration journeys for the original events plus one journey per added event, including: member A creates an issue, member B completes it, and A finds exactly one completion notification naming B within 5 seconds while B finds none; B cancels a second issue A follows and A gets one cancellation notification; B moves a followed issue from Todo to In Progress and raises it to Urgent in one edit and A gets one grouped notification naming both changes; B adds a blocker to it and A gets one blocking notification; and a merged-PR fixture under GITHUB-003 completes a followed issue and A's notification names the Git automation. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/follower-events.test.ts`, `tests/worker/follower-last-blocker.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/core-follower-journey.mjs`, `tests/worker/source-ingest.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-events.mjs`, `evidence/issue-follow-up/NOTIFY-001/` (Live Inbox journeys at 1440/390 exercise completion, cancellation, grouped status/Urgent, blocking/unblocking, workflow-status removal and evidence-triggered intake return in 0.5–3.2 seconds, with actor exclusion and one event per recipient. Worker routes prove last-blocker resolution, receipt-failure rollback and replay suppression. Reopened-thread notifications remain absent; triage, project/initiative, agent, Git review/automation and SLA events depend on their unbuilt clauses).

clauses.title: Followers
clauses.text: Issue creators, assignees, commenters, and directly mentioned operators follow the issue automatically; an operator can follow or unfollow it explicitly without changing anyone else's following. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/collaboration-events.mjs`, `tests/worker/collaboration-atomicity.test.ts`, `tests/worker/discussion-access.test.ts` (tests tagged NOTIFY-002). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/collaboration-events.mjs`.

clauses.title: No self-notification
clauses.text: An action never notifies its actor. One event creates at most one notification per recipient and issue even when the recipient qualifies through several follower rules. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/due-reminders.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-pagination.mjs`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-reads.mjs` (tests tagged NOTIFY-003). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/due-reminders.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Read and mute
clauses.text: Opening a notification marks it read, an operator can mark all of theirs read in one action, and the interface shows their unread count. An operator can mute an issue or an event type, which suppresses only their own later matching notifications and alters neither activity history nor another operator's notifications. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/collaboration-preferences.mjs`, `tests/worker/collaboration-final-admission.test.ts`, `tests/worker/collaboration-mail.test.ts` (tests tagged NOTIFY-004). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/collaboration-preferences.mjs`.

clauses.title: Due reminders
clauses.text: Within 5 minutes of the configured daily reminder time — 09:00 in the workspace timezone by default — Vector notifies the assignee once for each incomplete issue assigned to them that is due that day, and once more on the first run after it becomes overdue. Changing a due date makes the new date eligible and never repeats a reminder already delivered for the same issue and date. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/due-reminders.test.ts` (tests tagged NOTIFY-005). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/due-reminders.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Assignment and mention email
clauses.text: A qualifying assignment or direct mention creates at most one durable email intent per event, recipient and issue in the same transaction as its source mutation. With configured transactional mail and the recipient's enabled preference, Vector initiates delivery immediately after commit through Base mail. Mutes, actor exclusion and active-recipient checks apply to each qualifying cause and are rechecked before submission. Mail contains only the recipient address, issue title, identifier, readable actor and authenticated canonical app link; it includes no body, evidence, attachment or tracking. Accepted and development outcomes are terminal; uncertain or interrupted claims are never automatically resent. Definite rejection or rate limit permits finite scheduled retries, with failed and uncertain outcomes visible to the recipient. Erasure removes addressed delivery state and anonymizes retained actors; a request already in flight cannot be recalled. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/collaboration-delivery-ui.mjs`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-disabled.mjs`, `tests/e2e/collaboration-preferences.mjs` (tests tagged NOTIFY-006). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/collaboration-delivery-ui.mjs`.

clauses.title: Signed PR links
clauses.text: A current registered repository receiver verifies exact GitHub HMAC bytes before parsing an allowlisted pull_request delivery. Native issue identifiers in the PR title or body link stable repository/PR identity, safe HTTPS URL, title and open/closed/merged state. Unknown identifiers record diagnostics. A PR event changes issue status only through the team's Git automation rules (GITHUB-003), recorded as automation activity. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/github-links.test.ts` for signed linking and state, plus GITHUB-003's status journey. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/github-links.test.ts` (signed PR linking from identifiers in the title or body; branch names and status rules belong to GITHUB-003).

clauses.title: Durable latest PR state
clauses.text: Delivery replay identity and native version/configuration fences commit with PR/link history. Conflicting replay refuses, older state cannot regress newer state, and merged state stays terminal. Current authority gates both fresh and retained results. Safe histories are portable; credentials require destination re-entry and restored historical deliveries never replay. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/github-links.test.ts` (tests tagged GITHUB-002). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/github-links.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Native scoped API
clauses.text: Named reveal-once Base tokens admit only the explicit `/api/v1` routes under route-selected scopes: issue list/detail and description history use `issues:read`; issue create/version-checked update, description restore and description checklist mutations use `issues:write`; comment creation and author-only comment checklist mutations use `comments:write`; metadata uses `metadata:read`; project list/detail use `projects:read`; and project create/update use `projects:write`. The project list applies portfolio filters and returns matching counts; create and update accept native project fields, validate dates and record planning-field activity. Project lists currently return the complete workspace list without pagination (API-003). Token expiry, revocation, active issuer/workspace and resource authority are checked on every request; bearer tokens never admit documents, generated functions, private files or token administration. Existing native mutation and notification rules apply; no deletion API or product role is added. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/integration-api.test.ts`, `tests/worker/dev-credentials.test.ts` (tests tagged API-001). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/integration-api.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Token authority and usage
clauses.text: Settings exposes safe metadata/usage and revocation. Issuance and each mutation retain current authority inside the same SQL transaction. Usage-write failure denies admission. Removal revokes issued tokens.
