Stale writes and authority races publish no unauthorized changes; committed native notification intent remains durable after a response denial. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/integration-authority.test.ts`, `tests/worker/integration-api.test.ts` (tests tagged API-002). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/integration-authority.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Durable native delivery
clauses.text: Registered public HTTPS destinations receive minimal native created/updated/completed issue events under stable business identities. Base delivery attempts, backoff, cooldown and accepted/rejected/uncertain results survive restart. Ambiguous sends never retry under fresh IDs; explicit reconciliation requires receiver evidence. Mapped imports and restore create no delivery events. Until Settings has verified the hosting account’s domain inventory or an enforcing service is bound, outbound is visibly unconfigured and native events are retained. The built-in Base transport refuses private and account-owned destinations, pins TLS for non-Cloudflare answers, and uses its explicit all-Cloudflare platform-fetch route with the re-resolution and destination-zone TLS limits in docs/INTEGRATIONS.md. Failed sends never switch transports. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/outbound-webhooks.test.ts`, `tests/worker/issue-deletion-webhooks.test.ts` (tests tagged WEBHOOK-001). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/outbound-webhooks.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Export contents
clauses.text: The portable export contains a manifest, original attachment bytes, and every operator, team, workflow status, issue, comment, attachment metadata, link, relation, evidence revision, intake decision, project, cycle and snapshot, label, saved view, notification, custom field, non-secret setting, idempotency record, failed operation, and audit entry. It never contains a session, signing, source, or provider secret. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/data-http.test.ts`, `tests/worker/data-archive-failure.test.ts`, `tests/worker/data-http-collision.test.ts` (tests tagged DATA-001). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/data-http.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Mapped import preflight
clauses.text: Separately from portable restore, an Owner or Admin (role matrix; Members and Guests are refused 403) can preflight an import of issues supplied as CSV rows or as a JSON array of objects with the same field names, before anything is written. The fields are title, description, team, status, priority, assignee, project, cycle, labels, estimate, due date, expected outcome, customer impact, source ID, and source record ID. The preflight validates the mapping, the timestamps, and every team, status, assignee, project, cycle, label, duplicate, and dependency reference, and reports every row that would fail with its row number and reason, and every nonempty value it would not import. One preflight covers the whole file of a run, up to the measured run limits in docs/MOVE-IN.md. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/linear-import.test.ts`, `tests/worker/issue-deletion-import.test.ts` (tests tagged DATA-002), plus the import rows of the role-matrix journey: a Member's preflight, apply, resume and rollback are each refused 403 and write nothing, and an Admin's succeed. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/linear-import.test.ts` (preflight by any operator; the Owner/Admin restriction is open with ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Atomic mapped import
clauses.text: An Owner or Admin (role matrix) applying a successful preflight records an import-run identifier and publishes the run in batches, each written atomically, preserving supplied creation and update times. A failed batch writes none of that batch and leaves earlier batches of the run in place for resume (DATA-006). *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/data-import-atomic.test.ts` (tests tagged DATA-003), plus the import rows of the role-matrix journey (DATA-002). *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/data-import-atomic.test.ts` (apply by any operator; the Owner/Admin restriction is open with ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Idempotent mapped import
clauses.text: Reapplying the same import-run identifier and source record identifiers creates no duplicates and returns the first run's result. A mapped import creates normal activity and one audit entry for the run, and no operator notifications. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/data-import-atomic.test.ts`, `tests/worker/imported-person-erasure.test.ts`, `tests/worker/issue-deletion-import.test.ts` (tests tagged DATA-004). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/data-import-atomic.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Exact portable restore
clauses.text: `rer import --target local` restores a portable DATA-001 archive without synthesising activity, audit entries, notifications, or new timestamps; its records are equivalent after export, import, and export as `BASE-DATA-001` requires. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/data-archive-failure.test.ts`, `tests/worker/data-http-collision.test.ts`, `tests/worker/data-http-concurrency.test.ts` (tests tagged DATA-005). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/data-archive-failure.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Staged import run
clauses.text: Only an Owner or Admin starts, resumes or repeats a run (role matrix). One reviewed run of up to the measured limits in docs/MOVE-IN.md (tested at 2,000 issues; larger sources are split into the runs of one migration under DATA-017, never truncated) previews once and publishes in staged batches under one run identifier. Status says truthfully how many of its batches are applied and whether the last batch failed. An interrupted run (a stopped client or a failed batch) resumes from its last committed batch, and every source record lands exactly once. Issues already published are visible and marked as part of an unfinished run. Applying the same reviewed run again returns that run with no new rows; a different file under the same source name conflicts. No notification, mail or webhook is sent for an imported issue. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/data-staged-cli.mjs` (tests tagged DATA-006), plus the import rows of the role-matrix journey (DATA-002). *Status:* partial — `tests/e2e/data-staged-cli.mjs` (staged runs by any operator; the Owner/Admin restriction is open with ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Reconciliation report
clauses.text: For a finished or partial run, Settings and the terminal give one report and one CSV: source rows read against Vector issues written, by team, status, project, cycle and assignee; every omitted nonempty field with its count; every unresolved or ignored reference with its row; what the source file does not contain at all; and a mapping of each source ID to its Vector identifier. An imported issue shows its source ID, and searching for that source ID finds it. *Acceptance:* `tests/e2e/jira-public-journey.mjs` (exercises this behaviour; the test does not yet tag DATA-007). *Status:* done — `tests/e2e/jira-public-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Linear API enrichment file
clauses.text: A JSON file the owner produces with Linear's GraphQL API (docs/LINEAR-API-FILE.md) merges with a Linear CSV run by source ID. Comments become imported comments with their original time and a read-only author name; attachment links become named HTTPS links that are never fetched; blocks and duplicate relations become dependencies and duplicate links when both issues are in the run, and are reported otherwise. Attachment bytes are reported as not in the file. A malformed file (an unsafe link scheme, an unknown source ID, or a comment for an issue outside the run) is refused with row-level reasons and nothing written. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/linear-api-import.test.ts` (tests tagged DATA-008). *Status:* done — `tests/worker/linear-api-import.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Jira CSV preflight and loss review
clauses.text: A Jira All Fields CSV file is reviewed before any write, through the same staged import service. Source IDs stay distinct from mutable issue keys; repeated headers keep their positions and exact original bytes. All date-bearing cells, including comments and attachment metadata, determine one calendar pattern; ambiguous, mixed or impossible dates are refused, and offsetless instants require an explicitly supplied source offset. Every unsupported occurrence stays visible as an omission, and mappings must be confirmed and row errors fixed before apply. Qualification is synthetic-only against the documented file profile: no owner-supplied account file has been checked, and the Site has no verified importer receipt for this source. The exact publisher clause and acceptance details remain in the linked contract.

clauses.title: Jira staged apply and reconciliation
clauses.text: The reviewed Jira CSV imports preserved issue times (Resolved for completion, or an explicitly confirmed fallback), due dates, estimates, exact labels, confirmed status/priority/operator/sprint mappings, in-file parents and Blocks, canonical Duplicate links and original-author/time comments. Stable source IDs remain authoritative; old keys are visible and searchable. Outside-file and Relates targets are omissions and never bind a same-key native issue. Attachment bytes are never fetched; named HTTPS links require explicit opt-in. Preview, CLI review and stored report share one loss review and configuration fingerprint. Staged apply/replay, SQL reconciliation and whole-run rollback use the existing lifecycle; later native edits refuse the entire rollback without changes. Historical imports dispatch no notifications, mail, webhooks or agents. The public route requires a current Owner or Admin session (role matrix) and same origin; API tokens are not admitted. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/jira-apply.test.ts` (tests tagged DATA-010), plus the import rows of the role-matrix journey (DATA-002). *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/jira-apply.test.ts` (any operator session; the Owner/Admin restriction is open with ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Erasing an imported person
clauses.text: An Owner or Admin (role matrix; Members and Guests are refused 403) can erase a person that imports carried, by exact email and/or up to five exact display names, after a counts-only preview and a typed confirmation. One D1 batch removes the person from every import run, applied or still pending: records that hold them become permanent tombstones that never publish or replay, runs labelled with their email are retired, originals holding them are withdrawn, imported comments they wrote read as deleted with no author name, reconciliation reports lose those cells, and development mail naming them is dropped. Issues already written stay; a pending run still finishes, without the erased records and without links to them. A current or suspended member, or an open invitation, is refused here; a member's native and imported records are erased together by ROLE-012. The erasure journal is append-only, and an archive made before the erasure is refused on restore when a later archive's journal is supplied. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/imported-person-erasure.test.ts`, `tests/worker/base-refresh-upgrade.test.ts` (tests tagged DATA-011), plus a Member's erasure preview and confirmation each refused 403 with nothing erased. *Status:* partial — `tests/worker/imported-person-erasure.test.ts` (erasure by any operator; the Owner/Admin restriction is open with ROLE-008).

clauses.title: Signed owner claim
clauses.text: An explicitly configured signed installation claims its initial owner through Base native operator-auth using a five-minute signed claim bound to trusted issuer, installation, app origin and canonical owner email. Confirmation GET/HEAD is inert; native same-origin POST admits exactly once. No request provides configuration or setup secrets. Existing initialization and permanent admission ledgers refuse all subsequent claims. Ordinary local configured-owner setup remains the default without RER claim configuration. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/owner-claim.test.ts`, `tests/worker/owner-claim-upgrade.test.ts`. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/owner-claim.test.ts`.

clauses.title: Owner-gated editor
clauses.text: The optional same-origin Base editor is admitted only for a recorded installation owner with a current native Base owner session, active mapped Vector identity and restored-installation grant where applicable. Its config endpoint returns a no-store non-secret lease of at most thirty seconds and exact trusted management origin. Logout/authority loss removes the mount; lease expiry bounds silent revocation. Each hydrated destination controls compiled-edit readiness. Application CSP preserves unrelated directives and permits framing only by self and that exact management origin. A hosted management session and independently registered frame-ancestors remain required; source adoption is not hosted acceptance. *Acceptance:* `tests/worker/editor.test.ts`. *Status:* done — `tests/worker/editor.test.ts`.

nonGoals: Multiple workspaces, tenants, or organisations
Roles, per-team visibility, and granular permissions
External customer accounts, portals, forms, or public roadmaps
Source-specific Sentry, Slack, GitLab, Jira, or email integrations in core
AI triage, deduplication, ranking, or project-health inference
Custom workflow categories
Initiatives, roadmaps, Gantt charts, critical-path planning, time tracking
Per-issue checklists
Multiple assignees
Notification email beyond assignments and direct mentions; chat or push notification channels
Native mobile applications
Real-time collaborative text editing

seeds.name: coffer
seeds.oneLiner: Owner-run donor records and giving for a US nonprofit: donors and households, an immutable gift ledger with pledges and soft credits, Stripe card and monthly gifts, emailed receipts, letters and year-end statements, and a checked Little Green Light move-in.
seeds.summary: Owner-run donor records and giving for a US nonprofit: donors and households, an immutable gift ledger with pledges and soft credits, Stripe card and monthly gifts, emailed receipts, letters and year-end statements, and a checked Little Green Light move-in.
seeds.maturity: first release; independently gated on a computer and a hosted Cloudflare Worker on 18 October 2026

clauses.title: Private app boundary
clauses.text: Hono serves `/health` and owns `/api`; native owner/operator sessions protect `/app` and `/api/coffer`. Every handler checks the actor's role, the exact host and, for cookie changes, the same `Origin`. Each write batch re-checks the session or key inside the same D1 transaction, so a revoked session, role change or revoked key stops a request in flight. Unknown paths return real 404s. Public donor-facing pages added by the target (`GIVE-001`, `GIVE-005`, `CAMP-002`) live outside `/app` under their own rules and never widen this boundary. *Acceptance:* The role-boundary test signs in as owner, member and agent, sends cross-origin writes, revokes a key and deactivates a member, and every refused request returns 401 or 403. *Status:* done. Evidence: `tests/coffer.test.mjs`, `src/coffer/auth.ts`.

clauses.title: Donors and households
clauses.text: A donor has an email (or none) that no unrelated record shares. A household is found by name or created. Several emails, phones and postal addresses per constituent with one primary of each, and an email shared by members of one household, are `DONOR-013`; a person's name parts, salutations and envelope name are `DONOR-014`. Members, admins and the owner add and edit donors; edits are versioned, and a stale version is refused rather than overwritten. *Acceptance:* A member adds donors through HTTP and the browser journey adds, edits and opens donors; the donor page lists household members. *Status:* done. Evidence: `src/coffer/donors.ts`, `tests/coffer.test.mjs`, `tests/browser-journey.mjs`.

clauses.title: Immutable ledger
clauses.text: A gift is an integer-cent line with its date, method, fund, optional pledge and goods-or-services answer. Database triggers refuse changes to amounts, dates, donors or references; a correction is a reversal line of the opposite amount, once per gift. Dollar input is parsed exactly; the API takes `<field>Cents` for exact integers. Every later gift kind in this contract (online, recurring, split, soft-credited, in-kind, refunded) is written as lines in this one ledger. *Acceptance:* The ledger test records exact-cent gifts, refuses sub-cent, future-dated and duplicate-reference gifts, reverses one once and reads the lifetime and per-year totals back. *Status:* done. Evidence: `src/coffer/gifts.ts`, `migrations/core/0016_coffer.sql`, `tests/coffer.test.mjs`.

clauses.title: Consent history
clauses.text: Consent is append-only per donor and channel with method, evidence, capture date and who recorded it; the newest row is the current answer. Rows are removed only by erasure. The target adds SMS and phone channels, donor self-service changes and sender-synced unsubscribes as further rows of this same history (`COMM-001`). *Acceptance:* The appeal test records grants and withdrawals for several donors and channels and the donor history shows the newest answer per channel. *Status:* done. Evidence: `src/coffer/donors.ts`, `tests/coffer.test.mjs`.

clauses.title: Acknowledgement letters
clauses.text: Gifts at or over the threshold (default $250) without a live letter are due within the target days (default 14). No letter is prepared until a person has saved the settings; the letter must state donor name, amount, gift date, organization and the goods-or-services statement. A batch freezes its letters and content hash. A person approves the exact hash; export, then a recorded sent date. Imported gifts with an unknown goods answer wait for a person's answer. `RCPT-011` and the importers widen this: an imported gift takes its goods answer from the source's non-deductible amount (`MOVE-001` to `MOVE-006`), so only a gift whose source holds no answer waits; and a gift is due only while its acknowledgement status is "not acknowledged", so a gift acknowledged in Coffer or in the incumbent before the move, marked do not acknowledge, or received before the acknowledge-from date (`MOVE-007`) is never due or overdue, and recording a batch's sent date marks each of its gifts acknowledged by letter with the batch linked. This is the reviewed letter path for printed and hand-mailed acknowledgements; delivering the same approved letters by email is `RCPT-002`, print layouts are `RCPT-003` and one letter per household is `RCPT-009`. *Acceptance:* The acknowledgement test has an agent prepare a batch, refuses preparation before settings are reviewed, lets only a person approve, exports the CSV with the exact letter text and records the sent date. *Status:* done. Evidence: `src/coffer/acknowledgements.ts`, `src/coffer/settings.ts`, `tests/coffer.test.mjs`.

clauses.title: Consent-checked appeals
clauses.text: An audience includes only donors whose newest consent for the channel is yes and who have the needed address; exclusions are counted by reason. Each recipient is frozen with the exact consent row; approval, export and sending refuse if any of those rows is no longer current. Sending the approved audience through Mango or Mailchimp is `COMM-002`; this clause is the consent gate every send passes. Excluding inactive and deceased constituents is `DONOR-012`; excluding constituents with a solicitation restriction under the reason "do not solicit", and deliberately including one in a run, is `DONOR-015`; and one piece per household is `RCPT-009`. *Acceptance:* The appeal test prepares an audience, counts exclusions by reason, refuses approval after a withdrawal and exports only consenting recipients. *Status:* done. Evidence: `src/coffer/appeals.ts`, `tests/coffer.test.mjs`.

clauses.title: Prepare, then a person decides
clauses.text: An expiring, revocable bearer key reads records and runs only `ack.prepare` and `appeal.prepare`. Approvals keep the preparer's and approver's identity and role with the content hash. Wider, separately granted agent work is `DEV-012`; no agent key gains an action this clause does not name unless that grant says so. *Acceptance:* The role-boundary and acknowledgement tests create a key, prepare with it, are refused every other command, record agent and owner roles on the approval and stop working on revocation. *Status:* done. Evidence: `src/coffer/commands.ts`, `src/coffer/auth.ts`, `tests/coffer.test.mjs`.

clauses.title: Reviewed Stripe move-in
clauses.text: Saved Stripe customer and charge list pages go through Base's import kit. Preview writes nothing; apply needs the exact reviewed fingerprint; the journal retains the original pages; undo stops at anything a person has since built on. Failed, refunded, non-USD, duplicate and already-imported objects are skipped with reasons and never enter the plan. This saved-page path stays for history a live connection (`PAY-001`) is not granted, and for nonprofits that never give Coffer API access. *Acceptance:* The move-in test previews 15 gifts with every skip reason, refuses a wrong fingerprint, applies, reads the journal and undoes; a second test proves undo stops at a donor a person has since changed. *Status:* done. Evidence: `src/coffer/imports/service.ts`, `src/coffer/imports/snapshots.ts`, `tests/coffer.test.mjs`.

clauses.title: Custody and erasure
clauses.text: Base portability backs up product records, approvals and import custody, excluding identity and credentials, and restores only into an empty installation. A hosted Coffer backs up and restores the same archive with `rer run backup:hosted`, authenticated by the owner's session; its restore goes only into a newly deployed, empty environment and keeps that environment's own owner. The owner erases a donor with explicit `ERASE`: personal data, consent, letter text, gift notes and affected Stripe originals go; gifts move to an anonymous placeholder; hashed suppression stops re-import; a later journal fences older archives. Every record the target adds (interactions, tasks, opportunities, receipts, provider events) joins the same backup and the same erasure. *Acceptance:* The backup test restores into a fresh installation and compares donor histories and approvals; the hosted-restore test backs up through the command, restores into a fresh installation with large retained originals, keeps the destination owner and refuses a second restore; the erasure tests remove personal data, keep anonymous gifts, refuse re-import and fence an older archive. *Status:* done. Evidence: `src/coffer/archive-policy.mjs`, `src/coffer/imports/erasure.ts`, `scripts/backup-hosted.mjs`, `tests/coffer.test.mjs`, `tests/hosted-restore.test.mjs`.

nonGoals: US bank (ACH) checkout, PayPal, Venmo and text-to-give
Sending notes to the family for tribute gifts
A live QuickBooks Online connection
Native phone apps
Prospect research, grants and planned giving
Tax advice or non-cash gift valuation

seeds.name: Pantry
seeds.oneLiner: Keep the books for one US business: bank statements, receipts, invoices, bills and a month-end close you can review with your accountant.
seeds.summary: Keep the books for one US business: bank statements, receipts, invoices, bills and a month-end close you can review with your accountant.

clauses.title: Set up the business
clauses.text: The owner records the legal name, entity type, state, fiscal year start, books start date, the tax method declared with the accountant and the book/report policies; adds people with a role and grants and invites them to sign in. Each role is enforced by the server on every request, including a removed role on a live session and cross-site writes. **Acceptance evidence:** `ledger.test.mjs` › `PAN-01 a business is set up with declared policies and each role is enforced by the server`.

clauses.title: Chart of accounts and opening balances
clauses.text: A person starts from a small service-business chart or builds their own (one receivable, one payable and one retained-earnings control account); opening balances are a balanced draft that a second person posts. An account with postings keeps its type and role. **Acceptance evidence:** `ledger.test.mjs` › `PAN-02 a chart of accounts is configured and opening balances post only after review by a second person`.

clauses.title: Customers, vendors and documents
clauses.text: A person keeps customers and vendors with terms, and uploads source documents (PDF, image, text, CSV, OFX) whose exact bytes and SHA-256 are kept and returned. CAPTURE-001 to CAPTURE-007 add capture and reading on top of this store. **Acceptance evidence:** `ledger.test.mjs` › `PAN-03 customers, vendors and source documents are kept, with document bytes returned exactly`.

clauses.title: Invoices and credits
clauses.text: A person drafts an invoice with lines, income accounts and a sales tax code or exemption per line; a line with no tax decision stops approval. A second person approves the exact version, except the owner and ACCESS-003 atomic within-limit self-issue; automatic recurring runs, early-payment discounts, integration mappings, imported/opening sign-offs and ACCT-003 bulk write-offs retain their named approvals. Issuing posts receivable, income and sales tax. A credit for an issued invoice is approved and issued the same way and applies to that invoice. Sending, payment and follow-up are INVOICE-002 to INVOICE-005 and PAY-001 to PAY-005. Issuing limits that let a preparer issue alone within an amount the owner sets are ACCESS-003. **Acceptance evidence:** `subledgers.test.mjs` › `PAN-04 invoices are drafted, approved and issued; unknown tax stops approval; credits reduce what is owed`.

clauses.title: Bills and evidence
clauses.text: A person records a bill or expense with lines and posts it to payables, attaches its source document, and sees its payable status. A posted bill without a document is a close exception until a document is attached or someone with the post grant records why there is none. **Acceptance evidence:** `subledgers.test.mjs` › `PAN-05 bills post to payables with their evidence; a bill without evidence is a close exception until resolved`.

clauses.title: Payments recorded from outside Pantry
clauses.text: A person records a payment received or made outside Pantry (check, wire, Zelle, cash, a provider Pantry is not connected to) against a bank account and allocates it, wholly or partly, to open invoices or bills; unapplied money stays visible as a credit. Recording moves no funds. Reversing a payment reopens what it paid. Provider-backed collection and bill pay are PAY-001 and BILLPAY-001. Paying bills from a credit card or line of credit is BILL-003. **Acceptance evidence:** `subledgers.test.mjs` › `PAN-06 payments made outside Pantry are recorded and allocated to open items without moving money`.

clauses.title: Statement import
clauses.text: A person imports a CSV or OFX (QFX, QBO) bank statement for a named bank account. OFX must name that account; a CSV is confirmed by its last four digits. Re-importing the same file adds nothing; an overlapping download adds only new lines; a statement in the other format overlapping the same days is refused. The original file is kept. This remains the path for any account without a live feed and for history before a feed's reach (BANK-002). **Acceptance evidence:** `bank.test.mjs` › `PAN-07 CSV and OFX statements import against the right bank account, and repeats create no duplicates`.

clauses.title: Matching
clauses.text: A person (or an approved agent proposal) matches statement lines to ledger postings: one-to-one, one deposit split across several receipts, a fee or bank income the books lack, a transfer between accounts, a vendor payment, or a partial customer settlement. A payment already recorded is cleared by its bank line without being posted again. A match that does not balance is refused; a line or posting is matched once. **Acceptance evidence:** `bank.test.mjs` › `PAN-08 statement lines match to the books through splits, fees, transfers and partial settlements, never posting a recorded payment twice`.

clauses.title: Reconciliation
clauses.text: A statement reconciles only when its opening follows the last reconciled closing, its lines account for the change in balance, every line is matched, and the ledger's bank balance less items not yet on a statement equals the closing balance. Every remaining difference is listed; a completed reconciliation stores its proof and freezes its matches. Balances typed wrongly from a statement can be corrected, with a reason, before reconciliation. **Acceptance evidence:** `bank.test.mjs` › `PAN-09 a statement reconciles only when its balances are proven, and every difference is explained first`.

clauses.title: Journals
clauses.text: A person prepares a balanced manual entry, optionally citing a document; someone else with the post grant posts the exact revision they reviewed. Preparer, poster and approval are kept. Control accounts post only through invoices, bills and payments. **Acceptance evidence:** `ledger.test.mjs` › `PAN-10 a journal entry posts balanced, approved by someone other than its preparer, for the exact version reviewed`.

clauses.title: Reversal
clauses.text: A person with the post grant corrects a posted entry with a dated reversal linked both ways. Both entries stay in the ledger; an invoice is corrected by a credit instead; a matched posting must be unmatched first. **Acceptance evidence:** `ledger.test.mjs` › `PAN-11 a posted entry is corrected by a linked reversal and its history survives`.

clauses.title: Reports
clauses.text: Trial balance, general ledger with running balances, profit and loss, balance sheet (with calculated current and prior-year earnings) and receivables/payables aging, all from the same posted lines, with the subledgers tied to their control accounts. REPORT-001 to REPORT-008 extend these into the full reporting job. **Acceptance evidence:** `close.test.mjs` › `PAN-12 trial balance, general ledger, profit and loss, balance sheet and ageing all come from the same ledger`.

clauses.title: Close and lock
clauses.text: A period's checklist calculates whether every bank account is reconciled through month end, nothing is left unposted, bills have evidence, subledgers agree with control accounts, the trial balance balances, no agent proposal waits and every question Pantry asked about the month is answered (PAN-18); review tasks are completed by named people. Someone with the lock grant locks the month. A reopening is requested with a reason and approved by a different person holding the reopen grant. **Acceptance evidence:** `close.test.mjs` › `PAN-13 a period closes through its checklist and lock; locked dates refuse people and agents; reopening needs an approved request`.

clauses.title: Leave with the books
clauses.text: Anyone in the books downloads the accountant package for a period (entity and declared policies, close checklist, trial balance, P&L for the month and year to date, balance sheet, aging, general ledger, reconciliations with proof, reversals, approvals, notes, document index) and the general ledger as CSV. `rer export` and `rer import` restore the complete books, documents, reconciliations, close state and move-in journal into a fresh installation, refusing an archive whose posted entries do not balance. Connection credentials stay installation-local and are not in the archive (DATA-001). **Acceptance evidence:** `close.test.mjs` › `PAN-14 the accountant package holds the period's reports, reconciliations, approvals and reversal history`; `tests/restore/restore.test.mjs` export → fresh clone → `rer import` → `rer setup` → identical books and document bytes, then start over in the same folder, and a refused restore over existing books.

clauses.title: Agent preparation
clauses.text: The owner issues an agent token. The agent reads its context (unmatched lines and postings, documents marked as untrusted evidence, close status) and files typed proposals: a match, a journal entry citing its document and quoting the passages used, a close packet of exceptions, or a variance explanation citing entries. A person approves or rejects each; approval re-checks the cited records, the lock and the approver's grants. A proposal whose cited record changed becomes stale. Typed commands: `node scripts/pantry-agent.mjs` and [API.md](API.md). The built-in agents in AGENT-001 to AGENT-010 file the same proposal types. **Acceptance evidence:** `agent.test.mjs` › `PAN-15 an agent prepares matches, entries and close work that a person approves; stale or unauthorised work never lands`; the browser journey drives `scripts/pantry-agent.mjs`.

clauses.title: Move in from QuickBooks Online or Xero exports
clauses.text: A person uploads the seven QuickBooks Online report exports, or Xero's six standard exports (chart of accounts, contacts, sales invoices, bills, the Trial Balance and the bank accounts' Account Transactions), and the reconciled bank balance at cutover; a dry run shows counts, refused rows with reasons, tie-outs (trial balance balances, open invoices equal receivables, unpaid bills equal payables, each bank balance equals its statement, one control account each; from Xero, each bank account's transactions reach the trial balance), what does not come in and why, and missing documents. Import writes staged records through Base's import kit with its journal and originals; undo removes them while nothing has been posted; the accountant's sign-off re-checks the tie-outs and posts the opening balances, after which corrections are entries, not undo. After a Xero import, a person connects Xero (read-only invoices and attachments, with the installation's own Xero app, `XERO_CLIENT_ID` and `XERO_CLIENT_SECRET`) and the files attached to the imported open invoices and bills are kept byte for byte on those records; a file over the document limit is listed, not carried; undo removes them too. RER Managed cannot reach Xero yet and says so in one line. See [MOVE-IN.md](MOVE-IN.md). MIGRATE-001 to MIGRATE-007 add live-API move-in with history and attachments, the full Xero connection and FreshBooks. **Acceptance evidence:** `move-in.test.mjs` › `PAN-16 a QuickBooks Online cutover is previewed, imported as staged records, undone or signed off by the accountant`; `move-in.test.mjs` › `XERO-001 Xero exports are previewed, imported, carry their attachments over, undone, and sign off to Xero's trial balance to the cent` (Xero faked at its network edge with recorded responses). The supporting `tests/api/oauth-return.test.mjs` XERO-001 journey proves that a cross-site Xero return keeps the local owner signed in and connected while forged or missing state is refused.

clauses.title: Receipts caught, read and attached
clauses.text: A person takes a photo of a receipt from a phone browser or uploads a photo, PDF or saved email; on an installation with a domain on Cloudflare, the owner creates a private Pantry address on the settings page (the mailbox routed to the Worker by Email Routing plus a random tag), and receipts forwarded to it arrive on their own. Every original is kept byte for byte with its SHA-256, an email whole with its attachment beside it. With the installation's own AI model key, entered by the owner on the settings page and stored sealed, Pantry reads the vendor, date, total, tax, currency and expense account; with no key it says to add one and reads nothing. It proposes the matching bank or card line, bill, payment or entry by amount, date window and vendor, and attaches the receipt only when a person accepts or corrects what was read; accepting a line not yet in the books records it to the chosen account. A rule the owner sets (vendor, account, up to an amount) may attach a receipt that matches exactly one line. The close lists every expense paid from a bank account that has no receipt, to add one there or record why none is needed; each entry's receipts open from the entry, the report drill-down and the general-ledger CSV. RER Managed hosting has no outbound connection for AI providers or a domain for mail yet, and says so in one line. See [docs/receipts.md](docs/receipts.md). CAPTURE-001 to CAPTURE-008 and CONNECT-006 extend it to the full capture job. **Acceptance evidence:** `receipts.test.mjs` › `Receipts: a phone photo is kept byte for byte, read by the install's own model, and attached to its card charge only when a person accepts`; `receipts.test.mjs` › `Receipts: an email forwarded to the private Pantry address is kept whole, read from its PDF, and a rule the owner set attaches it` (model faked at its network edge).

clauses.title: Pantry asks about what doesn't add up
clauses.text: About hourly, and on request, Pantry's books agent checks the books by plain rules: a deposit nothing is matched to, money out with no category, or a cost (a bill, or bank spending filed to an expense) without a receipt or recorded reason past ages the owner sets; two payments to one vendor, or two charges from one payee, of the same amount close together; and a statement closing balance the books' opening balance plus every bank transaction cannot reach. Each finding is one question, asked once, beside its exact record, with numbered answers that each say what they change (a category with the month's net income before and after, the open invoice or bill of that amount, a transfer, the payment already recorded, a reason). New questions go to the owner by email first, a few a day, with a link to the record; replies to the Pantry address from that owner answer them (a number files it, "always" also makes a bank rule, an attached receipt is kept and attached, other words are read by the installation's own AI model key into an answer that waits for a "yes"). In the app a person with the record grant answers the same way. Nothing posts without the answer; a reason for a missing receipt needs the post grant. A question the books settle first closes itself and says why. At close the month's questions are one thread, each open one saying why it is open, and the lock waits until none is open. Without a key the rule checks still run and say so; RER Managed hosting has no outbound connection for AI providers or domain for replies yet, and says so. See [docs/questions.md](docs/questions.md). AGENT-002 extends it to other people, channels and connected systems. **Acceptance evidence:** `questions.test.mjs` › `BOOKS-AGENT the agent asks the owner what does not add up, by email first; the answer files it and the agent learns the rule only when told` (model and mail faked at their network edge; replies through the Worker's email handler).

clauses.title: Stripe payouts and Gusto payroll book themselves
clauses.text: With the business's own Stripe key connected, the owner names the bank account payouts land in, the sales income account and the Activity start date. Supported USD charges, refunds, disputes and fees post through Stripe clearing at each balance transaction’s provider creation date (UTC). Invoice-link charges adopt the existing receipt and fee entries rather than posting sales twice. A payout is one clearing-to-bank transfer at its provider event date; its arrival date remains the expected date for bank matching, and its reconciliation view keeps gross sales, invoiced charges, fees and refund totals. This corrects the former payout-arrival recognition timing to standard clearing practice. Every provider item is inventoried for comparison. Previously booked payout journals stay immutable and their constituent IDs are associated before any new recognition; native invoice receipts stay intact. Otherwise-unowned events before Activity start date remain named historical items for human reconciliation, never automatic historical sales or an invented opening adjustment. Supported events from that date post once at provider time; locked or unsupported events stay named with their reason. With the installation's own Gusto app (`GUSTO_CLIENT_ID`, `GUSTO_CLIENT_SECRET`), the owner connects the Gusto company by OAuth and names the bank account Gusto debits; each processed regular or off-cycle payroll posts as one balanced entry on its check date (gross wages, employer taxes, company benefits and reimbursements; Gusto's net pay, tax, reimbursement and child-support debits, the tax debit split into taxes withheld from employees and employer taxes; paper checks, deductions and deferred taxes to Payroll liabilities); totals that do not add up wait for a person with the difference. Each booked payout or payroll is matched automatically to the bank line(s) that show it, from a feed or a file (one combined debit or one per kind), with an undo after which it is the person's to match; reading again never books twice. RER Managed hosting has no outbound connection for Stripe or Gusto yet, and says so in one line. See [docs/stripe-and-gusto.md](docs/stripe-and-gusto.md). PROC-001 to PROC-003, PAYROLL-001 and PAYROLL-002 extend it to every processor and payroll provider. **Acceptance evidence:** `connected.test.mjs` › `PAYOUT-001 a Stripe payout is split into gross sales, Stripe fees and refunds, matched to its bank deposit, and never booked twice`; `connected.test.mjs` › `PAYROLL-001 a Gusto payroll posts as one balanced entry (wages, employer taxes, withholdings, net pay) matched to its bank debits, once` (Stripe and Gusto faked at their network edge).
